    - `DiffusersBackend`: Hugging Face `diffusers` pipeline integration defaulting to CivitAI photorealistic checkpoint `SG161222/RealVisXL_V5.0` (configurable via `LOCAL_HEADSHOT_MODEL_ID` or `--model-id`, supporting SDXL, SD 3.5, and Flux-schnell). Uses `DPMSolverMultistepScheduler` with Karras sigmas and guidance scale 5.0 for high-fidelity skin textures and facial anatomy. Integrates `CompelForSDXL` for prompt weighting and automatic multi-chunk embedding alignment, bypassing the 77-token CLIP limit so full 150–450 token media-day prompts run without truncation. Automatically configures execution devices (CUDA on Windows/WSL2, Apple Silicon MPS, or CPU fallback), 16-bit mixed precision (`fp16`/`bfloat16`), and VRAM optimization techniques (`enable_model_cpu_offload()`, `enable_vae_slicing()`, `enable_vae_tiling()`). Hooks for ControlNet (pose/depth for consistent camera angles across portraits) and IP-Adapter (face identity consistency across seasons). The loaded pipeline is kept across calls: `get_backend()` returns one shared `DiffusersBackend` per backend name + config (`reuse_instance`; `clear_backend_cache()` drops them), so a batch loads the model once. Per call, IP-Adapter weights are loaded when a `ref_image` is given and unloaded when not (a pipeline holding them errors without an image; config `use_ip_adapter: false` turns it off), and a change in ControlNet use rebuilds the pipeline. If `CompelForSDXL` is unavailable, the two-encoder `Compel` fallback pads prompt and negative embeddings to the same length.
    - `ComfyUIBackend`: Local REST client communicating with ComfyUI (`http://localhost:8188`), handling image uploads, prompt workflow dispatch, WebSocket polling, and output image retrieval.
    - `MockBackend`: Deterministic offline PIL generator for fast unit tests without requiring GPU hardware or multi-gigabyte model weights.
  - **Seamless Integration Adapter (`adapter.py`):** Provides `get_local_generator_if_enabled()` and monkey-patches `headshots.make_headshot` / `headshots.rookie_headshots` when `USE_LOCAL_HEADSHOTS=1` or `LOCAL_HEADSHOTS=1` is configured, automatically resolving the team's physical weight tier donor plate and calibrated aperture mask (`get_donor_plate`), while keeping existing trait sampling, prompt templates, and `rembg` cutout pipelines 100% intact.
  - **Direct Jersey Inpainting Architecture (Option B, Recommended):**
    - Directly synthesizes the player's head, face, hair, and neck within a masked collar aperture of a canonical official team jersey donor (`AutoPipelineForInpainting` with `SG161222/RealVisXL_V5.0`).
    - **Authentic Donor Template Sourcing:** Uses unauthenticated high-resolution media-day player portraits sourced from official league media feeds (e.g., ESPN CDN $1000 \times 1000$ RGBA headshots) rather than AI-generated database images. Solves the missing NFL logo issue caused by Gemini/cloud AI trademark suppression filters: official photos physically contain the authentic metallic silver NFL shield, Nike collar ribbing, and official fabric mesh.
    - **Aperture Masking & Geometry ($1024 \times 1024$):** Preserves 100% of the authentic team jersey, fabric mesh, collar stitching, NFL shield, and shoulder pads. The aperture mask traces the inner boundary of the dark collar band with a 2-pixel Gaussian blur for natural contact shadow blending, stopping 3–5 pixels into the collar ribbing ($y \approx 940\text{–}978$ depending on archetype) without masking a single pixel of the metallic NFL shield ($\Delta = 0$).
    - **Five-Bracket Weight System Architecture (Multi-Archetype Calibration):**
      - Direct physical weight mapping replacing coarse 3-archetype grouping, solving the "skinny skill" distortion by giving prototypical 200–224 lb players their own muscular donor plates instead of forcing them into slender slot-receiver apertures:
        - *Tier 1: Speed / Featherweight ($< 200\text{ lbs}$, $13.8\%$ of league):* Anchored to Chris Olave ($187\text{ lbs}$, WR). Slender neck ($14\text{–}15"$), narrow collar aperture ($w \approx 175\text{ px}$), lean shoulders for CBs, Ks, Ps, and slot receivers.
        - *Tier 2: Prototypical Skill ($200\text{ – }224\text{ lbs}$, $23.1\%$ of league):* Anchored to Kendre Miller ($220\text{ lbs}$, RB). Athletic muscular neck ($16\text{–}17"$), broader shoulders and chest plate for standard QBs, starting RBs, safeties, and outside receivers.
        - *Tier 3: Power / Hybrid ($225\text{ – }254\text{ lbs}$, $22.3\%$ of league):* Anchored to Juwan Johnson ($231\text{ lbs}$, TE). Muscular thick neck ($17\text{–}18"$), prominent traps and wide shoulder pads for off-ball LBs, athletic TEs, fullbacks, and power QBs.
        - *Tier 4: Edge / Heavy ($255\text{ – }289\text{ lbs}$, $10.5\%$ of league):* Anchored to Carl Granderson ($261\text{ lbs}$, DE). Imposing V-taper, thick neck ($18\text{–}19"$), massive shoulder span for DEs, edge rushers, and in-line blocking TEs.
        - *Tier 5: Anchor / Lineman ($\ge 290\text{ lbs}$, $30.4\%$ of league):* Anchored to Erik McCoy ($303\text{ lbs}$, Center). Heavyweight frame, broad round jaw, massive $20\text{–}22"$ neck ($w \approx 280\text{ px}$) for offensive tackles, guards, centers, and defensive tackles.
      - **Aperture Masking & NFL Shield Preservation:** All 5 tiers trace the inner boundary of the authentic team collar band with a 2-pixel Gaussian blur (`generate_tier_mask`), achieving $100\%$ bit-exact preservation of the genuine metallic silver NFL shield ($\text{Max } \Delta = 0$ px on Tiers 2–5, $<7$ px blur feather on Tier 1). Sourced and calibrated across all $32$ franchises ($5 \times 32 = 160$ total league plates and pre-rendered aperture masks in `data/headshots/donors/`). User review studio (`donor_library_reviewer.html`) enables visual inspection, candidate swapping, and disqualification logging across all 32 teams.
    - **Seamless Anatomical Fit:** Eliminates two-stage collar scaling, manual trapezius funnels, and shoulder protrusion artifacts. The diffusion model naturally renders the neck and trapezius emerging from inside the collar opening with authentic ambient occlusion, contact shadows, and natural skin folds.
    - **Model Benchmarks (RealVisXL vs. FLUX.2 Klein / FLUX 3):**
      - `RealVisXL_V5.0` (SDXL inpainting, 6.6 GB): Runs in ~6.1s per $1024 \times 1024$ portrait on the RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB VRAM) using DPM-Solver++ Karras scheduler (28 steps, guidance 5.0). Fits comfortably in VRAM (~7.1 GB peak, ~8.9 GB headroom), yielding broadcast-grade photorealism, authentic facial pore detail, and 100% bit-exact jersey/shield preservation.
      - `FLUX.2-klein-4B` / FLUX 3 (5.6B DiT + Qwen3 text encoder, 15.3 GB total weights): Evaluated on `pc-wsl`. Requires ~15.9 GB VRAM during full-resolution inpainting concatenation, saturating the RTX 5070 Ti VRAM limit and taking 80+s per step with heavy memory paging. For standard media-day headshot inpainting, RealVisXL delivers superior photorealism at 10× the generation speed.
  - **Two-Stage Jersey Plate Architecture (Option A, Fallback, `jersey_plate.py`):**
    - Standardizes the separation of anatomical face generation from team uniform compositing, solving donor neck contamination, shoulder protrusion, and texture resolution mismatches.
    - **Step 1 (Bare-Neck/Chest Portrait Generation):** Generates the player wearing no shirt/collar (`completely shirtless, bare chest, bare neck`) at native SDXL portrait resolution ($896 \times 1152$), ensuring 100% continuous skin and muscle down to mid-chest with zero AI clothing fighting the uniform.
    - **Step 2 (Official Jersey Collar Plate Overlay, `extract_clean_jersey_plate`):** Isolates the official team jersey and collar stitching with a transparent neck opening. Per column of the collar box, the inner collar rim is the first opaque pixel that is neither skin nor an opaque backdrop (matched to the top-left corner); everything above it is cleared, then skin pixels in a band just under the rim (`rim_band`, default 3% of the height) are cleared too. Skin = YCbCr chroma in Cb 77–127, Cr 133–173, excluding pixels within `fabric_tolerance` (40) of the jersey's own colours (`fabric_colors`, default the torso colour sampled below the collar box) since brown, burgundy and old-gold fabric share skin chroma; skin is never removed outside the rim band. Trim colours that read as skin (e.g. a gold collar stripe) can be passed in `fabric_colors`. Pixel defaults (collar box 680–1050 × 250–650) are for a 896×1200 plate and scale to the plate's size when left unset.
    - **Dynamic Anatomical Neck Corridor & Shoulder Funnel:** Connects the player's jawline/chin neck width smoothly down to the exact jersey collar apex columns ($x \in [305, 595]$ on $896 \times 1200$), eliminating all bare trapezius flare and deltoid shoulder protrusion above the jersey shoulder contour ($y < Y_{\text{jersey\_top}}[x]$) with soft anti-aliased feathering, while ensuring zero donor skin and zero gap around the collar ribbing.
    - **Format Normalization:** `composite_headshot_to_jersey` defaults (chin y 590, centre x 440, collar apexes 305/595, crop 800×1000 from y 40) are also for a 896×1200 plate and scale to the plate's size; the broadcast crop is resized to 800×1000 when the plate isn't the reference size. Exports full-resolution 4:5 broadcast portraits ($800 \times 1000$ / $896 \times 1200$) and standardized transparent media-day cutouts ($700 \times 508$ WebP) for `static/players/{player_id}.webp`.
  - **Standalone CLI (`cli.py`):** `python -m headshots.local.cli --prompt "..." --out test.png [--backend mock|diffusers|comfyui] [--model-id ID] [--seed 42] [--size 1024]`.
  - **Tests:** `tests/test_local_headshot.py` covers jersey fabric preservation, non-reference plate sizes, pipeline reuse and per-call IP-Adapter/ControlNet switching, mock generation, device/offload behavior, ComfyUI, adapter patching, CLI, silhouette compositing, five-tier weight routing, aliases, donor resolution, and aperture masks.
- **Coach Headshots (`headshots/coach_headshots.py`, `headshots/headshot_appearance_generator.py`, `headshots/local/jersey_plate.py`, `tools/build_coach_donor_library.py`, COACH_SAVE_WRITES_PLAN U4):**
  - `appearance(..., role="coach")` draws coaches without position weights: ages 32-72 with more grey and recession at 55+, glasses in about 25%, facial hair in about 40% (tunable `COACH_*` constants), a build from the profile's height/weight and `body_type`, and a skin tone pinned by Madden's 1-7 head group from `face_shape`/`generic_head`. The player default (`role="player"`) is unchanged, byte for byte.
  - Coach plates are real NFL coaching-top photos (polo / quarter-zip / jacket) from the club CDN (`static.clubs.nfl.com`, docs/reference/COACH_DONOR_PHOTOS.md), registered by `tools/build_coach_donor_library.py` in the git-ignored `data/headshots/coach_donors/registry.json` with 1024x1024 aperture masks (2-px feather; weight tiers do not apply; 2-3 plates a team). Their terms are personal, non-commercial and non-redistributable, so the plates are local only.
  - `headshots/local/jersey_plate.py`'s two calls take `garment="jersey"` (the default, the player behaviour unchanged) or `garment="coach"`: a higher, narrower coaching-collar socket, and fabric sampled in left/centre/right bands so a contrasting placket or quarter-zip panel is not erased as skin.
  - `generate_coach_headshot(profile, team)` routes the face through `headshots.local` and composites it into the team's coach plate, writing `static/coaches/{coach_key}.webp` (700x508 cutout) and `data/headshots/dds/coaches/{coach_key}.dds` (512x512 BC3). The positive prompt says "NFL coach, team-colour coaching polo/quarter-zip" and never contains "jersey"; the negative prompt carries "jersey, shoulder pads, helmet, number". Each generated profile sets `portrait_status = 'GENERATED'`.
  - CLI `python3 -m headshots.coach_headshots [--season N] [--coach-key K] [--dry-run]` generates only `source = 'CREATED'` coaches and coordinators without a headshot; starting real coaches keep their real photos.
  - **Offseason portrait pack (`tools/coach_portrait_pack.py`, COACH_SAVE_WRITES_PLAN §2.8):** `python3 -m tools.coach_portrait_pack --season N [--dry-run] [--mark-installed]`, run after the OFFSEASON_START write. Every `GENERATED` coach profile without a `portrait_id` gets the lowest free ID of `COACH_PORTRAIT_RANGE` 5324-5484 (measured free of every Coach and Player `Portrait` in CAREER-MUBASE, docs/reference/MADDEN_COACH_RECORDS.md §4.2), allocated against every stored `portrait_id` and every earlier pack's manifest so an ID is never reused across coaches or runs. It copies each coach's 512x512 BC3 DDS into `data/headshots/dds/coaches/pack_<N>/` under its portrait ID, writes `pack_<N>/portrait_manifest.csv` (`portrait_id, dds_file, coach_key`) for `/build-mod`, and sets `portrait_status = 'PACKED'`; the next league-office write pushes `Portrait = <id>` and `Portrait_Force_Silhouette = false` onto the save record. `--mark-installed` sets `INSTALLED` for the coaches named in that pack's manifest once JR confirms the mod is in; `--dry-run` prints the allocations and writes nothing.
- **Standalone Portrait Converter (`headshots/portrait_converter/`, `docs/done/PC_MIGRATION_PLAN.md` §9.4, `docs/not_started/PRE_PC_WORK_2.md` Item A5):**
  - Converts transparent WebP media-day cutouts into in-game portrait textures for Madden 27 modding (injecting into `library_icons_brt` via MMC Modding Tools / Frosty to replace retired player portrait IDs).
  - **Core Interface (`converter.py`):** `to_portrait(webp_bytes, width=512, height=512, fmt="DDS_BC3", crop_box=None) -> bytes`, file helper `convert_headshot_file(input_path, output_path, width=512, height=512, fmt="DDS_BC3") -> Path`, and `convert_headshots_batch(input_dir, output_dir, ...)` (numeric file names first in numeric order, then other names alphabetically).
  - **Framing & Normalization:** Detects alpha bounding box, resizes with Lanczos filter to preserve aspect ratio without distortion, centers subject horizontally, and anchors chest/shoulders to bottom with configurable headroom margin (`headroom_ratio`, default 5%).
  - **Pure Python / NumPy DDS Compression (`dds.py`):** Encodes Direct3D 9/10 compliant binary DDS textures with standard 128-byte headers (`b"DDS "` magic + 124-byte `DDS_HEADER` struct) and vectorized BC3 / DXT5 (interpolated 8-level alpha) and BC1 / DXT1 (1-bit alpha punchthrough) block compression. Encodes a 512×512 texture in ~60ms without requiring any external C DLL dependencies. Also supports uncompressed 32-bit `RGBA` and `DDS_RGBA`.
  - **Standalone CLI (`cli.py`):** Supports single file conversion (`python -m headshots.portrait_converter.cli input.webp --out output.dds [--width 512] [--height 512] [--fmt BC3]`) and batch directory processing (`python -m headshots.portrait_converter.cli --batch-dir static/players/ --out-dir portraits/ --limit 50`).

### 2.21 Player Progression Engine (`engines/progression.py`, `db/migrations/2027_01_08_player_progression.sql`, `2027_01_11_progression_rating_groups.sql`)

**Progression revision (JR, 2026-10-31; engine/adapters implemented, live U13 application pending):** permanent learning occurs at completed-game checkpoints and in offseason reconciliation. `progression_state` separates earned season from application season, authoritative base from native observations/form, and PREPARED proposals from APPLIED verified receipts. `progression_evidence` handles mental checkpoints every four completed team games, technical midpoint/end and configurable partial-season reviews (initially six fresh meaningful appearances); a closed sustained playoff run independently qualifies with initially three fresh meaningful appearances, including bye teams. `progression_inputs` supplies cutoff-bounded observed game lines and player-aligned schedules, conservative postseason closure and explicitly limited box-score comparison proxies. `progression_policy` returns fractional skill entitlements and separate technical/mental band revisions, with no hard youth cutoff, no direct form conversion and no actual dev-field writes. Dev display labels follow bands through a configurable provisional mapping; the independent promotion lottery is removed. Personality effects remain neutral. The ~30/70 in-season/offseason split is a calibration target, not a verified universal ratio or an individual hard cap. Detailed design: PROGRESSION_PLAN §§5.3, 5.7, 5.9, 5.11.

**Receipt integration (`engines/progression_checkpoint.py`):** explicit `bootstrap_pass` requires known-neutral form and ConfidenceRating 50; raw ingests never bootstrap themselves, with two exceptions (JR, 2026-11-10). The first is the ingest that seeds a `madden_tune_*` database, which bootstraps from the week-1 clone — `season_loop` seeds there because a played season's ConfidenceRatings have drifted off 50 and the pass would refuse silently; §2.21a, `docs/reference/TUNING_LEAGUE.md` §6. The second is the players a save load creates (`bootstrap_newcomers`, called by `watch_save.py` before any progression stage plans): only those ids, at the league year `league_office.setup_application_season` gives the stage, with form neutral and the confidence gate skipped — a newcomer has no Mu state to adopt, so his save ConfidenceRating is Madden's own, not a neutrality proof (madden_tune_p2g's rookie class: 23 of 389 were 51-61 at 2027 week 1). It never runs while the database has no progression state at all, so the seeding load keeps its own gate, and a missing state for an existing player stays a hard failure in `prepare_pass`. `prepare_weekly_pass(cur,snapshot,season,week,source_fingerprint=...)` returns a document, pending event IDs and edits hash without awarding growth. `prepare_offseason_pass` computes full-year calibrated targets from immutable annual-start ratings and `progression_offseason` subtracts already-verified gains per rating. `acknowledge_pass` requires unchanged edits, verified writer success, read-back matching both document and stored event targets, and the actual output fingerprint; only then does one savepoint advance permanent state, accounting, form and annual/C2 summaries. APIs never commit or replace a save. Failed writes spend nothing; retries cannot stack growth or reroll a consumed review. Historical applied or stale prepared targets cannot be rendered after a newer base revision; weekly processing refuses skipping offseason reconciliation. Comparative baselines and supported skill mappings are bounded to the original evidence period. U13 owns durable replacement, crash recovery and the final transaction commit. Its formerly planned three-argument hook must supply snapshot/fingerprint and retain/acknowledge the returned proposal; `progression.in_season_checkpoint` explicitly rejects missing receipt context. Legacy direct `--commit`/offseason edit builders refuse bypassing an already-managed league. **U13 handoff:** PROGRESSION_PLAN §5.3a is the authoritative API/composition/recovery contract and V2_CORE_BUILD_PLAN U13 references it. The preparation envelope is not run_progression-style rows; its document already includes form. Keep the progression edits hash distinct from the combined U13 document hash and durably retain PREPARED recovery information before replacing a save. Versioned weekly/annual explanation views and in-season writer access are implemented under PROGRESSION_PLAN §5.3b; raw annual/private event output remains private. Preparing reports does not change the opaque application envelope or its edits hash.

**Base/form separation:** `load_save` retains native ratings as observations. Managed permanent state overrides those observations for progression/form/drift; drift uses the overlay paired with the applied state revision, including neutral bootstrap overrides. Form remains ±3, touches no physical or Injury rating, and does not convert to permanent growth. Form document preparation defaults to no applied-state storage; the CLI never stores player_form merely for emitting edits. Annual numerical fitting/turnover simulation remains a diagnostic baseline; it does not replace receipt/event scenario tests or prove the new tuning constants reproduce NFL careers.

- **OVR change (`compute_player_delta`):**
  $$\Delta\text{OVR}_i = \text{age} + \text{dev} + \text{pull} + \text{play} + \text{injury} + \varepsilon_i + \text{offset}(\text{age band}) + \text{league} + \text{performance}$$
  - `age`: the `engines/trade_value.py` aging fit for the player's position group and age band.
  - `dev` (legacy column name): band growth from stored spread and technical ceiling. Incoming Madden dev is only a one-time band/ceiling initialization fallback; managed stored bands override it. Display-label changes do not award additional growth.
  - `pull`: `0.09 × (ceiling − OVR)` when below the ceiling.
  - `play`: +0.35 for 15+ games or 700+ downs, +0.15 for 11+ games or 400+, −0.05 for 6+, −0.25 below; without games, +0.30 starter / −0.10 otherwise.
  - `injury`: −0.80 on IR, −0.45 for 4+ weeks out, −0.20 for 2+.
  - `ε`: `random.Random(f"prog:{season}:{player_id}").gauss(0, 1)`.
  - `offset`: `AGE_BAND_OFFSET` (−0.86, −0.76, −0.65, −0.28, −0.19, −0.19 for ≤23, 24–26, 27–29, 30–31, 32–33, 34+), the calibration to Madden's 2035→2036 offseason.
  - `league` (JR 2026-10-28: the league keeps its 2036 shape, same 90+ count and mean OVR): a development term weighted by age (1.0 to 23, 0.75 to 26, 0.35 to 29, 0 after) and OVR (1.0 to 79, 0.5 to 85, 0.2 to 87, 0 above), plus a star term for players 86+ and 32 or younger; both fitted each offseason by `calibrate_league_term` against the league projected after the coming draft (class shaped like the real 2036 class). `--follow-madden` turns it off.
  - `performance` (`performance_scores`, `performance_term`; plan §5.15): last season's production ranked within its group (QB, RB, REC, OL, FRONT, DB, K, P; 6+ games), plus awards (First Team All-Pro +1; Second Team, MVP, OPOY, DPOY, OROY, DROY +0.5; at most +1.5), clamped to −1 … +2. Not fitted to Madden (correlation 0.03 with its changes).
    - `production`: per game; for OL, FRONT and DB with downs played (2035 on), per down scaled to the group's median downs per game. OL: sacks allowed; FRONT: tackles, TFL, sacks, picks, deflections, forced fumbles, TDs; DB: picks, deflections, forced fumbles, TDs (tackles don't count).
    - `unit_scores`: team z-scores, higher better. OL from the team's own stat lines (sack rate allowed, yards per carry; every season); DB from opponents' completion rate, yards per attempt and passing TDs per attempt, FRONT from opponents' yards per carry (regular-season `team_stats` joined to `games`, 2035 on). `raw_performance` blends own and unit z-scores (`UNIT_SHARE`: OL 0.5, DB 0.4, FRONT 0.2) and ranks the blend to −1 … +1.
    - `performance_reliability`: each group's year-to-year correlation of that rank, pooled over consecutive seasons that both have downs (30%+ of stat lines; 2035→2036 now), scaled so the most repeatable group is 1 and ≤ 0 becomes 0; cached per database and season. 2026-10-28: RB 1.0, REC 0.86, QB 0.79, OL 0.63, P 0.62, DB 0.60, FRONT 0.45, K 0.
    - Score = rank × group weight × games / (games + 4).
  - Clamped by age and OVR band (a 99 can't rise; 95+ at most +1; 32+ at most +1; 29–31 at most +2; ≤24 −4 … +8; others ±6), at most ±8, and to OVR 40–99.
  - Cause tag (stored in `player_progression_history.cause` with `--commit`): `INJURY`, `STANDOUT_SEASON`, `POOR_SEASON`, `BREAKOUT`, `CEILING`, `PLAYING_TIME`, `AGE`, `DEVELOPED`, `REGRESSED`, `ON_TRACK`, `STALLED`.
- **Ratings spread (`apply_ratings_progression`; plan §5.1, §5.4):** ratings are grouped by `rating_group`: physical (`PHYSICAL_RATINGS`: Speed, Acceleration, Agility, ChangeOfDirection, Strength, Jumping, Stamina, ThrowPower, KickPower, Toughness), mental (Awareness, PlayRecognition), fixed (Injury), technical (the rest). With `delta_ovr` (as `run_progression` calls it) the target is the ratings' own archetype grade plus the change, since the PS5 scan's ratings grade ~1.1 OVR above the older `player_seasons` read on average and the scan's OVR wins.
  1. Physical: Speed and Agility −1/−2 from 29 (less outside CB, RB, WR), Acceleration, Jumping and ChangeOfDirection −1 from 31, ThrowPower and KickPower −1 from 33; the strength program (+1 Strength and Stamina below 90 for `years_of_experience` 0–1); Speed and Acceleration lowered by injury severity.
  2. Mental (`mental_decline`, D10): from 30, a share of the draft-day-to-peak gain each season (`MENTAL_DECLINE_SHARE`: 4% at 30–31, 7% at 32–33, 10% at 34+), never below draft day. Draft-day mental ratings are estimated (`estimate_entry_mental`: current minus Madden's mean gain by years pro, `MADDEN_MENTAL_GAIN_BY_YEARS` from the sample save's `Original*Rating`: +0.2 / +15.3 / +32.6 / +37.0 at 0–1 / 2–3 / 4–6 / 7+, floor 20) until the PC save's `Original*Rating` is loaded; the peak is the higher of the stored `peak_mental` and current.
  3. The rest of the change with `ovr_weights.adjust_ratings` limited by `skills=`: growth first puts `MENTAL_GROWTH_SHARE` (0.3) of the OVR gain into mental skills, then technical and mental; decline comes from technical skills; all archetype skills only if that can't reach the target. 0.3 makes 1–3-year players gaining 3 OVR grow mental to technical 3.7 to 1 in points per rating (Madden's sample: 3.3 to 1). `settle_archetype` then keeps the archetype on top.
  - 2037 dry run (1,502 players with ratings): growing players +0.16 physical, +1.96 technical, +3.19 mental points on average; declining −2.45 / −3.58 / −2.15.
- **Ceilings (`seed_player_ceiling`):** a draftee's `scout_prospects.true_value` (`SCOUT_PROSPECT`); otherwise seeded per player (`random.Random(f"ceiling:{player_id}")`) as OVR plus headroom by dev rank (5 / 9 / 13 / 16 at 24 and under, ~70% of that to 28, about 1.5 after), capped at 99 (`SEEDED`). A stored ceiling is reused. Hidden: never in a view, writer tool or `#debug`.
- **Phase C2 terms (V2 core U7, 2026-10-30; persona and coach terms are 0 per D4):** the formula gains `+ wear + continuity + mentor`, with upkeep inside `league`. Phase C2 is built; form is phase E (`engines/form_engine.py`, below).
  - `dev` becomes band growth (`band_growth`, plan §5.9): rate by age (0.5 / 0.33 / 0.2 per unit spread at ≤24 / ≤26 / ≤28) × spread × room (technical ceiling − OVR, full at 3 points) plus a seeded ±0.1 × spread (`Random(f"band:{season}:{id}")`); from 29 it resists decline at 0.23 × spread. Spread by dev rank `BAND_SPREAD_BY_DEV` (0, 1, 2, 3) unless stored (`seed_ceiling_band`: floor, spread, group ceilings).
  - `wear` (§5.8): −0.5 × mileage excess (career wear vs the group's league-mean season wear × seasons, clamped −0.5…1.5) × (1.5 − durability) × age ramp (from 27, 26 for CB/RB/WR, full 4 years later), bounded −1.2…+0.4; round(−wear) extra Speed and Agility points in the ratings layer. Durability (`seed_durability`): 0.5 + (mean(Injury, Toughness) − 80)/40 in 0.15…0.85, plus (sha256("durability:"+id) − 0.5) × 0.3, stored and reused. Mileage (`season_mileage`): touches, hits and snaps weighted per group so a starter carries ~10 wear a season.
  - Lasting injury damage (in `injury`): a major structural injury last season (ACL tear, Achilles, Lisfranc, patella, dislocated knee; not partial) rolls `Random(f"injury_damage:{season}:{id}")` with chance 0.5 × (1.5 − durability) in 0.15…0.85 for −1…−3 to Speed, Acceleration or Agility (0.35 OVR per point) and lowers the physical ceiling.
  - `upkeep` (§5.10, inside `league`, so off with `--follow-madden` and in the backtest): above 90, −0.5 × (OVR − 90) × (1 − (score+1)/2) × (1 + 0.5 × min(missed games, 8)/8 + 0.25 × wear excess), at least −4.
  - `continuity` (§5.13): −0.25 in the first season under a new coordinator for his side (`coordinator_tenures`) or on a new team, +0.05 otherwise, × 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 by age ≤26 / ≤29 / older. `mentor`: +0.15 at 23 and under (+0.075 to 25) when a same-group teammate is 29+ with Awareness 85+.
  - Breakthrough (§5.9): 28 or younger and in the group's top quarter of `performance_scores` both of the last two seasons → 50% chance (`Random(f"breakthrough:{season}:{id}")`) of +1…4 to the technical and mental ceilings; cause `BREAKTHROUGH`. New causes also `UPKEEP`, `WEAR`.
  - `PT_*` (§5.12, `behaviour_changes`): at most one gained and one lost a season (`Random(f"pt:{season}:{id}")`): QBs with ≤3 years and a sack rate ≥8% (150+ attempts) may gain PT_HAPPYFEET / PT_SEEINGGHOSTS and lose them at ≤5.5% or with experience; RBs with 150+ touches and ≤0.4% fumbles may gain PT_COVERBALL, ≥1.5% loses it; losses only for flags passed in `run_progression(traits=)`. Stored, written to the save by the phase D pass.
  - `dev_after` = `dev_before` until phase H; "Superstar X-Factor" is stored as "X-Factor" (the columns are varchar(16)). `--commit` also writes `player_durability`, `player_mileage` and the C2 columns (`store_progression`, falling back to the old columns when the 2027_01_14 migration is missing).
- **Phase D save pass (`engines/progression_save.py`):** pure absolute-rating edit builders retain OVR/grades/PlayerType, PT changes, XP/skill clearing, morale 50, all four zero sliders including LS and both dev flags off. Managed offseason application uses `progression_checkpoint.prepare_offseason_pass` plus verified acknowledgement. Bare `pass_edits` rejects bypassing managed accounting.
- **Dev-label ownership:** `progression_policy.summarize_band` projects a desired Mu label from technical/mental bands using provisional configurable thresholds; label settings do not affect learning RNG. The independent `dev_transition` lottery is removed from annual calculation and turnover simulation. Actual `TraitDevelopment` writes stay gated until ability decoupling is proven.
- **Progression explanations and writer tool:** `engines/progression_report.py` supplies pure `project_event`, `project_annual` and nested-whitelist `sanitize_public` with schema_version1. `progression.development_report(result)` projects annual calculations; `progression_checkpoint.explain_prepared(cur,prepared)` projects retained proposals without changing their hashes. Status is explicitly CALCULATED, PROPOSED or APPLIED. Reports separate permanent rating deltas/planned and realized OVR (with RATINGS vs RECORDED_OVR source), requested form/absolute effective OVR/form contribution, safe recorded reasons/evidence and desired versus actually observed dev traits. Public projections omit raw bands, durability, fractional internals, seeds and provenance. Explicit private audit includes before/after ratings, fractional requests/carry, band revisions, calibration/nested term breakdown, clamp/rounding/rating-target-gap details and provenance; upkeep is included in league, not added twice. Missing facts stay unknown. New preparation captures immutable before context; verified acknowledgement captures actual dev-after and persists only the public projection as metadata.report_public within the receipt savepoint. Receipt-only enrichment is excluded from immutable proposal replay comparison. No schema migration is needed for these JSONB fields.
- **Writer access:** `newsroom.db_tools.get_player_progression` remains registered in the dispatcher and returns `changes` (sanitized legacy annual summaries) plus `events` (versioned public projections). It selects only APPLIED metadata.report_public, never private metadata, and sanitizes it again with identity/calendar checks. Current article week and future seasons are excluded; explicitly earlier seasons have no current-week restriction. Next-year offseason reports are application week0, while their earned-year observed week remains private. Applied annual events suppress matching legacy summaries even when unavailable, preventing fallback timing leaks. Unsupported legacy cause/label/OVR values become unknown. Older events without captured/public reports are not backfilled or fabricated. Tests: tests/test_progression_report.py, tests/test_progression_reporting_integration.py and tests/test_progression_writer.py, including isolated SQL and receipt rollback checks.
- **Phase E form (`engines/form_engine.py`):** ±3 OVR from recent completed nonpreseason/non-Pro-Bowl game lines; mental/technical overlay only, neutral offseason, morale50. `form_edits` defaults store=False; requesting storage without explicit verified context refuses. The CLI only builds edits and rolls back. Managed weekly application goes through the checkpoint proposal/receipt lifecycle, which persists player_form only after readback.
- **Personality development (PERSONALITY_DEVELOPMENT_COACHING_PLAN; off by default, no active preset):** `engines/personality_development.py` is pure. `DevelopmentConfig(version, mode='off'|'shadow'|'enabled', weights ⊂ {drive, film, technical_preparation, coasting, teaching, qb_teaching, mentor}, max_relative_change ≤ 1, max_annual_abs_points, max_annual_ovr_difference, max_per_rating_annual_difference)` rejects NaN/unknown keys/wrong signs (coasting ≤ 0, the rest ≥ 0); shadow/enabled need a version, enabled needs every cap > 0. `evaluate_learning_effect(neutral_result=evaluate_development output, player_view, coach_views=[{view, exposure 0..1}], mentor_view, context, config)` scales each positive MENTAL/TECHNICAL entitlement `b` to `b·(1+s)`, `s` = drive ((drive−5)/5·w) + FILM_ROOM_RAT (mental skills) + PERFECTIONIST (technical skills) + COASTING + the strongest single exposure-weighted teaching contribution (TEACHER, or QB_WHISPERER for QBs; never summed across coaches), clamped once to ±max_relative_change; zero learning stays zero, REVIEW/physical/fixed/negative deltas, bands, labels and dev writes are untouched; other traits/sliders (money, quiet, confidence, Loner, YOUTH_DEVELOPER, ...) have no effect; WORKOUT_FANATIC is reported as deferred. Shadow returns no delta plus a private comparison. `mentor_adjustment` is a bounded difference from the existing mental mentor component (MENTOR trait, verified exposure; Loner neutral). `limit_annual_effect` applies per-rating |applied+new|, cumulative absolute spend (both signs, no carry) and paired OVR (`ovr_at`, against the neutral counterfactual without applied effects; refused when unprovable) caps. Offline experiments: `tools/personality_development_demo.py` (synthetic only; missing config = off and every arm equals neutral). **Receipt integration (U3; no production caller passes a config or context, so nothing changes today):** `progression_checkpoint.prepare_player(..., development_context=None, development_config=None)` (and `prepare_pass(..., development_config=None)`, contexts per player in `player_inputs`) runs only when the config is shadow/enabled: for each MENTAL/TECHNICAL decision it weights coaches by `personality_development_inputs.exposure_by_coach` over that checkpoint's evidence weeks, calls `evaluate_learning_effect`, then `limit_annual_effect` against the APPLIED receipts' recorded effects (`applied_development_effects`; PREPARED proposals spend nothing, a new config version never resets spend) with exact unrounded archetype OVR, and adds the capped effect to the requested entitlement before `quantize_entitlement` (shadow adds nothing). The neutral decisions stay unchanged and `metadata.personality_development_v1` records mode, policy version, config/context hashes, profile refs, evidence IDs, neutral deltas, raw/capped channels, requested/attributed/shadow effect, annual abs spend, prior applied, neutral/effect targets, cap reasons, public reasons and `mentor: disabled (MENTOR_COMPONENT_NOT_ISOLATED)`; off adds no key, so proposals are byte-identical. Retries return the frozen original snapshot. `progression_offseason.prepare_offseason` adds the season's APPLIED attributed effects to the neutral annual target once (`include_personality_effects`, recorded as `annual_effect_included` / `neutral_annual_target`) before `reconcile_annual`; carry is never re-paid. `progression_report.project_event` adds PERSONALITY/COACHING reasons only for APPLIED enabled receipts with an attributed effect, and the private audit carries the block. Mentor personality effects stay disabled until progression isolates its mentor rating component; legacy `PERSONA_TERM`/`COACH_TERM` stay 0.
- **Mood is not form (PERSONALITY_RELATIONSHIPS_PLAN §2.4):** relationship reactions and mood (`personality/reactions.py`, §7.11) never write ratings, form overlays, ConfidenceRating or Madden morale (which stays 50 under its owners here) and add no progression effect; mentorship opportunity, if a development policy ever rewards it, must not count the same event twice.
- **Backtest (`--backtest`, 2035→2036, 1,385 players, scratch rerun 2026-10-30):** mean ΔOVR predicted −0.106 vs actual −0.147; MAE 1.134, RMSE 1.515, 72.0% within ±1. The performance term is excluded by default because Madden's changes barely follow production. This comparison evaluates OVR changes, not rating spreading or dev-tier accuracy.
- **Simulation (`--simulate N`):** runs from 2036 with Madden-shaped turnover, rookie classes and simulated production, refitting the league term each season and applying seeded dev transitions. Five-season scratch rerun (2026-10-30): 90+ count 143–147 (baseline 144), mean OVR 78.08–78.10 (78.13), starter mean 85.61–86.18 (85.51), mean age 26.05–26.31; passes `STABILITY_BOUNDS_2036`. This is an OVR/dev turnover simulation; it does not model every persisted C2 injury, mileage or personality path and does not replace in-game acceptance.
- **CLI:** `python3 -m engines.progression [--season S] [--commit] [--dry-run] [--follow-madden]` (default 2037; `--commit` writes `player_progression_history` and `player_ceilings`), `--backtest [--with-performance]`, `--simulate N [--follow-madden]`, `--dsn`.
- **With C2 (2026-10-30, on `madden_test`):** backtest mean predicted −0.106 vs −0.147, MAE 1.134, RMSE 1.515, 72.0% within ±1; `--simulate 5` keeps 143–147 players at 90+ (2036: 144), mean OVR 78.08–78.10.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_progression.py` (38 tests with C2: durability, wear, lasting damage, band growth, breakthroughs, upkeep, continuity, mentors, PT changes, persona/coach 0, synthetic league-shape bound, real C2 backtest/simulation bounds as integration tests; earlier 22: ceiling seeding, terms, clamping, reproducible seeds, ratings adjustment, rating groups, peak-based mental decline, draft-day estimate, groups kept apart in the ratings layer, league-shape simulation and calibration, rookie class, turnover rates, backtest reporting, DB writes, production ranking, DB tackles and per-down rates, reliability weights, simulated performance, performance term).




### 2.21a League Office (`pipeline/league_office.py`, `pipeline/save_reader/league_setup.mjs`, V2 core U13)
Turns each save into Project Mu's decisions for all 32 teams and writes them in one verified save write. CLI: `python3 -m pipeline.league_office --snapshot <reader JSON> --save <CAREER-file> [--stage auto|<STAGE>] [--wave 1-3] [--seed S] [--dry-run] [--dsn ...] [--confirm-franchise-closed]`; `--recover <run_id> [--save <file>]`; `setup --save <CAREER-file> --out <new-file> [--dsn ...]`.
- **Stages:** REGULAR_WEEK, PLAYOFF_WEEK, OFFSEASON_START, RESIGN, FREE_AGENCY, COMBINE, PRO_DAY, DRAFT, UDFA, CUTDOWN, PRESEASON. `detect_stage` follows Madden's 8 offseason stops (JR's walkthrough, docs/reference), keyed on (week_index, CurrentOffseasonStage): Staff (0,1) OFFSEASON_START; Re-sign (1,1) RESIGN; FA prep (2,1) FREE_AGENCY wave 1; Free agency (3,2) FREE_AGENCY wave 2; Combine (5,4) COMBINE, which runs free-agency wave 3; Pro day (7,6) PRO_DAY; Draft (11,9) DRAFT; Recap (15,10) UDFA. Stage ≥ 10 or week ≥ 15 is UDFA; any other stop is a StageError (pass `--stage`). PreSeason is PRESEASON before week 3 and CUTDOWN from it (estimate). League-state weeks: `contracts_engine.OFFSEASON_STAGE_WEEKS` plus COMBINE 27 and PRO_DAY 28.
- **Each run plans, in order:** JR's pending moves (`franchise_pending_moves`, marked WRITTEN / REFUSED), the engine's APPROVED CPU deals with flag `auto_approved` (`step_engine_trades`, §2.17: player legs at `PRIORITY_ENGINE_TRADE`, between JR's pending moves and the stage's moves; picks are never written to the save; a player claimed already refuses the whole deal for the write and leaves it APPROVED, and a second refusal expires it through `front_office.could_not_make`; a leg whose player is no longer on the team it says he leaves refuses the deal, and a deal whose trade window, season or stage has passed is expired on the spot (`gm_trade_engine.stale_reason`, the same rule `expire_stale` applies) instead of being retried past the deadline), accepted from_user offers, drift write-back (`drift_check.diff`; rating drift only outside progression stages, because drift_check reads observations rather than the managed progression state), then the stage's moves: in season injury durations, IR for 4+ weeks out, activations only when healthy, waivers, roster legality to 63 active (`ROSTER_LIMIT` 65 − buffer 2, so an injury doesn't trigger Madden's auto-signing) and coach depth charts; at OFFSEASON_START, `step_salary_cap` draws the new cap with `contracts_engine.next_cap(prev_cap, plan.target, cap_seed(league_id))`, writes `SalaryInfo.TeamSalaryCap` with the -12,000 raw offset, shifts all 32 teams' cap rooms, and updates `plan.league_cap_dollars` so promoted practice-squad contracts and subsequent signings price against the new cap; contracts for practice-squad players Madden promoted; at the decision stage (below) retirements (recorded in `retirement_decisions`; un-retired as free agents when age ≤ 32 with OVR ≥ 75, or a seeded 50% at 33–34 with OVR ≥ 85); at every later offseason stop through CUTDOWN the retirement window, right after the drift steps and before re-signings, free agency, the draft and cut-down; RESIGN re-signs; FREE_AGENCY / COMBINE free-agency waves; DRAFT all picks; UDFA signings; CUTDOWN / PRESEASON cuts and charts. On non-OFFSEASON_START stages, `step_drift` restores `SalaryInfo.TeamSalaryCap` and 32-team cap rooms from `drift['salary_cap']`. Every write also sets cap fields: `PLYR_CAPSALARY` and `TEAM_SALARY` in $10,000 units; `SalCapCapRoom`, `SalCapSpendingMoney`, `SalCapNextYearCapRoom` adjusted by the change at one unit per $10,000; `CAP_ROOM_RANGE` is widened to `(-40_000, 484_287)`. `verify_read_back` checks `raw_team_salary_cap` and `team_salary_cap`. Post-write DB sync (`_apply_db`) updates `team_cap_seasons` for `plan.target` with the new cap and applies move room deltas to `cap_space` and `total_spend`. A player takes one of release / sign / trade per write (first claim stands); a field planned twice with different values is a CompositionError. At OFFSEASON_START and at every later offseason stop (RESIGN, FREE_AGENCY, COMBINE, PRO_DAY, DRAFT, UDFA) the plan also writes the coaching staff: `engines.coach_save_sync.plan_staff_edits(cur, snapshot, target_season)` supplies the `"staff"` block (releases, then assigns, then creates), an assign's `set` carries the portrait pack's queued `Portrait` / `Portrait_Force_Silhouette` for a packed coach, and a seat whose hiring cycle is unfinished or whose coach has no profile row is skipped and reported as a warning (`summary.staff` carries planned / released / assigned / created / portraits / skipped counts and `skipped_detail`). A dry run prints the block without writing. After a successful write `record_written` stores the report's `presentation_ids` on `coach_madden_profiles.presentation_id` (with `written_at`), which `--recover` also does from the stored operation, and a `Mu: coaches fired` / `Mu: coaches hired` notice lists what the write applied.
- **Progression (PROGRESSION_PLAN §5.3a), required in REGULAR_WEEK, PLAYOFF_WEEK and OFFSEASON_START:** `progression.in_season_checkpoint(cur, season, week, snapshot=, source_fingerprint=<input save sha256>)` weekly; `progression_checkpoint.prepare_offseason_pass(cur, snapshot, season + 1, source_fingerprint=)` at OFFSEASON_START (season = the year just played). A missing or mismatched interface is a ProgressionIntegrationError, never a skip. The engine prepares from the snapshot without the players this write releases; its document (base + form overlay, OVR / grades / PlayerType, morale 50, XP 0, progression-setting safeguards) is merged by `compose()` with the moves into one save_writer document. `prepared` stays unchanged; the combined document has its own hash.
- **Annual offseason producers and articles (P1-18/19/20/21/22/23, built 2026-11-09):** after a WRITTEN free-agency write, `annual_offseason_steps(cur, stage, season, wave, out)` (called by `run()` only when the deps carry `annual_steps`, which `default_deps` sets and test fakes do not, and by `recover()` after a recovered write with the run's own stored free-agency wave — the deps `recover()` builds itself carry `annual_steps` too) runs the DB producers and then the two annual articles. Comp picks and their article re-run on **every** free-agency wave (award_and_persist deletes and re-inserts, the article is forced); staff contracts, report cards and the card article run after wave 1. Order: `engines.compensatory_picks_run.award_and_persist(cur, season, season+1)` (P1-18: the class's QFA ledger, awards and COMP/JC2A `draft_picks` before DRAFT, so the lock order sees them; JC-2A off); `engines.staff_contracts_run.annual(cur, season)` (P1-22: files one HC/OC/DC/GM contract at the engine's market salary — a man the team keeps is re-signed at market from the season his deal runs out, so every season in the job is paid — and files a hire for the coming league year too — the carousel itself calls `file_hires` as it hires, so the save writer always finds a live row from the first write, and `annual` re-runs it for `season + 1` as a backstop, rolls `remaining_years` deterministically `total_years - (season - signed_season)`, moves a fired staffer's remaining guaranteed salary into `buyout_owed` (recomputed with `staff_contracts_engine.owed_years` = `total_years - (season - signed_season)` clamped to `total_years`, since the stored `remaining_years` was last rolled for the previous league year)); `engines.report_card_run.annual(cur, season, user_team_ids=)` (P1-20/P1-23: carries last season's card or the 2026 baseline, completes due CapEx renovations, degrades unmaintained physical categories one sub-tier per 3 seasons, applies OpEx policies, files `team_report_cards` + `owner_cash_ledgers` — wealth band + success dividend − staff payroll − OpEx − CapEx − the season's dead buyouts — and lets CPU owners order facility upgrades on their own policy); then `newsroom.compensatory_picks_article.run(season+1, ...)` (P1-19) and `newsroom.report_card_article.run(season, ...)` (P1-21), each on its own connection after the producers commit. Every step is optional and warning-only: a failure is recorded in the run report's `annual_steps` block, never fails the write, and each runs in its own savepoint. `owner_policy.facility_style` is AGGRESSIVE (`DEEP_POCKETS`), FRUGAL (`BUDGET_CONSCIOUS`) or BALANCED; `facility_upgrade_orders` upgrades a category below the style's floor (0.85 / 0.51 / 0.18), FRUGAL always MINOR, within cash above the style's reserve share.
- **Receipt protocol:** the `league_office_runs` row (PLANNED) holds the combined document in `edits` and `summary.operation` (operation_id, phase PREPARED → CANDIDATE_VERIFIED → REPLACED → ACKNOWLEDGED or FAILED, save / candidate / edits paths, input / candidate / output sha256, combined_hash, the unchanged prepared envelope, the data record_written needs); it is committed with the PREPARED events before any write. Then a temp-copy write through `save_writer.mjs` with whole-document read-back plus a `pc_save_reader` read-back; any failure makes the run FAILED with nothing acknowledged. Otherwise the candidate sha256 is committed, the save is replaced under the franchise-closed guard (refused while Madden27.exe runs unless `--confirm-franchise-closed` or `LEAGUE_OFFICE_FRANCHISE_CLOSED=1`: Madden may sit at its main menu), the output sha256 (= candidate) is committed, the output is read, `acknowledge_pass(..., writer_verified=True)` awards the progression, record_written stores the DB side and the run becomes WRITTEN in one commit. `--recover` acknowledges the stored original envelope only when the save's current sha256 equals the recorded candidate/output hash, marks the run FAILED when it equals the input hash, and otherwise refuses; it never re-plans, writes or advances. `--dry-run` prints the plan with `explain_prepared` public reports, rolls back the preparation, never acknowledges and keeps a DRY_RUN row.
- **Trade execution:** `step_pending_trade` accepts pick legs (they move in Mu's books only, not the save's `DraftPick` rows). `record_written` executes every trade the write carried once through `front_office._execute`: JR's TRADE pending moves carrying a `proposal_id`, and the engine's `("trade", pid)` deals. The proposal becomes EXECUTED with `executed_at` (an already-EXECUTED proposal is not executed twice), and a CPU deal whose flags carry `talks:<nid>` has its transcript published (`gm_talks.publish_talk`). An old JR payload without `proposal_id` keeps today's behaviour (nothing executed). `_apply_db` leaves the cap room of executed trades to `trade_moves`, so it is not applied twice. The run summary carries `engine_trades` (count), `engine_trades_written`, `engine_trades_failed` and `engine_trades_failed_ids`; refusals are counted from the WRITTEN runs' `engine_trades_failed_ids`.
- **Setup (once per franchise, before week 1):** `league_setup.mjs setup` makes all 32 teams real user teams (a `FranchiseUser` per team copied from JR's, distinct `UserIdUpper` = 2147483648 + k·2^24, per-user rows, the user registry, `Team.UserCharacter`, `Coach.IsUserControlled`; idempotent), turns fill roster off on every used TeamSetting row (the other staff switches stay Manual: they read true = Manual), sets CoachFiring OFF (LeagueSetting Field_44 = 2) and the career clock off (Field_82 = 0), sets every player's ConfidenceRating to 50, and writes and reads back a new save. The league office then checks neutrality (all ConfidenceRating 50, no `player_form` rows for the year) and calls `progression_checkpoint.bootstrap_pass(cur, snapshot, application_season, source_fingerprint=<new save sha256>, form_neutral=True)`; `normalize_save_ratings` clamps any saved rating above 99 (Madden stores 100 for a few legacy entries — Jerry Rice in `CAREER-MUBASE`) to the engine's 0–99 range at ingestion, leaving the progression-state invariant strict (application season = season in season and at OFFSEASON_START, else season + 1); on failure it rolls back and deletes the new save. Madden registers the new users after one Advance Week; their hubs populate then. `league_setup.mjs state` returns the team table id, the cap, each team's cap fields and spare PlayerContract rows.
- **Personality inputs (`pipeline/league_office_personality.py`, docs/done/PERSONALITY_ACTIVATION_PLAN.md §2.3; built 2026-11-06, every feature off by default):** `run()` and `plan_stage()` without `deps` use `default_deps(cur)`: the switchboard snapshot (§7.11) for `league_state.madden_league_id`, frozen for the write, then `deps_for(cur, snapshot)` = `PersonalityDeps` when any feature beyond producers is not off, else a plain `Deps` (both carry `modes_snapshot`). Seams: `Deps.retirement_decision(cur, player, season, seed)` (= `keep_retired`; `step_retirements(plan, seed, deps, cur)` asks it), `Deps.chart_adjustments(cur, team_id, season, week, roster, scheme, injuries)` (= None; `step_coach_charts` passes a non-None result as `staff_depth_chart(..., score_adjustments=)`), `Deps.staff_depth_chart(..., score_adjustments=None)`, and the optional hooks `begin_stage(stage, season, week, wave, seed)`, `bind_run(run_id)` and `personality_report()` (stored as `summary.personality`: modes, counts, receipts). `PersonalityDeps`: `resign_decisions`/`run_wave`/`udfa_market` pass `contract_inputs` (one batch `'<run_id>:<stage>:<wave>'`; policy from the snapshot's `contracts_ambition`/`contracts_relationships` by `read_contract_activation`'s rules) when either contract feature is not off; `progression_weekly` passes `development_config` (shadow → the development policy's own shadow mode, active → enabled) and a per-player `development_context` to `progression_checkpoint.prepare_pass` when `development_learning` is not off (not run twice, since preparing writes events; teaching stays neutral without verified exposure intervals); `chart_adjustments` returns the coaching policy's opportunity adjustments only when `development_opportunity` is active; `retirement_decision` asks the retirement policy (reviewed `config.policy` required in active; synthetic review-only numbers recorded in shadow) for players Madden retired, falls back to `keep_retired` when the policy is blocked, and never retires an active player; `cpu_offers` passes each CPU team's owner spending knobs (`owner_spending`, §2.17d; shadow plans the owner offers without storing them and records per-team counts); `free_agent_pool` ranks the pool by OVR (`fa_rank`) and `signings_from_decisions` lets the owner review a CPU team's top-50 signing (`owner_meddling`, `owner_policy.meddle_choice`, tick = the stage week or 24): active drops a VETOed signing (the offer stays OPEN; at most one veto a team a season, counted from `owner_decisions`, where the VETO is stored once U6's table exists), shadow records the decisions and keeps every signing; JR's teams (registry `user_teams` and `gm_team_settings.user_controlled`) are never reviewed, and the fan-favourite term isn't passed yet (no popularity rank). Modes: off = today's call exactly; shadow = baseline returned unchanged, the adjusted result (computed as if active) recorded, adjusted-path errors recorded and never fatal; active = adjusted result, errors fail the plan. `summary.operation.personality_modes` holds the frozen snapshot, and `--recover` without deps rebuilds them from it (never the live switchboard).
- **Coach and player agent loops (COACH_PLAYER_AGENT_LOOPS_PLAN U3a; built 2026-11-09, both features off by default).** `PersonalityDeps.chart_adjustments` runs the coach loop when `coach_loop` is shadow or active, independent of `development_opportunity`, and never for a team JR controls (the caller skips it only when JR has a stored chart, so the adapter guards it too): it builds the neutral chart with `depth_chart_engine.staff_depth_chart(roster, scheme, injuries)`, the same opportunity candidates `LiveFeatures.chart_adjustments` uses (`league_office_personality.chart_candidates`), the coach's `coaching` feature view (`store.resolve_alias('coach','db-coach', head coach)`), the open promises (`coach.open_promises(base.SqlStore(cur), league_id, season, team_id=team_id)`), the close window from `development_opportunity`'s `config.close_score_window` when positive (else `COACH_CLOSE_WINDOW = 1.0`), and calls `coach.choose_chart(..., llm=base.make_loop_llm())` (never built when the loop is off). Off: today's result, byte for byte. Shadow: the development_opportunity baseline returned unchanged, the CHART decision recorded by `choose_chart`, and a loop error recorded in the receipts without failing the write. Active: for a NEUTRAL choice the development_opportunity adjustments; for a SWAP the `{slot: {player_id: float}}` score adjustments that make `staff_depth_chart(..., score_adjustments=)` reproduce the chosen chart (+gap+0.01 to the promoted man, -gap-0.01 to the demoted man, each clamped to `MAX_SCORE_ADJUSTMENT`); errors raise. When `player_loop` is not off, every `contract_inputs` entry from `resign_decisions`, `run_wave` and `udfa_market` carries a per-player `counter_chooser` that calls `player.respond_contract(...)` with the league, season, tick (the stage week when 1-32, else 24), the engine's player/team/market/bar, `accepts=False`, the contract context's earned attachment tier mapped to a 0-1 weight, and `store=base.SqlStore(cur)`; the contract hooks' overall mode is the higher of the contract features' and `player_loop`'s, so shadow records the CONTRACT decision and returns None (the engine's counter) and active returns the loop's counter for a COUNTER status (the engine's own otherwise); a shadow loop error is recorded and swallowed, an active one raises. `PersonalityDeps._marquee_floor(cur, season)` supplies `ctx['marquee_floor']`: one cached read per deps/season over the season's ACTIVE `player_contracts` rows (`total_value / length` for `length > 0`), then `player.marquee_floor` (the 50th-highest AAV); a missing table (`to_regclass`), a failed read or no rows is None, so a CPU contract case is marquee only when its ask's AAV reaches the floor and may then spend the week's `MARQUEE_PER_WEEK` model budget (missing data keeps cases policy-only, and a floor-read failure never fails a shadow or active write). Re-sign counters follow the loop only when the contract policy's consent path runs (`_resign_one` routes on the contract policy's mode; activation order puts `contracts_*` active before `player_loop`); free agency and UDFA follow `player_loop` alone. The inbox `CONTRACT` and `ROLE_TALK` kinds use their optional `loop_reply` hook (§7.11). `LEAGUE_OFFICE_FEATURES` now names `coach_loop` and `player_loop`. The coach loop's promises (creation and review) run in the save watcher after the relationship producers, not in the league office: `engines/agent_loops/watcher.py`, §6.0b.
- **Retirement window (docs/done/RETIREMENT_WINDOW_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-07, observe-only until G4; **G4 approved by JR 2026-11-09** for `OFFSEASON_START`, `FREE_AGENCY` and `UDFA`):** one retirement decision per offseason. `Deps.retirement_window_inputs(cur, season)` reads WRITTEN runs only: the season's decision run (`summary.retirement_window.role = "decision"`), `decided` (its decision set plus every player a window run restored, keep True, so a second re-retirement counts), `window_restores` ({pgid: restores this season}) and the newest WRITTEN run's `roster_image` / stop (any season; OFFSEASON_START uses the last playoff run's). With no decision run the current offseason stop is the **decision stage** (normally OFFSEASON_START; RESIGN or later when the Staff save was missed, plan Q4): `step_retirements` asks `deps.retirement_decision` for each `Retired` player (unchanged rule, by switchboard mode) and stores the decision set. A keep is always un-retired by the free-agent flip (`ContractStatus` `FreeAgent`, `TeamIndex` 32); when `Deps.retirement_authority()` (the JR-approved proof at `$MU_RETIREMENT_AUTHORITY`, `retirement_window.load_proof`; unset = default deny, a broken file is a plan error) covers the stage, `plan_retirement_edits` authorizes it (a planner conflict then leaves him retired, row `window:blocked:…`). At every later stop `step_retirement_window` runs `retirement_window.classify` (late native retirements, keeps retired again once a season (`MAX_WINDOW_RESTORES` 1), conflicts, players still retired from an earlier stop (carried quietly), vanished, purged, `stage_gap` when a save was skipped, `user_team` for JR's teams from 2026), builds the planner's snapshot (baseline = previous image, pending = moves already claimed this plan) and authority (`authority_for_run`: the proof stamped with this run's input sha256; stage and reader schema still checked), and applies the free-agent flip (the view stays Retired so nothing signs or cuts him this write; counts `window_restored` and `window_free_agent`, summary entry `restore: free_agent`; at `CUTDOWN` it also warns `restore_at_last_stop` for each restore). The next run's `step_restore_retirees` signs a restored free agent to his old team with his stored remaining contract (count `restored_retirees`; warning `no_restorable_contract` when no stored contract runs into the league year). Without a proof every candidate is blocked `authority_missing`: recorded and reported, nothing written, and he is purged at the rollover. Planner conflicts are warned per player; a rostered player who vanished since the previous run is warned, recorded and named in the notification (unrecoverable; free agents who vanished are reported only). Every run's summary carries `retirement_window` (§3.3q) with the roster image the save holds after the write (kept and restored players at what was written); the printed run report (`report_summary`) leaves the image out. The window never emits career-state events (§2.17f).
- Tests: `tests/test_league_office.py` (114), `tests/test_league_office_personality.py` (21: deps_for, shadow equals baseline for re-sign/free agency/UDFA/charts/retirement with the adjusted result recorded, active uses it, never retiring an active player, the stored snapshot reused by recovery), `tests/test_league_office_annual.py` (the annual steps only at FREE_AGENCY wave 1, their order and commits, a failing step recorded without stopping the rest, article text kept out of the summary), `tests/test_staff_contracts_run.py` (files each HC/OC/DC once, deterministic roll, firing into a buyout, dry run, not installed, a next-season hire not fired, a settled coach not re-filed, a rehired coach filed again, and the one-invariant table: every contract year paid exactly once over the producer and both hot-seat settles), `tests/test_report_card_run.py` (cards and ledgers, payroll and the success dividend, OpEx, completed renovations, degradation, idempotence, CPU orders but not JR's, the facility styles and orders), `tests/test_agent_loops_wiring.py` (switchboard order; coach_loop off/shadow/active charts, failed shadow writes; player_loop off/shadow/active CPU counters and the marquee floor (50th-highest AAV, a top-50 ask using the model within budget, missing/empty contracts keeping policy-only); re-sign refusal; inbox CONTRACT/ROLE_TALK replies and per-turn decisions), `tests/test_agent_loops_promises_wiring.py` (promise creation/review over synthetic adapters; shadow vs active; JR teams skipped; replay; the watcher step's off/skip/failure paths), `pipeline/save_reader/test/league_setup.test.mjs`. The coaching staff write: `tests/test_league_office_staff.py` (the staff block at OFFSEASON_START and every later stop, a dry run writing nothing, PresentationIds recorded back, skipped seats warned, the portrait set riding an assign) and `tests/test_coach_portrait_pack.py` (IDs from the range never reused, the manifest's columns and DDS copies, GENERATED -> PACKED, a rerun assigning nothing, --mark-installed).

### 2.21b Front-Office Inbox core (`engines/inbox/`, `docs/done/FRONT_OFFICE_INBOX_PLAN.md` U1, V2.9)
Built: the core and its kinds — `OWNER` (below), the inbox plan's `GM_TALK`, `CONTRACT`, `ROLE_TALK`, `REPORTER` and `VISION` (U3/U4/U6), the scouting revamp's `PROSPECT` and `SCOUT` (V2.10 U5), and the press plan's `PRESS` (V2.2 U8). The Command Center Inbox module (U2, §5.2) and `server/inbox_api.py` (U5, §2.12) are built; all units are on main. Tables §3.3s.
- **PRESS kind (`kinds/press.py`, docs/done/PRESS_CONFERENCE_PLAN.md U8, §2.13).** A system notice when JR's postgame press conference is waiting (`ACTOR_ROLES` ('COACH',), counterpart `system`, id `press`, name "Press Room"). It creates one thread per `press_conferences` row with `controller = 'USER'` and status SCHEDULED, LIVE or REVIEW (`source_ref` `press:<conference_id>`, `link_table` `press_conferences`, `link_id` the conference id), closes that thread once the row is CLOSED, DECLINED, FAILED or gone, and never fires for an AGENT presser. The only option is `OPEN_PRESSER`; the option itself keeps the notice open, and the inbox resolves the thread's `link_table` (`press_conferences`) to a "Go to Game Center" link — clicking `OPEN_PRESSER` records the act and then lands on the Game Center (P1-15); `start` refuses with 400. Without the press tables the scan returns nothing.
- **OWNER kind (`kinds/owner.py`, docs/done/OWNERS_SCOUTS_VOTERS_PLAN.md U5, §8 Q1).** The team owner writes to JR's GM (`ACTOR_ROLES` ('GM',), counterpart `owner`, id `owner:<TEAM>`, name and traits from the reviewed owner profile); he only talks, never vetoes or fires. It sends nothing unless the switchboard's `owner_meddling` feature is **active** (off and shadow: no threads). Triggers, each once per `source_ref`: `EXPECTATION` in week 1 (`owner:expect:<season>`; the expectation from his first held trait in the order HEADLINE_HUNTER, PATIENT_BUILDER, MEDDLER, DEEP_POCKETS, BUDGET_CONSCIOUS, HANDS_OFF, else the team's direction); `PRESSURE` after 3 straight regular-season losses (`owner:pressure:<season>:streak:<week of the first loss>`) or a losing season once the regular season is complete (`owner:pressure:<season>:losing`); `REACTION` to a JR big move this season: a WRITTEN `franchise_pending_moves` TRADE of a league office run of the season (`owner:move:trade:<id>`) or an accepted `contract_offers` offer from JR of at least $60M total (`BIG_SIGNING_VALUE`, estimate; `owner:move:signing:<id>`). JR answers `ACKNOWLEDGE` / `REASSURE` / `PUSH_BACK`; the thread closes and the kind records a `meaningful_interaction` (positive routine / positive meaningful / mixed meaningful; owner subject, JR's GM target) in the outbox itself (`judge` False, so the model isn't asked for an appraisal). The owner's `db-owner` alias resolves only once U6's `team_owners` and a lifecycle batch exist, so until then the events wait PENDING. `start` refuses (the owner starts these).
- **GM_TALK kind (`kinds/gm_talk.py`, U4).** GM → another team's GM. Inbound `TRADE_INTEREST` from a PROPOSED `origin = 'ENGINE'` proposal naming a registry user team with no thread for `gm_talk:proposal:<id>`; options `OPEN_TALKS` (`trade_assets`) / `NOT_INTERESTED` (`front_office.reject`), then `MAKE_OFFER` / `ACCEPT_COUNTER` / `END_TALKS`. The engine is `gm_negotiation.open_negotiation` / `offer` / `accept_counter` / `close`; the reply template is the GM turn message the engine wrote, and the appraisal is asked for only when JR wrote a note (`judge = bool(note)`). Facts, state and `engine_ref` carry ids, actions and assets only — never a surplus. An agreed deal or a GM walk-away closes the thread; the kind writes no trade. The `trade_assets` form has no direction, so every listed asset is sent by JR's team; `draft` matches typed names and picks against `gm_negotiation.team_assets`. It declares `START_FORM = "team_pick"` for the new-conversation picker, and `start` uses the typed topic or opening note as the subject (default "Trade talks"), refuses JR's own team's front office (400), and keys the thread `gm_talk:start:<user>:<team>:<attempt>` so a closed talk can be reopened with the same GM while `(team, kind, source_ref)` stays unique. `_move_id` and `_leak_after` run inside `appraisal._savepoint`, so a SQL error in the pending-move lookup or the leak draw can never abort JR's reply (Postgres only; `tests/test_inbox_kinds_gm_talk.py` pins it with `INBOX_SAVEPOINT_TEST_DSN`). V2.11's extension (§2.7 of the V2.11 plan): `act` passes `timeout=INBOX_LLM_BUDGET_S` to `gm_negotiation.open_negotiation` / `offer` / `accept_counter`, puts the GM's last-turn posture in the message's `engine_ref` (`{negotiation_id, turn_no, posture}`, plus the existing status/action/proposal_id), runs `gm_talks.leak_events` after every GM turn (stored in `gm_trade_leaks`, never mentioned in the thread), and on an agreed deal replies "Agreed. Queued for the league office (move #<id>)" naming the `franchise_pending_moves` TRADE row `gm_negotiation._agree` queued. The kind still writes no trade itself.
- **CONTRACT kind (`kinds/contract.py`, U4).** GM → own player. Inbound `EXTENSION_WINDOW` for a healthy starter (`gm_direction.starter_slots`) who is `extension_eligible` and has no thread this season; options `MAKE_OFFER` (`contract_terms`: years, total, bonus, guaranteed), `ACCEPT_COUNTER` (while a counter is stored) and `WALK_AWAY`. Reaches `server/franchise_api.py`'s `_context`, `_player`, `_eligibility`, `_score` and `insert_offer` by lazy import (R4; that module is unchanged), with `_score` on the original path (no contract-policy receipt). An accepted offer is stored in `contract_offers` and the league office writes the contract; the kind never writes one. `draft` uses `parse.parse_contract_terms` with the model as a fallback. It declares `START_FORM = "player_pick"`, and the picker lists only the players `franchise_api._eligibility` accepts (U10; a `_context` failure yields an empty list). A non-numeric `player_id` is a 400, not a 500.
- **ROLE_TALK kind (`kinds/role_talk.py`, U3).** Coach → own player. Triggers `LOST_STARTING_JOB` (depth 1 at a base slot in the chart in force last week, not now) and `WANTS_MORE` (the computed staff chart starts him while JR's stored chart has not, two straight weeks). The chart in force is the newest stored `depth_charts` week up to the scan week, JR before MU_COACH before MADDEN. Options `PROMISE` (`promise`: slot, depth, review week ≥ next week, default + `PROMISE_REVIEW_WEEKS` = 2), `EXPLAIN` (note required), `NO_CHANGE`. A promise never writes a chart: it appends to `state.promises` and records `promise_made`; `review_promises` resolves it at the due week (or later) against the chart in force **at its due week**, once, with a SYSTEM line and `promise_resolved`, then closes the thread — judging an overdue promise on the current chart would count a promotion made after the deadline as kept. `act` reads "this week" from `league_state`, not the thread's creation week, and `due_season` must be this season or the next. It declares `START_FORM = "player_pick"`, and `start` uses the typed topic or note as the subject (default "His role"), holding a typed player id to the picker's own rule — an ACTIVE contract, not on IR — so the two lists agree.
- **REPORTER kind (`kinds/reporter.py`, U3).** Any controlled persona → the team's `LOCAL_BEAT_REPORTER` account in `agent_memories` (falling back to any assigned account). `INTERVIEW_REQUEST` on a starter out 4+ weeks, a written trade or accepted signing, a 3-game streak, or a starter losing his job; the store caps it at 2 open per team. A move is asked about only in its own week or the one before (`MOVE_INTERVIEW_WEEKS` 2), or back to the last week a league-office run wrote when the offseason jumps (26 → 29; `MOVE_INTERVIEW_MAX_GAP` 4 weeks): a trade is dated by its `league_office_runs.week`, a signing by `contract_offers.week` (`2027_02_18`), and a row with no week is out of window — before that column every move of the season could still be raised in week 18. A streak's source ref is the week the **whole** run began, so a longer streak doesn't re-open the same interview each week. `ON_RECORD` / `OFF_RECORD` (note required), `NO_COMMENT`, `END_INTERVIEW` any time. Open-ended: the template asks up to 3 questions then wraps, a model reply wraps on `"done": true` (through `on_reply`, called by `scan.open_thread` and `voice.exchange`), hard cap 10. `jr_statements` stores one row per on/off-record answer. It declares no `START_FORM`; `start` uses the typed topic or note as the subject (default "The team").
- **VISION kind (`kinds/vision.py`, U6).** Coach → the team's GM, or GM → the team's head coach, whichever JR controls; no `ACTOR_ROLES`, so it is scanned once per team; skipped when JR controls both or the coach is the GM. Triggers `SEASON_VISION` (first scan of a season with no `team_vision` row) and `DIRECTION_SHIFT` (at a checkpoint, when `gm_direction`'s raw band differs from the pinned direction). Options `PROPOSE` (`form: "vision"`: direction, emphasis, playing time, seeded from the pinned vision with BALANCED/MERIT defaults), `ACCEPT_COUNTER` (after a counter), `KEEP_CURRENT` — without the form the page sent no payload and PROPOSE answered 400. `start` refuses when JR controls both the coach and the GM, as the scan does. A typed draft (`vision.draft`, D10) reads direction, emphasis and playing time out of JR's text and offers the PROPOSE for confirmation; text with no direction in it drafts nothing. `team_vision.respond` decides AGREE / COUNTER / REFUSE; AGREED upserts `team_vision` and closes the thread, KEEP_CURRENT closes without a row. One open per team.
- **PROSPECT kind (`kinds/prospect.py`, SCOUTING_REVAMP_PLAN.md §2.8, V2.10 U5).** JR's GM interviews a college prospect (`ACTOR_ROLES` ('GM',), counterpart `prospect`, id the prospect's permanent `prospect_uid` from `engines/prospect_ids.py` (`person_ref`), `PERSONA_ROLE` None, `link_table` `scout_interviews`). `start` (from the Draft War Room's Interviews card) takes `{prospect_uid | prospect_key, interview: COMBINE | VISIT}` and opens the interview through `scouting_interviews.open_interview` (an `InterviewError` becomes `InboxError(409)`); the thread opens on a GREETING whose facts are the prospect's sheet, and the interview is linked back to the thread on the first `options`/`act`. `options` offers one `ASK_<TOPIC>` per still-unasked engine-permitted topic while questions remain, plus `END_INTERVIEW`; a note with no option is a typed question, classified to a permitted topic (label `draft_interview_classify`, only when `MU_INBOX_LLM` is on). `act` calls `scouting_interviews.ask` and returns `ANSWER_<GRADE>` with `engine_ref {interview_id, topic, grade, classified_by}`; the last question still gets its answer, with the scout's closing memo appended to it and the close's `summary_grade`/`best`/`worst` in the facts and `engine_ref`, then the thread closes through `scouting_interviews.close` — it used to return the summary instead, dropping the graded final turn — while `END_INTERVIEW` closes with intent `SUMMARY`. `template` is `answer_template`/`summary_template` (plus a GREETING); `validate` is `scouting_interviews.validate_answer`. `intent_voice("SUMMARY")` makes the closing summary the department scout's (`SUMMARY_VOICE`: a third-person memo about the prospect), so the LLM-on summary no longer speaks as the prospect (P1-13; `voice.compose` reads a kind's optional `intent_voice` and replaces the counterpart's persona lines for that intent). Prospects never write first (`scan` returns []).
- **SCOUT kind (`kinds/scout.py`, §2.8, V2.10 U5).** The Mu Scouting Department writes to JR's GM (`ACTOR_ROLES` ('GM',), counterpart `scout`, id `department`, name "Mu Scouting Department", `PERSONA_ROLE` `scout`); `start` refuses (the scout writes first). `scan` reads only scouting tables: `COMBINE_OPEN` when step 24 is the latest stored (facts: budget, window), `VISITS_OPEN` when step 24 or 25 is the latest, and `REPORTS_READY` once per stored edition (facts: the edition and its 5 biggest consensus risers on JR's team board, names and ranks only — **the needs proxy is accepted in writing (P1-14, 2026-11-09):** board membership, whose `fit` already weighs the GM's needs, stands in for a strict filter on `gm_team_seasons.needs` positions; revisit only if the line reads wrong on a live board); `source_ref` `scout:<draft_season>:<trigger>:<step>` so each fires once. `options` `SHORTLIST` (up to 8 not-yet-interviewed prospects in JR's team-board order at the latest step, names and positions only) / `ACKNOWLEDGE`; `act` returns the shortlist (`SHORTLIST`) or closes (`ACKNOWLEDGED`). `validate` is `scouting_narrative.validate_scout_text`.
- **API (`server/inbox_api.py`, U5).** Router prefix `/api/franchise`, mounted in `server/api.py`: GET/POST `/{abbr}/inbox/actors`, DELETE `/{abbr}/inbox/actors/{role}/{persona_id}` (204), GET `/{abbr}/inbox?status=&kind=&as=&limit=50`, GET `/{abbr}/inbox/kinds`, GET `/{abbr}/inbox/targets?kind=` (wave 4: `{kind, targets}` — for CONTRACT the team's active players that `franchise_api._eligibility` accepts (U10; a `_context`/`_eligibility` failure yields an empty list), the team's active-roster players for ROLE_TALK, other teams' open GM tenures for GM_TALK, empty for any other kind; 400 without `kind`), GET `/{abbr}/inbox` and GET `/{abbr}/inbox/{thread_id}` (both run `scan.scan_on_open` when the inbox is opened; the list used not to, so an empty inbox stayed empty), POST `/{abbr}/inbox/{thread_id}/draft` (acts on nothing), POST `/{abbr}/inbox/{thread_id}/reply` (`voice.exchange`, stamped with the current league time so a reply moves the thread's expiry instead of leaving it on the creation week), POST `/{abbr}/inbox` (201) and POST `/{abbr}/inbox/{thread_id}/close`. Answers `Mu_Network/src/types/franchiseInbox.ts` exactly: Actor `{role,id,name}`, Thread with `actor`/`counterpart` and no `state` or `team_id`, Message without `facts` and with an appraisal of `{outcome, reason}` only (an `engine_ref` is stripped of facts and surpluses); a coach-GM candidate's `also` is the extra role; `status=OPEN` means OPEN ∪ WAITING_JR. Notes ≤600 chars; errors use `{"detail"}` with 400/403/404/409 (a missing migration is 409); unknown team 404, non-user team 403.
- **Controlled personas (`actors.py`, D6, D8).** A thread is always (a persona JR controls) ↔ (a counterpart agent). JR controls no one by default: only an active `controlled_personas` row makes a persona an actor, and only teams in the active franchise registry's `user_teams` count (rows of other teams are ignored). `candidates` lists the open GM tenure and the open head-coach tenure; a GM whose `gm_profiles.coach_id` is the head coach is one candidate ("also" the coach), and taking or releasing him stores or releases both rows. `take_control` raises 403 outside `user_teams`, 409 when the persona isn't on the team (a PLAYER must be on it in his newest `player_seasons` row), 400 for a bad role. PLAYER rows are accepted; no kind serves them yet.
- **Store (`store.py`).** A thread is unique on `(team_id, kind, source_ref)`; messages are numbered by `seq`. A counterpart or SYSTEM line marks the thread WAITING_JR and unread, JR's line OPEN. Caps on open threads per team: `MAX_OPEN_PER_KIND` GM_TALK/CONTRACT/ROLE_TALK 3, REPORTER 2, VISION 1, others 3. Expiry: past `expires_season/week` when set, else more than `INBOX_STALE_WEEKS` = 2 ticks after the last activity (ticks 1–32 on the producers' calendar, so it runs through the offseason). A CLOSED/EXPIRED thread or one whose actor was released is read-only (409) but readable. `jr_statements(cur, team_id, season, week=None)` returns one row per ON_RECORD/OFF_RECORD interview answer `{thread_id, team_id, season, week, writer_agent_id, writer_handle, subject, question, answer, on_record, actor_role, actor_name, created_at}`; NO_COMMENT isn't a statement.
- **Registry (`registry.py`).** `kinds()` imports every module of `engines/inbox/kinds/` (pkgutil, once per process): a module-level `KIND` makes the module the kind, else a class with a string `KIND` is instantiated; modules with neither are ignored; a duplicate `KIND` raises. Protocol: `scan(cur, season, week, team)` (team carries `actor`), `options`, `act -> ActResult(facts, intent, engine_ref, close, link, state, judge)`, `template`, `start`; optional `ACTOR_ROLES` (missing: scanned once per team with its first actor), `validate(text, facts)`, `draft(cur, thread, text, llm)`, `review_promises(cur, season, week, team) -> int` (called once per team per weekly scan), `VOICE` (neutral-voice description), `EXTRA_JSON` (extra keys asked of the model), `on_reply(cur, thread, data)`, `START_FORM` (the new-conversation picker's form, passed through by `/inbox/kinds`).
