- **Voice (`voice.py`, D7).** The engine decides; the model only says it. `compose` makes one call (`call_with_budget`, `INBOX_LLM_BUDGET_S` = 4.0 s, set by the P1-09 spike 2026-11-09: p50 1.99 s, p95 2.46 s, max 2.50 s on `gemini-3.8-flash` with Madden open — see `docs/reference/P1_LATENCY_AND_INBOX_GATE.md`) returning `{"message", "appraisal", …}`; the words are kept only when `gm_rationale.validate_rationale` passes against the fact sheet, the kind's `validate` passes, and the intent check finds no contradiction of the decision; otherwise (and on a timeout, `MU_INBOX_LLM=0`, no key) the kind's template is used. `persona_view`: the personality core's `feature_view(profile, 'inbox')` when a profile resolves; GMs and writers fall back to `persona_sliders`/`persona_traits` (status `legacy`); everyone else is neutral ("plain and professional"). The appraisal is asked for only when `appraisal.allowed(view)`. Relationship lines enter the prompt only through the relationships plan's `relationship_context` once `personality.relationships` exists (none today). `exchange` runs one JR turn in order: `act` → JR's line (with the decision's `engine_ref`) → the reply → the outbox event; notes are at most 600 characters. A **null `option_id` with a note is talk by default** (FRONT_OFFICE_INBOX_PLAN §2.7): no engine act, no state or outcome change, the counterpart answers with the last turn's facts minus the decision keys (`decision`, `engine_status`, `reply`, `offer_id`, `pending_move_id`) and JR keeps the buttons he had; a kind whose `KIND` is in `TYPED_TEXT_KINDS` (`PROSPECT`, the typed interview question) still reads the note through its own `act`. A null option with no words is a 400. A talk turn reuses the newest counterpart turn's facts with every decision fact a kind's `act` sets removed (`decision`, `gm_message`, `action`, `status`, `counter`, `direction`, `reasons`, …), so the template cannot re-convey an old decision; it keeps JR's buttons, and its model reply is held to both contradiction guards — nothing is being decided, so "we have a deal" and "no deal" are equally rejected and fall back to the template.
- **Relationship events (`appraisal.py`, D15–D18).** The inbox never writes `persona_relationships` and computes no trust. An appraised model reply records one event in `inbox_relationship_events`: `treatment` (`disrespect`) when the counterpart says it was mistreated, else `meaningful_interaction` (outcome, significance, reason); a template reply records none. `promise_made` / `promise_resolved` (kept / broken / unknown, never broken without a chart) are facts recorded with or without a model. Envelopes follow PERSONALITY_RELATIONSHIPS_PLAN §2.2; PersonRefs carry aliases (`db-gm`, `db-coach`, `db-player`, `agent-memory`) and `occurred_at` is `{season, tick}`. `allowed`: true for a loaded profile or legacy persona, false for neutral views, including real coaches without a stored (reviewed) profile; a stored real profile counts as reviewed and is read in full (core extensions D1, views-v2). `flush` is a no-op until `personality.relationship_store` imports and its table exists; then it resolves aliases, reads the head and calls `append_events(expected_head=…)`; unresolved refs and conflicts stay PENDING with `status_reason`. Since 2026-11-04 the store module exists (§3.3t), so `flush` reports `relationship_tables_missing` until `2027_01_27` is applied; its default `team_registry` is `{}`, so `treatment` events (which carry a `team_key`) come back in `receipt.rejected` and stay PENDING until a caller passes the production registry. `tests/test_inbox_appraisal.py::test_flush_is_a_noop_without_the_relationships_store` still assumes the module is absent and fails until the inbox plan updates it (set `sys.modules['personality.relationship_store'] = None`).
- **Drafts (`parse.py`, D10).** `parse_contract_terms` needs a length and a total ("3 years, 40 million, 15 guaranteed" → 3 / $40M / $15M / $0; bare numbers under 1000 mean millions; "40" alone is None); `parse_with_llm` accepts only listed ids, enum values and in-range numbers; `draft_summary` writes the confirm line. A draft acts on nothing.
- **Scan (`scan.py`).** `scan(cur, season, week, teams=None, llm=None)`: for each registry user team with actors, each kind and each actor it serves, `kind.scan` → triggers → `open_thread` (idempotent, capped; opening message via `compose` without appraisal), each kind's `review_promises` once per team, `expire_stale`, `appraisal.flush`; a failing kind is rolled back to a savepoint, logged and skipped; `dry_run` stores nothing. `scan_on_open` runs a template-only scan once per (team, season, week, stage) per process, without reviews or flush. `start_thread` opens a JR-started conversation (403 / 400 / 409). `step_inbox(season)` is the weekly step (§6.0; never raises).
- **CLI:** `python3 -m engines.inbox scan [--season S --week W] [--team CAR] [--no-llm] [--dry-run] | list --team CAR | show <id> | control --team CAR [--role GM|COACH|PLAYER --persona ID] [--off] | flush-events` (DATABASE_URL; `--dry-run`, `list` and `show` roll back).
- **Tests:** `tests/test_inbox_{actors,store,registry,voice,appraisal,parse,scan}.py`, `tests/test_weekly_capture_inbox.py` (102, offline; fake models only); the OWNER kind in `tests/test_owner_wiring.py`; ROLE_TALK and REPORTER in `tests/test_inbox_kinds_role_talk.py` and `tests/test_inbox_kinds_reporter.py`; GM_TALK and CONTRACT in `tests/test_inbox_kinds_gm_talk.py` and `tests/test_inbox_kinds_contract.py`; VISION in `tests/test_inbox_kinds_vision.py` and `tests/test_team_vision.py`.


### 2.22 Press Conference Casting (`newsroom/press_cast.py`, `newsroom/config/press_pool.json`, PRESS_CONFERENCE_PLAN U2)

Postgame press conference attendance is cast from pre-game interest only; the game's result never enters casting. `pregame_interest(cur, game) -> {"interest", "inputs"}` scores one game 0–100 as `0.45 × rescaled display_excitement(projected_excitement)` (70–100 rescaled to 0–100; 50 when missing) `+ 0.35 ×` the two teams' Base Market Gravity B mean `+ 0.20 ×` the two teams' form (win share in games before the week, blended with last season's for the first four games, as `mod_packs.form`) `+ 8` for SNF/MNF/TNF `+ 5` for a division game `+ 5` from week 15 when both teams are .500 or better. Playoff games carry the round's floor: Wild Card 70, Divisional 80, Conference 90, Super Bowl 100.

Tiers and the national count at a game: QUIET (<45) 0–1 `INSIDER` (1 in 3 games, seeded); NOTABLE (45–65) 1–2 `INSIDER`/`REPORTER`; BIG (65–80) 2–4 plus `COLUMNIST`; MARQUEE (≥80 or any playoff game) 4–6 plus `TV`; the Super Bowl takes the whole non-excluded pool, up to 8. `cast_week(cur, season, week)` ranks the week's games by interest and assigns nationals, each person key to at most one game, with former-team slants weighted up (`former_team_bonus` 2.0); `relationship_bonus` stays 0 and no `persona_relationships` row is read until `relationship_context` exists for this consumer. Every `LOCAL_BEAT_REPORTER` with an `assigned_team_id` attends only its own team's presser. The draw is seeded `random.Random(f"press:{season}:{week}:{game_id}")`. `Cast = {"game_id", "interest", "tier", "inputs", "nationals": [Attendee], "beats": {team_id: [Attendee]}}`, `Attendee = {"agent_id", "person_key", "archetype", "display_name", "handle", "role": "BEAT"|"NATIONAL", "pool_tier"}`. The approved pool and a reason for every archetype's placement live in `press_pool.json`; `validate_pool` enforces known archetypes, no tier/excluded overlap, every national candidate placed, a neutral relationship weight and a note per archetype.
## 3. Database Schema & Architecture (PostgreSQL)

The database utilizes a relational temporal model in PostgreSQL (`dbname=madden` by default; on the PC the 2036 universe is the archive `madden_2036`, and each Madden franchise has its own `madden_<name>` database with this same schema, §1.2, §6.0b). `db/init_db.sql` reproduces the full live schema (tables, constraints, generated columns, views, functions, triggers) on an empty database and is safe to re-run; it does not add columns to existing tables, so schema changes to the live DB ship as migrations under `db/migrations/` and must also be folded into `init_db.sql`. Applied state is a query, not an investigation: `db/migrate.py` records every `db/migrations/*.sql` file in the `schema_migrations` ledger (`version`, `filename`, `checksum`, `applied_at`, `source`), and `init_db.sql` ends with a generated block that marks every migration applied, because it mirrors them all — so a fresh build reports nothing pending and `apply` is a no-op (§1.2). Last checked **2026-11-09** with `python3 -m db.migrate diff`: a database built from `init_db.sql` is schema-identical (tables, columns, types, nullability and defaults, PKs, FKs, unique/check constraints, indexes, view and function definitions, triggers) to `madden_test` after the six migrations it was behind (`2027_01_20` press, `2027_02_02` owners/scouts/voters, `2027_02_06` comp picks, both `2027_02_07` staff files, `2027_02_08` report cards) and `2027_02_09` (the parity repair) were applied, and those seven are no-ops on a fresh `init_db.sql` build (`tests/test_migrate.py`). Trade talks (`2027_01_22`) and its trigger (`2027_02_05`) were already applied on 2026-11-08. The press-conference tables (`2027_01_20`, §3.3y) are folded in beside the inbox block. The personality migrations (`2027_01_16`, `_23`, `_24`, `_25`, `_27`, `_29`, `_30`, `_31`, `2027_02_01`, `_03`) are folded in one block before the `nfl_*` tables, without their guard DO blocks; they seed nothing (the `persona_core_catalogues` row is upserted by `personality/store.py`). Every `2027_*` migration is a no-op on a fresh `init_db.sql` database; a few early ones are one-shot (`2026_10_12`, `2026_10_23` and `2026_10_26` rebuild views or columns later migrations extended, and `seed_clean_db.py` drops the record views before re-running `2026_10_26`) or need league data (coach, Panthers and record-book data loads). `tests/test_init_db_schema.py` fails if any table, index or view a migration creates is missing from `init_db.sql`. Earlier (2026-10-29) it was checked against `madden_2036` with every migration through `2027_01_12`; `league_state.madden_league_id` (`2027_01_13_franchise_identity.sql`) is applied to `madden_test` and every franchise database, not to the frozen `madden_2036`. The two differences that used to be tolerated — `napper_leagues.season` / `napper_drafts.season` NOT NULL and `gm_profiles.start_season >= 1970` (the migration's `>= 2030` would reject real-NFL GM tenures that `seed_clean_db.py` writes) — are now closed by `2027_02_09_init_db_parity.sql`, so a fully-migrated database and a fresh `init_db.sql` build differ in nothing. Column **order** is part of the same contract: a column a migration appends goes last in `init_db.sql` too, and a fresh build matches the live franchise database `madden_mu2026` column for column (2,720 columns, checked 2026-11-09) — `gm_profiles.voice_card` / `voice_card_source` were the one drift, now moved last as `2027_02_13_gm_voice_cards.sql` appends them. `db/migrate.py diff` keys columns by name, so it compares types, nullability and defaults but never position and will not catch a column placed mid-table; `madden_test` carries eleven cosmetic ordering artifacts from the older build it was migrated up from.

For starting a brand new franchise save (e.g. PC migration or fresh modded sim restart), `db/seed_clean_db.py` bootstraps a completely fresh database from scratch (`python3 -m db.seed_clean_db [--season 2024] [--week 1] [--user-team IND] [--dry-run]`): applies `init_db.sql` if tables are missing, populates the 32 NFL franchises (`teams`), sets `league_state`, configures `gm_team_settings` with user-control flags, loads historical NFL records through 2025 (then deletes the old universe's 2026–2035 `BOOK` rows that `2026_10_28_league_record_book.sql` and `2026_11_15_defense_kicking_history.sql` also load; the BOOK categories stay, empty), seeds real NFL head coaches and coordinators with schemes and slants (`COACHES_DATA`, `COORDINATORS_DATA`: the staffs as they stood on the eve of the 2026 season, opener 2026-09-09, matching Madden 27's starting staffs, per JR 2026-11-06; exactly one OC and one DC per team, the titled one; Tampa Bay has no titled DC, so run game coordinator Larry Foote fills it; `start_season` is the first season in that role with that team), seeds 32 GM personas with 3 upcoming draft classes (`draft_picks`), seeds the 40 writer archetype personas (`agent_personas.json` → `persona_sliders`/`persona_traits`/`persona_views`) and the 201 writer and social accounts (`newsroom/config/agent_accounts.json` → `agent_memories`: 66 beat reporters and 81 die-hard fans across all 32 teams, 20 bandwagon fans, 34 national writers and social accounts (including the two D7 accounts); identity only, exported from `madden_2036` on 2026-10-29. Left out: the 20 `FORMER_PLAYER` accounts, written as retired before 2035 while most still play in a 2034 franchise, so the social desk's ex-player role finds no one and skips. Added: `Mel_Kiper_Jr` for `MEL_KIPER`, which the draft article types and the offseason slate name but which had no account in 2036 either. `ESPN` and `SCHEFTER` are personas no article type or desk assigns, so they get no account; Schefter posts as `SCHEFTER_TWEET`. Every account carries a `person_key` (default `agent_id`; `Skip_Bayless_National` and `Skip_Bayless` both `Skip_Bayless`). After the accounts the seed calls `relationships.seed_writer_relationships(cur, season)` and reports the written rows as `writer_relationships` (425 on a fresh scratch database)), and sets the default Napper fantasy manager profile.

### 3.1 Core Entity & State Tables
- **`teams`**:
  - `id` (PK, int), `name` (varchar), `city` (varchar), `abbreviation` (varchar, e.g. 'CAR', 'TB', 'KC'), `conference` (varchar), `division` (varchar), `team_color` (varchar hex), `stadium_name` (varchar). `UNIQUE(name)`.
- **`players`**:
  - `id` (PK, int), `full_name` (varchar), `player_name` (varchar, e.g. 'G. Crawford'), `player_number` (int - jersey number, default 0), `height` (varchar), `weight` (int lbs), `espn_id` (int, nullable), `madden_pgid` (int, nullable, unique when set; `2027_01_05_madden_pgid.sql`: Madden's `Player.PresentationId` on the PC save, written by `pipeline/load_save.py`; players it creates get `origin` = `SAVE`).
- **`league_state`**:
  - `id` (PK, int, default 1 — single row), `current_season` (int), `current_week` (int), `madden_league_id` (bigint, nullable; `2027_01_13_franchise_identity.sql`: the save's `Franchise.LeagueID`, stamped by `pipeline/watch_save.py` when it seeds a franchise database, checked before every load). Column defaults are 2024 / 1; the live league row is currently season 2036, week 4 (2026-10-19). `current_week` is Madden's current (next unplayed) week in `games.week` numbering, set by each weekly capture load from the captured week label (`pipeline/load_capture.py`); `current_season` is set by hand at a new season or automatically incremented (with `current_week` reset to 1) when starting a start-of-season cadence run (`--mode season`). The backfill, `pipeline/main.py`'s trigger and `DatabaseHandler.get_current_league_state()` read both and never infer or write them.
- **`player_attributes`** (`2027_01_06_player_attributes.sql`, native Madden ratings):
  - `id` (PK), `player_id` (FK players), `season` (int), `team_id` (FK teams), `capture_folder` (varchar, default `save_<season>` or the capture folder), `position`, `age`, `overall_rating` (the OVR from the save), `predicted_ovr` / `ovr_check` (engines/ovr_weights check), `confirmed` (smallint, count of ratings stored, 54 for native PC save rows), `ratings` (jsonb `{"Speed": 99, ...}`, all 54 Madden 27 Player.<field>Rating names, 0–99), `flags` (text: `'native_save'` season baseline, `'in_season_change'`; older PS5-scan rows carry read notes or NULL), `created_at`. Unique (`player_id`, `capture_folder`): each player's 54 native ratings from PC save snapshots, written by `pipeline/load_save.py` only when they change, since Project Mu owns progression: a `native_save` row the first time a player is loaded in a season (the baseline, e.g. after the offseason progression write, or a new player), then an `in_season_change` row only if a later capture's ratings differ from the newest stored row; unchanged captures write nothing. The comparison skips the capture's own row and anything stored after it, so reloading a capture rewrites it in place. The load report counts `player_attributes` (rows written), `player_attributes_unchanged` and `player_attributes_in_season_changes`; the last should stay 0 once Madden's XP sliders are at 0 (PROGRESSION_PLAN.md phase A check 1). Read by `engines/progression.py` (`fetch_player_attributes_map`) for progression and attribute auditing.
- **`player_name_aliases`** (`2027_01_07_player_name_aliases.sql`, Commentary surname renames, docs/done/PRE_PC_WORK.md §2; written by `pipeline/commentary_names.py`):
  - `player_id` (FK players ON DELETE CASCADE), `alias` (varchar 128), `kind` (varchar 32, default `'commentary_rename'`), `created_at` (timestamptz). Primary key (`player_id`, `alias`); indexed on `alias`. Stores historical original names when surnames are renamed to match Madden commentary IDs, allowing global player search (`/api/search` and Napper API) to find players by previous names. Readers check `player_name_aliases_exist(cur)` so that unmigrated databases seamlessly omit the alias clause without query failure.

### 3.2 Temporal Snapshot Ledgers
- **`team_seasons`**:
  - `id` (PK), `team_id` (FK), `season` (int), `wins` (int), `losses` (int), `team_ovr` (int), `off_ovr` (int), `def_ovr` (int), `pass_off_rank` (int), `rush_off_rank` (int), `pass_rush_rank` (int), `coverage_rank` (int) (`team_ovr`/`off_ovr`/`def_ovr`: PS5 from the Team Overalls OCR capture, PC from the save's Team.TEAM_RATINGOVR/OFF/DEF via `pipeline/load_save.py`; the rank columns only from the OCR capture, so NULL on a PC franchise), `watchability_index` (float8), `popularity_index` (float8), `opp_adj_credit`, `opp_adj_credit_recent`, `sos_rating`, `expected_wins` (float8, nullable; see 2.4, added by `db/migrations/2026_10_14_opp_adj_credit.sql`), `watchability_sigma_top`, `p_draft`, `y_prod`, `purgatory_penalty` (float8, nullable; TWI components, see 2.2, added by `db/migrations/2026_10_15_stored_index_components.sql`), `trajectory_multiplier` (2.4), `pythagorean_wins`, `pace_production` (2.6) (float8, nullable; added by `db/migrations/2026_10_16_trajectory_and_efficiency.sql`), `s_playoff` (2.7; added by `db/migrations/2026_10_17_playoff_clout_awards_exposure.sql`); Team Stats tabs from the capture (nullable, `2026_10_23_capture_loader.sql`, not read yet): `third_down_conv`/`_att`/`_pct`, `fourth_down_conv`/`_att`/`_pct`, `two_point_conv`/`_att`/`_pct`, `red_zone_att`/`_td`/`_fg`/`_pct`, `red_zone_def_att`/`_td`/`_fg`/`_pct`, `penalties`, `penalty_yards`; observed tendencies (§2.12, `2026_11_13_observed_tendencies.sql`): `pass_rate_oe`, `fourth_down_oe` (float8), `observed_pass_lean`, `observed_fourth_down` (`Low` / `Medium` / `High`), `tendency_games` (int). `UNIQUE(team_id, season)`; `wins`/`losses` are maintained by `trigger_update_team_records` (see 3.6).
- **`player_seasons`**:
  - `id` (PK), `player_id` (FK), `team_id` (FK), `season` (int), `position` (varchar), `age` (int), `overall_rating` (int; NULL for a CPU free-agent signing created from League Transactions until the next roster scan rates him: the Excitement engine leaves him out of the top-3 OVR, TWI's draft pedigree and starter age skip or sort him last, and player popularity treats him as `UNRATED_OVR` 65, i.e. no rating bonus), `years_of_experience` (int; 0 = rookie, 1 = second-year), `popularity_index` (float8), `spike_index`, `r_rating`, `f_platform`, `t_success`, `a_awards`, `e_exposure` (float8, nullable; player Pop components, see 2.5), `s_playoff` (float8, nullable; 2.7); roster card fields `dev_trait` (`Normal` | `Star` | `Superstar` | `Superstar X-Factor` | `Hidden`: Madden hides a rookie's dev until 500 snaps, often on Star/Superstar rookies; the 47 hidden 2036 rookies were set from the 2026-10-17 roster capture on 2026-10-20), `archetype`, `role` (varchar, nullable; `2026_10_23_capture_loader.sql`; `overall_rating` is the roster list OVR, the card's base OVR and morale aren't stored); `released_week` (int, nullable; `2026_12_08_transactions.sql`: set when a League Transactions release makes him a free agent, NULL = on the team's roster; `team_id` keeps his last team, §3.3e). `UNIQUE(player_id, season)`.

### 3.3 Games & Statistics Tables
- **`games`**:
  - `id` (PK), `season` (int), `week` (int), `home_team_id` (FK), `away_team_id` (FK), `home_score` (int), `away_score` (int), `status` (varchar: 'COMPLETED' | 'SCHEDULED' | 'BYE'), `game_time` (varchar, e.g. 'Sun 1:00 PM'), `game_type` (varchar, default 'REGULAR_SEASON'; playoff games `WILD_CARD` (week 19), `DIVISIONAL` (20), `CONFERENCE` (21), `SUPER_BOWL` (23), created by the weekly capture load from Madden's schedule, `pipeline/load_capture.PLAYOFF_GAME_TYPES`), `excitement_index` (float8), `projected_excitement` (float8, nullable; pre-game projected $E$), `completed_at` (timestamp). `UNIQUE(season, week, home_team_id, away_team_id)` (constraint `games_season_week_home_away_key`).
- **`player_stats`**:
  - `id` (PK), `game_id` (FK), `team_id` (FK), `player_name` (varchar), `position` (varchar), `completions`, `pass_attempts`, `pass_yards`, `pass_tds`, `interceptions`, `rush_attempts`, `rush_yards`, `rush_tds`, `receptions`, `rec_yards`, `rec_tds`, `fumb`, `fantasy_points` (numeric(6,2), **generated column**); from `2026_10_23_capture_loader.sql` (nullable, written only by the capture loader's games mode, not read yet): `player_id` (FK; keyed in a later migration), `pass_comp_pct`, `pass_rating`, `pass_ypa`, `pass_long`, `pass_sacks`, `rush_avg`, `rush_btk`, `rush_yac`, `rush_long`, `rec_avg`, `rec_rac`, `rec_rac_avg`, `rec_long`; `line_source` (`2026_11_14_player_stats_line_source.sql`): `CAPTURED` (written by the capture loader's games mode and the legacy `db_handler` loader), `WEEKLY` (the backfill filled the team's only missing game: exact) or `DISTRIBUTED` (spread over several games: synthetic); existing rows were set from whether the game has captured category lines (2035: Week 17 captured, the rest distributed). unique index `player_stats_game_name_position_team` on `(game_id, player_name, position, team_id)`, mirrored by name in `init_db.sql` (`2027_02_23_player_stats_team_key.sql`: two players can share an abbreviated name and position — J. Williams, HB, on two teams — and be in the same game; the key used to ignore the team and the second line was refused, failing a whole tuning season's ingest) and, from `2026_10_24_player_id_keys.py`, unique `(game_id, player_id)` where `player_id` is set; trigger `player_stats_fill_player_id` fills `player_id` on inserts that only name the player (the backfill), from players + player_seasons (same team and position, list name).
  - `fantasy_points` is a PostgreSQL `GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED` column computed from the row's box score with full-PPR scoring: 0.04/pass yd (1 per 25), 4/pass TD, −2/INT, 0.1/rush & rec yd (1 per 10), 6/rush & rec TD, 1/reception, −2/fumble; NULL stats count as 0. It recomputes automatically on every insert or stat correction and is read-only: ingestion and backfill code must **not** insert or update it (Postgres rejects writes). All fantasy surfaces (`vw_fantasy_scores`, `vw_fantasy_defense_vs_position`, game logs, rankings, player popularity) read this column.
  - Introduced by `db/migrations/2026_10_12_fantasy_points_generated.sql` (self-verifying; rolls back on any value change). Restoring a database dump taken before 2026-10-12 brings back the old plain column; re-apply the migration afterwards. Fresh databases built from `db/init_db.sql` already have the generated column.
- **`team_stats`**:
  - `id` (PK), `game_id` (FK), `team_name` (varchar), `score`, `first_downs`, `total_offense`, `total_plays`, `rushing_attempts`, `rushing_yards`, `rushing_tds`, `passing_completions`, `passing_attempts`, `passing_yards`, `passing_tds`, `third_down_attempts`, `third_down_conversions`, `fourth_down_attempts`, `fourth_down_conversions` (int, no default: NULL = unknown until the estimator fills them, 2026_10_29), `turnovers` (all int); box-score fields from `2026_10_23_capture_loader.sql` (nullable): `q1`–`q4`, `ot` (NULL when the digits were unreadable), `punt_return_yards`, `kick_return_yards`, `total_yards_gained`, `two_point_conversions`, `red_zone_pct`, `red_zone_tds`, `red_zone_fgs`, `penalty_yards`, `time_of_possession_s`; from `2026_10_29_team_box_estimates.sql`: `red_zone_attempts`, `two_point_attempts`, `penalties` (int, nullable) and `estimated_fields` (text[], default `{}`: the columns `engines/team_box_estimator.py` filled rather than a capture); from `2026_10_31_team_box_exact_fields.sql`: `exact_fields` (text[], default `{}`: the estimated columns that are exact, i.e. a team's only missing cell for that column; the 2035 Weeks 1–17 backlog has none). `UNIQUE(game_id, team_name)`.
- **`season_stats`**:
  - `id` (PK), `season` (int), `player_id` (FK), `player_name` (varchar), `team_id` (FK), `position` (varchar), the same box-score counters as `player_stats`, `total_fantasy_points` (numeric(7,2)), `ppg_fantasy_points` (numeric(5,2)); offense extras from `2026_10_23_capture_loader.sql` (nullable, not read yet): `pass_comp_pct`, `pass_ypg`, `pass_rating`, `pass_ypa`, `pass_long`, `pass_sacks`, `rush_avg`, `rush_ypg`, `rush_btk`, `rush_yac`, `rush_long`, `rec_avg`, `rec_ypg`, `rec_rac`, `rec_rac_avg`, `rec_long`. `UNIQUE(season, player_name, team_id, position)` and unique `(season, player_id)` where `player_id` is set (`2026_10_24_player_id_keys.py`, which re-linked the existing rows from the refreshed roster and merged a player's duplicate rows, larger value per stat); trigger `season_stats_fill_player_id` as for `player_stats`.
- **Capture stat categories** (`2026_10_23_capture_loader.sql`; hybrid layout, docs/done/PIPELINE_MIGRATION.md phase 3): every category the Season Stats / game player-stats capture has beyond offense, in a season table (`season`, `player_id`, PK both) and a game table (`game_id` FK ON DELETE CASCADE, `player_id`, PK both), each with `team_id`, `position`: `season_stat_defense` / `game_stat_defense` (`solo`, `assists`, `tackles`, `tfl`, `sacks`, `ints`, `int_yds`, `int_avg`, `int_long`, `deflections`, `forced_fumbles`, `fumble_recoveries`, `fumble_yds`, `blocks`, `safeties`, `tds`), `_kicking` (`fgm`, `fga`, `fg_pct`, `fg_long`, `fg_blocked`, `xpm`, `xpa`, `xp_pct`, `xp_blocked`, `fgm_29` … `fga_50`, `kickoffs`, `touchbacks`), `_punting` (`punts`, `yards`, `average`, `net_yards`, `net_average`, `blocked`, `inside_20`, `touchbacks`, `longest`), `_kickreturn` / `_puntreturn` (`returns`, `yards`, `average`, `tds`, `longest`), `_blocking` (`sacks_allowed`), `_general` (`games_played`, `downs_played`; game level `downs_played` only). A row exists only where Madden lists the player (defense is listed by tackles, about the top 250 defenders; a missing row is unknown, not zero). Madden's Season Stats screens cover the regular season only (JR, Oct 14): in the postseason the season tables (and `season_stats`, `team_seasons` Team Stats totals) stop at Week 18, and playoff production exists only where a game's box score is captured (`games` mode). The writer tools read them through the `season_stat_lines` / `game_stat_lines` views (§7: `get_player_season_stats`, `get_game_box_score`, `get_top_rated_players`, `get_defense_special_teams_leaders`).
- **Views** `season_stat_lines` (one row per `player_seasons` row: offense from `season_stats` + every category, prefixed `blk_`, `def_`, `kick_`, `punt_`, `kr_`, `pr_`) and `game_stat_lines` (one row per player and game that has any game-level row).
- **`game_scripts`** (`2026_11_18_game_scripts.sql`, §2.14): `game_id` (PK, FK `games` ON DELETE CASCADE), `season`, `week`, `version` (`SCRIPT_VERSION`), `facts_hash` (the recorded facts the script was built from), `script` (jsonb), `generated_at`. Index on `(season, week)`.
- **`game_highlights`** (`2026_11_23_game_highlights.sql`, §2.14): `game_id` (PK, FK `games` ON DELETE CASCADE), `season`, `week`, `highlights` (jsonb array of real highlight plays: `quarter`, `clock`, `play_type`, `play`, `rating`), `created_at`. Index on `(season, week)`. Populated by `pipeline/load_capture.py` from `games/<NN>/highlights.json`, and by `pipeline/load_save.py` with the save's scoring plays only (`play` like `CAR TOUCHDOWN`, plus `points`, `team`, `scoring`, `source` = `SAVE`) for games without captured highlights.
- **`captures`**: one row per capture run: `folder` (unique), `mode` (weekly | roster | season_schedule | games | playoff | contracts; a folder with `game_scores.csv` and `schedule.csv` loads as `playoff`), `season`, `week`, `status` (captured | extracted | loaded | failed), `row_counts` (jsonb), Gemini token totals, `error`, `captured_at` / `extracted_at` / `loaded_at`.
- **`llm_usage`**: one row per model call: `source`, `capture_id` (FK, nullable), `label`, `model` (clean Gemini model or `ollama/<model_name>` for local models), `input_tokens` (Gemini cached included; Ollama `prompt_eval_count`), `cached_tokens`, `output_tokens` (Gemini candidates; Ollama `eval_count`), `thinking_tokens` (0 for Ollama unless reported), `created_at`. Sources: `extract` (label = screenshot; per capture), `newsroom` (label = `@handle ARTICLE_TYPE`, every tool-loop call), `agent_wire` (`agent_id KIND`, `newsroom/social_publish.py`'s writer), `agent_memory` (`takes #<article id>` after each article, `summary <agent_id>` before a week), `custom_commission` (`classify_prompt`), `gm_persona` / `gm_rationale` / `gm_negotiation` / `scouting_notes` / `scout_report` / `draft_interview_classify` (`engines/gm_llm.py` / `engines/llm_provider.py`), and the legacy video pipeline's `ocr_extractor` / `heal_roster`. Logging never fails a run: without a database it prints a warning.
- **`awards`**:
  - `id` (PK), `season` (int), `award_type` (varchar), `player_id` (FK), `player_name` (varchar), `team_id` (FK), `coach_name` (varchar), `coach_id` (FK `coaches`, COTY rows; `2026_10_30_coaches.sql`), `position` (varchar). Partial unique indexes (`2026_11_20_all_pro_awards.sql`): `UNIQUE(season, award_type, position, player_id) WHERE player_id IS NOT NULL` (supporting First/Second Team All-Pro multi-player and multi-slot honors while preventing duplicate selections), `UNIQUE(season, award_type)` for major player awards (`MVP`, `OPOY`, `DPOY`, `OROY`, `DROY`, `SBMVP`), and `UNIQUE(season, award_type) WHERE award_type = 'COTY'`. The historical import (`pipeline/batch_menus.py`) writes COTY with both `coach_name` and `coach_id`, creating the `coaches` row if the name is new; year-end major awards (`MVP`, `OPOY`, `OROY`, `DPOY`, `DROY`, `COTY`) are parsed and recorded from the Week 22 `AWARDS_TRACKER` (`AWARDS_WINNERS`) article by `newsroom/award_winners.py` (§7.6c); `SBMVP` is parsed and recorded from the post-Super Bowl `SUPER_BOWL_GAME_RECAP` article by `newsroom/award_winners.py` (§7.6d); year-end All-Pro teams are populated from `OFFICIAL_AP_ALL_PRO_ROSTER` by `newsroom/all_pro.py` (§7.6b).

### 3.3a Coaches & Staff (`db/migrations/2026_10_30_coaches.sql`, `2026_10_31_coach_baseline.sql`, `2026_11_01_coach_schemes.sql`, `2026_11_02_drop_coach_archetype.sql`, `2026_11_03_whitfield_2034.sql`, `2026_11_05_coach_tendencies.sql`, `2026_11_06_coty_scores.sql`, `2026_11_07_coach_2034_totals.sql`, `2026_11_09_coach_full_names.sql`, `2026_11_10_whitfield_tendencies.sql`, `2026_11_11_whitfield_ratings.sql`, `2026_11_24_coty_historical_records.sql`, `2026_11_25_coordinators_and_slants.sql`, `2026_11_27_whitfield_bears_coordinator_lore.sql`, `2026_11_28_panthers_bears_coordinators_update.sql`, `2026_11_29_panthers_shavon_bell_dc.sql`, `2026_12_01_coach_tenures_correction.sql`, `2026_12_14_coordinator_tenure_repair.sql`, `2026_12_15_colts_oc_evan_marsh.sql`, `2026_12_16_name_2036_coordinators.sql`, `2026_12_22_coach_hot_seat.sql`, `2026_12_23_coaching_carousel.sql`, `2026_12_24_staff_moves_inputs.sql`, `2026_12_25_saleh_2025_baseline.sql`, `2027_02_21_coach_madden_profiles.sql`)
Head coaches and coordinator staffs (docs/done/COACH_SLANTS_AND_COORDINATORS_PLAN.md). `engines/coty_engine.py` reads `coaches` and `coach_tenures` (§2.11). The writer tools read coaches, coordinators, tenures, snapshots, and tendencies through `engines/coach_profile.py` (§7: `get_coach_profile` (head coach plus `offensive_coordinator` / `defensive_coordinator`), `get_team_context` (`head_coach`) and `get_matchup_edges` (`coaching_matchup`)). Every article prompt also carries the whole league's staffs: `league_staff_directory(cur, season)` gives one line per team (`HC …; OC …; DC …`), which `compile_agent_prompt` puts in a `LEAGUE COACHING STAFFS (Season N)` block telling writers to name coaches only from it, never from real life (§7). `fetch_team_staff` takes the latest-starting active tenure per role, and a placeholder coordinator the offseason package creates (`<Team> Interim OC/DC`, `<Coach> Offensive/Defensive Lieutenant`, `PLACEHOLDER_COORDINATOR`) comes back with `name` None and a `name_note`; the directory shows it as "unnamed", to be called by title only. A head coach or coordinator the carousel fired after the season is marked "(fired on Black Monday after the S season)", "(fired after the S playoffs)" or, for a coordinator, "(fired after the S season)"; the hiring cycle's moves start the next season, so they never show for the concluded one. They count only games the article may see: the latest `coach_seasons` snapshot before the article's season plus visible games, the same sum as `coach_records`, which has no cutoff and serves ad-hoc queries. `tests/test_coach_profile.py` and `tests/test_coordinators.py` cover staff totals, scheme inheritance, Carolina continuity (Canales HC 2024–2033 with Brad Idzik OC and Ejiro Evero DC; Marcus Whitfield HC from 2034 with Charles Grant OC and Shavon Bell DC 2034–2035, then from 2036 David Wallace OC, a former Stanford OC who replaced Grant when Indianapolis hired him, and Phil Taylor DC, promoted from Panthers defensive line coach when Philadelphia hired Bell), and Chicago Bears continuity (Ben Johnson HC 2025–present, Thomas Brown OC 2026–2027, Marcus Whitfield OC 2028–2033 until hired by Carolina, Brett Vance OC 2034–present promoted from QB coach/college coordinator, Dennis Allen DC 2026–present). **Coaching changes come from Mu's coaching carousel** (§2.19) from 2036 on: it fires head coaches and coordinators and makes every hire for CPU teams; JR mirrors the head-coach changes in Madden (Mu's hire stands for whichever coach he hires there). JR's own teams change through the offseason manifest (§7.10) or a migration that closes old tenures (`end_season`) and adds new ones. Never commit `engines/coordinator_seeder.py` over the live database after an offseason: its upsert resets `end_season` to NULL and its slant pass resets coaches it doesn't know to `OFFENSIVE` (`test_seeder_idempotency` rolls back for this reason). `2026_12_14_coordinator_tenure_repair.sql` undid one such run: it closes tenures superseded by a 2036 tenure and the old coordinator jobs of the six coordinators hired as 2036 head coaches, deletes five cross-seeded baseline tenures (Curry at BAL, Doyle at NO, Staley at IND, Anarumo at NO, Bradley at KC), restores Shavon Bell's and Brian Flores's `DEFENSIVE` slants, and turns Carolina's stand-ins into David Wallace (`Panthers Interim OC`; Wide Zone West Coast, Carolina Offense) and Phil Taylor (`Panthers Interim DC`; Bell's 3-4 Carolina Defense and blitz/coverage tendencies), per JR. `2026_12_15_colts_oc_evan_marsh.sql` names the Colts' stand-in `Charles Grant Offensive Lieutenant` Evan Marsh, Grant's former Panthers quarterbacks coach (name chosen by Claude at JR's request; Wide Zone West Coast, Colts Offense). `2026_12_16_name_2036_coordinators.sql` names the other nine stand-ins, also invented at JR's request: internal promotions who inherit the predecessor's scheme, playbook and tendencies (LAC OC Derek Halvorsen, LAR OC Tyler Voss, MIN OC Jordan Pruitt, MIN DC Calvin Okafor) and assistants who followed the new head coach and keep the package's scheme (GB OC Nate Ellery, MIA OC Ross Kincaid, NYJ OC Sam Delacroix, PHI DC Greg Pellerin, TEN DC Andre Szabo). No 2036 coordinator is unnamed now; the "unnamed" handling stays for future offseason stand-ins.
- **Coaching trees (no table; docs/done/COACHING_TREES_PLAN.md):** who learned under whom, which tenures alone don't say. Reviewed edges live in `newsroom/config/coaching_trees/` (`coaching-trees-v1`): `trees.json` is the named-tree registry (`{key, label, root, parent, summary, evidence, review}`; parents chain, no cycles) and `batch_<A|B|C>.json` hold researched mentor → protégé edges among the 2026 seed's 96 HCs/coordinators (`key` `coach:<T>:<R>>coach:<T>:<R>`, seed refs without names, `stints`, `outcome` positive | mixed, ≥ 2 sources dated ≤ 2026-09-08 with one medium/high; boss over assistant ≥ 2 seasons, or 1 season plus a source marked `mentorship`), named-tree memberships and `proposed_trees`. Only approved/edited entries load. `personality/coaching_trees.py` keys people by `person_key(name)` (the carousel's own rule) and gives `reviewed_edges`, `reviewed_members`, `registry_trees`, `edge_events` (two `meaningful_interaction` facets, `direction` mentee / mentor, `source_event_id mu:coach-tree:<key>`, public, `reviewed_evidence`, season 2026 tick 1, `prehistory`; appended later by the lifecycle apply, not here), the in-sim rule `sim_edges` (a coordinator with `TREE_MIN_SEASONS` = 2 simulated seasons from 2026 as OC/DC under one head coach, summed across teams, becomes his protégé in the season the count is reached, `crossed_season`; `mixed` when his last stint ended with `fired` while the mentor stayed; reviewed pairs skipped) and `lineage` / `lineage_line` (own memberships, then up to `LINEAGE_DEPTH` = 3 mentor hops to the nearest named trees: registry roots, members' trees, or a computed `<Surname> tree` for a coach with `NAMED_TREE_MIN_HCS` = 2 protégés who became head coaches; registry parents give e.g. "McVay tree (Shanahan lineage)"). `engines/coaching_tree_facts.py` reads `staff_seasons` (coach/coordinator tenures expanded per season, clipped to 2026..through, `fired` from `coordinator_hot_seat` in the stint's last season), `tree_graph` and `tree_context` (lineage + line for one name, or None; savepoint, missing tables read as None). Reads are factual and don't wait for the personality switchboard.
- **Reviewed personality profiles (no table; §7.11):** each 2026 head coach and coordinator gets a `coach-profile-v1` file in `newsroom/config/coach_personas/<TEAM>_<ROLE>.json`, mapped to his `COACHES_DATA` / `COORDINATORS_DATA` row by `seed_ref`; the lifecycle plan resolves `seed_ref` to `coaches.id` or `coordinators.id` at its reviewed apply. Nothing here writes these tables.
- **`coaches`**: `id` (PK), `coach_name` (varchar, unique), `slant` (`OFFENSIVE` | `DEFENSIVE` | `CEO`, default `OFFENSIVE`, `2026_11_25_coordinators_and_slants.sql`), `offensive_scheme`, `defensive_scheme` (varchar, nullable). Head coach slants set tactical specialization:
  - `OFFENSIVE`: Head coach imports offensive scheme, playbook, and pass-lean tendency; defensive scheme remains intact under DC.
  - `DEFENSIVE`: Head coach imports defensive front (`3-4` or `4-3`), blitz rate, and man coverage; offensive scheme remains intact under OC.
  - `CEO`: Program manager focusing on fourth-down aggressiveness and game management; unit schemes delegated to OC and DC.
- **`coordinators`**: `id` (PK), `coordinator_name` (varchar), `side` (`OFFENSIVE` | `DEFENSIVE`), `scheme` (varchar), `playbook` (varchar), `pass_lean`, `blitz_rate`, `man_coverage` (each `Low`/`Medium`/`High`), `origin_notes` (text). Seeded by `engines/coordinator_seeder.py` from 2026 baseline with procedural fallbacks.
- **`coordinator_tenures`**: `id` (PK), `coordinator_id` (FK `coordinators`), `team_id` (FK `teams`), `role` (`OC` | `DC`), `start_season` (int), `end_season` (int, NULL = active). `UNIQUE(coordinator_id, team_id, role, start_season)`. Every active franchise maintains exactly one OC and one DC per season.
- **`coach_tenures`**: `coach_id` (FK), `team_id` (FK), `start_season`, `end_season` (NULL = current). `UNIQUE(coach_id, team_id, start_season)`. A coach's per-season record in the franchise comes from joining this to `team_seasons`. Originally all seeded with `start_season = 2026` in `2026_10_31_coach_baseline.sql`, tenures were corrected in `2026_12_01_coach_tenures_correction.sql` to reflect accurate historical hiring years: Shanahan (SF, 2017), McVay (LAR, 2017), LaFleur (GB, 2019–2035), Taylor (CIN, 2019), Campbell (DET, 2021), Sirianni (PHI, 2021–2035), O'Connell (MIN, 2022), Bowles (TB, 2022), Ryans (HOU, 2023), Steichen (IND, 2023–2035), Canales (CAR, 2024–2033), Harbaugh (LAC, 2024), Macdonald (SEA, 2024), Quinn (WAS, 2024), Johnson (CHI, 2025), Schottenheimer (DAL, 2025), Coen (JAX, 2025), Moore (NO, 2025), and Glenn (NYJ, 2025–2035). Historical prior stints are also recorded for veteran coaches: Harbaugh (Ravens 2008–2025), McCarthy (Packers 2006–2018, Cowboys 2020–2024), Stefanski (Browns 2020–2025), Vrabel (Titans 2018–2023), Saleh (Jets 2021–2024), Bowles (Jets 2015–2018), Quinn (Falcons 2015–2020), and Harbaugh (49ers 2011–2014). Carolina: Dave Canales 2024–2033, Marcus Whitfield from 2034. The Broncos' and Chiefs' coaches since 2026 are Peter Gaffney and Ron Leonard (Madden coaches with no earlier career; full names from `2026_11_09_coach_full_names.sql`), not Sean Payton and Andy Reid, who were removed (`2026_11_07_coach_2034_totals.sql`). They took over those teams' schemes and pass/blitz/man tendencies (playbooks unchanged since 2026), with Medium fourth-down aggressiveness.
- **`coach_seasons`**: `coach_id` (FK), `team_id` (FK), `season`, and the Madden coach screen's career counters as of that season: `career_wins`, `career_losses`, `career_ties`, `winning_seasons`, `playoff_wins`, `playoff_losses`, `super_bowl_wins`, `super_bowl_losses`. `UNIQUE(coach_id, season)`. These totals include pre-franchise NFL careers, so they are stored as shown rather than rebuilt from `games`. **Baseline row:** season 2025 holds each 2026 coach's real NFL head-coaching career through 2025, the starting point of the franchise (`2026_10_31_coach_baseline.sql`; source: Wikipedia's current-coaches list as of 2026-07-12, plus each coach's year-by-year record for winning seasons (W > L, partial and interim seasons included) and Super Bowl results), with `team_id` linked to their active franchise as of 2025 (`2026_12_01_coach_tenures_correction.sql`). Whitfield had no head-coaching career before 2034, so he has no baseline row. His one franchise-season row is 2034 (Carolina): 13-4, a #1-seed bye, 3-0 in the playoffs and a Super Bowl win (`2026_11_03_whitfield_2034.sql`, per JR; the 2034 regular season and early playoff rounds aren't in `games`). No other franchise-season rows (2026–2035) yet. **End-of-2034 rows** (`2026_11_07_coach_2034_totals.sql`): all 32 active coaches' totals at the end of 2034, from Madden's coach screen at 2035 Week 18 minus each team's 2035 record at that point (Carolina 17-0, the rest 16 games). The view matched the screen for every coach except Whitfield, one win short until Carolina's Week 18 game is loaded. Whitfield's 2034 row equals the earlier hand entry. Madden's careers start from different numbers than the real ones for Saleh (no Jets record) and Bowles (one more loss, and no winning seasons: a 2025 save lists none, JR 2026-10-26). Bowles's 2025 row stays real-life history. Saleh's was set to all zeros, Madden's starting point (JR, 2026-10-26: the row was stale; `2026_12_25_saleh_2025_baseline.sql`), so the Titans' 2025 → 2034 difference is 83-70. Dave Canales's latest row is still 2025.
- **View `coach_records`**: each coach's current career totals, the latest `coach_seasons` row (totals at the end of that season) plus every completed game his team played in later seasons while he held the job (`coach_tenures`). Regular-season games add wins, losses and ties; any non-`REGULAR_SEASON` game adds playoff wins and losses; `SUPER_BOWL` games add Super Bowl wins and losses. A winning season counts once the team's 17-game regular season is complete and wins exceed losses (Madden adds winning seasons only at season's end). Columns: `coach_id`, `coach_name`, `snapshot_season`, `career_wins`, `career_losses`, `career_ties`, `winning_seasons`, `playoff_wins`, `playoff_losses`, `super_bowl_wins`, `super_bowl_losses`. No coach-screen capture is needed: the weekly game captures keep it current.
- **`coty_scores`**: `coach_id` (FK), `team_id` (FK), `season`, `coty_score`, `coty_rank`, `win_pct`, `wins_above_expected`, `roster_outperformance` (nullable: no `team_ovr`), `win_pct_change` (nullable: no previous regular season), `first_year_with_team` (bool), `historical_bonus` (double precision, default 0.0), `historical_notes` (text[]). `UNIQUE(coach_id, season)`. The Coach of the Year race (§2.11), rewritten per season by `python3 -m engines.coty_engine [--season N]`; 32 rows for 2035.
- **`coach_hot_seat`** (`2026_12_22_coach_hot_seat.sql`, `phase` from `2026_12_23_coaching_carousel.sql`): `season`, `team_id` (PK together), `coach_id`, `score`, `fired` (bool), `inputs` (jsonb: coach, wins, losses, expected_wins, tenure, terms, made_playoffs, playoff_wins, p, draw, safe, capped), `decided_at`, `phase` (`BLACK_MONDAY` | `PLAYOFF_EXIT`). One row per head coach and season, written once by §2.19.
- **`coordinator_hot_seat`** (`2026_12_23_coaching_carousel.sql`): `season`, `team_id`, `role` (`OC` | `DC`; PK together), `coordinator_id`, `score`, `fired`, `phase`, `inputs` (coordinator, unit_rank, talent_rank, tenure, terms, p, draw, safe, capped), `decided_at`. The coordinators of every team whose head coach kept his job.
- **`staff_moves`** (`2026_12_23_coaching_carousel.sql`): the hiring cycle's log for the staff of season + 1: `id`, `season` (concluded), `team_id`, `role` (`HC` | `OC` | `DC`), `action` (`HIRED` | `LEFT`: a coordinator who left for a head-coach job | `REPLACED`: a coordinator the new head coach replaced with his own), `person`, `coach_id`, `coordinator_id`, `source` (HIRED: `POACHED`, `PROMOTED`, `RETREAD`, `REHIRED`, `HC_STAFF`, `OUTSIDE`), `from_team_id`, `from_role`, `slant`, `score`, `notes`, `created_at`, `inputs` (jsonb, `2026_12_24_staff_moves_inputs.sql`; head-coach hires: opening_rank, openings, appeal, parts).
- **`staff_contracts`** (`db/migrations/2027_02_07_staff_contracts_and_full_control.sql`, STAFF_CONTRACTS_AND_FULL_CONTROL_PLAN §2.4): `id` (SERIAL PK), `team_id` (FK `teams`), `person_id` (int, polymorphic — HC→coaches.id, GM→gm_profiles.id, OC/DC→coordinators.id — disambiguated by `person_kind`, so no FK), `person_kind` (`VARCHAR(6)` CHECK HC/GM/OC/DC), `annual_salary` (bigint), `total_years` (smallint), `remaining_years` (smallint), `signed_season` (int), `full_control` (bool, default false), `buyout_owed` (bigint, default 0), `buyout_charged_season` (int, `2027_02_19`, superseded and never written), `buyout_total` (bigint), `buyout_fired_season` (int), `buyout_years` (smallint) (`2027_02_20`: the buyout's instalment schedule), `created_at` (timestamptz). One row per contract; `engines/staff_contracts_engine.py` tiers salaries from experience/championships (GM: ELITE `$8.0M–$12.0M`, `$10.0M` midpoint, `championships >= 1`; STANDARD `$4.0M–$7.5M`, `$5.75M`, `experience >= GM_STANDARD_EXPERIENCE` 3; PROMOTION `$2.0M–$3.5M`, `$2.75M`, a first-time GM), deducts `annual_cash_pool − staff_payroll − opex − dead_buyouts` (payroll into `owner_cash_ledgers.staff_payroll`), rolls `remaining_years` down each season and moves the remaining guaranteed salary into `buyout_owed` on a firing. A firing also records its instalment schedule (`staff_contracts_engine.firing_columns`): the whole buyout in `buyout_total`, its first league year in `buyout_fired_season`, its length in `buyout_years`; `buyout_instalment` charges one even instalment in each of those years, the last taking the remainder, from the stored schedule, so rerunning a season charges the same amount and the instalments sum to the buyout. The years owed are `staff_contracts_engine.owed_years(total_years, signed_season, season)` (`total_years - (season - signed_season)`, clamped to the deal): the annual producer passes the season it runs, and the two hot-seat settles (a fired GM in `gm_rollover._settle_gm_contract`, a fired Full Control HC in `coach_hot_seat._settle_full_control`) pass the firing season, whose row they zero before the annual run sees it. `current_staff` reads a tenure as current through its `end_season` (`end_season >= season`, so a coordinator who left during the season is not charged a buyout), and its settled-row skip (a row with `remaining_years = 0` and `buyout_owed > 0`) is bounded by the tenure's start, so a coach re-hired into the same seat is filed a new contract. When a deal runs out under a man still in the job, the team decides then (JR, 2026-11-10, via M-0165/M-0179): **kept**, he is re-signed at market from that season, his own pay as a floor (a full-control HC keeps full control, is paid the HC market above that floor, and still counts toward the 2-coach ceiling; the cooldown is not reset); **leaving** (his tenure ends that season, or a hot-seat settle closed his row), only the season he actually worked is filed, as a one-year deal at exactly his old salary with no full-control flag, so it is paid, nothing is owed beyond it, and his seat is released. A man with no contract row at all (a league-start hire the settle could not find) gets his deal filed from his tenure start and the firing loop settles the rest. A hire for the coming league year is filed at once, signed for that season: `coaching_carousel.run` calls `staff_contracts_run.file_hires(cur, season + 1)` inside `hiring_cycle` as it hires, `annual` runs the same pass as a backstop, and `coach_link.link_staff` calls it for the starting staff it seats at league start (`starting_only=False` files every current staffer with no row, not just a hire). A hire's own deal is not charged to this season (`signed_season <= season`) and never read as a departure; a starting coach's is charged to it, with the save's remaining years, so the re-sign and buyout timing follows Madden. Either way the save writer finds a live row from the first write (M-0200, M-0225). A GM counts as current through his `end_season` too, so a league-start GM fired before the first annual run is still filed and paid. For a hot-seat firing the settle zeroes the row before the annual run, so the firing season is booked as the first buyout instalment (`dead_buyouts`) rather than as `staff_payroll`; the annual path books it as payroll. The cash total is salary x length either way. `staff_contracts_run.current_staff` measures a coach's or coordinator's experience as the seasons in the role across all his tenures (a coordinator's OC and DC seasons count together; a GM's id is per hire, so his is `season - start_season + 1`), at least 1, so a veteran stays STANDARD, a first-year hire is PROMOTION and a re-sign after long service earns the raise. One active contract per person, team and role: the partial unique index `staff_contracts_active_once` on `(team_id, person_kind, person_id) WHERE remaining_years > 0` (`2027_02_17_staff_contract_active_once.sql`); a settled row keeps `remaining_years = 0` and may coexist with a newer one.
- **`full_control_history`** (`2027_02_07_staff_contracts_and_full_control.sql`): `id` (SERIAL PK), `season` (int), `team_id` (FK `teams`), `coach_id` (FK `coaches`), `annual_salary` (bigint), `contract_years` (smallint), `trigger_reason` (text). One row per Godfather offer; the R2 rarity governor (at most 2 active full-control coaches league-wide and ≥5 seasons since the last offer) reads it via `staff_contracts_engine.godfather_gate`.
- **`coach_madden_profiles`** (`db/migrations/2027_02_21_coach_madden_profiles.sql`, COACH_SAVE_WRITES_PLAN §2.1): one row per Mu head coach or coordinator, holding every Madden `Coach` field Mu writes plus the link to the save record. `id` (SERIAL PK), `person_kind` (`COACH` | `COORD` — `coaches.id` or `coordinators.id`), `person_id` (int), `source` (`SAVE` | `CREATED`), `presentation_id` (int, NULL until linked/written), `first_name`, `last_name`, `age`, `position` (StaffPosition: `HeadCoach` | `OffensiveCoordinator` | `DefensiveCoordinator`), `archetype` (StaffArchetypeEnum), `specialty` (CoachSpecialty), `level`, `years_coaching`, `offensive_playbook`, `defensive_playbook`, `offensive_scheme`, `defensive_scheme`, `team_philosophy`, `personality`, `demeanor`, `body_type`, `height`, `weight`, `face_shape`, `generic_head`, `talents` (jsonb `[{slot, talent, tier}]`), `ratings` (jsonb `COACH_*` values), `tendencies` (jsonb `COACH_*TENDENCY*` fields), `visuals_template` (the save coach's `PresentationId` whose visuals are cloned), `portrait_id` (0 = silhouette), `portrait_status` (`NONE` | `GENERATED` | `PACKED` | `INSTALLED`), `headshot_path`, `seed`, `written_at`. `UNIQUE (person_kind, person_id)`; partial unique index `coach_madden_profiles_pid` on `presentation_id` where not NULL. The contract stays in `staff_contracts`. `engines/coach_madden_profile.build_profile(person, role, *, slant, scheme, playbook, tendencies, sliders, background, contract, seed)` is the pure, seeded builder for an invented person: Spike A's `PLAYBOOK_MAP`/`SCHEME_MAP` (an unmapped Mu name raises), `TALENT_TEMPLATES` scaled by `LEVEL_BY_YEARS`, personality/demeanor from the sliders, and a seeded look. All draws come from `random.Random(seed)` with `seed = madden-coach:<coach_key>`.

### 3.3b Injuries (`db/migrations/2026_11_08_injuries.sql`)
- **`injuries`** (`mu_weeks_out` smallint from `2027_01_14`: Project Mu's duration, written back to the save; NULL = Madden's own):
  - `id` (SERIAL PK), `season` (int), `week` (int), `team_id` (FK `teams` ON DELETE CASCADE), `player_id` (FK `players` ON DELETE SET NULL), `player_name` (varchar), `position` (varchar), `ovr` (int), `injury_type` (varchar, diagnosis e.g. 'TURF TOE', 'BROKEN COLLARBONE', 'NONE'), `duration` (varchar, e.g. 'WEEK TO WEEK', '4 - 8 WEEKS', '0 WEEKS'), `weeks_remaining` (int, default 0), `is_ir` (bool, default false), `captured_at` (timestamptz, default now()). `UNIQUE(season, week, team_id, player_name)` and unique partial index on `(season, week, player_id) WHERE player_id IS NOT NULL`.
  - Populated weekly by `pipeline/load_capture.py` from `captures/<run>/injuries.csv` (extracted via on-device Apple Vision OCR across all 32 teams). Players on IR or with `weeks_remaining > 0` are factored into `engines/fantasy_projection_engine.py` (projected points zeroed out, omitted from `pos_rank`, discounted in `ros_total_points`). Napper reads the same rows through `engines/napper_injuries.py` (OUT/IR badges, IR-slot eligibility, AI lineups), with the same countdown rule.
  - **Madden IR bug (JR, 2026-10-27):** Madden never takes a healed player off IR: he stays on the report as `injury_type` NONE, `duration` '0 WEEKS', `weeks_remaining` 0, `is_ir` true, and never plays again (2036 through week 18: 129 of 131 players who went on IR recorded no stat afterwards; the two who did dropped off the report, i.e. were activated). JR activates them by hand (take control of the team, activate, fix the depth chart). `pipeline/ir_returns.py` lists who is due before week W: the player's latest report up to W is his team's latest report (absent from a newer one = activated), he is on IR, and `weeks_remaining` counted down to W is ≤ 0; in the postseason only teams with a game in W, a team's reports being the regular-season ones plus the playoff weeks it played. Each entry carries `healed_week` (first report of the stint with 0 weeks, else the countdown) and `new` (healed this week). Position/OVR fall back to `player_seasons` (healed rows often read blank). The weekly run shows it twice (§6.0): projected in the "your turn" notice after the capture, and confirmed after the load (Step 6c). Tests: `tests/test_ir_returns.py`.

### 3.3c Draft (`db/migrations/2026_11_19_draft_board.sql`, `2026_11_26_draft_selections.sql`, §2.10)
- **`draft_prospects`**: `id` (SERIAL PK), `draft_season` (int, the class: league season + 1), `projected_pick` (int, nullable for unprojected off-board picks), `projected_round` (varchar, '1'–'7' or 'UDFA'), `round_pick` (smallint), `full_name` (varchar), `position`, `college`, `height_in`, `weight`, `age`, `ovr` (scouted), `archetype`, `notes`, `source_capture` (the `captures/<run>` folder), `player_id` (FK `players` ON DELETE SET NULL; set by the rookie link), `loaded_at`; actual draft selection results (`2026_11_26_draft_selections.sql`): `actual_round` (varchar), `actual_round_pick` (smallint), `actual_pick` (smallint 1–300), `drafted_team_id` (FK `teams`), `selection_notes` (text). Unique index on `(draft_season, actual_pick) WHERE actual_pick IS NOT NULL` and index on `(draft_season, drafted_team_id)`. Populated pre-draft by `pipeline/draft_board.py` (board scan) and post-draft by `pipeline/draft_results.py` (actual results across all rounds, default 224 picks up to 300, or Round 1 loaded via CLI or `--mode draft-results`). After loading, `resolve_and_load_picks` calls `engines/draft_room.validate` (team management step 4): each Draft Room pick 1–32 in `scout_draft_picks` is compared with the recap's `actual_pick`/`drafted_team_id` (`madden_match` MATCH / MISMATCH, `madden_prospect_id`; mismatches listed in the load report's `draft_room` and on the card, never auto-edited: the recap is Madden's truth for `actual_*`), and the class's scouting rows become `DRAFTED` or `UDFA` from the recap. Enables direct comparison of projected vs actual selection (risers, fallers, reaches).
- **PC franchises:** no Draft Board scan; `pipeline/load_save.py` (reader_version ≥ 5) writes the coming class (league season + 1) from the save's prospects (status Draft) in Madden's board order (`DraftPlayer.InitialDraftRank`): projected pick 1…, round 1–7 then UDFA, Mu position and archetype, age, height, weight, `ovr` = the save's true OVR (Mu's scouting adds the uncertainty), `college` from the prospect's `Player.College` reference through `pipeline/colleges.college_name` (Madden's own college list, `data/scouting/madden27_colleges.json`, upper-cased like the PS5 scan; NULL for an unknown reference: on CAREER-WEEK1 all 389 prospects get one, 374 of them a school the scouting list knows, §2.18), `source_capture` = the run folder. Only when the class has no board yet: a scanned or already loaded board is kept, so ids, mock drafts and scouting links never move. Season + 1 holds through the whole offseason (checked 2026-11-03 on the stage saves CAREER-STAFF … CAREER-DRAFT: calendar year 2026 and the same class until the draft; after it, CAREER-RECAPPOSTLIVE has no prospects and the 224 rookies have year_drafted 1 = 2027). The next class isn't in the save at 2027 preseason week 1 (it is by week 5 of the 2027 sample save); a load without one adds nothing.
- **Pick ownership** for future drafts is `draft_picks` (§3.3f): who owns each team's round 1–7 pick after trades.
- **Compensatory picks** (`db/migrations/2027_02_06_compensatory_draft_picks.sql`, §2.17g): `draft_picks`' primary key expands to `(draft_season, round, original_team_id, pick_suffix)` (`pick_suffix VARCHAR(4) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`) so a team can hold multiple comp picks in one round, and the `source` CHECK adds `'COMP'` and `'JC2A'`. New ledgers `qualifying_free_agents` (`season`, `player_id`, `old_team_id`, `new_team_id`, `signed_date`, `total_value`, `years`, `apy`, `snap_pct NUMERIC(4,3)`, `honors_points`, `round_tier` 3–7, `qualifies`, `canceled_by_qfa_id` self-FK) and `compensatory_pick_awards` (`draft_season`, `team_id`, `round` 3–7, `slot_in_round`, `overall_pick`, `award_kind` CBA/JC2A, `source_player_id`, `source_coach_id`, `reason`).
- **Staff development award data path** (`db/migrations/2027_02_07_staff_development_award.sql`, COMPENSATORY_PICKS_PLAN follow-up U6, §2.17g): Resolution JC-2A is modelled as *reviewed program eligibility*, never inferred — no ethnicity/race/minority column exists on `coaches`, `coordinators` or `staff_moves`. `staff_development_eligibility` holds JR's reviewed rows (`person_kind` COACH/COORDINATOR/EXECUTIVE, `person_key`, `eligible`, `source`, `reviewed_by`, `as_of`; absent = not eligible); `staff_development_departures` journals qualifying hire-aways (`season`, from/to team, from/to role, `tenure_years`, `eligible`, `source`, plus `person_kind`/`person_key` — the reviewed registry row — and `hire_coach_id`, the coaches row the hire created, `2027_02_15_jc2a_source_ids.sql`; before that migration the journal held only the person's name, so a JC-2A award's `source_coach_id` stayed NULL rather than matching on a name). `staff_moves.role` widens to `VARCHAR(16)` with CHECK `HC/OC/DC/GM/AGM` so an executive hire can be recorded.
- **Scouting rows** (§3.3g) don't key on `draft_prospects.id`, which a board re-scan replaces: the older tables key on `prospect_key` = `draft_season:NAMEKEY:GROUP` (`engines/scouting_value.prospect_key`; the name upper-cased letters only, the mock draft's position group), which breaks on a rename, a group change or a same-name pair; it is now only the current alias of the permanent `prospect_uid` (`scout_prospect_ids`, §3.3g), which the V2.10 tables key on. `pipeline/load_save.py` allocates the coming class's permanent IDs and stores its prospects' native ratings on every load (`pipeline/prospect_ratings.store_prospect_ratings`, after `load_draft_class`; ID rows are the Draft-status players in the snapshot's `draft_class`, or all Draft-status players when it has none; CAREER-WEEK1: 389 prospects, all rated, no key collisions). `pipeline/load_capture.load_prospects` calls `scouting_engine.relink` after `write_board` (no-op before the class is initialized) and allocates the class's permanent prospect IDs (`prospect_ids.ensure_prospect_ids`, keyed by `prospect_key`, pgid NULL) — a scanned (PS5) class has no ratings, so `store_prospect_ratings` never runs.
- **`mock_draft_picks`**: `season` (league season of the order and needs), `week`, `pick`, `team_id` (FK `teams`), `prospect_id` (FK `draft_prospects` ON DELETE CASCADE, so a re-scanned board drops its old mocks), `locked` (bool), `selection_status`, `fit_score` (numeric), `rationale`, `generated_at`. PK `(season, week, pick)`. Written by `MockDraftEngine.save` (`pipeline/draft_board.save_mock`, replacing the week's earlier run).
- **Person lifecycle aliases (§2.10, §7.11):** board rows (`draft_prospects.id`) are only time-scoped `draft:<class>:<capture>` lifecycle bindings, never identity; prospects' immutable source is the pgid (save classes) or a reviewed supplier-ID sidecar (imported classes).

### 3.3d Contracts & Cap (`db/migrations/2026_12_07_contracts.sql`, docs/done/TEAM_MANAGEMENT_PLAN.md §2.1)
On PC, `team_cap_seasons` comes from the save on every load (`pipeline/load_save.py` `load_team_caps` populates it under `cap_season(snapshot, season)`, which is `season + 1` during OffSeason, with true $10k units converted to whole dollars; §1.1, §6.0b); on PS5 it is scanned from Manage Roster > TEAM SALARY once a season (the Season scan, after rosters) and kept current between scans from League Transactions (§3.3e; no automatic per-team re-scans; `--mode contracts --teams` re-scans by hand). **Money is `bigint` whole dollars** (`$16.8M` → 16800000), always parsed through `pipeline/money.parse_money`.
- **`team_cap_seasons`**: `team_id` (FK `teams`), `season`, `cap`, `rollover`, `adjusted_cap`, `cap_space` (can be negative), `salaries`, `cap_penalty`, `total_spend`, `next_rookie_reserve` (bigint, nullable), `scanned_at` (timestamptz), `capture_id` (FK `captures` ON DELETE SET NULL). PK `(team_id, season)`; the latest scan wins.
- **`player_contracts`**: `id` (SERIAL PK), `player_id` (FK `players`), `team_id` (FK `teams`), `season` (the league season it was scanned in), `length`, `years_remaining` (int), `total_value`, `bonus`, `cut_savings`, `cut_penalty` (bigint), `no_trade_clause` (bool, default false), `incentive` (text; the Team Salary table shows YES/NO: NO or NONE → NULL, YES → `'YES'`; the incentive's name is only on the player card), `status` (`ACTIVE` | `SUPERSEDED` | `RELEASED` | `TRADED`, default ACTIVE), `source` (`SCAN` | `TRANSACTION`, default SCAN), `scanned_at`, `capture_id`. Partial unique index `player_contracts_one_active (player_id, season) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'`; index `(team_id, season, status)`. **Re-scan semantics:** a team's new scan marks that team's earlier `ACTIVE` rows for the season (and any other ACTIVE row of a player it lists) `SUPERSEDED` and inserts fresh rows; rows are never otherwise updated in place, so history shows what changed. Step 2 marks `RELEASED` and inserts `source = 'TRANSACTION'` rows; step 3 marks `TRADED` when JR confirms a trade.
- **`player_contract_years`**: `contract_id` (FK ON DELETE CASCADE), `year` (calendar year, e.g. 2036), `cap_hit` (bigint, NOT NULL). PK `(contract_id, year)`. One row per year column on screen (five: season … season+4); a $0 year is stored as 0. The contract ends in `season + years_remaining − 1`, not where the first $0 falls.
- **V2 contract instruments** (`2027_01_14_v2_franchise_os.sql`): `player_contracts` gains `contract_type` (varchar(16), default `STANDARD`; STANDARD, ROOKIE, UDFA, FIFTH_YEAR_OPTION, FRANCHISE_EXCL, FRANCHISE_NONEXCL, TRANSITION, RFA_TENDER, ERFA_TENDER, MINIMUM), `guaranteed` (bigint, default 0), `signed_season`, `signed_week`, `last_restructure_season` (int), `drafted_round` (smallint, NULL = undrafted). The contracts engine (§2.17a) applies the same cut rule as `contract_values` when nothing is guaranteed.
- **`contract_offers`**: every free-agency, re-sign, extension, tender or UDFA offer, JR's or a CPU team's: `id`, `season`, `stage` (league office stage), `wave` (1–3 or NULL), `kind` (FREE_AGENT | RESIGN | EXTENSION | TENDER | UDFA), `player_id`, `team_id`, `from_user`, `years`, `total_value`, `bonus`, `guaranteed`, `utility` (numeric(6,4), NULL until scored), `status` (OPEN | ACCEPTED | REJECTED | COUNTERED | WITHDRAWN | EXPIRED), `counter` (JSONB), `seed`, `week` (`2027_02_18_contract_offer_week.sql`: the league week the offer was made in, read by the REPORTER's move window; NULL for a pre-migration row, which is out of window), `created_at`; index `(player_id, season, status)`. CPU free-agency offers are written by `transactions_engine.cpu_offers` (OPEN, from_user false).
- **`waiver_claims`**: `id`, `season`, `week`, `player_id`, `team_id`, `priority` (1 = worst record), `awarded`. Written by `transactions_engine.waivers`: one row per claimant, the lowest priority awarded.
- **View `vw_team_cap_sheet`**: one row per `ACTIVE` contract: `team_id`, `abbreviation`, `season`, `contract_id`, `player_id`, `player_name`, `position` (`player_seasons` for that season), `length`, `years_remaining`, `contract_end_season`, `total_value`, `bonus`, `cut_savings`, `cut_penalty`, `no_trade_clause`, `incentive`, `cap_hit_y0` … `cap_hit_y4` (years season … season+4), and the team's `cap`, `adjusted_cap`, `cap_space`, `total_spend`, `next_rookie_reserve` (LEFT JOIN `team_cap_seasons`). GM agents (step 3) and newsroom cap tools (step 5) read this view.

### 3.3e League Transactions (`db/migrations/2026_12_08_transactions.sql`, `docs/done/team_management/02_LEAGUE_TRANSACTIONS_PLAN.md`)
Madden's CPU signs and releases (master plan D1); Mu's trades are made by hand (D2/D3). The League > LEAGUE TRANSACTIONS list is scanned weekly and loaded here.
- **`transactions`**: `id` (SERIAL PK), `season`, `week` (games.week; NULL for preseason/offseason headings), `txn_date` (text, the cleaned heading, e.g. `2036 SEASON - WEEK 4`), `type` (`SIGNED` | `RELEASED` | `TRADED` | `RE_SIGNED` | `EXTENDED` | `RESTRUCTURED` (`2026_12_09_transactions_restructured.sql`) | `RETIRED` (`2027_01_03_player_season_ledger.sql`; allowed now, parsed in continuity plan phase 2b once the first offseason scan shows the wording) | `OTHER`), `player_id` (FK `players` ON DELETE SET NULL: a signed depth player can be deleted by the next roster scan), `player_name` (as the row spells it), `position`, `from_team_id` / `to_team_id` (FK `teams`; release/trade: from; signing/trade: to; re-sign/extension: to = his team), `contract_years`, `contract_value` (bigint dollars), `raw_text`, `row_key`, `seq`, `parse_ok`, `flags` (comma-separated), `applied` (bool, default true; false = history only), `trade_group`, `gm_proposal_id` (FK `gm_trade_proposals` ON DELETE SET NULL, added by `2026_12_10_gm_agents.sql`) (step 3 writes one `TRADED` row per leg of every confirmed trade: `trade_group = 'gm:<proposal>'`, `row_key = 'gm:<proposal>:<n>'` (no scanned key starts with `gm:`), `txn_date` `<season> SEASON - WEEK <n>` or `<season> OFFSEASON`, `raw_text` in the list's grammar, `capture_id` NULL; the scan skips trade rows), `capture_id` (FK `captures` ON DELETE SET NULL), `created_at`. `UNIQUE (season, txn_date, row_key, seq)`; indexes on `(season, week)`, `player_id`, `trade_group`.
  - **Key** (`pipeline/transactions_parse.py`): the list has no finer date than its heading and identical rows are legitimate, so `row_key` is built from the parsed fields (`type|team|to_team|pos|full_key(name)|years|amount`; trades: sorted leg keys), so two OCR readings of one row collide; an unparsed row's key is `raw:` + its folded text. One trade row becomes one transactions row per player/pick leg (`row_key` + `#P1`, `#A1`, …). `seq` counts equal `(heading, row_key)` rows from the oldest row of the heading group up, so it is stable when newer rows appear at the top.
  - **Headings**: `clean_heading` applies the week-label digit fixes (T/I/L→1, O→0); `heading_ordinal` = `(year, phase, week/stage)` with preseason < season < post season < offseason (offseason rows carry the year of the season just finished, JR 2026-10-19; offseason stages share one ordinal, so a `--since` in the offseason re-reads the offseason part of the list; in season the list only goes back to the season's start); `heading_week` gives games.week (postseason via `capture_matching.db_week`).
- **Load** (`pipeline/load_transactions.py`, called by `pipeline/load_capture.py` in its one DB transaction): rows are inserted `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; effects run only for rows inserted now, oldest first, so a reload changes nothing. Checks (any stops the load, nothing written): a heading year after the season, an unreadable heading, a parsed team missing from `teams`, a heading group with fewer rows than already stored (the scan missed rows). A `--since` scan that didn't reach the list's end drops rows older than `since` (its oldest group is partial; they were loaded before). Rows that aren't roster moves (`is_move`: no move verb and no `(POS) NAME`, e.g. the draft-class notice) are skipped, not stored, and listed in the report's `skipped_not_moves` (JR, 2026-10-19). Rows before `<season> SEASON - WEEK 1` are skipped, not stored (`skipped_before_week_1`; JR, 2026-10-19: the Week 1 roster already has every preseason move); the season's own offseason rows order later and are kept. With `--apply-from`, rows between Week 1 and that heading are stored `applied = false` with no effects.
  - **Effects** (players matched by full name, list name and position; several hits = ambiguous: `player_id` NULL, flag `ambiguous`, no move): `SIGNED` → resolve among this season's released players, then this season's rows, then players with no row this season (full name + position); none → create `players` (`player_name` "D. Taylor", `full_name` "Devonta Taylor") + `player_seasons`; `team_id` = new team, `released_week` NULL; with `player_contracts` present, an old ACTIVE row → SUPERSEDED and a `source = 'TRANSACTION'` ACTIVE row (length = years remaining = N, `total_value` = parse_money(amount), bonus/savings/penalty NULL, cap hits total/N for N years then 0, at least five year rows). `RELEASED` → `released_week` = the week (preseason 0, offseason 24), `team_id` kept; ACTIVE contract → RELEASED. Trade rows are skipped and listed in `skipped_trades` (JR, 2026-10-19: the GM agents' approval flow, step 3, moves the players and contracts when JR confirms a trade); with step 3's migration applied they are also stored in `gm_trade_sightings` and matched to confirmed trades (`record_sightings`, report key `trade_sightings`), never applied. `RESTRUCTURED` ("TEAM HAVE RESTRUCTURED THE CONTRACT OF (POS) NAME GENERATING $X IN ADDITIONAL CAP SPACE") → this season's cap hit − X, the deal's later years + X spread evenly (`projected`), team `salaries` − X. Practice-squad signings ("SIGN (POS) NAME TO THEIR PRACTICE SQUAD", flag `practice_squad`) move the player with no contract; "SIGNED FROM OTHER TEAM PRACTICE SQUAD …" is a normal signing. Releases and re-signs also match a player with no row this season by full name + position. Moves for a player with no ACTIVE contract are listed in `no_contract`. `RE_SIGNED` / `EXTENDED` → this season unchanged (D8): the ACTIVE contract gets `extension_years`, `extension_value`, `extended_transaction_id`, and `projected = true` year rows for the new deal, starting `season + years_remaining` (the season after the current deal ends), hits = amount × `year_shares(N)`. No Team Salary screen is re-scanned automatically (JR, 2026-10-19). Report: `transactions_seen`, `transactions_new`, `unparsed`, `ambiguous`, `created_players`, `not_applied`, `older_seasons`, `contract_ops`, `cap_deltas`, `no_contract`, `cap_rows_missing`, `apply_from`, `skipped_not_moves`, `skipped_trades`, `skipped_before_week_1`.
  - **Cap deltas** (`team_cap_seasons` for the season; a team with no row is listed in `cap_rows_missing`): a signing adds its season cap hit to `salaries`; a release removes the hit from `salaries` and adds the stored `cut_penalty` (NULL = 0) to `cap_penalty` as dead money. `total_spend` moves by the sum and `cap_space` by minus it, and the row gets `derived_at` / `derived_transaction_id` (derived when `derived_at` is later than `scanned_at`). The next Season scan overwrites everything.
  - **Re-signing shares** (`average_shares` / `year_shares` / `projected_hits`, pure): from the latest Season scan's ACTIVE `SCAN` contracts whose every year is visible (`years_remaining = length ≤ 5`), each length's average share of the total per year; fewer than 10 contracts of a length (or none) → an even split; rounding goes to the last year so the hits sum to the amount.
  - `load_roster` clears `released_week` for every player on a scanned roster (the roster scan stays authoritative).
  - **Experience carry-over** (`carry_experience`, after every load, idempotent): the `player_seasons` rows the effects create carry only team, position and release week, so a blank `years_of_experience` this season is filled from the player's previous-season card + 1 (0 = rookie). A player with no earlier card (a brand-new free agent) stays blank until the next roster scan; fantasy D/ST rows (`DEF`) are skipped. The report gets `experience_carried` (rows filled). The 2036 backfill filled 58 rows; 15 players and the 32 D/ST rows stayed blank.
- Columns on step 1's tables (same migration): `player_contracts.extension_years`, `extension_value` (bigint), `extended_transaction_id` (FK `transactions` ON DELETE SET NULL); `player_contract_years.projected` (bool, default false: a re-signing's projected hit, not read off the screen); `team_cap_seasons.derived_at` (timestamptz), `derived_transaction_id` (FK `transactions` ON DELETE SET NULL).
- `player_seasons.released_week` (§3.1).

### 3.3f Front Office: GM agents (`db/migrations/2026_12_10_gm_agents.sql`, `docs/done/team_management/03_GM_AGENTS_PLAN.md`)
Mu's GM agents decide trades (master plan D2): they propose, JR approves and makes them by hand in Madden, then confirms on `#debug`. Madden's CPU keeps signings and releases (D1).
- **`gm_profiles`**: one row per GM tenure (the `coach_tenures` shape): `id`, `team_id`, `gm_name`, `bio` (short, invented), `voice` (style notes for the rationale writer), `voice_card` JSONB (the GM's speech card: `register`, `samples`, `tics`, `avoids`, `wants`; `engines/gm_voices.py`, `2027_02_13_gm_voice_cards.sql`) and `voice_card_source` (`AUTHORED` | `LLM` | `TEMPLATE`), `bio_source` (`LLM` | `TEMPLATE`), `start_season` (invented, ≥ 2030), `first_draft_season` (`2026_12_18_gm_first_draft.sql`: the first class he picks; the launch GMs = `start_season`, a replacement seeded by `gm_personas.seed --replace` (by hand, after that year's draft) = season + 1, while a GM the coaching carousel hires for an emptied seat (`gm_rollover.fill_vacant_gms`) is hired after the Super Bowl and BEFORE that season's draft, so he runs it: = season; the draft score counts only classes from it on), `coach_id` (FK `coaches`, `2026_12_19_charles_grant_full_control.sql`: a head coach who also serves as GM, i.e. full control of football operations; NULL for a GM who is only a GM), `end_season` (NULL = current), `end_reason`, traits `risk_appetite`, `aggressiveness` (0–1), `pick_affinity` (0.6–1.4), `youth_bias` (−1 veterans … +1 youth), `position_bias` JSONB (`{group: multiplier}`, ≤ 3 groups, each within ±15%), `seed`, `created_at`. Partial unique index: one open tenure per team. Rows are never regenerated; replacing a GM closes the tenure and seeds a new row. **Coach-GMs:** Indianapolis gave Charles Grant (head coach, 2036–present) full control when it hired him (JR): Russell Finch's tenure (2031–2035) closes with that reason and Grant's GM tenure starts 2036 (`first_draft_season` 2036, the draft came after the hire; traits the seeded `replacement_traits('IND', 2036)` draw; bio and voice invented at JR's request, `bio_source` `LLM`). Marcus Whitfield (Panthers head coach, 2034–present) has also been Carolina's GM since 2034 (JR; `2026_12_20_marcus_whitfield_full_control.sql`): the seeded persona Bennett Thorne (2036) never held the job, so his row became Whitfield's in place (same id and seeded traits, `start_season` and `first_draft_season` 2034, new bio and voice). The offseason manifest (`newsroom/offseason_service.apply_coaching_moves`) doesn't create coach-GMs; one is recorded by hand.
  - **Seeding** (`engines/gm_personas.py`): traits are deterministic (`random.Random(sha256("gm:" + abbr))`) and stratified across the league (each trait's 32 strata dealt out by a seeded permutation; aggressiveness spans 0.12–0.88, so 9–10 GMs sit at ≥ 0.65 and 9–10 at ≤ 0.35; the plan's bound is 6–10). A replacement GM (`--replace`, seed `gm:<abbr>:<season>`) is redrawn until both bands still hold. Name, bio and voice: one Gemini call per GM (`engines/gm_llm.py`, label `gm_persona`) validated by `parse_persona` (2–3-word invented name not already used or the head coach's; no number but the start year; no claims about picks or trades), else the seeded name-pool template (last names unique across the league).
