Every new GM also gets a speech card: the authored `data/gm_voices_2026.json` card when the file covers the season, else the model's validated `voice_card`, else the deterministic trait template (`engines/gm_voices.template_card`; `template_card(..., role="COACH_GM")` for a Godfather coach-GM hire). `insert_gm` writes `voice_card` and `voice_card_source`; `backfill-bios` fills a missing card on a legacy row. Seeding and insertions invoke `ensure_gm_persona(cur, gm_id)` to ensure structured persona sliders (budget 30) and 3–5 role-weighted traits are seeded in `persona_sliders` and `persona_traits` (§3.3o).
- **Season rollover** (`engines/gm_rollover.py`, run by the Season scan's `step_preseason_engines` for the new season; `rollover_actions` is pure and returns only what's missing, so a re-run changes nothing): (1) the **automatic hot seat** (JR, sub-plan §7 Q4), once per finished season: `score = (expected wins for last season's direction (CONTEND 10.5, RETOOL 8.5, REBUILD 6) − wins)/3 + 0.5 (two straight seasons ≤ 6 wins) + 0.25 (4+ seasons in the job) − 1.5 · fo_score` (`FO_WEIGHT`; the front-office standing score from `fo_standing.live` over `scored_season(season)` — the newest season whose ratings card exists, which after the Super Bowl is the season just played, since `fo_quality` joins `player_seasons` for the season it scores and the coming season has no card yet — the GM's own drafting and player development, about ±0.45 points; `front_office_scores` runs it under a savepoint and a failure counts 0), stored on last season's row (`hot_seat_inputs` adds `fo_score`, `fo_rank`, `fo_points`) (`hot_seat_score`, `hot_seat_inputs`); a GM with ≥ 2 seasons, score ≥ 1.0 and a seeded draw under `min(0.9, 0.35 + 0.3·(score − 1))` is replaced, worst first, at most 4 a year, never on a team JR controls (his GMs are scored, so the seat can be warm, but never fired): his tenure closes (a coach-GM loses the GM job only and stays head coach, since head coaches change only through the coach hot seat (§2.19: a coach-GM is fired like any head coach, and `_vacate_gm_seat` then vacates the GM seat too, with his full-control HC contract settled) and the offseason manifest; `end_reason` adds "stays head coach") at the season just finished (`end_reason` "hot seat after …") and the opening's personnel-director candidates are gated by the team's enhanced opening appeal and scored by appeal and the owner's staff budget (`gm_rollover.gm_candidate_pool`/`gm_candidate_score`/`gm_search`: an ELITE (`$10.0M`), a STANDARD (`$5.75M`) and a first-time PROMOTION (`$2.75M`) candidate at `staff_contracts_engine.market_salary`, each with his tier's `GM_MIN_APPEAL` acceptance floor — ELITE `0.55`, STANDARD `0.35`, PROMOTION `0.0`; a candidate whose effective appeal (opening appeal plus `owner_policy.appeal_term`) is below his floor refuses, recording `{key, tier, reason: 'appeal', min_appeal, appeal}` in `declined`, and one whose willing salary exceeds the budget records `{key, tier, reason: 'budget', salary, budget}` instead; the score is stature plus `GM_APPEAL_WEIGHT` (ELITE `0.40`, STANDARD `0.20`, PROMOTION `0.05`) times surplus appeal above the floor plus `owner_policy.gm_hiring_key`; the highest score among the willing and affordable wins, else the cheapest willing candidate, else the cheapest candidate overall, so a PROMOTION is the fallback when higher tiers decline or exceed budget). The search report carries `effective_appeal` and `declined`, and `owner_hiring` applies the owner's terms to CPU teams only (`off`/`shadow`/`active`, §2.19 Owner wiring); the winner's persona is seeded (starting the new season, `first_draft_season` season + 1) and a GM `staff_contracts` row is written at his market salary); (2) the new season's `gm_team_seasons` rows with a preseason direction (`week 1`, `g = 0`: last season's wins and this season's `team_ovr`; when the new season's `team_seasons` rows aren't loaded yet the first engine run sets it) and needs (last season's still-open proposals expire first: the offseason is over); (3) `fo_quality` (+ inputs, at) carried forward from last season until step 4 writes it, except on a team that just replaced its GM (the new GM starts at the baseline 1.00, and step 4's recompute scores only his own tenure); (4) own picks seeded for the new third draft out (existing rows, i.e. traded picks, never touched); (5) every pick of a draft already held (`draft_season ≤` the new season) marked `used`.
- **`gm_offseason_state`**: `season` PK (the season just finished), `stage` (1–5, the last offseason stage the engine ran), `stage_run_at`, `proposals`.
- **`gm_team_settings`**: `team_id` PK, `user_controlled` (JR runs the team in Madden: its GM only advises), `suggestions_on` (JR can switch an advisory GM's suggestions off per team), `updated_at`. The migration seeds CAR and IND as user-controlled (JR, 2026-10-20). No row = CPU-run, suggestions on. The franchise registry's `user_teams` is the source of truth for which teams JR controls (V2.11 plan §2.10, D8): `front_office.controlled_team_ids(cur)` matches `current_database()` to a registry entry and maps its abbreviations to team ids (no entry or an unreadable registry → None; an entry with an empty list → no team is JR's, the 2026–2033 all-CPU era). `user_controlled` here is only the fallback for a database with no registry entry (tests, `madden_2036`); `set_team_control` refuses a `user_controlled` change with 409 on a registered franchise (`python3 -m db.franchises` is the way to change it) while `suggestions_on` still saves, and `front_office_state` reports control from the same overlay. `gm_trade_engine.read_books` calls `controlled_team_ids(cur)` after loading the settings and, when it isn't None, sets each team's `user_controlled` from it — so the registry also drives `open_negotiation`'s check, `eligible_team`, the `advisory:` flags, the engine CLI's Madden steps and the CPU-talk filter — while `suggestions_on` still comes from `gm_team_settings`.
- **`gm_team_seasons`**: PK `(team_id, season)`, `gm_id`, `direction` (`CONTEND` | `RETOOL` | `REBUILD`), `direction_score`, `direction_week`, `direction_inputs`, `needs` (ranked JSON), `needs_week`, `surplus`, `urgent_need` (injury trigger), step 4's `fo_quality` (NUMERIC(4,2), default 1.00, CHECK 0.5–1.6; step 3 never writes it after the default; `engines/fo_quality.recompute` writes it, §2.18), `fo_quality_inputs` (the scored picks with labels, H, H*, n, credit, streaks), `fo_quality_at`, `dev_quality` (NUMERIC(5,3), nullable: NULL = not scored), `dev_quality_inputs`, `dev_quality_at` (`2026_12_17_dev_quality.sql`; written by `engines/dev_quality.recompute`, §2.18), `hot_seat_score`, `hot_seat_inputs`, `updated_at`. Seeding creates the season's rows.
- **View `vw_gm_profiles`**: the open tenure per team with `league_state.current_season`'s `gm_team_seasons` row and `gm_team_settings` (`user_controlled`, `suggestions_on`): master §2.4's single "GM profile".
- **GM records across tenures** (`engines/gm_record.py`, read-only; writers' `get_gm_record`): `gm_record(cur, team_id, season)` takes the team's GM tenure covering `season`, every tenure in the league under the same `gm_name` (persona names are unique league-wide) and the team's earlier tenures (newest first), and sums each tenure's finished seasons (`team_season_results` rows with that `gm_id` and season < `season`). Pure `tenure_summary` / `tenure_facts` give team, role (GM, or head coach and GM with full control from `coach_id`), years (`2031–2035` / `2034–present`), `current`, `how_it_ended` (`end_reason`, closed tenures only), regular-season record, winning seasons, division titles (`division_place` 1), playoff trips, Super Bowl appearances, title seasons, best finish and a line per season ("2033: 14-3, lost in the Divisional round"); a tenure with no finished season says so. `gms_on_record_since` is the team's first season with a `gm_id` (GM tenures start 2030; NULL = no GM before the current one), and writers say nothing about who ran a team before it. Never a score (hot seat, q, D*). Tests: `tests/test_gm_record.py` (pure: totals and finishes, ties, titles and Super Bowls, no finished season, how a closed tenure ended, an open coach-GM tenure, no scores, the tool registered).
- **`draft_picks`**: PK `(draft_season, round, original_team_id, pick_suffix)` (`pick_suffix VARCHAR(4) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, `''` for every standard row; the comp expansion is in §3.3c), `owner_team_id`, `overall_pick` (step 4 fills it), `source` (`SEED` | `TRADE` | `JR` | `COMP` | `JC2A`), `acquired_proposal_id` (FK `gm_trade_proposals`), `used`. Seeded with every team owning its own picks for the next three drafts (C5: 2037–2039 from 2036; 672 rows); seeding never overwrites an existing row. JR corrects a CPU-era pick trade in the `#debug` table editor. The 24 CPU-era pick trades JR listed on 2026-10-20 (23 in 2037, one 2038 seventh) were loaded by `db/migrations/2026_12_11_draft_pick_owners.sql` (`source = 'JR'`; idempotent, stops if a listed pick is missing).
- **`gm_trade_proposals`**: `id`, `season`, `week` (`league_state.current_week` when made), `trade_window` (`IN_SEASON` | `OFFSEASON` | `DRAFT_DAY`; the plan's `window`, renamed because WINDOW is reserved), `trigger_kind` (`NEED` | `INJURY` | `SELL` | `DRAFT` | `USER`; the plan's `trigger`), `origin` (`ENGINE` | `USER`: a trade JR recorded or applied from a sighting), `expires_week`, `team_a_id` (initiator), `team_b_id`, `value_a` / `value_b` (each side's surplus Δ, dollars), `league_value_a` / `league_value_b` (neutral value each side receives), `cap_space_before_a/b`, `cap_space_after_a/b`, `dead_money_a/b`, `roster_after_a/b`, `cap_derived_a/b`, `legality` JSONB (`{check: {ok, detail}}`), `rationale_a`, `rationale_b`, `headline`, `rationale_source` (`LLM` | `TEMPLATE`), `status` (`PROPOSED` → `APPROVED` → `EXECUTED` | `REJECTED` | `EXPIRED` | `STALLED`; `STALLED` = a CPU talk broke down: decided for pacing, but its players are never barred the way a REJECTED player is), `status_reason`, `approved_at`, `executed_at`, `executed_as` (`PROPOSED` | `JR_EDITED` | `SIGHTING`), `rumor_ok` (step 5 may use a non-executed proposal as a rumor), `counts_for_pacing` (bool, default true; `2026_12_13_gm_pacing.sql`: false leaves a proposal out of the budget's `p_exec` and "already made this week" without deleting it; JR reset the week 4–5 proposals made under the old search, 2026-10-20), `flags` TEXT[] (`advisory:`, `negotiated:`, `talks:` / `auto_approved` (a CPU talk's outcome; an APPROVED `auto_approved` row is held out of the engine's stale expiry until the league office writes it or expires it after a second refusal, §2.17 Talks), `trade_request:`, `rescan:` / `projected_cap:`, `stage:`, `pick:`, `shape:`, `release:`, `llm_rejected:`), `deal_hash`, `created_at`. `UNIQUE (season, deal_hash)`, index `(season, status)`.
- **`gm_trade_assets`**: `id`, `proposal_id` (FK CASCADE), `from_team_id`, `to_team_id`, `asset_type` (`PLAYER` | `PICK`), `player_id`, `contract_id`, `pick_draft_season`, `pick_round`, `pick_original_team_id`, `cap_hit_now`, `value_from`, `value_to`, `value_league`.
- **`gm_trade_sightings`**: trade rows the League Transactions scan read (the loader never applies them): `id`, `season`, `txn_date`, `raw_text`, `parsed` JSONB, `capture_id`, `proposal_id` (FK SET NULL), `match_status` (`MATCHED` | `PARTIAL` | `UNMATCHED`), `created_at`; `UNIQUE (season, txn_date, raw_text)`.
- **`gm_trade_negotiations`** (`2026_12_21_gm_negotiations.sql`, extended by `2027_01_22_trade_talks.sql`): `id`, `season`, `week` (engine week when opened), `trade_window` (`IN_SEASON` | `OFFSEASON`), `offseason_stage`, `user_team_id` (JR's team; a CPU talk's initiator), `gm_team_id` (the other GM), `kind` (`USER` | `CPU`, default `USER`), `initiator_team_id` (CPU: the GM who called), `source_proposal_id` (FK `gm_trade_proposals` SET NULL: the row the talk produced), `carried_weeks` (default 0), `published_at` (set once an agreed CPU deal's transcript is published), `status` (`OPEN` → `AGREED` | `WALKED_AWAY` | `CLOSED` | `EXPIRED` | `STALLED`), `status_reason`, `patience` (a CPU talk: the initiator's), `patience_left` (a CPU talk: the other GM's), `proposal_id` (FK `gm_trade_proposals` SET NULL: the agreed or stalled deal), `trigger_kind` (`2027_02_05_trade_talk_trigger.sql`: the engine trigger a talk was opened from, so a carried talk's outcome proposal records it; NULL for a JR talk), `flags TEXT[]` (`2027_02_12_trade_talk_flags.sql`: the stored-path `shape:`/`stage:`/`release:` flags, so a carried talk's eventual proposal keeps them), `created_at`, `updated_at`; index `(season, status)`.
- **`gm_trade_negotiation_turns`**: `id`, `negotiation_id` (FK CASCADE), `turn_no` (UNIQUE per negotiation), `actor` (`JR` | `GM` | `GM_A`; `GM_A` = a CPU talk's initiating GM, `GM` the other), `action` (`OFFER` | `COUNTER` | `ACCEPT` | `REJECT` | `WALK_AWAY` | `CLOSE`), `actor_team_id`, `assets` JSONB (Front Office JSON legs), `options` JSONB (`[{key, action, assets, su, sg}]` the chooser saw; never public), `choice`, `choice_source` (`POLICY` | `JR`; `2027_02_16_choice_source_no_llm.sql` drops the pre-writer `LLM` value, since the writer only writes the words, never the move), `posture` (`FIRM` | `ANCHOR` | `SQUEEZE` | `MEET` | `HOLD`), `surplus_user`, `surplus_gm` (never shown to JR), `mood` (`CLOSE` | `APART` | `INSULTED`), `legality` JSONB, `message` (JR's note or the GM's reply), `message_source` (`JR` | `LLM` | `TEMPLATE`), `created_at`, `week` / `stage` (`2027_02_14_trade_turn_stop.sql`: the engine week and offseason stage the turn was actually played at; the talks' writer stamps them, and a pre-migration turn was backfilled with its talk's own week/stage).
- **`gm_trade_leaks`** (`2027_01_22_trade_talks.sql`): `id`, `negotiation_id` (FK CASCADE), `turn_no`, `season`, `week` (engine week of the leak), `leaker_team_id`, `stage` (`OPENED` | `CLOSE` | `STALLED`), `named_player_ids` INT[] (empty = positions only), `detail` JSONB (`{teams: [abbr, abbr], initiator: abbr, positions: [{pos, from, to}], picks}` — `initiator` is the initiating team's abbreviation, beside the two `teams`), `insider_key` (the writer who got it first), `created_at`; `UNIQUE (negotiation_id, turn_no)`; index `(season, week)`.
  - **Persona Integration (`engines/gm_trade_engine.py`, `engines/gm_negotiation.py`):** `read_books()` loads structured sliders and traits (§3.3o) into `b["gm"]["sliders"]` and `b["gm"]["traits"]`. In negotiation turns, `message_prompt()` incorporates GM disposition and active traits into LLM prompt context, and `template_message()` phrases GM dialogue to reflect aggressiveness, loyalty (`LOYAL`), and patience (`GRUDGE_HOLDER`, measured). Core trade mathematics, surplus evaluation, counter asset selection, and legality checks remain strictly deterministic.
  - **Inbox entry point (FRONT_OFFICE_INBOX_PLAN §2.21b, U4):** the `GM_TALK` kind drives the same `open_negotiation` / `offer` / `accept_counter` / `close` functions from an inbound `TRADE_INTEREST` (a PROPOSED `origin = 'ENGINE'` proposal) or a JR-started talk, and `front_office.reject` turns a proposal down. An agreed deal or a GM walk-away closes the inbox thread; the kind writes no trade itself and never exposes a surplus.
- FK `transactions.gm_proposal_id → gm_trade_proposals` (`transactions_gm_proposal_fk`, ON DELETE SET NULL) and `draft_picks.acquired_proposal_id → gm_trade_proposals` (`draft_picks_acquired_proposal_fk`).
- **Execution** (`pipeline/trade_moves.py`; the scan never moves a traded player, JR 2026-10-19, and every trade must move its players, JR 2026-10-20): `plan_trade_ops(proposal, state)` (pure) → `execute_trade(cur, ops, season)` in one DB transaction: one `TRADED` `transactions` row per leg (first, so the cap stamps can point at them); the pick leg upserts `draft_picks` on its full primary key `(draft_season, round, original_team_id, pick_suffix)` — the target must match the unique index exactly, and a three-column target made every traded pick fail on PostgreSQL after `2027_02_06` added `pick_suffix` (a traded seed pick is the `''` suffix row); `player_seasons.team_id` → the receiver (`released_week` cleared); the `ACTIVE` contract → `TRADED` and a row-for-row copy on the new team (`source = 'TRANSACTION'`, every `player_contract_years` row with its `projected` flag, the extension terms; `contracts.insert_contract`); both teams' `team_cap_seasons`: `salaries` ∓ this season's hit, the sender's `cap_penalty` + its `cut_penalty` (`TRADE_DEAD_MONEY`, C4), `total_spend` / `cap_space` to match, `derived_at` / `derived_transaction_id`; `draft_picks.owner_team_id` → the receiver (`source = 'TRADE'`, `acquired_proposal_id`); the proposal → `EXECUTED` with `executed_at` / `executed_as`. Warnings (player on another team in Mu, no contract, no cap row, unknown pick) never block: Madden is the truth once JR made the trade. The league office's `record_written` is the automatic path that runs the same `front_office._execute` for every trade a write carried (JR's TRADE pending moves with a `proposal_id`, and the engine's `auto_approved` deals): idempotent (an EXECUTED proposal is skipped), picks move in Mu's books only, and a CPU deal with a `talks:<nid>` flag has its transcript published.
- **How a trade gets confirmed** (`engines/front_office.py`, on `#debug`): **Made it** (`confirm`, an APPROVED proposal, or a PROPOSED/EXPIRED one JR made anyway; legality re-checked and reported, never blocking; executed_as `PROPOSED`); **Made a different trade** (`record` with the proposal's id: JR's legs replace its assets, `JR_EDITED`); **Record a trade** (`record` without one: a new `origin = 'USER'`, `trigger_kind = 'USER'` proposal, `JR_EDITED`, e.g. a Panthers/Colts deal before any scan sees it); **Apply this trade** (`apply_sighting`: the unmatched rows of the sighting's heading between the same two teams, merged into one trade, their parsed legs resolved by team + full name / list-name key and pick year/round, or JR's corrected legs → a USER proposal, `SIGHTING`, every one of those rows MATCHED). **Approve** re-checks legality (illegal now → EXPIRED and refused); **Reject** → REJECTED; **Couldn't make it** → EXPIRED with Madden's reason. The engine never applies an unmatched trade on its own. **The league office** is the automatic path: `record_written` executes each trade the write carried (JR's TRADE pending moves with a `proposal_id`, and APPROVED CPU deals with `auto_approved`); an ENGINE deal refused twice by the save planner is EXPIRED through `could_not_make` with "the league office couldn't make it".
- **Sightings and flags** (computed, never auto-edited): Madden logs a trade one row per asset (C8, seen week 5 of 2036: `PACKERS TRADE (FS) MIKE KEATON TO BENGALS`, `BENGALS TRADE 2037 ROUND 5 (155) DRAFT PICK TO PACKERS`), so `match_sightings` re-reads every row with the current grammar (refreshing `parsed` when it reads differently), groups a heading's rows by team pair (`sighting_group`, `merge_sightings`) and matches each group as one trade against EXECUTED proposals no other group has matched: same two teams, the same players (full-name keys) and the same picks (season, round, sender) → MATCHED, same teams and some players or picks → PARTIAL, else UNMATCHED; every row in the group gets that status and `proposal_id` (a group already all MATCHED is never downgraded; it sets only `match_status` / `proposal_id` / `parsed`). Two separate trades between the same teams under one heading would show as PARTIAL. `consistency_flags`: `unmatched_sighting` / `partial_sighting`, `not_yet_seen` (an EXECUTED trade with no MATCHED sighting after a later scanned transaction), `moved_since` (a traded player whose roster team or ACTIVE contract team isn't the receiver, unless he was traded again). C8 (the real wording of a trade row) is settled: one row per asset, `<GIVER> TRADE (POS) NAME TO <RECEIVER>` and `<GIVER> TRADE YYYY ROUND N (overall) DRAFT PICK TO <RECEIVER>`; `_parse_trade` and `pick_from_text` read both and the older guessed forms.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_trade_moves.py` (contract copy keeps every year and the projected flag, both cap rows move by the same hit, dead money follows the mode, pick ownership, one transactions row per leg, row keys can't collide with scan keys, warnings vs errors, execution order), `tests/test_front_office.py` (matcher: matched / partial / unmatched, one row per asset merged into one trade, pick text, flags and rumors are read-only, sightings only when the table exists, steps for a user-controlled team, `controlled_team_ids` for a registry entry / an empty list / no entry / an unreadable registry, `set_team_control`'s 409 on a registered franchise with `suggestions_on` still saving, the state overlay, leak rows joining `trade_rumors` without duplicating the talk's proposal, `executed_trades` quotes only for published talks), `tests/test_load_transactions.py` (trade rows → sightings only when the table exists).
- **Read helpers** (`engines/front_office.py`, the hand-off to steps 4 and 5; read-only): `get_gm(cur, team_id, season)`, `team_directions(cur, season)`, `draft_pick_owner(cur, draft_season, round, original_team_id)`, `trade_value(cur, season, team_id=None, player_id=None, pick=None)` (+ `player_value` / `pick_value` / `league_value` re-exported), `controlled_team_ids(cur)` (JR's teams from the franchise registry; None when this database has no entry), `executed_trades(cur, season, week=None)` (EXECUTED trades with legs: names, positions, OVR, picks; a proposal with a `talks:<nid>` flag for a published talk also carries `talk_id` and `talk_quotes`, up to 3 GM lines LLM-sourced first), `trade_rumors(cur, season, week)` (ENGINE proposals made by `week`, `rumor_ok`, never EXECUTED, plus one row per `gm_trade_leaks` row made by `week` when that table exists; a proposal rumor keeps an integer id, while a leak row carries `rumor_id: "leak:<id>"`, `source: "LEAK"`, `stage`, `insider_key` and `named` players — teams and asset types/positions only, a leak may name a player its leaker named but never as traded, no package, no cap figures, a leaked talk's proposal never duplicated, `status: "RUMOR"`), `deadline_summary(cur, season)` (buyers = CONTEND, sellers = REBUILD with top needs, RETOOL, executed trades by week), `legality_check(cur, season, week, team_a, team_b, assets)` (step 3's checks for any package), `front_office_state(cur, season)` (#debug; `user_controlled` from the registry overlay).

### 3.3g Scouting & draft (`db/migrations/2026_12_12_scouting.sql`, `docs/done/team_management/04_SCOUTING_AND_DRAFT_PLAN.md`, §2.18)
Mu's scouting layer for the draft class (league season + 1). **Hidden columns** (never in a view, writer tool or `#debug` panel, JR included): `scout_prospects.true_value`/`true_rank`/`value_inputs`, `scout_consensus.err`, `scout_events.impact`, every `scout_prospect_ratings` row, and every `scout_team_boards` row (shown only in the Draft Room's on-the-clock panel).
- **`scout_prospects`**: `id`, `draft_season`, `prospect_key` (§3.3c), `prospect_id` (FK `draft_prospects` ON DELETE SET NULL, re-linked after each board load), `true_value` NUMERIC(6,2), `true_rank`, `value_inputs` JSONB (`ovr`, `position`, `group`, `age`, `pv`, `age_adj`, `unrated`), `class_year`, `conference`, `first_step`, `status` (`ACTIVE` | `WITHDRAWN` | `DRAFTED` | `UDFA`), `seed` (sha256 of the key), `created_at`. `UNIQUE (draft_season, prospect_key)`. Written by `scouting_engine init` (from `draft_prospects`) and `relink` (re-link by key; a prospect missing from the new board → `WITHDRAWN`; a new one is added at the current step; true ranks recomputed).
- **`scout_runs`**: PK `(draft_season, step)` (1–27), `season`, `week`, `stage`, `params` JSONB (constants, code version), `n_events`, `created_at`. One row guards each stored step.
- **`scout_consensus`**: PK `(draft_season, step, prospect_key)`, `season`, `week`, `stage`, `grade` NUMERIC(5,1), `rank`, `round_label`, `delta_grade`, `delta_rank`, `err` (hidden), `event_ids` INT[]. FK `(draft_season, step) → scout_runs` ON DELETE CASCADE.
- **`scout_events`**: `id`, `draft_season`, `step`, `prospect_key`, `kind` (`GAME` | `STORYLINE` | `DECLARE` | `AWARD` | `ALL_STAR` | `COMBINE` | `PRO_DAY` | `VISIT` | `MEDICAL` | `BUZZ`), `team_id` (a `VISIT`'s team), `payload` JSONB (stat line, opponent, measurables; keys starting `_` are hidden), `impact` (hidden), `headline`, `blurb`, `text_source` (`LLM` | `TEMPLATE`), `seq`, `created_at`. `UNIQUE (draft_season, step, prospect_key, kind, seq)`; FK to `scout_runs` CASCADE.
- **`scout_team_boards`**: PK `(draft_season, step, team_id, prospect_key)`, `team_grade`, `team_rank`, `fit`, `bias`, `err` (hidden). Top 100 per team per step.
- **`scout_draft_picks`**: PK `(draft_season, overall_pick)` (1–32), `round`, `team_id` (owner on the clock), `original_team_id`, `prospect_key` (UNIQUE per class), `prospect_id`, `recommended_key`, `choice_source` (`GM` | `OFF_SCRIPT` | `JR_TEAM`), `alternatives` JSONB, `rationale`, `rationale_source`, `trade_proposal_id` (FK `gm_trade_proposals` SET NULL), `recorded_at`, `madden_match` (`MATCH` | `MISMATCH`), `madden_prospect_id`.
- **`draft_round_starts`** (`2027_01_02_draft_round_starts.sql`): PK `(draft_season, round)` (2–7), `started_at`, `proposals` (stored when the round started). One row per round JR started in the Draft Room, so a round with no proposals still counts.
- **V2.10 tables** (`db/migrations/2027_01_21_scouting_reports.sql`, also in `db/init_db.sql` after the inbox tables because `scout_interviews` references `inbox_threads`; docs/done/SCOUTING_REVAMP_PLAN.md §2.1, U1–U6 built):
  - **`scout_prospect_ids`**: `prospect_uid` UUID PK, `birth_key` UNIQUE, `draft_season`, `pgid` (NULL for a scanned class), `prospect_key` (current alias), `key_history` JSONB (`[{prospect_key, until_capture}]`), `status` (`OK` | `KEY_COLLISION`), `source_person_id` (set by the personality lifecycle plan), `first_seen` (capture folder), `created_at`; index `(draft_season, prospect_key)`. **Permanent prospect ID rule** (`engines/prospect_ids.py`): `prospect_uid = uuid5(MU_PROSPECT_NS, birth_key)`, birth key `save-pgid:<class>:<pgid>` for a save class or `board:<class>:<first prospect_key>` for a scanned class, written once and never recomputed. A save row matches its person by pgid (a rename or group change moves the alias and appends `key_history`), a scanned row by key; two rows of a class sharing a key are both `KEY_COLLISION` (no ratings, report or interview; back to `OK` when the key is unique again). `uid_for` resolves a current alias (OK only); `person_ref` returns `source_person_id` once set, else `prospect_uid`. The lifecycle plan adopts `prospect_uid` as `source_person_id` (or, allocating another UUID, writes it here and binds `scout-uid`/`prospect_uid` to it).
  - **`scout_prospect_ratings`** (hidden): `prospect_uid` PK (FK `scout_prospect_ids`), `draft_season`, `prospect_key` (alias at load), `pgid`, `ratings` JSONB (the save's native rating names without "Rating", 0–99, the same dict `player_attributes` stores), `capture_folder`, `loaded_at`. Upserted on every save load.
  - **`scout_reports`**: no primary key since `2027_02_11_scout_report_team_rows.sql`; two partial unique indexes instead — `scout_reports_dept_once` on `(prospect_uid, edition) WHERE team_id IS NULL` and `scout_reports_team_once` on `(prospect_uid, edition, team_id) WHERE team_id IS NOT NULL`. Columns: `draft_season`, `step` (FK `scout_runs` ON DELETE CASCADE), `prospect_key`, `edition` (`FALL` | `BOWLS` | `FINAL`), `grade`, `rank`, `round_label`, `role`, `traits` / `strengths` / `concerns` / `flags` / `body` JSONB, `text_source` (`TEMPLATE` | `LLM`), `scout_id` / `voice` / `team_id` (all NULL = the department row; `team_id` set = that team's private director-voiced row), `created_at`.
  - **`scout_interviews`**: `id`, `draft_season`, `team_id`, `prospect_uid`, `prospect_key`, `kind` (`COMBINE` | `VISIT`), `thread_id` (FK `inbox_threads` SET NULL), `window_step`, `logged_step`, `status` (`OPEN` | `CLOSED`), `questions_max`, `tone` (`STRONG` | `STEADY` | `MIXED`), `disposition_src` (`NEUTRAL` | `PERSONALITY`), `turns` JSONB, `summary_grade`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`; `UNIQUE (draft_season, team_id, prospect_uid, kind)`. Interviews are never personality evidence.
- **View `vw_scout_board_public`**: consensus rows + the prospect's name, position, college, height, weight, age, class year, conference, status and the step's top non-visit event headline. No `true_value`, `err`, `impact`, team boards or Madden OVR. Step 5 reads only this view and `engines/scouting_read.py`.
- **Lifecycle adoption of `prospect_uid`:** a save-class prospect's lifecycle `source_person_id` is his `prospect_uid`; an imported class's sidecar UUID differs, so `load_capture.class_personality` writes it to `scout_prospect_ids.source_person_id` (only when empty; a different one is a conflict) and binds the `scout-uid` alias, so `prospect_ids.person_ref` returns it. A KEY_COLLISION prospect has no unique `prospect_uid` and is not linked.

### 3.3h Season archive (`db/migrations/2026_12_24_season_archive.sql`, `engines/season_archive.py`, `docs/done/SEASON_CONTINUITY_PLAN.md` phase 1)
Each finished season from 2035, frozen once its Super Bowl is `COMPLETED`. Everything is computed from `games`, never read off a Madden screen. 2026–2034 live in the same tables as generated history (`source = 'SYNTH'`, §3.3j); the archive writes `source = 'CAPTURE'` and **never writes over a season with SYNTH rows**, `--replace` included (`history_season`; status `history`; continuity plan D9). With-team coach records count from 2026 over both sources (`coach_profile.RECORDS_FROM`, JR 2026-10-27: the 2026–2034 per-coach totals are exact, so the wins aren't synthetic).
- **`league_seasons`**: `season` PK, `champion_team_id`, `runner_up_team_id`, `super_bowl_game_id`, `regular_season_games`, `postseason_games`, `notes` (problems found, e.g. a team with fewer than 17 games), `finalized_at`, `source` (`CAPTURE`; `SYNTH` for the generated 2026–2034 rows, §3.3j; `team_season_results` and `coach_season_lines` carry the same column).
- **`team_season_results`** (`season`, `team_id`) PK: `wins`, `losses`, `ties`, `points_for`, `points_against`, `division_place` 1–4 with `division_tiebreak` (the rule that put it above a team with the same record: head-to-head, division record, common games, conference record, strength of victory, strength of schedule, net points; `UNBROKEN` when none did, listed by abbreviation), `conference_seed` 1–7 (NULL = out), `playoff_result` (`MISSED` | `WILD_CARD` | `DIVISIONAL` | `CONFERENCE` | `SUPER_BOWL_LOSS` | `CHAMPION`), `playoff_wins`, `playoff_losses`, `head_coach_id`, `gm_id`.
  - **Tiebreakers** (`break_tie`): each pass finds the single best team; a step that narrows the group restarts from step 1 with the leaders (the NFL rule). A conference head-to-head counts only when every tied team played every other; conference common games need 4.
  - **Seeds** come from the bracket, exactly: the conference's Divisional-round team with no Wild Card game is #1, the Wild Card home teams are 2–4 (ordered by record and the conference tiebreakers) and each one's opponent is 9 − its seed. A bracket of any other shape gets no seeds and a problem note.
- **`coach_season_lines`** (`coach_id`, `team_id`, `season`) PK: the head coach's regular-season W-L-T, `games`, playoff W-L and `playoff_result` (one coach per team per season).
- **`coach_seasons`** (existing career snapshots) gets the season's row: the coach's previous snapshot + every season since (`coach_profile.accumulate`; refused with a note when a season in between isn't fully on record). New column `mu_era_only`: a coach with no earlier snapshot (a carousel hire) starts at zero and his earlier career is never filled in. `coach_records` is unchanged by a new snapshot (it is still the latest snapshot + later games).
- **Fresh-database baseline:** a fresh franchise database has no `coach_seasons` rows, so without a baseline every head coach would start at zero (`mu_era_only`). `python3 -m engines.nfl_history coach-baseline --db <db> --apply` (also part of `init`, §3.3x) writes one row per head coach with an open tenure for season 2025, `team_id` NULL: his real career W-L-T, winning seasons (full seasons with W > L), playoff and Super Bowl W-L from `nfl_coach_seasons`; first-time head coaches get a zero row. It must run before the first archive and refuses, naming them, when a coach already has a row after 2025 (then rerun `season_archive --replace`).
- **Run:** the weekly run's Step 7d, `step_season_archive`, before the coaching carousel, in weekly, playoff and postgame runs, for league_state's season and the one before; a season already archived is skipped (`--replace` rewrites it). Skipped without the migration; a failure only warns. Migration applied 2026-10-26 after a backup (`madden_backup_20261026_133350.sql`); 2035 backfilled (champion CAR, 32 coach lines and snapshots; `coach_records` checked unchanged for all 32 coaches).
- **Tests:** `tests/test_season_archive.py` (standings and ties, playoff games not counted, head-to-head, `UNBROKEN`, three-way narrowing, seeds from a synthetic bracket and a missing bracket's note, playoff lines, the Super Bowl required; live read-only: 2035's champion, 272 + 13 games, seeds 1–7 in both conferences, every Wild Card pairing summing to 9, a 2035 coach snapshot from 2034, a SYNTH season refused with `--replace` and its rows unchanged, and a 2035 re-archive writing only `CAPTURE` rows); `tests/test_coach_profile.py` `WithTeamRecordTests` (lines then current games, ties, a missing finished season is unknown, a season from its full games without a line, a line winning over partial games). The weekly-run tests stub `step_season_archive`.

### 3.3i Career totals (`db/migrations/2026_12_26_player_career_totals.sql`, `2026_12_27_career_fit_fixes.sql`, `pipeline/load_career_totals.py`, `engines/history_backfill/remainder.py`, `docs/done/HISTORY_BACKFILL_PLAN.md` phase 1)

**[OBSOLETE_FRESH_SAVE, marked for deletion: AUDIT_LEDGER.md §3b]** Mu's 2026–2036 history is discarded for the fresh 2034 save; these tables stay only in `madden_2036`.
Madden's Career Stats lists, the input the 2026–2034 history backfill spreads over generated seasons. A career line holds a veteran's real NFL stats through 2025, every season since and the current season so far (JR, 2026-10-26); the lists show active players only.
- **`player_career_totals`**: `id`, `captured_season`, `captured_week`, `capture_folder`, `category` (passing, rushing, receiving, defense, kicking, punting, kickreturn, puntreturn, blocking), `player_id` (FK `players`, NULL when the row couldn't be settled), `list_name`, `position`, `stats` JSONB (the list's columns in `season_stat_lines` names, plus `games_played` from GP), `flags` (`team_list`, `unmatched`, `ambiguous`, `below_season_total`, `misread_copy`, `moved_team`, `name_slip`), `loaded_at`. Unique per (`captured_season`, `category`, `player_id`) where `player_id` is set. A reload of a captured season replaces that season's rows per category.
- **Matching** (`pipeline/load_career_totals.py`): team-by-team rows (`career_scope_<team>_<cat>.csv`) by list name key + position + team, then the league-wide rows by name key + position against the season's roster, skipping rows already settled. Players sharing a name and position are settled by their season lines (`fits`: no counting stat below the season total; `settle`: exactly one assignment). Rows still unmatched after every exact match get a second pass (unique, untaken, `fits`): a team-list row whose player is stored on another team (`moved_team`: same name key + position on any team; the career list shows his current team), then one OCR slip in the name (`name_slip`, `one_slip`: same position, and the same team for a team-list row). Nothing is guessed. The report lists, per category, the players with a season line but no career row; a cut-off category without team lists gets a warning naming the `--only career-teams --category` capture.
- **Remainders** (`engines/history_backfill/remainder.py`; reads only): per player and counting stat, mu = career − captured seasons 2035..S (`season_stat_lines`) − real NFL through 2025 (`data/history/nfl_careers_through_2025.csv`), and generate = mu − stored 2026–2034 `season_stats` canon rows; open seasons max(2026, first season)..2034. Only the columns the player's career rows carry are subtracted (no row in a category is unknown, not zero), and games played are left out (Madden's career GP isn't comparable to season games: 16 career against 15 + 16 captured). Flags `negative`, `no_open_seasons` (on the first load these were mostly 2035/2036 players whose captured season line is empty because they fell below the 250-row season lists: the leftover is that uncaptured season), `missing_pre2026`, `untracked_pre2026` (stats nflverse lacks, e.g. broken tackles, YAC, sacks allowed). Players with a captured line but no career row are split into rostered in S and no longer rostered (gone before the capture). Career Stats lists carry players on a Madden roster only, so a rostered player with no row is almost always a Madden free agent (the report shows `released_week` where we have the release); his 2026–2034 share is unconstrained, like a retired player's. Writes `verify_output/history_remainders_<S>.csv` and `.md`.
- **Fixes from the first load** (`2026_12_27_career_fit_fixes.sql`): C. Alonso's 2035 receiving line was J. Alonso's row read as "C.Alonso" in the Week 18 capture (a fake one-game +16 catches, +27 yards); his line is back to 9-46, the Week 18 game line's receiving is zeroed and the 16-catch game is out of `league_record_entries`. K. Franklin's seeded 2032–2033 Panthers lines are reshaped so 2032–2034 sum exactly to his career minus 2035–2036 (481-2,291-23 rushing, 96-682-4 receiving; 2034, which has game lines, unchanged). N. Bayless's 2036 position `OB` → QB.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_history_career.py` (pure: fits, settle, matching with and without team lists, the moved-team and name-slip pass, games played, remainder subtraction, columns without a career row, flags).

### 3.3j Team arc 2026–2034 (`db/migrations/2026_12_28_history_team_arc.sql`, `engines/history_backfill/team_arc.py`, `docs/done/HISTORY_BACKFILL_PLAN.md` phase 2)

**[OBSOLETE_FRESH_SAVE, marked for deletion: AUDIT_LEDGER.md §3b]** Mu's 2026–2036 history is discarded for the fresh 2034 save; these tables stay only in `madden_2036`.
Generated standings, playoffs, points and coach lines for 2026–2034, written into the §3.3h tables with `source = 'SYNTH'` only when JR applies a candidate.
- **Facts** (`load_facts`, `derive`; any problem stops `generate`): each coach's 2025 → 2034 `coach_seasons` difference is his 9-season W-L, winning seasons (W > L), playoff W-L and Super Bowl W-L (every team had one coach for 2026–2034 except Carolina). The one coach with no 2034 snapshot (Canales, CAR 2026–2033) takes the league's remainder: 26-110 with no playoff games, so Carolina 2026–2030 is 18-67. Adjustments: Bowles (TB) −1 loss and +4 winning seasons (`BOWLES`: his difference is 154 games, and Madden's 2025 baseline lists no winning seasons, so all 5 by 2034 are 2026–2034); Leonard (KC) started 0-0 and his 153 games are all nine seasons, so his 1 winning season is exact; the AFC's differences give 64 playoff trips against 63, so one AFC coach with a real pre-2026 record carries one playoff loss his stored 2025 row lacks (the solver picks him, the report names him; `"playoff_loss_offset": ["HOU"]` in `data/history/pins.json` pins him). Stored games: each playoff game fixes that round's meeting and winner (the Super Bowls, Carolina's 2034 Divisional and Conference wins), a team with all 17 regular-season games stored has its record and points from them (Carolina 2034: 13-4, 535-347), other stored games bound wins and losses. `CANON` (Panthers Full History.pdf): Carolina 0-17 in 2031 (alone at the bottom), 4-13 in 2032 and 2033 (tied for the worst record), the 2034 1 seed, no playoffs and at most 8 wins 2026–2030; Chicago the No. 1 offense 2029–2033 (most points). Pins: `{"team_seasons": [{"team": "CHI", "season": 2029, "wins": 11, "playoffs": true}]}`.
- **Model** (`build`, `solve`; OR-Tools CP-SAT, 8 workers, 1% gap, `--time-limit` per candidate; CBC through PuLP couldn't find a feasible point): per team-season wins, a winning-season flag, a playoff flag, a seed 1–7 and a round flag (lost in the Wild Card / Divisional / Conference round, or won the conference). Seeds 1–4 are division winners (the division's most wins), ordered by wins; 5–7 the rest, ordered, with at least as many wins as any conference team that missed; ties are allowed. The bracket holds by seed: one Wild Card loser in each of 2v7, 3v6, 4v5; in the Divisional round exactly one loser between the 1 seed and the lowest seed left; playoff wins follow from the round flag and the bye. Objective (tenths of a win): distance from a strength arc per team (`default_targets`: an AR(1) path, stationary SD 3.0 wins and year-to-year correlation 0.65, from the 2026 projection stretched ×1.2 to outcome spread, bent to land on the real 2035 record (the AR(1) bridge), shifted to each coach's total; each candidate's seed draws different arcs), zig-zags (second differences, 0.25 a win) over steady change (0.05), a spread term (about five 12+ win and five 5- win teams a season, as in 2035, 3 per missing team; at most about 11 teams at 8-9, 2 per extra team), and soft story terms (COTY and MVP teams win 11+ and make the playoffs, COTY teams improve by 3+, Super Bowl teams win 11+ (2 per win short), playoff teams win 9+, Chicago 2029–2033 wins 10+). `_diff` works around OR-Tools 9.12's `AddAbsEquality`, which mishandles an expression with a constant offset.
- **Rows** (`finish`): playoff results and wins from the round flags; division places by wins with ties `division_tiebreak = 'GENERATED'`; points: differential 31.5 × (W − 8.5) + noise (σ 35), points for at the season's league mean (383 in 2026 rising to 416 by 2035) + half the differential + noise (σ 28), each season balanced so points for = points against, stored-game points kept, Chicago 2029–2033 raised (with its points against, keeping the differential) above every other team; head coach from `coach_tenures`, GM from `gm_profiles` (NULL before a GM's first season).
- **`verify`** re-checks every fact on the rows without the solver (272 wins and 13 playoff games a season, seeds and ordering, a bracket that some outcome of the 64 produces, the Super Bowls, every coach total with the offset, stored games, canon, pins).
- **Staging and writes:** `generate` adds candidates (earlier ones stay, so a liked candidate is never lost; the report shows the run's own): `history_candidates` (`seed`, `objective`, `solver_status`, `pins`, `report` with verify's problems and the offset, `applied_at`) and `history_team_seasons` (a candidate's rows in `team_season_results`' shape). `apply --candidate N` refuses a candidate with problems or any non-SYNTH 2026–2034 row, then in one transaction replaces the SYNTH rows: `league_seasons` (champion and runner-up, the stored Super Bowl game, 272 + 13 games), `team_season_results`, `coach_season_lines`. `revert` deletes every SYNTH row. Applied 2026-10-26: JR picked candidate 14 (backup `madden_backup_20261026_193605.sql`); 9 + 288 + 288 SYNTH rows for 2026–2034, with the AFC's extra playoff loss on Houston. Nothing reads these seasons yet (phase 4); the season archive only touches 2035 on.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_history_team_arc.py` (pure: the 64 outcomes and reseeding, `bracket_ok`, `derive` on a synthetic league built from a known history (clean, bad totals, an extra playoff trip, an adjustment), a two-season solve that `verify` passes with a canon record and balanced points, an impossible pin reported infeasible).

### 3.3k Player lines 2026–2034 (`db/migrations/2026_12_29_history_player_lines.sql`, `2026_12_29_franklin_2032_record.sql`, `2026_12_30_history_player_rows.sql`, `engines/history_backfill/cast.py`, `team_totals.py`, `player_lines.py`, `fillins.py`, `players.py`, `docs/done/HISTORY_BACKFILL_PLAN.md` phase 3)

**[OBSOLETE_FRESH_SAVE, marked for deletion: AUDIT_LEDGER.md §3b]** Mu's 2026–2036 history is discarded for the fresh 2034 save; these tables stay only in `madden_2036`.
Season lines for everyone who played 2026–2034. Run 19 is applied (2026-10-26, after backup `madden_backup_20261026_210047.sql`; it replaced runs 6, 10, 11, 13, 16, 17, 18).
- **Cast** (`cast.py`): *pool* players (2035 or 2036 rosters; seasons from `season − years_of_experience` to 2034; team = 2035 team, the real 2026 team in 2026, and any team an award or record-book entry names that season, moving halfway between known teams) and *vets* (real 2026 roster players outside the pool: they retired during 2026–2034; last season drawn from age and position, `CAREER_END` ± 2, later for a productive 2025, never before a season an award or record names them; long snappers skipped). A record holder only matches a player whose group can hold the stat (`record_groups`); one nobody can be becomes a named fill-in (Bayo Ojulari, a second Josh Perez).
- **Team totals** (`team_totals.py`): every stat a least-squares line on points for and against, fitted to the 64 captured 2035–2036 team-seasons, drawn for the applied team arc with residual noise; receptions / receiving yards / TDs mirror passing, sacks allowed mirror sacks taken, each season's interceptions and sacks made are scaled to those thrown and taken.
- **Lines** (`player_lines.py`): within a team-season, members are ranked in their group by quality (talent from 2035 overall and dev trait, or a vet's 2025 production; an age curve with group peaks; a rookie ramp) and each stat family's total is split by group (`STAT_GROUPS`) and rank (`RANK_SHARES`, calibrated to 2035–2036 team concentration: the starting QB 97%, the top back 66%, receivers 41/30/16%; JR 2026-10-26, after the first shares left too few big seasons). *Constrained* players (pool players with a remainder, §3.3i) get each stat's remainder spread over their seasons by those shares (`allocate`: record-book pins first, game-record floors as pins when short, made stats capped by tries, exact integer sums); a seeded canon row's non-zero columns are kept and its zeros count as unknown; a remainder with no season left but a canon one is added to that row (listed as a canon adjustment: Crawford's 2034 attempts 540 → 614, completions 340 → 392). *Free* players (vets, and pool players who left after 2035 and so have no career row) split what's left of the team total by their shares, capped at 1.4× (`VET_CAP`). Records: no season that isn't a record-book entry reaches the current NFL top 10 or a franchise record as it stood that season (rookie categories for rookie seasons); a constrained player's excess moves to his other seasons. Awards: MVP / OPOY seasons top 3 at the position, DPOY top 3 in sacks, tackles or interceptions (taken from his other seasons); OROY / DROY must be rookie seasons; records outrank awards (a second ceiling pass). Free lines are made consistent (completions ≤ attempts, YAC / run after catch / net punting ≤ their yards); games played by role (a starter 14–17).
- **Fill-ins** (`fillins.py`): a team-season leftover of at least 60% of a starter's season in a family's key stat (QB 3,900 passing yards, HB 1,000 rushing, WR 950 receiving, edge 9 sacks, CB 10 deflections, LB 70 solo tackles, K 24 FGs, P 65 punts) becomes a fill-in, taking up to 1.2 starters' seasons (`FILL_CAP`); consecutive seasons are one career; names mix real first and last names but never a real pair or an existing name; offensive-line leftovers stay unassigned.
- **Run** (`players.py`, `validate`): every constrained sum, pin, ceiling and rookie award re-checked; staged as `history_player_runs` (`seed`, `team_arc_candidate`, `report` with problems and counts), `history_players` (`key` p&lt;id&gt; / e&lt;espn id&gt; / f&lt;n&gt;, `kind` pool / vet / fillin) and `history_player_lines` (team, position, age, experience, `stats` JSONB in `season_stat_lines` names plus `games_played`); `verify_output/history_player_lines.md` lists counts, each season's leaders and the fill-ins by team. Run 6 (2026-10-26): 3,293 players (1,418 pool, 1,805 vets, 70 fill-ins), 14,841 lines, about 1,600–1,800 a season; the only problems are the twelve tiny negative remainders and the Crawford canon adjustment.
- **Apply** (`apply-players --run N`, `apply_run`, one transaction; refuses a run with problems other than zero-counted negatives and canon adjustments, or when SYNTH player rows exist): creates `players` rows for vets (`origin = 'HISTORY'`) and fill-ins (`'HISTORY_FILLIN'`); writes `player_seasons`, `season_stats` (offense, with the rates `derived()` computes; a second teammate with the same list name, team and position gets his full name for the unique key) and `season_stat_defense` / `_kicking` / `_punting` / `_kickreturn` / `_puntreturn` / `_blocking` / `_general`, all `source = 'SYNTH'`. A canon `season_stats` row (the seeded Panthers lines) is updated in place, only in its unstated columns and the canon adjustments, with the old values kept in the run's report. `revert-players` restores those, deletes every SYNTH player row and the players with an origin. Migration `2026_12_30_history_player_rows.sql`: `source` (default `CAPTURE`) on `player_seasons`, `season_stats` and the seven side tables, `players.origin`, and `season_stat_lines` exposes `ps.source`. Run 19 wrote 14,245 player-seasons, 4,386 `season_stats` rows, 7,922 defense, 323 kicking, 318 punting, 1,957 kick-return, 1,807 punt-return, 1,885 blocking rows and 8 canon updates; afterwards every 2026–2034 career remainder (§3.3i, `include_synth=True`) is zero apart from the twelve tiny negatives and the `no_open_seasons` leftovers (uncaptured 2035–2036 lines).
- **Readers** (audit 2026-10-26: every read of `player_seasons`, `season_stats` and `season_stat_*` across seasons, and every name lookup on `players`). Phase 4 turned history on where it belongs: the player page's career rows and totals, the team History tab and the writer tools `get_player_career` / `get_team_history` (§3.3l). Name lookups prefer today's players over a backfilled namesake (`ORDER BY origin IS NOT NULL`: `server/api.py` player search, the `newsroom/db_tools.py` resolvers, `newsroom/agent_memory.py`, the `newsroom/swarm_dispatcher.py` name list). Still skipping SYNTH rows: the site's season list (`player_seasons` part; 2026–2034 already appear from the stored Super Bowls and Panthers seasons), `newsroom/social_desk.py` tenure counts, `engines/napper_trade_engine.py`'s position fallback; `pipeline/heal_roster.py` skips backfilled players. Every other read is scoped to one season (league_state's) and can't see 2026–2034.
- **Awards and record-book links** (`link_facts`, run on apply and by `link-facts`): every 2026–2034 award and record-book row with a name and no `player_id` points at the player with that full name who played that season (on the row's team when it names one); 177 rows (only Coach of the Year rows stay coach-only). Kept in the run's report; `revert-players` unlinks them first (`awards.player_id` blocks deleting a referenced player).
- **Stat dependencies** (`CAPPED_BY`, `NEEDS`, `support_pins`): a constrained player's TDs, interceptions and completions are capped per season by their attempts or catches and his yards go only to seasons with an attempt or catch (the exact sum wins if they can't fit, listed); a free line is zeroed or capped the same way, and a pinned record season gets the attempts or catches behind it, up to their own record ceiling. Generation reads only non-SYNTH rows (`remainder.build(include_synth=False)`; the post-apply check passes `True`). Run 10 (replacing run 6, whose 99 lines had yards without carries or TDs above catches) had no impossible combinations; run 11 (applied 2026-10-26, steeper depth shares) per season: 10–18 4,000-yard passers (2035–36: 18.5), 13–27 1,000-yard rushers (22.5), 22 1,000-yard receivers in 2026 rising to 34–41 by 2030–2034 (43.5), the starting QB 94% of team passing (96%), the top three receivers 66% of team receiving (72%); single-season receiving TDs stay under today's NFL top 10 by design; a few vets' ratios still run odd (2% of 1,500-yard passer seasons by yards per TD, against 1.5% captured), because a free player's stats are each a share of what's left of the team total. A revert and re-apply gives the history players new ids.
- **Franklin:** `2026_12_29_franklin_2032_record.sql` puts his 2032 line back to the record book's 1,016 yards (190-1,016-8) and takes the earlier trim from 2034 (180-680-5).
- **Tests:** `tests/test_history_player_lines.py` (pure: team paths, the cast with a namesake record, team-total fits and identities, `split_exact` / `split_capped` / `allocate`, `consistent`, a generate with exact remainders and vets filling, pins and ceilings, capped fill-in careers).
