- **Season-picker pages** (`is_history_season`: a season before 2035 with SYNTH `team_season_results`): `GET /api/standings/{season}` returns `history_standings` (record, points, `divisionPlace`, `seed`, `playoffResult`, `isHistory: true`; splits, streak and last five `None`; the game-based standings now count regular-season games only, so 2035 no longer adds playoff games); `GET /api/stats/player` passing / rushing / receiving / scoring come from the season lines (`history_offense_leaders`; defense and special teams already read `season_stat_lines`); `GET /api/stats/team` sums the season lines by team with points from `team_season_results` (`history_team_stats`; depth players who weren't tracked are missing); postseason and situational stats are empty. The Standings page shows "—" for splits, orders tied records by the generated division place, marks seeds (🏆 for the champion) and a "hist" note; the Stats page adds the note for any season before 2035; the Standings masthead names the selected year.
- **Generator fixes found through these pages (runs 13–16):** free players fill each stat group as a block (`FREE_GROUPS`: one factor from the group's key stat, so their ratios are the team's); team totals draw attempts, completions, interceptions, TDs, punting, return and kicking yards as rates of their base (`team_totals.RATIOS`, from the 2035–2036 team-seasons: 50.7 yards a punt, 23.3 a kick return, 90% on field goals); a record holder ranks first in his group that season, and a free record season carries the rest of its line at 2035–2036 starter rates (`pin_line`: 6.95 yards an attempt, 61% completions, 4.7% TDs, 1% INTs); return, punting and interception yards need their base, and a free line's TFLs and tackles are at least its sacks. Run 16 against run 11: no sacks above tackles (134), interception yards without interceptions 0 (2,086), odd punting averages 0 (101 of 306), odd kick-return averages 0, field goals under 60% 9 kickers (27), odd 1,500-yard passer lines 14 of 296; offensive milestones unchanged.
- **Records check** (`python3 -m engines.history_backfill records-check`, `records_check`; read-only): `engines/records_engine.evaluate` over each history season against the record book as it stood before it; writes `verify_output/history_records_check.md`. It found two gaps the generator had: rushing + receiving TDs (the scrimmage-TD category) weren't capped, and fill-ins skipped the record caps (both fixed: `_scrimmage` trims the unpinned part to the scrimmage ceiling, moving a constrained player's excess to his other seasons; fill-in lines are capped in `players.run`). Run 19 found four franchise events the record book itself implied but didn't list; JR had them added as `BOOK` rows (`2027_01_01_record_book_implied.sql`, linked by `link-facts`): Washington's season receiving TDs, Evan Smith 18 (2029, his book rookie record beats the 12); the Raiders' and Jets' scrimmage TDs, Ashton Jeanty 18 (2032) and Ben Gore 15 (2034), as ties with Marcus Allen and Thomas Jones; Carolina's season points, the 2034 Panthers' 535 from the stored games (above 2015's 500). The check is now clean: no franchise record outside the book, no season in today's NFL top 10 outside the book, no book record the stats miss. The generator skips team records (no player holds them) and doesn't pin scrimmage TDs (no single line column; the ceilings and `_scrimmage` cover it). 4 seasons would have ranked in an NFL top 10 as the lists stood then but not today (the stored lists are today's, so a season pushed out later is consistent; 16 on run 18, before capped seasons stopped landing exactly on the cap).
- **Leader-range report** (`python3 -m engines.history_backfill leaders-report`, `leaders_report`; read-only): for each history season, the leader, top-10 average and per-team total of 14 stats and five milestone counts (4,000-yard passers, 1,000-yard rushers and receivers, 10-sack and 100-tackle seasons), each against the captured 2035–2036 range (`range_flag`: more than 10% outside it); writes `verify_output/history_leaders_report.md`. Run 18 (2026-10-26): 163 of 414 measures outside. Passing and receiving TD and receiving-yard leaders sit under the Madden era by design (the record caps keep them under today's NFL top 10); per-team sacks run above the captured range because the captured defense lines stop at 250 rows (the generated totals balance to sacks taken); passing, rushing and receiving volume per team is inside it. Run 18 showed five generator gaps, fixed in run 19 (131 measures outside): capped seasons piled up exactly at the cap (127 catches every season; `below_cap` now lands up to 4% under it, fixed per player-season); free players' small counts lost volume to rounding (each free group's total is now split exactly: defensive interceptions per team 3.8–4.6 → 4.9–6.5 against 5.4–5.9); returns now go to one primary returner (kick-return leaders 217–513 → 538–1,113 against 552–1,582); tackles and sacks concentrate on starters (`RANK_SHARES` for tackles and edge sacks; tackle top-10 average 123–153 → 138–155 against 148–154, 100-tackle seasons 8–42 → 31–45 against 78–82, 10-sack seasons 17–30 → 21–32); extreme seasons are held inside the captured era (team rates clamped to ±1.5 SD, `RATE_CLAMP`; soft caps at 105% of each stat's 2035–2036 season maximum, `_soft_caps`, moving a constrained player's excess to his other seasons: interceptions-thrown leaders 12–27 → 11–14 against 10–14, tackle leaders up to 216 → up to 185). Still outside by design or the capture: the capped passing / receiving TD and receiving-yard leaders, per-team sacks, 1,000-yard receivers rising from real-NFL levels; kick-return yards per team (243–452 against 403–573) and 100-tackle seasons stay below.
- **All-Pro teams 2026–2034** (`engines/history_backfill/all_pro.py`, `python3 -m engines.history_backfill all-pro [--dry-run]`; migration `2026_12_31_awards_source.sql` adds `awards.source`, default `CAPTURE`): First and Second Team for each history season in the stored 2035–2036 shape (31 slots each, `SLOTS`), picked from `season_stat_lines` by a score per slot (`SCORES`: yards and TDs for skill players, games and sacks allowed for linemen, sacks / TFL / tackles for the front, tackles plus big plays for linebackers and safeties, interceptions and deflections for corners, field goals and accuracy, net punting, return yards), the team's wins a small tiebreaker. MVP, OPOY and DPOY winners are First Team at their slot; AP is the best all-purpose yardage among players not already picked; SCB the next corner after the two picked; KR / PR may also hold a roster slot; LS is a long snapper active that season (a 2035–2036 one by experience, else a real 2026 one by name and team, no player link: 2026–2027); ST a backup linebacker, safety or corner. Stored as `awards` rows with `source = 'SYNTH'` (558 rows on 2026-10-26; every season's award winners First Team, no player in two roster slots); `apply-players` re-picks them (a re-apply gives the history players new ids) and `revert-players` deletes them first. `GET /api/awards/all-pro` and the Awards page's All-Pro season picker now run back to 2026; writers can cite them, and the popularity engine's Awards Equity counts them as past honors (older seasons at career weight). Report: `verify_output/history_all_pro.md`.
- **Done-when checks (2026-10-26):** Justin Herbert, the 2028 MVP (a real veteran who retired in the history), has a page with his MVP badge, nine "hist" seasons and career totals; the Titans' History tab lists 2026–2036 with Saleh's 2031 title and his two Coach of the Year seasons.

### 3.3m Player season ledger (`db/migrations/2027_01_03_player_season_ledger.sql`, `engines/season_ledger.py`, `docs/done/SEASON_CONTINUITY_PLAN.md` phase 2a)
Each player's fate between two **captured** seasons (2035 → 2036 on; 2026–2034 are generated history, plan D10). Retirements come from the save (Madden's, until league office phase F) or Project Mu's own decisions on the PC; the PS5 League Transactions source JR named on 2026-10-26 never runs because no PS5 offseason does (plan C1, C5). A player on last season's rosters who isn't on this season's and isn't recorded as retiring is a **free agent** (D1).
- **`player_season_transitions`** (`player_id` FK `ON DELETE CASCADE`, `to_season`) PK: `from_season`, `from_team_id` (team at the end of last season), `to_team_id` (team at the start of this one), `status` (`RETAINED` | `MOVED` | `RETIRED` | `FREE_AGENT` | `DRAFTED` | `NEW`), `source` (`TRADE` / `TRANSACTION` when an offseason League Transactions row explains a move, else `ROSTER_SCAN`; `DRAFT` for a draftee; `TRANSACTION` for an in-season arrival), ratings, development trait, age and experience before and after, `flags` (`retirement_scan_missing`: no retirements on record for that season yet, so a free agent may turn out to have retired; `released_in_season`; `signed_in_season:week N`; `undrafted_rookie`; `returned`; `no_prior_capture`: an experienced arrival no earlier captured roster lists, e.g. a depth player the 2035 roster capture missed).
  - **Start of a season** (`opening_team`): the team before the season's first in-season move: released or traded away → the team he left; re-signed / extended / restructured → his team; signed off his own practice squad → that team; any other signing → none (a free agent at the start, joined in Week N).
  - **Status** (`classify`, pure): same team → `RETAINED`; another → `MOVED`; no team at the start → `RETIRED` if `player_retirements` names him for the season he left, else `FREE_AGENT`; an arrival with no row last season → `DRAFTED` (experience 0 and a `draft_prospects` pick of that class) or `NEW`.
- **`player_retirements`** (`season` he retired after, `player_id` FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` or NULL with flags, `player_name`, `position`, `team_id`, `transaction_id`, `capture_id`) and **`players.retired_season`**: **filled by the loader (phase 2b, P1-26, 2026-11-09).** `pipeline/load_save.load_retirements` reads every Player row the snapshot exports with `ContractStatus = Retired` (the save is the retirement source, plan C1 as superseded; `transaction_id` stays NULL) and, once per `(season, player_id)`, writes a `player_retirements` row and `players.retired_season`; `retirement_season` uses the snapshot's own season in the offseason and one season earlier if the new preseason still shows him `Retired`. A later roster row or signing clears `players.retired_season` (D8), and the load report counts `retirements`. History players (`players.origin` `HISTORY` / `HISTORY_FILLIN`) are retired by their origin, never by these (D11).
- **Helpers:** `free_agent_pool(cur, season)` (last seen on a captured roster, none now or released this season, not retired, no history players; best rated first) and `career_path(cur, player_id)` (every season, generated ones marked `history`, the ledger status on arrival, and `now`: active, free agent, retired by retirement, or retired after his last history season).
- **Run:** the Season scan's `step_season_ledger`, after the Napper week 1 lineups and before the GM rollover; `build` rewrites one boundary, so a rerun after the loader's retirements (phase 2b, built 2026-11-09) turns flagged free agents into `RETIRED`.
- **2035 → 2036 (built 2026-10-27, after backup `madden_backup_20261027_035051.sql`):** 2,090 players: 1,277 retained, 133 moved (all `ROSTER_SCAN`: no 2035 offseason transactions were captured), 341 free agents (all `retirement_scan_missing`; 80 of them signed during 2036), 182 drafted, 157 new (13 undrafted rookies, 126 `no_prior_capture`). The 2036 free-agent pool holds 307 (the 261 who never returned plus 46 released in 2036); its top names (Abdul Carter 98, Will Anderson Jr 96, Jalon Walker 91) are more likely retirements or roster-capture gaps than unsigned players, which phase 2b's scan settles.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_season_ledger.py` (pure: opening teams, every status, D1 and its flag, in-season signings, arrivals; integration on `madden_test`: the 2036 boundary accounts for every captured player, no `RETIRED` without a scan, idempotent, 2035 refused as a history boundary, no history players in the pool, a history player's path ends retired).

### 3.3n Player Progression & Ceilings (`db/migrations/2027_01_08_player_progression.sql`, `engines/progression.py`, `docs/in_progress/PROGRESSION_PLAN.md`)
Offline progression history and latent development ceilings for all players across offseason boundaries (Item 11, V2.14).
- **`player_progression_history`**:
  - `season` (int), `player_id` (FK `players.id` ON DELETE CASCADE), `old_ovr` (int), `new_ovr` (int), `delta_ovr` (int), `age_term` (numeric), `dev_term` (numeric), `ceiling_term` (numeric), `play_term` (numeric), `injury_term` (numeric), `noise_term` (numeric), `league_term` (numeric: development + star term holding the 2036 league shape; 0 with --follow-madden), `performance_term` (numeric: last season's production rank + awards), `ratings_diff` (JSONB: rating → change, for changed ratings), `created_at` (timestamptz), `cause` (varchar(32): main cause tag, §2.21; `2027_01_11`). `id` SERIAL PK, `UNIQUE (season, player_id)` (re-runs upsert).
  - One row per player per run with `--commit`. From `2027_01_14` (V2 core U1; filled by the engine's C2 pass: `checkpoint` 'OFFSEASON', `dev_before`/`dev_after` (same until phase H; 'Superstar X-Factor' stored as 'X-Factor'), `group_changes` = rating points per group, `behaviour_changes` = {gained: [{flag, cause}], lost: [...]}; `player_ceilings`, `player_durability` and `player_mileage` written by `engines/progression.py --commit`): `checkpoint` (varchar(12), default `OFFSEASON`), `dev_before`, `dev_after`, `group_changes` (JSONB), `wear_term`, `upkeep_term`, `continuity_term`, `mentor_term` (numeric(6,3)), `persona_term`, `coach_term` (numeric(6,3), default 0: traits ship at 0), `behaviour_changes` (JSONB, `PT_*` gained or lost).
- **`player_ceilings`**:
  - `player_id` (PK, FK `players.id` ON DELETE CASCADE), `ceiling` (numeric(5,2), at most 99), `source` (varchar: `SCOUT_PROSPECT`, `SEEDED`, or `STORED` once reused), `updated_season` (int), `created_at` (timestamptz); from `2027_01_11`: `peak_mental` (JSONB: career-high Awareness and PlayRecognition, raised each run), `entry_mental` (JSONB: draft-day values, written once), `entry_source` (varchar(16): `ESTIMATED` from Madden's mean gain by years pro; the PC loader will write the save's `Original*Rating`).
  - From the prospect's `scout_prospects.true_value`, or seeded from OVR, age and dev trait (§2.21). Hidden.
- `player_ceilings` from `2027_01_14`: `floor`, `spread` (numeric(5,2)), `group_ceilings` (JSONB: physical, technical, mental).
- **Personality development attribution (PERSONALITY_DEVELOPMENT_COACHING_PLAN, no migration):** versioned private metadata inside existing `progression_events.metadata` (`personality_development_v1` on checkpoints, `annual_effect_included` on the offseason final); older receipts without it mean no recorded effect, never reconstructed history.
- **`player_durability`** (hidden): `player_id` (PK), `durability` (numeric(4,3), 0–1), `source`, `updated_season`.
- **`player_mileage`**: PK `(player_id, season)`; `touches`, `hits`, `snaps` (int), `wear` (numeric(6,2)).
- **`player_form`** (phase E, written by `engines/form_engine.py` each week): PK `(player_id, season, week)`; `form` (numeric(4,2), −3..3 OVR points), `overlay` (JSONB {RatingName: delta} on top of the base ratings; {} at form 0). A run replaces that week's rows, one per player with base ratings; `pipeline/drift_check.py` reads the newest row up to the week.
- Applied to `madden_2036` and `madden_test` (both migrations; 2026-10-29). `2027_01_14` applied to `madden_test` (2026-10-30).

- **Receipt-driven storage (`2027_01_15_progression_state.sql`, mirrored in init_db.sql):** `progression_player_state` stores one authoritative permanent base/band revision per player. `progression_events` preserves stable identity `(player, earned season, kind, ordinal, rules version)`, input fingerprint, prior revision, absolute candidate base/band, separate overlay, annual deltas, private provenance/evidence, PREPARED/APPLIED status, edits/output fingerprints and receipt times. `progression_annual_accounting` stores per-rating applied totals by player/earned season; fractional carry and immutable annual-start ratings are retained in applied-event metadata. `progression_evidence_consumption` uniquely records awarded game IDs by player/earned season/purpose. Legacy `player_progression_history` remains the compatible annual summary, not the checkpoint ledger. Only verified acknowledgement spends development; explicit savepoints/CAS protect whole-save batches without committing the caller's transaction. Migration validation uses isolated schemas on madden_test; no archive migration or live activation is implied.

### 3.3o League Memory Index (`db/migrations/2027_01_10_league_memory.sql`, `newsroom/league_memory.py`, docs/done/PRE_PC_WORK.md §9, docs/in_progress/V2_MASTER_PLAN.md V2.8)
Narrative search index over historical universe events (articles, writer takes, franchise records, league records) for authentic callbacks in newsroom writing. Works with PostgreSQL 14 without `pgvector` by storing embeddings as `REAL[]` and executing vectorized cosine similarity in Python/numpy (~30ms for 8,000 vectors).
- **`league_memory`**:
  - `id` (PK), `source_table` (varchar(32), e.g. `'news_feed'`, `'agent_memory_entries'`, `'franchise_records'`, `'league_record_entries'`), `source_id` (int), `season` (int, nullable), `week` (int, nullable), `team_ids` (`VARCHAR(8)[]`, array of team abbreviations e.g. `ARRAY['CAR']`), `player_ids` (`INT[]`), `text_chunk` (text), `embedding` (`REAL[]`, dimension 3072 for `gemini-embedding-001`), `model` (varchar(64)), `created_at` (timestamptz default `NOW()`). `UNIQUE (source_table, source_id)`.
  - Indexed on `(source_table, source_id)` and `(season, week)`. Ingested and maintained incrementally via `python3 -m newsroom.league_memory index [--limit N] [--season S] [--commit] [--dry-run] [--batch-size 100]`. Metered in `llm_usage` under source `'memory_index'`.

### 3.3p Persona Systems & Structured Profiles (`db/migrations/2027_01_09_personas.sql`, `2027_01_17_persona_slider_band.sql`, `newsroom/personas.py`, `docs/in_progress/PERSONALITY_PLAN.md` §4, §9)
Unified Sims-style structured personality tables keyed by `(persona_type, persona_id)` supporting writers, GMs, players, coaches, owners, agents, and scouts (Item 10, V2.13).
- **`persona_sliders`**:
  - `persona_type` (varchar, CHECK `'writer', 'gm', 'player', 'coach', 'owner', 'scout'`; no `media` role in the SQL or the core), `persona_id` (varchar, e.g. 'KIMES' or gm_id), `temperament`, `sociability`, `confidence`, `openness`, `warmth`, `drive` (smallint, 0–10 each; `chk_persona_sliders_budget` requires the total BETWEEN 24 AND 36, set by `2027_01_17_persona_slider_band.sql` (a guarded DO block, a no-op without the table) and stated in `db/init_db.sql`; it was exactly 30), `created_at`, `updated_at`. PK `(persona_type, persona_id)`.
- **`persona_traits`**:
  - `persona_type`, `persona_id`, `trait_id` (varchar, FK references active catalogue), `created_at`. PK `(persona_type, persona_id, trait_id)`.
- **`persona_views`**:
  - `id` (bigserial PK), `persona_type`, `persona_id`, `topic` (varchar), `stance` (text), `when_tags` (text[] default '{}'), `created_at`.
- **`persona_relationships`**:
  - `id` (serial PK), `persona_type` (CHECK as above), `persona_id`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `trust` (numeric(3,2), −1.00..1.00, default 0), `note`, `tags` (text[]), `created_at`, `updated_at`, `evidence` (JSONB, the last events that moved trust; `2027_01_18_writer_voice.sql`); UNIQUE `(persona_type, persona_id, target_type, target_id)`. One-way: A→B and B→A are separate rows. This is the newsroom's legacy writer-bias store (`newsroom/relationships.py`); the relationships feature never reads, adopts or dual-writes it (its ledger is §3.3t). Writer rows are `persona_type = 'writer'`, `persona_id` = the person key (`agent_memories.person_key`, so Skip Bayless's two accounts share one bias set), targets a player, coach or team, with tags `FAVOURITE`, `GRUDGE`, `OWN_TEAM`, `RIVAL`, `FORMER_TEAM`, `BELIEVER`, `DOUBTER`. They are seeded deterministically per person at clean-seed time, grown from the writer's own takes, earned by being right or wrong on graded picks and calls, decayed at season rollover, and rendered as plain sentences into post and article prompts (AGENT_WIRE_VOICE_PLAN §2.2).
- **`persona_relationship_event_refs`** (`db/migrations/2027_02_22_relationship_applied_refs.sql`): `persona_type`, `persona_id`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `ref` (`pick:<agent_predictions.id>` or `call:<agent_season_calls.id>`), `season`, `applied_at`; PK `(persona_type, persona_id, target_type, target_id, ref)`. The exact set of graded events a writer's relationship row has been charged for, written in the same transaction as the trust update; `apply_graded` reads it together with the row's evidence and its sticky entry (the union), and rows written before the table were backfilled once from those two.
- **`persona_trait_history`**:
  - `id` (bigserial PK), `persona_type`, `persona_id`, `trait_id`, `season` (int), `action` ('ADDED'|'REMOVED'), `reason` (text), `created_at`.
- **Catalogue & Seeding (`newsroom/config/persona_traits.json`, `newsroom/personas.py`):**
  - 61 traits across 7 categories (Cognitive, Social, Risk/Strategy, Emotional, Values, Football Philosophy, Quirks); the 11 owner and scout traits (OWNERS_SCOUTS_VOTERS_PLAN §2.1) carry a `group` (`ownership`, `scouting`). Each trait defines role eligibility/odds, conflicts, "tends to" prompt instruction, application `when` triggers, and engine effects.
  - Deterministic pseudo-random seeding keyed by `f"{persona_type}:{persona_id}"` enforces exact 30 slider budget, 3–5 role-weighted traits (max 2 per category, no conflicts).
  - Seeded 38 writers (from `agent_personas.json`) and 32 NFL general managers into live test schema.

- **Personality core sidecars (`db/migrations/2027_01_16_personality_core.sql`, `2027_01_29_personality_core_extensions.sql`; both mirrored in `db/init_db.sql` (the extension columns last, the partial evolution index instead of the season UNIQUE); applying them to an existing database is deliberate; §7.11):**
  - `persona_core_catalogues` (content-addressed catalogue snapshots), `persona_core_profiles` (PK `(persona_type, persona_id)`, FK to `persona_sliders`; universe, birth key, origin, revision, metadata), `persona_core_aliases` (verified external IDs).
  - `persona_core_events`: one receipt per change (`event_id`, `source_event_id`, `season`, `request`, `before_state`, `after_state`) plus, from `2027_01_29`, `kind` (`evolution` | `override` | `adoption` | `role_link`, existing rows `evolution`), `effective_tick` (1–32, null = untimed), `actor` (`JR` for overrides, the reviewer for adoptions), `seq` (identity, write order) and `recorded_at`. The one-change-a-season rule is the partial unique index `persona_core_events_one_evolution_per_season` (`WHERE kind = 'evolution'`); the migration finds the old `UNIQUE (persona_type, persona_id, season)` by its columns, drops it, and fails if it is missing.
  - `persona_core_links`: role-change carry-over (`universe_id`, `from_type`/`from_id` → `to_type`/`to_id`, `link_kind = 'role_change'`, `effective_season`, `effective_tick`, `receipt`); PK `(to_type, to_id)`, `UNIQUE (from_type, from_id, to_type)`, both sides FK to `persona_core_profiles`.
  - Adopted legacy personas (writers, GMs) keep their legacy `persona_id` (e.g. `ESPN`, a `gm_profiles.id`), with birth key `legacy:<role>:<id>`; their `persona_sliders` / `persona_traits` rows stay where they are.
- **Personality evolution records (`db/migrations/2027_01_30_personality_evolution.sql`, requires `2027_01_16` and `2027_01_29`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`, applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09); `personality/evolution_store.py`, docs/done/PERSONALITY_EVOLUTION_PLAN.md §2.4):** seeds nothing; a rerun checks both tables' columns and primary keys and the index, and refuses an incompatible one. The applied changes themselves are `persona_core_events` receipts (kind `evolution`, event_id `evo:<universe>:<persona>:<season>`).
- **Personality feature switchboard (`db/migrations/2027_01_31_personality_feature_modes.sql`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`, applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09); `personality/features.py`, docs/done/PERSONALITY_ACTIVATION_PLAN.md §2.2):** `personality_feature_modes` (PK `league_id, feature`: `mode` off|shadow|active, `version`, `config` JSONB, `review_ref`, `shadow_since_season/tick`, `set_by`, `set_at`), `personality_feature_mode_changes` (append-only: `from_mode`, `to_mode`, `version`, `review_ref`, `force_reason`, `at_season`, `at_tick`, `set_by`) and `personality_feature_clearances` (PK `league_id, feature, version`: `source_db`, `source_label`, `shadow_from/to_season/tick`, `report_path`, `report_sha256`, `config`, `cleared_by`). Keyed by `league_state.madden_league_id`; seeds nothing (a missing row reads `off`); a rerun checks all three tables' columns and primary keys and refuses an incompatible one.
  - `persona_evolution_runs`: PK `(universe_id, season, rules_version)`; `input_hash` (sha256 of the season facts without profile_view, plus the external candidates), `counts` JSONB, `status` `APPLIED` | `PREVIEW` | `FAILED`, `error`, `created_at`.
  - `persona_evolution_candidates`: `candidate_id` PK (`<universe>:<persona>:<season>:<rule_id | external:<event_id>>`), `universe_id`, `persona_type`, `persona_id`, `season`, `source` (`RULE` | `RELATIONSHIPS` | `DEVELOPMENT` | `OTHER`), `rule_id`, `rules_version`, `change` JSONB, `chance` NUMERIC(5,4) (null for external), `draw`, `source_event_ids` TEXT[], `note`, `status` (`drawn_out` | `blocked` | `superseded` | `applied` | `reverted`), `reason`, `core_event_id`, `created_at`; `UNIQUE (universe_id, persona_type, persona_id, season, rule_id)`; index `persona_evolution_candidates_season (universe_id, season, status)`.
  - Store (explicit cursor, savepoint, never commits): `record_candidates(cur, rows)` (insert once, returns how many were new), `record_run(cur, run)` (insert or replace), `read_run`, `read_candidates(cur, universe, season)`, `read_candidate`, `mark_reverted(cur, candidate_id, override_receipt)` (applied only).
- **Agent loop decisions (`db/migrations/2027_02_01_agent_loops.sql`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`, applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09); `engines/agent_loops/base.py`, docs/done/COACH_PLAYER_AGENT_LOOPS_PLAN.md §2.4):** seeds nothing; a rerun checks the table's columns, primary key, unique constraint and partial index and refuses an incompatible one.
  - `agent_loop_decisions`: `id` BIGSERIAL PK, `league_id`, `season`, `tick` SMALLINT, `kind` (`CHART` | `PROMISE` | `PROMISE_REVIEW` | `CONTRACT` | `INBOX_REPLY` | `LEAK`), `subject_key` (`team:<id>:chart`, `player:<id>:promise`, `promise:<promise_id>`, ...), `persona_type`, `persona_id`, `options` JSONB (`[{key, action, detail, label}]`, labels only), `policy_key`, `chosen_key`, `choice_source` (`POLICY` | `MODEL` | `MODEL_REJECTED`), `text` (grounded model words or null), `visibility` (`private` default | `public`), `facts` JSONB, `cause_refs` JSONB, `created_at`; `UNIQUE (league_id, season, tick, kind, subject_key)` (record, don't replay); partial index `agent_loop_decisions_public (league_id, season, tick) WHERE visibility = 'public'`.
- **Owners, scouting directors and media-voter ballots (`db/migrations/2027_02_02_owners_scouts_voters.sql`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`, applied to madden_test and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09); docs/done/OWNERS_SCOUTS_VOTERS_PLAN.md §2.6):** seeds nothing; a rerun checks the four tables' column fingerprint (a DO block) and refuses an incompatible one. `team_owners` (id serial PK, team_id FK teams, owner_name, profile_key, start_season/end_season, UNIQUE (team_id, start_season)); `owner_decisions` (id bigserial PK, season, tick, team_id, move_kind TRADE|SIGNING|HIRE, move_ref JSONB, decision APPROVE|VETO|PUSH, alternative, loop_decision_id, created_at; idempotency via unique index `owner_decisions_once` on (season, tick, team_id, move_kind, (move_ref::text))); `scout_directors` (id serial PK, team_id, name, persona_id varchar(64), start_season/end_season, UNIQUE (team_id, start_season)); `award_ballots` (PK (season, award, voter), ranking JSONB, ballot_version, created_at).
- **Persona focus (`db/migrations/2027_02_03_persona_focus.sql`, requires `2027_01_16` and `2027_01_24`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`, applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), not to madden_2036 or any franchise database (JR's call); `personality/focus_store.py`, docs/done/INFERRED_SLIDERS_AND_FOCUS_PLAN.md §2.5):** seeds nothing; a rerun checks both tables' columns and primary keys (a DO block) and refuses an incompatible one.
  - `persona_focus`: append-only current-focus history of real coaches and owners. `focus_id` PK (`focus:<universe_id>:<persona_id>:<slot>:<seq>`), `universe_id`, `persona_type` (`coach` | `owner`), `persona_id` (FK `(persona_type, persona_id)` → `persona_core_profiles`), `slot` (`want` | `fear`), `seq` (0 = from the profile, +1 per later row), `text`, `subjects` JSONB (`[{kind, name, binding {namespace, external_id} | null}]`), `anchor` JSONB (`{team, seat}`), `until_season`, `source` (`profile` | `template` | `jr`), `template_id`, `rules_version`, `status` (`active` | `superseded` | `reverted`), `valid_from_season`, `valid_from_tick` (1–32), `supersedes` (FK → `persona_focus`), `stale_causes` JSONB, `reason` (the change note), `actor` (`system`, or `JR` for set and revert), `created_at`; UNIQUE `(universe_id, persona_id, slot, seq)`, partial UNIQUE index `persona_focus_one_active` on `(universe_id, persona_id, slot) WHERE status = 'active'`.
  - `persona_focus_runs`: PK `(universe_id, season, rules_version)`; `input_hash` (sha256 of the facts and active rows), `counts` JSONB, `status` `APPLIED` | `PREVIEW` | `FAILED`, `error`, `created_at`.
