  - `persona_lifecycle_universes`: `universe_id` PK (`mu:<uuid>`), `league_id` UNIQUE, `initial_snapshot_sha256`, `start_season`, `start_cutoff` JSONB, `manifest_version`, `registration` JSONB (the full immutable record incl. `pgid_lifetime`).
  - `persona_lifecycle_people`: PK `(universe_id, source_person_id UUID, role)`, UNIQUE `(universe_id, role, birth_key)`; `classification` (generated/real/unknown), `classification_receipt`, `first_seen` (cutoff), `state` (pending/ready/quarantined/archived), nullable `persona_id` with FK `(role, persona_id)` → `persona_core_profiles`, `revision` (lifecycle row; bumps on archive). Only initialized people are stored: pending and quarantined people stay in the batch report, never as a profile or a classification.
  - `persona_lifecycle_bindings`: PK `(universe_id, role, namespace, external_id)` → `source_person_id`, `valid_from`/`valid_to` cutoffs, `receipt`; FK to the person. Namespaces: `source-person`, `save-pgid:<lifetime>`, `db-player`, `db-coach`, `db-coordinator`, `scout:<class>` (also core aliases) and replaceable `draft:<class>:<capture>` board IDs (lifecycle-only, closable). Conflicts never overwrite.
  - `persona_lifecycle_batches`: `batch_id` PK (= the manifest's `manifest_sha256`), `universe_id`, `manifest`, `before_state`, `after_state`, `status` (applied/reverted), `applied_at`, `review_receipt`, `revert_receipt` (nullable).

- **Simulation event producers (§3.3r):** `engines/relationship_producers/` turns rosters, depth charts, moves, contracts, injuries, awards, results and coach moves into relationship events for the ledger (§3.3t); off by default.
- **Inbox as an event producer (§2.21b, §3.3s):** the front-office inbox records `meaningful_interaction`, `treatment`, `promise_made` and `promise_resolved` events for the relationships plan in its outbox `inbox_relationship_events`; it never writes `persona_relationships` and never reads it.

### 3.3q League Office & Franchise State (`db/migrations/2027_01_14_v2_franchise_os.sql`, `docs/done/V2_CORE_BUILD_PLAN.md`)
- **`depth_charts`**: PK `(team_id, season, week, source, position_slot, depth)`; `position_slot` (varchar(8), Madden's DepthChart field name), `depth` (1–6), `player_id`, `source` (MADDEN | MU_COACH | JR).
- **`franchise_pending_moves`**: JR's queued `Mu_Network` moves, applied at the next league office write: `id`, `team_id`, `kind` (DEPTH_CHART | RELEASE | SIGN | TRADE | PS_PROMOTE | PS_DEMOTE | IR_PLACE | IR_ACTIVATE | RESTRUCTURE | EXTENSION | TAG | OPTION), `payload` (JSONB), `status` (PENDING | WRITTEN | REFUSED | CANCELLED), `reason`, `created_at`, `written_run`.
- **`league_office_runs`**: one row per run and save write (`summary.operation` holds the durable operation record of the receipt protocol, §2.21a; no schema change): `id`, `season`, `week`, `stage`, `save_name`, `status` (PLANNED | WRITTEN | FAILED | DRY_RUN), `edits` (JSONB, the exact save_writer document), `summary`, `drift` (JSONB), `error`, `started_at`, `finished_at`. `summary.retirement_window` (retirement window, §2.21a; no schema change) on every run: `{version retirement-window-v1, role image|decision|window, season, stop, roster_image {"<pgid>": [status, team_index]}}`; a decision run adds `decided {"<pgid>": {player_id, keep, reason}}`, `restored`, `blocked`; a window run adds classify's `prior_stop`, `stage_gap`, `decided_retired`, `restore`, `conflicts`, `carried`, `vanished`, `purged` plus `restored`, `blocked` (planner reasons), `decision_run_id`, `decision_stop`. Only WRITTEN runs are read back.
- **`retirement_decisions`**: PK `(season, player_id)`; `madden_retired`, `mu_keep` (Project Mu un-retires him), `reason`. The league office's compatibility projection (observed native retirement plus the `keep_retired` override; retirement-window rows use reason prefixes `window:restored:<STAGE>`, `window:blocked:<STAGE>:<first planner reason>`, `window:conflict:<STAGE>:re_retired_again` (or `no_baseline`) with `mu_keep` false, and `window:vanished:<STAGE>` for a rostered player who vanished in one advance); retirement policy intent, draws and save-write receipts live in the §3.3w sidecars, never here.
- Applied to `madden_test` (2026-10-30). `depth_charts` is written and read by `engines/depth_chart_engine.store` / `load` (§2.17c); `pipeline/load_save.py` stores the save's charts as source MADDEN each load, and `pipeline/drift_check.py` compares the newest MU_COACH/JR chart against the save (its report is what `league_office_runs.drift` will hold); the other tables here have no writer until the league office (wave 5).

### 3.3r Relationship Event Producers (`db/migrations/2027_01_28_relationship_producers.sql`, also in `db/init_db.sql`; `engines/relationship_producers/`, docs/done/RELATIONSHIP_EVENT_PRODUCERS_PLAN.md)
Built 2026-11-04 (waves 1–2): tables, rules, store, sources, runner, catch-up, CLI and the watcher step (§6.0b). Off by default and never run on a franchise: the migration isn't applied, and JR turns the step on (switchboard `producers`, §7.11; or `MU_RELATIONSHIP_PRODUCERS=on`) after reviewing a preview and a `catch-up --dry-run` report. The run needs both these tables and the relationships ledger (§3.3t). All three tables are keyed by `league_id` so held events can exist before the lifecycle plan registers the universe.
- **`relationship_producer_runs`**: PK `(league_id, season, tick, rules_version)`, tick 1–32; `source` (SAVE | CATCHUP), `input_hash`, `registry_hash`, `event_hashes` (JSONB `{"<source_event_id>|<facet_key>": {"hash", "ref"}}`, the events in effect after the run), `counts`, `status` (APPENDED | HELD | NOOP | FAILED), `error`, `created_at`.
- **`relationship_roster_observations`**: PK `(league_id, season, tick, player_id)`; `team_id` (NULL = free agent), `source`. The loader overwrites `player_seasons.team_id` every load, so this is the only per-week team record.
- **`relationship_pending_events`**: PK `(league_id, source_event_id, facet_key)`; `subject_alias`, `envelope`, `status` (PENDING | APPENDED | DROPPED), `reason` (universe_unregistered | relationship_store_missing | subject_unresolved | target_unresolved | `rejected: <append_events reason>`; an `unknown_identity` rejection stays PENDING and is retried, any other is DROPPED), `created_at`, `appended_at`; index `relationship_pending_open (league_id, status)`.
- The migration is one transaction; it refuses an existing table whose columns, types, nullability or primary key differ (CHECK constraints and foreign keys aren't compared) and seeds nothing. Not yet applied to any database.
- **Rules** (`rules.py`, producers-v2, pure; plan D1–D2): a role tier is STARTER (a `starters_by_base_slot` starter), ROTATION (depth 1 in SLWR/3DRB/PWHB/SUBLB/SLCB/RLE/RRE/RDT/NT, or the first after the starters in a base slot) or RESERVE. A week is ineligible offseason, without a MADDEN chart, on a bye, injured (weeks_remaining > 0 or IR, Madden's stuck IR included) or in a player's first week on a team. The established role is the highest tier held for `ROLE_ESTABLISHED_WEEKS` = 4 consecutive eligible weeks of the current tenure (resets at a season boundary to the most-held tier, none on a new team); a private `role_window` is unsatisfied only when an eligible week sits below it, and rating rank is a fact only. Moves: release → dismissal + departure; expiry → departure; trade → departure + arrival; draft or above-minimum signing → positive arrival; same-team new contract → recognition; an unknown cause gives no treatment. Situations: injury at `INJURY_SITUATION_WEEKS` = 2+ weeks out (or IR with a real injury) and resolved on healing; awards; `STREAK_GAMES` = 3 streaks; season outcomes; contract year at tick 1, valid until RESIGN (25). Coach facts: fired → dismissal, promoted → recognition, other hires → arrival, kept with score ≥ `HOT_SEAT_PRESSURE` 0.5 × the firing line → job pressure; coordinators are core role `coach` with alias namespace `db-coordinator`. `source_refs` hold only a row the occurrence owns outright (injuries, awards, staff_moves, hot-seat row, a re-sign's new contract); shared evidence (roster, chart, game, league-office run, cause row) is only in `attribution.evidence_refs`, since the ledger lets one external ref name one occurrence. Every envelope is `verified_simulation`, confidence high (SAVE) or medium (CATCHUP), with `payload.rule` `<rule>@producers-v2`; HISTORY-origin players are skipped. The thresholds are review-only starting points (plan Q2).
- **Coaching trees** (`coaching_tree`, producers-v2, docs/done/COACHING_TREES_PLAN.md §2.6): from `TREE_TICK` (= `FIRST_OFFSEASON_TICK`, 24) `read_tick` adds `tree_staff` (`engines.coaching_tree_facts.staff_seasons(cur, through=season)`) and `tree_reviewed_pairs` (reviewed edges from the files), and `run._coach_events` emits, for each season 2026..season, every `personality.coaching_trees.sim_edges` edge that crossed in that season (read as of its crossing, so seasons and outcome are frozen and later ticks rebuild identical facets): `coaching_tree_events(edge)` = two `meaningful_interaction` facets sharing `tree_source_id` `mu:tree:<coach_id>:<coordinator_id>` at `(crossed_season, 24)`, the protégé's `db-coordinator` alias toward the mentor's `db-coach` alias (`target_alias`) with `direction 'mentee'` and the mirror with `direction 'mentor'`; payload `{relationship_kind mentorship, outcome, significance meaningful, opportunity_ref 'coach_tenures:<id>|coordinator_tenures:<id>', direction, seasons, rule}`, public, `evidence_scope ['coach_tenures', 'coordinator_tenures']`. Held until both aliases resolve. `facet_key` uses `target_alias` when present. Reviewed pairs are skipped. Producer appends don't check the calendar, so historical crossings (2026 on) append on a later first run.
- **Store** (`store.py`; caller owns the transaction, savepoint per batch, never commits or connects): `append_or_hold` resolves each subject through `personality.store.resolve_alias` and appends through `personality.relationship_store.append_events`; it holds the event otherwise. Changed ticks produce relationships-plan `correction` envelopes from `corrections()` (a replacement, or a null retraction for a vanished event). An event's hash ignores `universe_id`/`persona_id`, so it doesn't change when identity resolves. Rejected envelopes in the `append_events` receipt are never counted as appended (held or DROPPED, above); corrections own no source ref.
- **Sources and runner** (`sources.py`, `run.py`): `read_tick` gathers one tick's inputs as plain JSON (its sha256 is `input_hash`): the roster (the watcher passes the snapshot's, as the loader places players; otherwise `player_seasons` minus retired players; catch-up: MADDEN chart membership, then the week's injuries rows), the previous roster observation, the window (ticks after the previous producer run), in-season weeks of the season before and this season for role history (a week's membership is its observation, else its charts), causes for changed teams (an applied `transactions` row; a WRITTEN `league_office_runs` release/sign/trade edit by pgid, flagged JR when a WRITTEN `franchise_pending_moves` row of that run names the player; a DRAFTED or traded `player_season_transitions` row; an expiring last contract), injuries, games, new re-sign contracts above the previous run's `player_contracts` id watermark, contract years, awards, staff moves and hot-seat rows. `build_events` is pure. Timing is deterministic: windows, moves and recognitions at the run's tick; injury starts/heals, streaks, contract years and season outcomes when their tick is in the window; awards at (season, 23), hot-seat pressure at 19 / 23 by phase, a coach's LEFT at his hot-seat phase tick and HIRED at 24, repeated on later runs as ledger duplicates. `run_tick` returns NOOP on the same inputs and registry; changed inputs append corrections for changed or vanished events; then observations, append-or-hold, flush and the run row in one savepoint. `record_failure` writes a FAILED row unless a good run holds the key. `catch_up` replays in-season ticks with MADDEN charts from the first save (`captures` mode `save`, else the first chart season) as CATCHUP runs (coverage partial, confidence medium, no recognitions), refuses any range with a SAVE run at or before `through`, and `--dry-run` rolls everything back.

### 3.3s Front-Office Inbox (`db/migrations/2027_01_19_front_office_inbox.sql`, also in `db/init_db.sql`; `engines/inbox/`, §2.21b)
Built in U1 (2026-11-03); not yet applied to any database. Idempotent, seeds nothing.
- **`controlled_personas`**: PK `(team_id, role, persona_id)`; `role` GM | COACH | PLAYER, `persona_id` (gm_profiles.id / coaches.id / players.id as text), `active`, `taken_at`, `released_at`. No rows = JR controls no one.
- **`inbox_threads`**: `id`, `team_id`, `kind` (registry key, no CHECK), `actor_role` (GM | COACH | PLAYER | TEAM), `actor_id`, `counterpart_type` (gm | coach | player | writer | prospect | scout | owner | system), `counterpart_id` (gm_profiles.id, coaches.id, players.id, agent_memories.agent_id, or a prospect's permanent `prospect_uid` from `engines/prospect_ids.py`, never `prospect_key`; a plain SQL comment in the DDL, not `COMMENT ON`, so madden_test needs nothing re-applied), `counterpart_name`, `subject`, `status` (OPEN | WAITING_JR | CLOSED | EXPIRED), `started_by` (JR | COUNTERPART | SYSTEM), `source_ref`, `link_table`, `link_id`, `state` (JSONB, kind-owned; `_touched` = last activity), `season`, `week`, `offseason_stage`, `expires_season`, `expires_week`, `unread`, `created_at`, `updated_at`; UNIQUE `(team_id, kind, source_ref)`; index `inbox_threads_team_status (team_id, status, updated_at DESC)`.
- **`inbox_messages`**: `id`, `thread_id` (CASCADE), `seq` (UNIQUE per thread), `author` (JR | COUNTERPART | SYSTEM), `body`, `body_source` (JR | LLM | TEMPLATE | ENGINE), `option_id`, `options` (JSONB), `facts` (never sent to the UI), `engine_ref`, `appraisal` (the counterpart's appraisal of the JR line it answers), `created_at`.
- **`inbox_relationship_events`** (outbox for the relationships store): `id`, `source_event_id` UNIQUE (`inbox:msg:<id>`, `inbox:promise:<thread>:<n>:made|resolved`), `kind` (meaningful_interaction | treatment | promise_made | promise_resolved), `thread_id`, `message_id` (SET NULL), `event` (the full envelope), `sim_time` `{season, week, offseason_stage}`, `status` (PENDING | APPENDED | REJECTED), `status_reason`, `appended_at`, `created_at`.
- **`team_vision`**: PK `(team_id, season)`; `direction` (CONTEND | RETOOL | REBUILD, NULL = no pin), `emphasis` (OFFENSE | DEFENSE | BALANCED), `playing_time` (YOUTH | VETERANS | MERIT, stored only), `thread_id`, `agreed_at`. Written and read by `engines/team_vision.py` (inbox U6): an agreed vision pins the direction in `gm_direction.compute` (the overrides still win) and weights that side's needs by 1.15; playing time has no consumer yet.

### 3.3t Relationship Ledger (`db/migrations/2027_01_27_personality_relationships.sql`, requires `2027_01_16`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`; `personality/relationship_store.py`, docs/done/PERSONALITY_RELATIONSHIPS_PLAN.md §2.6)
Built 2026-11-04; applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), not to madden_2036 or any franchise database (production application, intake and numeric trust each need JR's go-ahead, plan §6 gates). Additive feature tables beside the core and the legacy `persona_relationships` (no dual-write, no backfill). One transaction; a rerun checks each table's columns, types, nullability and primary key and the time index, failing on an incompatible definition; seeds nothing.
- **`persona_relationship_batches`**: PK `(universe_id, head)`, UNIQUE `(universe_id, batch_hash)`; `expected_head` (= head − 1), `receipt` (JSONB object), `created_at`. A universe's serialized head starts at 1.
- **`persona_relationship_events`**: PK `(universe_id, source_event_id, facet_key)`, UNIQUE `(universe_id, event_id, facet_key)`, FK `(universe_id, head)` → batches; `occurred_season`, `occurred_tick` (≥ 0), `schema_version` (`relationships-v1`), `payload_hash`, `envelope` (the canonical §7.11 envelope; CHECKs that it is an object carrying the row's schema version and source ID), `created_at`; index `persona_relationship_events_time (universe_id, occurred_season, occurred_tick)`. `facet_key` = `f:` + sha256 of subject / target / kind (first 40 hex).
- **`persona_relationship_sources`**: PK `(universe_id, namespace, external_key)` → `source_event_id`. Many external refs may name one occurrence; remapping one is a conflict.
- **Store** (`relationship_store.py`; explicit cursor on a non-autocommit connection, savepoint plus `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('relationships:<universe>', 0))`, never connects or commits): `read_head(cur, universe_id)` (0 before the first batch); `append_events(cur, events, *, expected_head, team_registry)` validates every envelope and checks every PersonRef against `persona_core_profiles` in its universe (failures are excluded into `receipt.rejected` [{source_event_id, event_id, reason}], not appended), returns an exact earlier batch's stored receipt (`replayed: true`) before the head check, raises `StaleHeadError` on a moved head, treats a stored facet with the same hash as a no-op (`duplicates`, with its original head) and refuses the whole batch (`RelationshipConflictError`) for the same facet with different content, a reused transport `event_id` with other content, or a source ref already naming another occurrence. A batch with nothing new writes nothing and keeps the head. Receipt: `{universe_id, status (appended | noop | rejected), head, expected_head, batch_hash, registry_hash, appended, duplicates, rejected, source_refs, replayed}`. `read_events(cur, *, subject, as_of, known_through=None)` returns the subject's facts (corrections included) by effective time and ingestion head, each with `head`. `EVENTS_TABLE` names the table the inbox's `flush` checks for.
- **Producers:** the inbox outbox (§3.3s) and the relationship producers (§3.3r) append through `append_events(cur, events, expected_head=read_head(...), team_registry=...)`. The producers' wave 2 (sources, runner, catch-up, watcher step) is the next build; nothing calls the store in production yet.

### 3.3u Contract Policy Receipts (`db/migrations/2027_01_23_contract_personality_policy.sql`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`; `engines/personality_contract_store.py`, docs/done/PERSONALITY_CONTRACT_POLICY_PLAN.md §2.5)
Built 2026-11-06; applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), not to madden_2036 or any franchise database (scratch first, production needs JR's go-ahead). Additive, seeds nothing, no backfill; one transaction whose DO block checks each existing table's columns, types, nullability and primary key and fails on an incompatible definition.
- **`contract_policy_decisions`**: PK `(universe_id, decision_id)` (decision_id = an actual negotiation attempt or batch entry, never player-season); `season`, `week`, `stage`, `player_id` BIGINT, `persona_id`/`revision` (NULL without a profile), `mode` CHECK off/shadow/active, `policy_version`, `input_hash` (sha256 of the canonical snapshot), `snapshot` JSONB (permitted view, revision, provider versions and as-of, canonical offer order, market basis, components, gates, draws, bars, counters, baseline and adjusted outcomes), `result` JSONB (links offer/execution ids), `created_at`. No FK to the mutable profile, so archive/retirement never breaks replay.
- **`contract_policy_event_outbox`**: PK `(universe_id, event_id)`, FK `(universe_id, decision_id)` → decisions; `kind` CHECK `CONTRACT_OFFER_SUBMITTED` / `CONTRACT_RESPONSE_RECORDED` / `CONTRACT_EXECUTED` / `CONTRACT_INSTRUMENT_APPLIED`, `payload` (v1: event_id, source_decision_id, universe_id, player_persona_id, team_id, gm_persona_id, as_of, offer_id, terms, market_reference, response, execution_id), `delivered_at`. Factual only: no preview, LOWBALL, trust, promise or grudge events; the relationships owner classifies facts.
- **Store** (caller owns the transaction, savepoints, never commits): `record_contract_decision(cur, receipt)` (insert once with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; same id + hash → the original, status `replayed`; changed hash → `ContractStoreConflict`; races resolve by reread), `read_contract_decision`, `enqueue_contract_events(cur, receipt, facts)` (event id `<decision_id>:<kind>`, same dedupe), `read_contract_activation(cur, universe_id)` → `{config, source, families}` from the shared switchboard `personality.features.config(cur, universe_id, 'contracts_ambition' / 'contracts_relationships')` (activation plan D1; one mode per decision, the most active family's, a family in a lower mode disabled); `source: default` and mode off while that module does not exist. There is no `contract_policy_activation` table.

### 3.3v Player Trade Requests (`db/migrations/2027_01_25_player_trade_requests.sql`, requires `2027_01_16` and `teams`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`; `engines/player_trade_request_store.py`, docs/done/PERSONALITY_TRADE_REQUESTS_PLAN.md §2.6)
Built 2026-11-06; applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), not to madden_2036 or any franchise database (scratch tests passed 2026-11-07; production needs JR's go-ahead, plan gate G5). Additive, seeds nothing, no backfill or historical requests; one transaction that first requires `persona_core_profiles` and `teams`, then checks each existing table's columns, types, nullability and primary key and fails on an incompatible definition.
- **`player_trade_request_decisions`**: PK `(universe_id, persona_id, season)`, UNIQUE `decision_id` (UUID5 of the annual key); `outcome` CHECK REQUEST/NO_REQUEST (never a deferred reservation), `input_hash`, `policy_version`, `seed_algorithm`, `draw` CHECK [0, 1), `receipt` (JSONB `{annual, decision}`), `created_at`.
- **`player_trade_requests`**: PK `request_id` (UUID5), UNIQUE `decision_id` → decisions, `persona_type` CHECK `'player'` with FK `(persona_type, persona_id)` → `persona_core_profiles`, `team_id` → `teams(id)` (the requesting team; teams' PK is `id`), `opened_season`, `revision` ≥ 0, `status` CHECK ACTIVE/WITHDRAWN/RESOLVED_TRADE/CLOSED_EMPLOYMENT/VOIDED_CORRECTION, `state` (the full episode JSON; its status and revision must match the columns), `updated_at`. Partial unique index `player_trade_requests_one_active (universe_id, persona_id) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'`.
- **`player_trade_request_actions`**: PK `(universe_id, persona_id, event_id)`, UNIQUE `(universe_id, persona_id, source_event_id, action_kind)` and `(universe_id, persona_id, season, window_id, checkpoint_id, action_kind)`; nullable `request_id` → requests, `action_kind` CHECK REVIEW plus the nine lifecycle actions, `payload_hash`, nullable `before_state`/`after_state`, `receipt`. Every checkpoint review is recorded, no-op and deferred ones included (event ID `review:<season>:<window_id>:<checkpoint_id>`).
- **Store** (caller owns a non-autocommit transaction; savepoint plus `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on a 64-bit key of `trade-requests:<universe>:<persona>`; never connects, commits, seeds or migrates): `record_decision(cur, context, clock, policy, *, mode)` (ENABLED with an approved policy only; SHADOW raises, DISABLED returns the no-op without SQL) and `apply_action(cur, request_id, action, context, clock, policy)`: lock, core binding (a `FOR SHARE` read: a stored `player` profile of this universe, else `BindingError`), exact replay by event ID before revision checks (same payload hash → the original receipt, status `replayed`; changed → `StoreConflict`), source-event reuse conflict, `MixedRewindError` when a stored episode or this season's decision is newer than the clock, then the engine's decision/transition and the writes (update guarded by `revision`). `read_active`, `read_annual`, `read_receipt`.
- **Rollback:** disable the feature and keep/export the ledgers; never reverse real trades or contracts; no automatic down migration.

### 3.3w Retirement Policy (`db/migrations/2027_01_26_retirement_policy.sql`, requires `players` and `league_office_runs`; mirrored in `db/init_db.sql`; `engines/retirement_store.py`, docs/done/PERSONALITY_RETIREMENT_PLAN.md §2.5)
Built 2026-11-06; applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), not to madden_2036 or any franchise database (scratch tests passed 2026-11-07; production needs JR's go-ahead, plan gate G5). Additive, seeds nothing, no backfill; `player_retirements` (captured, §3.3m) and `retirement_decisions` (the league office's projection, §3.3q) are untouched. Transactional and rerunnable: an existing table with other columns or primary key fails loudly.
- **`career_decision_states`**: PK `(universe_id, person_key, earned_season)`, UNIQUE `decision_id` (UUID5, `retirement_policy.decision_id_for`), `player_id` FK `players(id)`, `state` CHECK the ten §2.17f states, `revision` ≥ 0 (CAS), nullable `reservation` JSONB, `updated_at`.
- **`retirement_policy_events`**: PK `event_id` UUID (reviews: UUID5 of decision, checkpoint, source event), FK `decision_id`, `checkpoint` (`OPEN`/`MARKET_CLOSE`/`ROLLOVER_REVIEW`, or `EVENT` for state events), `event_kind` (`REVIEW` or the state-machine event), `source_event_id`, `request_hash`, `input_snapshot`/`policy_snapshot` JSONB, nullable `draw_hex` and `breakdown` (reviews only: base, modifiers, final_p, warnings), `before_state`/`after_state`, `receipt`; UNIQUE `(decision_id, source_event_id)`.
- **`retirement_write_receipts`**: PK `operation_id` UUID, FK `decision_id`, `status` CHECK PREPARED/VERIFIED/FAILED/CONFLICT, `source_save_hash`, nullable `output_hash`, `edits_hash`, nullable `league_office_run` FK `league_office_runs(id)`, `before_image`, nullable `verification`, `request_hash`, nullable `ack_hash` (NULL exactly while PREPARED), `created_at`, `acknowledged_at`; one PREPARED row per decision (partial unique index).
- **Store** (caller owns a non-autocommit transaction; savepoint plus `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on a 64-bit key of `retirement:<universe>:<person>`; never connects, commits, seeds or migrates): `record_review(cur, decision, *, player_id, source_event_id, input_snapshot, policy_snapshot)` creates the OPEN state and applies ANNUAL_REVIEW, records later checkpoints without a state change, and refuses a review whose draw differs from the stored one; `apply_event`, `reserve_contract(cur, decision_id, offer_id, expected_revision, ...)`, `prepare_retirement(cur, decision_id, expected_revision, *, operation_id, ...)` run `career_decision_state.transition` and update by CAS (STALE → `StoreConflict`, REJECTED → `TransitionRejected`, nothing written); the same event ID and payload returns the original receipt even after newer revisions, a changed payload or a reused source event is a conflict. `prepare(cur, request, expected_revision)` stores the immutable save-write request for a RETIRE_PENDING decision with the same operation; `acknowledge(cur, operation_id, receipt)` moves PREPARED → VERIFIED (needs output hash and save receipt ID) / FAILED / CONFLICT by CAS and applies RETIREMENT_VERIFIED / RETIREMENT_FAILED / FLAG_CONFLICT. No live caller.
- The retirement window (§2.17f) writes none of these sidecars in v1: its record is `league_office_runs.summary.retirement_window` and `retirement_decisions` (§3.3q).
- **Rollback:** before activation, disable consumers and drop the empty sidecars; once audit rows exist keep the tables and disable the feature. A save write is never undone by a database rollback (reconcile receipts or restore the exact pre-write disposable save with the watcher paused); acknowledged draws are never redrawn.

### 3.3x Real NFL history 1999–2025 (`db/migrations/2027_02_04_nfl_history.sql`, mirrored at the end of `db/init_db.sql`; `engines/nfl_history/`, docs/done/REAL_NFL_HISTORY_PLAN.md)
Real NFL history in its own tables, never the league's (no real row in `season_stats`, `season_stat_*`, `player_seasons`, `awards`, `team_season_results`, `coach_season_lines`, the record book, `players` or `coaches`; the one exception is the 2025 `coach_seasons` baseline, §3.3h). A reader that wants both reads both and labels them. Applied to `madden_test` on 2026-11-07 (JR's go-ahead): migration `2027_02_04` plus `load --apply` (24,873 players, 61,537 season lines, 7,276 games, 861 team seasons, 904 coach seasons, 1,740 awards, 7,154 draft picks; a second load gave identical counts; `check`: 7 differences in 417 record rows). `link` and `coach-baseline` were not run there, because madden_test is the old 2036 test league with no Madden pgids; they run per PC franchise database after its first save load and before the first season archive. Team ids are the current franchise (`teams.id`; OAK/LV → LV, SD → LAC, STL/LA → LAR); the historical code stays in `team_abbr`.
- **`nfl_players`** (`gsis_id` PK; `espn_id`, `pfr_id`, names, position, birth date, college, height, weight, rookie/last season, draft year/round/pick/team): nflverse `players.csv` plus the few stat-file players missing from it; upserted, never deleted.
- **`nfl_player_seasons`** PK (`gsis_id`, `season`, `season_type` REG/POST): `team_id`, `team_abbr` (a midseason trade puts the season with his last team), `position`, `games_played` and the stat columns `store.STAT_COLUMNS` (season_stat_lines names: passing, rushing, receiving incl. `rec_targets`, defense incl. `def_tackles` = solo + assists, kicking incl. the four FG ranges and `kick_fg_long`, punting, returns; `st_tds` keeps nflverse's unsplit special-teams TDs, `kr_tds`/`pr_tds` stay NULL). NULL = nflverse has no value. Defensive tackles and deflections are thin before about 2001 (the load report lists tackle coverage per season).
- **`nfl_games`** (`game_id` PK, nflverse id): season, week, `game_type` REG/WC/DIV/CON/SB, date, both teams (id and code), scores, overtime, both head coaches.
- **`nfl_team_seasons`** PK (`season`, `team_id`): conference and division that season (six-team Centrals 1999–2001), W-L-T, points, `division_place`, `conference_seed`, `playoff_result` (MISSED … CHAMPION), playoff W-L, `head_coach` (most regular-season games), `head_coach_id` (only for coaches in this database), `standings_source` (`NFLDATA`: nflverse nfldata standings, 2002 on; `COMPUTED` for 1999–2001: place by win percentage, head-to-head, net points; seeds from the bracket; approximate).
- **`nfl_coach_seasons`** PK (`coach_name`, `season`, `team_id`): from the per-game head coach (interim coaches included), W-L-T, games, `full_season`, playoff W-L and result, Super Bowl W-L, `coach_id` when he is in `coaches`.
- **`nfl_awards`**: season, `award_type` (`MVP, OPOY, DPOY, OROY, DROY, COTY, SBMVP, First Team All-Pro, Second Team All-Pro`; `Pro Bowl` is a valid type but not loaded), `gsis_id`, player or coach name, team, position (Wikipedia's All-Pro positions: `LT`, `EDGE`, `SCB`, `APR`, ...). Unique on (season, type, position, gsis_id or name). Source: the committed `data/history/nfl_awards_1999_2025.csv` (1,740 rows), built by `python3 -m engines.nfl_history.awards build` from Wikipedia's award and `<season> All-Pro Team` pages (AP selections only), because Pro-Football-Reference refuses automated fetches; its `gsis_id` is resolved from nflverse by name, team and season (2 rows unresolved).
- **`nfl_draft_picks`** PK (`season`, `overall`): 1999–2026 (2026 = Madden 27's real rookies), round, pick in round, team, `gsis_id`, name, position, college.
- **`nfl_player_links`** (`player_id` PK FK `players` ON DELETE CASCADE, `gsis_id` UNIQUE): this database's Madden player ↔ the real person, `method` (`OVERRIDE`, `ESPN`, `EXACT`, `ALIAS`, `FUZZY`), `score`, `evidence`. `link.match`: overrides from `data/history/nfl_link_overrides.csv` (`madden_pgid, full_name, position, gsis_id, note`; `none` = no real person; refused when name or position group disagree); then the same normalized name (or a `player_name_aliases` name), position group (Madden LE/RE match nflverse LB/DE/DL; CB/FS/SS match any DB) and entry season (±1) or real 2026 team (`rosters_2026.csv` by ESPN id) agreeing, the best score leading by 2.0 when several share the name; then fuzzy (same first initial or a nickname, last name within edit distance 2, with position, entry season and 2026 team all agreeing), linked and listed; a person claimed twice makes both ambiguous. Evidence weights: position 3, entry 3, draft year 2 (snapshot: 2027 + `year_drafted`), college 2, team 2, height 1, weight 1. Every run writes `verify_output/nfl_history/link_<db>.md` / `.csv` (counts, ambiguous, fuzzy, unmatched veterans by OVR, unmatched rookies, real 2025 players with no link). On the CAREER-WEEK1 snapshot (offline): 97.3% of veterans linked, every 80+ player but the legends Elway and Rice and one rookie.
- **`nfl_history_loads`**: one row per applied step (`kind` players/stats/games/teams/awards/draft/link/coach_baseline, season range, source files with sha256, counts, report).
- **`nfl_season_lines`** view: `nfl_player_seasons` + `display_name` + the linked `player_id` + `source = 'NFL'`, ready to `UNION ALL` with `season_stat_lines`.
- **Loading** (`python3 -m engines.nfl_history`, §1.2): `fetch` caches nflverse `players.csv`, `stats_player_{reg,post}_<season>.csv`, `games.csv`, `draft_picks.csv` and nfldata `standings.csv` in `data/history/.cache/` (generic client name, polite delay); `load` reads only the cache and, per kind, deletes and reinserts its season range in one transaction (a rerun with the same files gives the same rows); `init` = load, link, coach-baseline. A full scratch load: 24,873 players, 61,537 season lines, 7,276 games, 861 team and 904 coach seasons, 1,740 awards, 7,154 picks, in about 5 s.
- **Readers** (`engines/nfl_history/read.py`; every function returns empty when the tables are missing): `player_nfl_career`, `nfl_career_before`, `nfl_first_seasons`, `team_nfl_seasons`, `nfl_awards_by_season`, `nfl_champions`, `nfl_player_awards`. Used by the player page, Team History and Awards page (§4.2, §4.3, §4.7, §5.2), the writer tools (§7), career milestones (§3.3m: career = real + league) and popularity Awards Equity (§2.5). Coach records, hot seat, playoff clout, progression and the record book keep reading league tables only.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_nfl_history_store.py` (writes, reads, schema text; an integration test applies the migration twice on a throwaway `mu_scratch_*` database), `test_nfl_history_nflverse.py`, `test_nfl_history_awards.py`, `test_nfl_history_link.py`, `test_nfl_history_coach_baseline.py`, `test_nfl_history_cli.py`, `test_nfl_history_api.py`, `test_nfl_history_writer_tools.py`; real careers in `test_career_milestones.py` and `test_player_and_playoff_metrics.py`.

### 3.4 Fantasy Analytics & Projections
- **`fantasy_projections`**:
  - `id` (PK), `season` (int), `week` (int), `player_id` (int, players.id — no FK constraint), `player_name` (varchar), `position` (varchar), `team_id` (FK, int), `projected_points` (numeric), `avg_points` (numeric), `matchup_stars` (int 1–5), `pos_rank` (varchar e.g. 'QB1', 'WR1'), `adp_rank` (int), `ros_rank` (varchar), `ros_total_points` (numeric), `delta` (numeric). `UNIQUE(season, week, player_id)`.
  - **Week 1 = preseason ADP board & baseline projections**: `engines/fantasy_adp_engine.py` seeds the top 300 players by simulated ADP (`fantasy_sim_adp.adp`, ties by `draft_score`), setting `adp_rank` = that order. Preseason calibration by `engines/fantasy_projection_engine.py` then projects Week 1 and rest-of-season for all rostered QB/HB/FB/WR/TE/K/DEF:
    - Preseason baseline weights the player's prior-season stats shrunk toward the depth-chart prior by `PRESEASON_PRIOR_GAMES = 4.0`: `baseline = (total_prev + 4.0 * slot_prior) / (games_prev + 4.0)`. `avg_points` reflects prior-season per-game average; `delta` = `projected_points − avg_points`.
    - For rookies or players without prior-season lines, baseline uses the depth-chart slot prior scaled by player overall rating: `slot_prior * max(0.6, min(1.4, 1.0 + (ovr - 80) * 0.015))`, with `avg_points` and `delta` NULL. Slot priors come from the prior season; with no prior-season games they fall back to `DEFAULT_SLOT_PRIORS` (e.g. QB1 17.0, RB1 12.0, WR1 16.0, TE1 8.5, K 7.5, DEF 6.5).
    - Prior-season K/DEF lines use the same kicking/defense scoring as in-season (below). Only 29 of 285 completed 2035 games have `game_stat_defense` lines (and 71 kicking lines), so 2036 week-1 DEF projections are mostly the points-allowed tier (≈0.4 average); seasons captured weekly have full lines.
    - Preseason matchup factors and `matchup_stars` use the prior season's defensive allowed-per-game per position group shrunk toward the league average.
    - Active injuries (`injuries` row with `weeks_remaining > 0` or `is_ir = true`) zero out `projected_points`, omit the player from `pos_rank`, and exclude injured weeks from `ros_total_points`.
    - Every playing, non-injured player receives `pos_rank` (`QB1`, `RB1`, etc.), and every rostered player receives `ros_total_points` (sum of projections across weeks 1–18) and `ros_rank`. Preseason `adp_rank` is preserved on the week 1 rows so `rank_trend` (`adp_rank − overall_ros_rank`) works across the board.
  - **Weeks 2–18 = in-season weekly projections**, written by `engines/fantasy_projection_engine.py`: one row per rostered QB/HB/FB/WR/TE, kicker (K) and team defense (DEF, one `player_seasons` row per team), using only games completed before that week, so past weeks show what was projected before kickoff. Re-running a week replaces its rows (rows for players no longer projected are deleted).
    - **Points per game line** (`load_points_rows`): skill players from `player_stats.fantasy_points` (positions QB/HB/FB/WR/TE only, so K/DEF are never double-counted); kickers from `game_stat_kicking` with yardage-based scoring (minimum 3 points under 30 yds, fractional 0.1/yd: 3.x for 30–39, 4.x for 40–49, 5.x for 50+, with `fg_long * 0.1` exactness for the longest kick, 1 per XP, -1 per missed FG or XP); DEF from `game_stat_defense` + return stats (`game_stat_kickreturn`, `game_stat_puntreturn`) summed per team and game: `sacks + 2·INT + 2·fumble recoveries + 6·(def_td + ret_td) + 2·safeties + 2·blocks` plus a points-allowed tier (0 → 10, ≤6 → 7, ≤13 → 4, ≤20 → 1, ≤27 → 0, ≤34 → −1, more → −4). The K/DEF SQL lives in `KICKING_POINTS_SQL` / `DEF_POINTS_SQL` / `DEF_STATS_JOIN_SQL` and is unified in `vw_fantasy_scores` and Napper's actual-score CTE (`server/napper_api.py`), so projections and fantasy scores agree.
    - `projected_points` = baseline × matchup factor. Baseline is the player's PPR per team game to date (team games with no stat line count as 0; the weeks are his current team's completed weeks plus every week he has a line, so a traded player keeps his old-team games and points, League Transactions §3.3e), shrunk toward a depth-chart prior by 0.25 pseudo-games; the prior is the league's PPR per team game for that depth slot (rank by OVR within team and group, capped at QB2/RB3/WR4/TE2/K1/DEF1). Matchup factor = (opponent's PPR allowed to the group, shrunk toward the league average by 16 pseudo-games, ÷ league average)^0.5; because D/ST points can be negative, the ratio is floored at `MIN_MATCHUP_RATIO = 0.25` and a league average ≤ 0 gives a neutral 1.0.
    - `avg_points` = PPR per appearance to date; `delta` = `projected_points − avg_points`.
    - `matchup_stars` = the opponent's PPR allowed per game to the group, split into five even groups (Postgres-style `NTILE(5)`) across the 32 defenses, 1 = toughest, 5 = easiest. Point-in-time and per game, so it can differ from `vw_fantasy_defense_vs_position` (season totals).
    - `pos_rank` ranks players with a game that week within QB/RB/WR/TE/K/DEF (RB = HB + FB), e.g. `RB12`, `K3`, `DEF7`. Players on bye get `projected_points` 0, NULL `pos_rank`/`matchup_stars`/`delta`, so they stay on the ROS board but drop out of that week's rankings. Active injuries (`weeks_remaining > 0` or `is_ir = true` in `injuries`) similarly zero out `projected_points` and set NULL `pos_rank`/`matchup_stars`/`delta`, with injured weeks excluded from `ros_total_points`.
    - `ros_total_points` = sum of the player's projections for that week through week 18 against each remaining opponent; `ros_rank` ranks it within the group.
    - **Released players** (`player_seasons.released_week` ≤ the week, §3.3e) have no team game: `projected_points` 0 like a bye, no depth slot (they don't shift the depth-chart priors), and no ROS weeks from the release on.
    - `adp_rank` is copied from the season's week 1 row so ROS `TREND` (`adp_rank − overall_ros_rank`) works.
    - **Accuracy (2035 backtest, weeks 2–17, depth-chart starters QB1/RB1–2/WR1–3/TE1):** MAE 3.29 PPR vs. 6.18 for guessing the league average; correlation 0.79. Almost all of it comes from the per-game average. Production here is very stable week to week; the matchup factor adds little, and recency weighting was tested and dropped. Check with `--backtest` (now includes K/DEF: 4,608 starter-weeks, MAE 3.25, correlation 0.805). K/DEF on their own are noisy: on 2036 weeks 2–4 they trail a league-average guess (K MAE 4.87 vs 4.13, DEF 5.23 vs 3.87), as expected with two or three games of data.
  - When a player has no stored row for the week, the player outlook (`GET /api/player/{id}`, §4.3) falls back to a rough estimate with no ranks.
- **Simulated fantasy leagues** (`engines/fantasy_league_sim.py`, `db/migrations/2026_10_21_fantasy_league_sim.sql`; design in `docs/done/FANTASY_EDITORIAL_MATRIX.md` §5). 100 leagues × 12 teams, full PPR, 15 rounds, lineup QB/2 RB/2 WR/TE/FLEX/K/DEF (9 starters: 7 skill players + 1 K + 1 DEF, 6 bench):
  - **Draft** (once per season, from `fantasy_adp_engine`; stored, so in-season OVR changes don't redraft): snake order. Each manager reads `draft_score` with personal noise (sd 1.2%) and values players over replacement (the 12th QB/TE/K/DEF, 30th RB/WR; QB value × 0.4, TE × 0.8, K × 0.25, DEF × 0.30), minus backup penalties (6 per QB, 10 per TE, 25 per K/DEF already rostered; RB/WR past five fade) and caps (`DRAFT_CAP`: QB/TE 2, RB/WR 7, K/DEF 1; `SEASON_CAP`: QB/TE 3, RB/WR 8, K/DEF 2); late picks are forced to fill an empty starting slot. K and DEF carry late-round gating (-35.0 before round 13) ensuring they are drafted in rounds 13–15. Strategy adjustments: `BPA` none; `HERO_RB` one RB in rounds 1–2 then none through round 5; `ZERO_RB` no RB before round 5; `RB_HEAVY` 2–3 RBs in rounds 1–4; `EARLY_QB` / `EARLY_TE` one in rounds 1–3. Seats draw strategies independently from the season mix.
  - **Strategy mix:** first season `DEFAULT_MIX` (BPA 35%, Hero RB 15%, Zero RB 15%, RB Heavy 15%, Early QB 10%, Early TE 10%). Later seasons: lift = title share ÷ manager share; new ∝ old × lift^0.5, blended 50/50 with the old mix, floor 5%.
  - **Season** (re-simulated from the stored draft on every run, seeded per season/league/week): lineups start the highest `projected_points` (week 1: best ADP); scores are actual PPR (`vw_fantasy_scores` including K and DEF); 12-team round robin weeks 1–14; seeds by wins then points for; 6-team playoffs (seeds 1–2 bye in week 15, semifinals week 16, final week 17; ties to the higher seed). Before each week, managers in reverse-standings order make up to 2 add/drops (each with probability = `activity`, 0.2–1.0) when a free agent's value beats the drop's by 15% + 1 point: value = `ros_total_points` scaled to the fantasy weeks left (playoff weeks: next game × weeks left; `ros_base`), × (1 + `reactivity` (0–0.5) × last week's PPR vs. his average, clamped −0.5..1; `hot_signal`). Napper's waiver run reuses `ros_base` and `hot_signal` and the same manager traits (§4.4b). They also stream any starting position (QB/RB/WR/TE/K/DEF) when no rostered player at that spot plays that week.
  - **`fantasy_sim_picks`**: `season`, `league`, `pick` (1–180), `round`, `team` (1–12 = draft slot), `player_id`. PK `(season, league, pick)`.
  - **`fantasy_sim_adp`**: `season`, `player_id`, `adp` (mean pick over 100 drafts; undrafted = pick 181), `min_pick`/`max_pick` (drafted leagues only; NULL if never drafted), `draft_pct`. Every board player (QB/HB/WR/TE/K/DEF) has a row.
  - **`fantasy_sim_player_weeks`**: `season`, `week` (rosters/lineups going into that week), `player_id`, `rostered_pct`, `started_pct` (NULL for a week without projections). Only players on at least one roster. Rewritten on every run.
  - **`fantasy_sim_teams`**: per league seat: `strategy`, `activity`, `reactivity`, `wins`/`losses`/`ties`, `points_for`/`points_against`, `seed` (after week 14), `playoff_finish` (`CHAMPION`, `RUNNER_UP`, `SEMIFINAL`, `QUARTERFINAL`, `MISSED`), `final_rank` (1–12 once week 17 is final).
  - **`fantasy_sim_strategy_mix`**: per season and strategy: `share` (target mix), `managers` (seats drawn), and once week 17 is final `titles`, `playoff_teams`, `avg_points_for` (regular season). Feeds the next season's mix; not published in articles.
  - 2035 (first run, drafted from end-of-season ratings): ADP 1 Trey'Mane Davis 1.8 (range 1–6); titles BPA 33, Zero RB 24, Early QB 20, Hero RB 14, RB Heavy 8, Early TE 1. A full season simulates in about 3 seconds.
- **`vw_fantasy_scores` (View)**:
  - `game_id`, `player_name`, `team_id`, `season`, `week`, `ppr_score`, `player_id`. Unifies offensive skill players (`player_stats`), kickers (`game_stat_kicking` with yardage-based fractional scoring: min 3 for <30 yds, 3.x, 4.x, 5.x), and team defenses (`player_seasons` DEF with sacks, turnovers, safeties, blocks, defensive/return TDs, and points-allowed tiers).
- **`vw_fantasy_defense_vs_position` (View)**:
  - Aggregates PPR fantasy points conceded by each defensive team per position across completed games.
  - Dynamically calculates:
    - `total_allowed`, `avg_allowed`
    - `min_allowed`, `max_allowed`, `league_avg_allowed`
    - `matchup_stars`: `NTILE(5) OVER (PARTITION BY season, position ORDER BY total_allowed ASC)::numeric`.

### 3.4b Napper Interactive Fantasy Platform (`db/migrations/2026_12_02_napper_fantasy.sql`)
- **League history and restart** (`2027_01_04_napper_lineage.sql`, `docs/done/SEASON_CONTINUITY_PLAN.md` phase 3; JR 2026-10-26: one-season redraft, history kept): `napper_leagues.previous_league_id` (FK self, ON DELETE SET NULL; at most one successor), `lineage_id` (the lineage's first league, backfilled to `id`), `completed_at`, and status `COMPLETE`; `napper_teams.playoff_finish` (`CHAMPION` | `RUNNER_UP` | `SEMIFINAL` | `QUARTERFINAL` | `MISSED`) and `final_rank` (1 = champion). When the Week 17 final is decided, `napper_playoffs.complete_league` freezes each team's regular-season record, points, seed, finish and rank (`final_ranks`: by finish, then seed) and marks the league `COMPLETE` (week 17), so an old season reads the same after the NFL rollover. The weekly lineup, waiver and trade engines only run `IN_SEASON` leagues. Applied 2026-10-27 after backup `madden_backup_20261027_040330.sql`; leagues 1, 2 and 15 (Teen Titans) completed then.
Multi-league interactive Sleeper-style fantasy ecosystem supporting real-time matchups, AI trade negotiations, free agency waivers, and autonomous manager chat banter:
- **`napper_user_profiles`**:
  - `id` (SERIAL PK), `handle` (varchar(32) UNIQUE, e.g. `@jrereyi2000`), `display_name` (varchar(64)), `avatar_url` (text), `trophies` (int DEFAULT 0), `created_at` (timestamptz).
- **`napper_leagues`**:
  - `id` (SERIAL PK), `name` (varchar(64)), `season` (int; Napper-created leagues use the active `league_state.current_season`), `teams_count` (smallint DEFAULT 8), `scoring_type` (varchar(16) DEFAULT 'PPR'), `roster_format` (jsonb DEFAULT standard 1-QB slots: `{"QB": 1, "RB": 2, "WR": 2, "TE": 1, "FLEX": 1, "SUPERFLEX": 0, "K": 1, "DEF": 1, "BN": 6, "IR": 1}`; Superflex is included only when configured; `IR` = injured-reserve slots, added to every league by `2026_12_04_napper_ir_slot.sql`), `current_week` (int; new in-season leagues use `league_state.current_week`), `status` (varchar(16) DEFAULT 'IN_SEASON'), `avatar_url` (text), `is_seed` (boolean DEFAULT FALSE; seed leagues are excluded from the active league list), `champion_team_id` (FK `napper_teams(id)` ON DELETE SET NULL; set when the week 17 final is decided, `2026_12_06_napper_playoffs.sql`).
- **`napper_teams`**:
  - `id` (SERIAL PK), `league_id` (FK `napper_leagues(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE), `user_id` (FK `napper_user_profiles(id)` ON DELETE SET NULL, NULL for AI teams), `team_name` (varchar(64)), `manager_handle` (varchar(32)), `avatar_url` (text), `is_ai` (boolean DEFAULT FALSE), `persona` (varchar(32), e.g. `USER`, `TRASH_TALKER`, `ANALYTICS_NERD`, `WAIVER_HAWK`, `DIE_HARD`, `ZERO_RB_ZEALOT`, `HERO_RB`, `TRADE_FIEND`, `UNDERDOG`), `wins` (int DEFAULT 0), `losses` (int DEFAULT 0), `ties` (int DEFAULT 0), `points_for` (numeric(8,2) DEFAULT 0), `points_against` (numeric(8,2) DEFAULT 0), `seed` (smallint).
- **`napper_rosters`**:
  - `id` (SERIAL PK), `league_id` (FK `napper_leagues(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE), `team_id` (FK `napper_teams(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE), `week` (int NOT NULL), `player_id` (FK `players(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE), `slot` (varchar(16) NOT NULL, e.g. `QB`, `RB`, `WR`, `TE`, `FLEX`, `SUPERFLEX`, `K`, `DEF`, `BN`, `IR`). `BN` and `IR` don't start or score; `IR` players are also left out of trades and of the matchup view. Unique constraint: `UNIQUE(team_id, week, player_id)`.
- **`napper_matchups`**:
  - `playoff_round` (varchar(16), `2026_12_06_napper_playoffs.sql`): `QUARTERFINAL` (week 15), `SEMIFINAL` (16), `FINAL` (17), NULL in the regular season. Playoff-week rows are written only by `engines/napper_playoffs.sync_playoffs`; teams outside the bracket have no matchup in weeks 15–17.
  - `id` (SERIAL PK), `league_id` (FK `napper_leagues(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE), `week` (int NOT NULL), `home_team_id` (FK `napper_teams(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE), `away_team_id` (FK `napper_teams(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE), `home_score` (numeric(6,2) DEFAULT 0), `away_score` (numeric(6,2) DEFAULT 0), `home_proj` (numeric(6,2) DEFAULT 0), `away_proj` (numeric(6,2) DEFAULT 0), `win_prob_home` (numeric(4,3) DEFAULT 0.500), `is_final` (boolean DEFAULT FALSE).
- **`napper_trades`**:

Standalone mock drafts are client-side only and are not written to `napper_drafts` or `napper_draft_picks`; their picks are saved when the user creates a league.
- **`napper_draft_picks`**:
  - `id` (SERIAL PK), `draft_id` (FK `napper_drafts(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE), `round_num` (int NOT NULL), `pick_num` (int NOT NULL), `overall_pick` (int NOT NULL), `team_id` (FK `napper_teams(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE, nullable for mock drafts), `team_name` (varchar(64)), `slot_num` (int NOT NULL), `player_id` (FK `players(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE, nullable until selected), `picked_by` (varchar(16) DEFAULT 'AI' — `USER`, `AI`, `AUTO`), `pick_notes` (text), `created_at` (timestamptz DEFAULT NOW()). Unique constraint: `UNIQUE(draft_id, overall_pick)`.
- **Waivers** (`db/migrations/2026_12_05_napper_waivers.sql`, used by `engines/napper_waiver_engine.py`):
  - **`napper_waiver_claims`**: `id` (SERIAL PK), `league_id` (FK, CASCADE), `team_id` (FK `napper_teams`, CASCADE), `add_player_id` (FK `players`), `drop_player_id` (FK `players`, nullable), `rank` (smallint; the team's preference order among its pending claims), `status` (`PENDING`, `WON`, `LOST`, `INVALID`, `CANCELLED`), `reason` (`CLAIM` for the user's claims; AI pickups `NEED`, `STREAM`, `UPGRADE`), `note` (why a claim was lost or invalid), `week` (the waiver run that decided it), `created_at`, `processed_at`. The user's claims on players on waivers wait as `PENDING`; AI pickups are logged as `WON` when a run makes them.
  - **`napper_waiver_wire`**: players on waivers, i.e. dropped since the last run: `league_id`, `player_id` (PK together), `dropped_by_team_id`, `clears_week` (the run that decides them; unclaimed, they become free agents then), `dropped_at`.
  - **`napper_waiver_runs`**: one row per completed run, `(league_id, week)` PK, `priority` (int[]; team ids in claim order), `processed_at`. A re-run of the same week is skipped.

### 3.6 Triggers
- **`trigger_update_team_records`** (`AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON games`, function `update_team_records()`): on insert, or when `status`/scores change, recomputes both teams' `wins`/`losses` for that season from completed **regular-season** games and upserts them into `team_seasons` (playoff games don't count; `2026_11_04_playoff_games.sql`). Seasons before 2035 hold only their Super Bowl, so their stored records still show that one game until a row of theirs changes.
- **`trigger_sync_season_stats_team`** (`AFTER UPDATE OF team_id ON player_seasons`, function `sync_team_to_season_stats()`): when a player's team changes, moves their `season_stats` rows for that season (team NULL or the old team) to the new team, merging counters into an existing new-team row where one exists.

### 3.3y Press Conferences (`db/migrations/2027_01_20_press_conferences.sql`, also in `db/init_db.sql`; `newsroom/press_room.py`, §7.14)

Idempotent, seeds nothing. `press_conferences`: `id`, `season`, `week`, `game_id`/`team_id` FKs (CASCADE), `subject_type` coach|player, `subject_id`, `subject_name`, `controller` USER|AGENT, `status` SCHEDULED|LIVE|REVIEW|CLOSED|DECLINED|FAILED, `end_reason` RAN_OUT|SUBJECT_ENDED|PATIENCE|CAP|DECLINED, `interest`, `tier`, `cast_inputs`, `facts` (the frozen fact sheet), `patience` (budget/spent/mood plus the session scratch keys: the drafted hands, round, picks and per-reporter counters), `model`, `calls`/`input_tokens`/`output_tokens`, `effects_applied`, timestamps; UNIQUE (game_id, team_id, subject_type, subject_id); index `idx_press_conferences_week (season, week, status)`. `press_attendees` PK (conference_id, agent_id): person_key, role BEAT|NATIONAL, pool_tier, questions/passes/done, hands/picked, judgment JSONB. `press_hands` PK (conference_id, round, agent_id): picked, pick_source AGENT|USER|FALLBACK. `press_turns`: id, conference_id, seq (UNIQUE per conference), speaker REPORTER|SUBJECT, agent_id, kind OPENING|QUESTION|FOLLOW_UP|REACT|ANSWER|NO_COMMENT|CLOSING|NOTE, reply_to, text, about JSONB, tone, source AGENT|USER|FALLBACK|ENGINE, issues JSONB, retries, on_record, created_at. `agent_memory_entries.kind` gains `'PRESS'` rows written by `close_effects`. Every reader in `press_room` guards with `to_regclass('press_conferences')`.

### 3.3z NFLPA Report Cards (`db/migrations/2027_02_08_nflpa_report_cards.sql`, also in `db/init_db.sql`; §2.17h)
Idempotent, seeds nothing; requires `teams`. `owner_cash_ledgers` PK (season, team_id): the owner's annual cash pool outside the cap — `wealth_band` (TIER_1..TIER_4), `base_budget`, `success_dividend`, `total_cash_budget`, `staff_payroll`, `opex_committed`, `capex_spent`, `dead_buyouts` (this season's instalments of the team's staff buyouts, `2027_02_19`/`2027_02_20`), `accumulated_reserve`. `team_report_cards` PK (season, team_id): the eight VARCHAR(2) category grades, `overall_score` NUMERIC(4,3), `overall_grade`, `summary_text`, `last_renovated_season`. `facility_upgrades`: id, team_id, season_ordered, category, cost_dollars, target_grade, completion_season, status (IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/CANCELLED). `team_operating_policies`: team_id PK, luxury_travel_enabled, no_roommate_policy, family_daycare_enabled, private_chef_program, annual_opex_cost, updated_at.

## 4. Backend Architecture (`server/api.py` - FastAPI)

The backend operates on Python 3.11+ using FastAPI, `uvicorn`, and `psycopg` (connection pooling with `dict_row`).

### 4.1 System & Schedules
- `GET /api/status`: Returns current league season and week from `league_state`, and `last_updated` (the latest `captures.loaded_at` of a loaded run; the Stats page's "Updated" stamp, hidden when null).
- `GET /api/schedule?season={season}&week={week}`:
  - Returns matchups for the week, records, kickoff times, home/away TWI (`home_twi`, `away_twi`), combined matchup `watchability`, and `excitement_index` on the 70–100 display scale. That is the final $E$ for completed games and the projection otherwise; `excitement_projected` is true for projections, and the value is null if a game hasn't been projected yet.
- `GET /api/standings/{season}`:
  - Division and conference standings, wins, losses, win percentage, streak, points for/against, and last 5 games.
- `GET /api/power_rankings?season={season}&week={week}`:
  - Stored weekly Power Rankings (7.6): `season`, `week`, `available_weeks`, the source `article` (`id`, `headline`, `excerpt`, `persona`, `created_at`), and `rankings` ordered 1–32 (`rank`, `previous_rank`, `movement`, `record`, `kicker`, `blurb`, `team_id`, `abbr`, `name`, `city`, `team_color`, `conference`, `division`). `season` defaults to the current season and `week` to its latest stored week; a week with no stored ranking returns an empty `rankings` list. The same article is also served by `GET /api/news/week/{week}` in `slotted.standalone`.

### 4.2 Team & Roster Hubs
- `GET /api/team/{abbr}?season={season}`: Team metadata (record, overall/offensive/defensive ratings, team color) and the season's `roster` (id, full name, jersey number, ESPN id, position, experience, OVR; best OVR first). A released player (`released_week` set; he keeps his old `team_id`) is left out; a signing elsewhere, or by the same team again, clears `released_week` and lists him on his new team. The fantasy D/ST row (`position = 'DEF'`, e.g. "Bengals D/ST") isn't a player and is left out too. `season` defaults to `league_state.current_season`.
- `GET /api/team/{abbr}/schedule?season={season}`: Full 18-week schedule with completed scores and upcoming dates.
- History seasons (2026–2034) on `GET /api/standings/{season}`, `GET /api/stats/player` and `GET /api/stats/team` come from the reconstructed history (§3.3l).
- `GET /api/team/{abbr}/history`: the Team hub's History tab (§3.3l): `{seasons: [{season, wins, losses, ties, points_for, points_against, division_place, conference_seed, playoff_result, playoff_wins, playoff_losses, source, coach_name, gm_name, history, in_progress?, awards: [{award, name}]}], summary: {since, wins, losses, playoffs, titles, super_bowls}, nfl_seasons}`. `nfl_seasons`: the franchise's real NFL seasons 1999–2025 (`read.team_nfl_seasons`, §3.3x: record, points, division place, seed, playoff result, head coach, the team's award winners), newest first, `[]` without the tables; `summary` stays league-only.
- `GET /api/team/{abbr}/news?season={season}&limit={limit}`: Returns news articles and beat coverage specifically tagged for or assigned to a franchise (`article_teams` join or `news_feed.team_id`), prioritized by `mention_type` (`PRIMARY` > `FEATURED` > `MENTIONED`) and week recency, while strictly excluding opposing teams' beat reporters (`WHERE NOT (n.persona = 'LOCAL_BEAT_REPORTER' AND n.team_id IS DISTINCT FROM %s)`). When `limit` is omitted, all articles written for the franchise across the entire season are returned (powering the horizontally scrollable season feed). Author display names correctly reflect the author's franchise for beat writers. If the team's local beat hasn't been woken for the current week (no article filed under the team with a `Local Beat N` slot that week; national primers use `Slot 6–8` and don't count), it starts the on-demand local swarm wakeup (`SwarmDispatcher.dispatch_team_local`, `live=True`, `save_to_db=True`) in a background thread via `start_local_wakeup` (the check is `maybe_start_team_wakeup`, shared with the Agent Wire Team Hub) and returns the existing feed immediately; the new beat reports and the team's Agent Wire posts appear on a later load. Each (team, season, week) is attempted at most once every `LOCAL_WAKEUP_RETRY_SECONDS` (600s), which covers a run in progress and keeps repeat views from re-triggering a failed one. `NEWSROOM_AUTO_LOCAL_WAKEUP=0` disables it.
- `GET /api/team/{id}/season_stats/{season}`: Aggregated season totals (passing yards, rushing yards, points per game, points allowed per game).
- `GET /api/team/{abbr}/front-office?season={season}` (`server/front_office_api.py`, read-only): the Front Office tab. `season` defaults to `league_state.current_season`; `ARI`/`WSH` aliases resolve; an unknown team is 404. Returns `{season, team {id, name, abbreviation}, year_columns (season … season+4), cap, contracts, committed, transactions, draft_picks, staff, staff_contracts}` as raw whole-dollar numbers, from the writer tools' own fetches (`fetch_cap_rows`, `fetch_team_contracts` in `newsroom/db_tools.py`), so the page and the writers read the same books. `cap`: cap, adjusted cap, cap space with `cap_space_rank` of `teams` (1 = most space), salaries, `dead_money` (`cap_penalty`), total spend, next rookie reserve, `estimated` (moves applied since the last scan) and its `basis` text (`roster_moves.cap_basis`). `contracts` (ACTIVE only, largest this-season hit first): player, position, length, years remaining, `through`, `expiring` (contract year), `cap_hit` this season, total value, bonus, cut savings, `cut_penalty` (dead money if cut), no-trade clause, incentive flag, `source` (`SCAN` / `TRANSACTION`), `basis`, every year's `{year, cap_hit, projected}` and `new_deal {years, total_value, starts}` for a re-signing or extension. A term not recorded stays `null` (never 0). `committed`: per year column, the scanned hits and projected new-deal hits summed apart, plus the number of players under contract. `transactions` (`fetch_moves` / `fetch_trades` with no article cutoff, so every loaded move of the season shows): `moves`, the team's League Transactions rows (trade legs left out), newest week first and offseason rows last, each `{id, week, type, direction ('in' / 'out' for a release), player_id, name, position, from_team (a signing's old team), contract_years, contract_value, dead_money (a release's stored cut penalty), depth_slot, is_starter, practice_squad, new_deal_start, later_team / later_week (a released player signed elsewhere), notable (`roster_moves.notability`)}`; and `trades`, the executed GM trades this team was in, newest first, from its side: `{proposal_id, week, partner, received, sent}`, each leg a player `{player_id, name, position, cap_hit}` or a pick `{draft_season, round, original_team}`. Only the assets are served, not the GMs' rationale or headline. `draft_picks` (needs the GM migration): `{drafts (the next 3), picks}`, every unused `draft_picks` row of those drafts the team owns or originally held: `{draft_season, round, overall_pick, original_team, owner_team, status (OWN / ACQUIRED / TRADED_AWAY), source, trade_week (the GM trade that moved it)}`. `staff` (`fetch_staff`; null without a head coach): `head_coach` (with `id`, `coaches.id`) from `engines/coach_profile.coach_profile` (every completed game visible, this season's awards not): `{name, slant, since, season_with_team, replaced {coach, seasons}, offense, defensive_front, tendencies {pass_lean / fourth_down_aggressiveness / man_coverage: {tier, meaning (TENDENCY_WORDS), measured (true when measured in this league, else the real-world tier or reputation)}}, this_season, record_with_team / playoff_record_with_team with record_with_team_since (counted from 2026, the first season with coach lines, when the tenure began earlier; null only when a season since isn't on record), career with career_scope (`full career` or `since joining this league`), super_bowls_with_team, coach_of_the_year}`; `coordinators` (OC then DC, the latest open tenure per role) `{role, id (coordinators.id), name (null for an offseason stand-in, PLACEHOLDER_COORDINATOR), scheme, playbook, since}`; with the GM migration, `gm` `{id (gm_profiles.id), name, bio, since, head_coach_too (gm_profiles.coach_id set: full control)}`, `direction` (CONTEND / RETOOL / REBUILD), `needs` (the top 3 of `gm_team_seasons.needs`, `{group, label, reasons}` with reasons in words for each component above zero: thin at the starting spots, injuries, expiring deals) and `urgent_need` `{group, label}`. No direction or need scores, persona dials, fo_quality / dev_quality / hot-seat numbers, or user control are served. `staff_contracts` (needs the staff-contracts migration): the team's active staff contracts (`remaining_years > 0`) in HC, GM, OC, DC order, each `{person_id (polymorphic by person_kind: HC→coaches.id, GM→gm_profiles.id, OC/DC→coordinators.id), person_kind, name (read from that role's own table — `coach_name` / `gm_name` / `coordinator_name`, so an OC and a DC cost one read — and null when the person row is gone), annual_salary, total_years, remaining_years, signed_season, full_control}`; `null` when the table is absent or no rows remain. A block is `null` when its tables don't exist (or, for cap and contracts, have no rows). Nothing from the GM queue (proposals, rumors, front-office scores) is served. Tests: `tests/test_front_office_api.py` (pure shaping of contracts, cap, moves and trades from either side; the endpoint tests only read the live database and skip when Postgres is down: sort orders, no trade legs among moves, 7 own-or-traded picks per draft, the staff block's keys carry no scores).
- `POST /api/team/{abbr}/staff/offer` `{person_kind (HC/GM/OC/DC), person_id, annual_salary, total_years, full_control? (default false), signed_season? (defaults to the current season)}` → `{team, season, contract {person_id, person_kind, annual_salary, total_years, remaining_years, signed_season, full_control}}`: validates (unknown kind, non-positive salary or length, or full control on a non-HC offer → 400), inserts an active `staff_contracts` row (`remaining_years = total_years`), and on a full-control head-coach offer enforces the Godfather rarity gate (`staff_contracts_engine.godfather_gate`: fewer than 2 active full-control coaches and ≥ 5 seasons since the last offer, else 409). 409 when the migration isn't applied or `league_state` has no season. Tests: `tests/test_staff_contracts_api.py`.

- `GET /api/team/{abbr}/report-card?season={season}` (`server/front_office_api.py`, NFLPA_REPORT_CARD_PLAN U3, read-only): `season` defaults to `league_state.current_season`; ARI/WSH aliases resolve; unknown team 404. Returns `{season, team {id, name, abbreviation}, cards (the team's team_report_cards, newest season first: the eight category grades, overall_score, overall_grade, summary_text), current (the season's card), rank {rank (1 = best overall score, ties share), percentile (share of the league at or below, 0–100), teams} for the season, policies {luxury_travel, family_daycare, private_chef, annual_opex_cost}, upgrades (open IN_PROGRESS facility_upgrades)}`. Every block is null when its table isn't applied or has no rows (a grade is never invented). `POST /api/team/{abbr}/facilities/upgrade` `{category (one of the eight), tier (MINOR $5M / STANDARD $12M / OVERHAUL $25M)}` → `{team, season, order {id, season_ordered, category, cost_dollars, target_grade, completion_season, status IN_PROGRESS}}`: validates, reads the current card and the owner cash ledger (`total_cash_budget − capex_spent − staff_payroll − opex_committed − dead_buyouts` must cover the cost, else 409; a database without the buyout migration reads `dead_buyouts` as 0 rather than failing), inserts a `facility_upgrades` row completing season + 1. `POST /api/team/{abbr}/facilities/policy` `{policy (luxury_travel / family_daycare / private_chef), enabled}` → `{team, season, policy, enabled, annual_opex_cost, policies, category, grade, overall_score, overall_grade}`: upserts `team_operating_policies` (toggle + summed annual opex cost), checks the same owner cash ledger when the toggles add cost (`total_cash_budget − capex_spent − staff_payroll − opex_committed − dead_buyouts` must cover the increase, else 409), and, when enabling, applies the immediate grade effect to the current card (raises to target, never lowers; a disable leaves the current card alone). 409 when the migration, card or ledger is missing. Tests: `tests/test_report_card_api.py`.

### 4.3 Player Analytics, Global Search & Modal Overlays
- `GET /api/search?q={query}&season={season}&limit={limit}`:
  - Global search endpoint across all 32 NFL franchises and players for the main site search bar (`GlobalSearchModal`, keyboard shortcut ⌘K / Ctrl+K).
  - Teams match on name, city, abbreviation, or combined city + name; returns team logo, full name, division, and abbreviation.
  - Players match on full name; returns player ID, name, position, overall rating, jersey number, team abbreviation, team name, and ESPN ID.
- `GET /api/player/{id}?season={season}`:
  - `nfl_career`: the player's real NFL career through 2025 (`read.player_nfl_career`, §3.3x: REG seasons newest first with `team_abbr` and `mu_team`, `postseason`, `totals`, `postseason_totals`, `awards`, `draft`), null when he isn't linked or the tables are missing; read last in the request. `career_stats` / `career_totals` stay league-only.
  - Player personal information and ratings. Decoupled base player query gracefully falls back to historical `season_stats` or the player's most recent roster record when queried with a season prior to entry, preventing "Player not found" errors on past seasons.
  - Full 18-week `game_log` (accounting for bye weeks and completed game fantasy statistics). Switching `gameLogSeason` in `PlayerPage` immediately re-fetches the game log for that season.
  - Multi-season `career_stats` with games played, yards, touchdowns, and overall fantasy rank, plus each season's `season_stat_lines` defense (`def_*`), kicking (`kick_*`), punting (`punt_*`), returns (`kr_*`, `pr_*`) and `blk_sacks_allowed` with `has_capture_line`. Merges historical entries from `season_stats` (e.g. 2034, 2033, 2032) so past season totals appear in Career Stats.
  - Interactive season selection: on `PlayerPage`, selecting a season from the Game Log dropdown or clicking any row in the Career Stats table immediately switches the active season, updating the hero highlight card and game log.
  - `articles`: up to six newsroom articles that mention the player (`article_players`, the entity tagger's PRIMARY / FEATURED / MENTIONED tags), newest first, with id, season, week, headline, excerpt, short type label (the `article_types.json` name without a leading "The" or trailing parenthetical) and author display name. Opposing teams' beat reporters are strictly excluded so only national coverage and the player's own franchise beat writers appear. The player page's Player Coverage list shows them (linking to `#article-{id}`) and is hidden when there are none.
  - `stat_group`: `passing` (QB), `rushing` (HB/FB), `receiving` (WR/TE), `blocking` (OL), `kicking` (K), `punting` (P, LS) or `defense`. The player page (`PlayerPage`) uses it for its season card, game-log and career columns (defenders: tackles, sacks, TFL, INT, PD, FF, TD; kickers: FG, long, 50+, XP; punters: punts, average, net, inside the 20; linemen: sacks allowed), shows "—" for a game or season with no recorded line, and names every position (`POSITION_LABELS`).
  - `awards`: every stored award for the player (`history_api.fetch_player_awards`: year-end awards, SB MVP, First/Second Team All-Pro), `{season, award_type, position, team}` newest first; the player page's Honors row (§5.2 item 13). Empty without the `awards` table.
  - `weekly_outlook` for the league's current week (`league_state.current_week`): opponent, home/away, kickoff, `projection`, `pos_rank`/`ecr_rank`, `ros_rank` and 1–5 `stars`, all from that week's `fantasy_projections` row (`projected: true`).
    - **Bye:** if the league plays that week but the player's team doesn't, it returns `bye: true`, `projection` "0.0", the stored `ros_rank`, and null ranks/stars (no opponent fields). The modal shows a "BYE WEEK" card.
    - **No stored row** (e.g. week 1): `projection` is a rough estimate (season PPR average × 0.85–1.15 by matchup stars), `projected: false`, and the ranks are null. The modal shows "—" rather than a rank.
    - If the season has no games in the current week (e.g. viewing a past season), it uses the team's last game of that season and that week's projection row.
- `GET /api/stats/player?season={season}&category={category}&season_type={regular|postseason}`:
  - `season_type` (default `regular`) filters games on `game_type` (`season_type_filter`): regular season only, or every non-`REGULAR_SEASON` game. For the regular season the defense, special-teams, Downs and Red Zone Defense tables come from Madden's Season Stats / Team Stats screens; for the postseason they sum the season's captured playoff box scores instead (`POSTSEASON_LINES` over `game_stat_lines` in `player_st_leaders(..., postseason=True)`; `team_situational_postseason` over real `team_stats` values). A playoff box score has conversions but no attempts and penalty yards but no count, so postseason Downs returns only 3D CONV, 4D CONV, 2PT, RZ ATT, RZ TD, RZ TD% and PEN YDS (null where a game didn't record one), and the page shows only those columns (`postseasonStatColumns`, filtered to what the API returned).
  - Passing, Rushing, Receiving and Scoring player leaderboards, summed from the player's `player_stats` game lines by `player_id` (a traded player's lines for every team), shown under the season's team.
  - Defense (Tackles, Sacks, Interceptions) and special teams (Kicking, Punting, Kick Returns, Punt Returns) from `season_stat_lines` (`PLAYER_ST_CATEGORIES` / `player_st_leaders` in `server/api.py`): Madden's listed leaders only, shown under the season's team.
- `GET /api/game/{id}`: the game with both teams' records, `stats` (each `player_stats` line), `team_stats` and, from `game_stat_lines`, `defense` (every defender with a line: tackles, sacks, TFL, INT, PD, FF, FR, TD; biggest playmakers first), `kicking` and `punting` (empty for games whose player stats weren't captured). `team_stats` rows go through `real_team_stats`: a field in `estimated_fields` is blanked unless it is in `exact_fields` (the writers' box-score rule), `box_score_captured` says whether the row came from a captured box score, and without one `first_downs` (a backfill 0) is blanked; `total_plays` is never captured and always blank. The estimator's arrays aren't returned.
- **Season and week defaults:** every endpoint whose `season` / `week` is omitted uses `league_state` (`season_week()` in `server/api.py`): the current season, and for it the current week; another season's default week is 18. Players on the game page (`GET /api/game/{id}`), the player page's game log and career, and the fantasy rankings, search and dashboard finishes are joined on `player_stats.player_id`, never by name.
- `GET /api/stats/team?season={season}&category={category}&season_type={regular|postseason}`:
  - Team leaderboards for the same four categories, summed from `team_stats` over completed games, plus `Downs` (third/fourth-down conversions and rates, two-point tries, red-zone trips/TDs/TD rate, penalties and yards) and `Red Zone Defense` (points allowed and per game, red-zone trips/TDs/FGs allowed, TD and scoring rate allowed) from the `team_seasons` Team Stats totals (`team_situational_table`).

### 4.4 Fantasy Analytics Endpoints
- `GET /api/fantasy/dashboard?season={season}&week={week}`:
  - **Articles:** `hero` and `articles` (the 3 front-page cards) come from the stored Mu Fantasy slate (`news_feed`, `article_type` `FANTASY_*`) for the week shown: the requested week, weeks after 18 show Week 18, and a week without a slate shows the latest earlier one (`articles_week`). Each card: `id`, `slot`, `label` (article type name), `title`, `excerpt`, `author` (agent display name, else `fantasy_writers.json`), `time` (~230 words/min), `updated`, `team` (most-tagged team, lower-case, or null). `more_analysis_count` = shelf articles behind "View all". With no stored slate, `articles_source` is `placeholder` and the old placeholder hero/cards are returned.
  - Top 3 marquee games (`excitement_games`). These are ranked by editorial interest: raw (projected) $E$, +3 for a division game, and +2 per team not yet mathematically eliminated (regular season). This is the same `rank_games_by_interest` used for matchup-primer picks. Each game has `score` (display scale), `projected`, and a `note` such as "Week 18 · Projected · Division game · Playoff race".
  - Waiver wire trends, weekly projections, preseason ADP movers, and rest-of-season rank snapshots. The ADP card reads only week 1 rows with a `player_id` (later weeks carry a copy of `adp_rank`).
  - **Social takes** (`social_takes`): the requested week's 3 most-liked Agent Wire posts by the fantasy accounts (The Flex Spot, Berry, Yates), no replies or shares (`social_api.fantasy_takes`): `{id, quote, author, handle, tag}`, where `tag` is the subject player's team and position ("MIN • WR") or the post type ("START / SIT"). Empty when the week has none.
- `GET /api/fantasy/articles?season={season}&week={week}`: every Mu Fantasy article for the week shown (same week rule as the dashboard): `front_page` (Hero, Fantasy 1–3) and `more_analysis` (shelf, in order), cards as above, plus `available_weeks` (weeks with a fantasy slate) and `week` (null when none). Article text comes from `GET /api/news/article/{id}`.
- `GET /api/fantasy/rankings/weekly?season={season}&week={week}&position={pos}&limit={limit}`:
  - `mode`: `final` when every game that week is completed (ranked by actual PPR points), otherwise `projected` from that week's `fantasy_projections` rows (players on bye are excluded), and `unavailable` if neither exists.
  - Dynamic positional ranking (`pos_rank` e.g. `QB1`, `RB1`).
  - Prior-week positional finish comparison (`trend`).
  - Exact 1–5 matchup stars.
  - FLEX view strictly excludes QBs and presents a dedicated `POS` column.
- `GET /api/fantasy/rankings/ros?season={season}&position={pos}&limit={limit}`:
  - Rest-of-season consensus rankings ordered by `ros_total_points DESC`.
  - Columns: `RANK`, `PLAYER`, `ROS RANK` (on FLEX), `SEASON SOS` (1–5 stars), `PLAYOFF SOS` (Weeks 15–17, 1–5 stars), `PROJECTED ROS FPTS`, and `TREND` (`adp_rank - overall_ros_rank`).
- `GET /api/fantasy/rankings/adp?season={season}&position={pos}&limit={limit}`:
  - Consensus preseason draft board ordered by `adp_rank ASC`.
  - Columns: `RANK`, `PLAYER`, `POSITION` (positional rank ordered by ADP, e.g. first RB is `RB1`, first WR is `WR1`), `TEAM (BYE)` (e.g. `CAR (12)`), `SEASON SOS`, and `PLAYOFF SOS`.
  - Position filter and week selectors omitted for an unobstructed full-draft view.
- `GET /api/fantasy/players?season={season}&min_points={min_points}&q={query}`:
  - Returns fantasy skill players (`QB`, `HB`, `FB`, `WR`, `TE`, `K`) for the season, left-joining completed games and projections so that in preseason or unplayed weeks, players are returned with projected fantasy points rather than being dropped.
  - Powers zero-latency client search in `FantasyHeader`, supporting keyboard shortcuts (⌘K), outside click dismissal, and Enter key selection.
- **Agent Wire** (`server/social_api.py`, §7.8). Only posts written by the social desk (with an `agent_id`) are served. `season` defaults to `league_state.current_season`; `week` to the latest week with posts. A post is `{id, season, week, kind, kind_label, text, posted_at, likes, reposts, replies (simulated + real), real_replies, views, hashtags, team_abbr, local, subject_game_id, subject_player_id, author {agent_id, handle, display_name, archetype, label, team_abbr, team_color, followers}, reply_to {id, handle, display_name} | null, article {id, headline, excerpt, article_type} | null}`.
  - `GET /api/social/feed?season&week&tab=foryou|latest&team={ABBR}&trend={KIND:KEY}&limit=30&offset=0`: the week's top-level posts (no replies).
