The sidebar Power Rankings card shows the top 3 from `GET /api/power_rankings` (latest stored week), or a placeholder when none is stored.
8. **Team & League Logos**:
   - Pulls high-resolution official SVG/PNG logos from ESPN's global CDN (`https://a.espncdn.com/i/teamlogos/nfl/500/${abbr}.png`), normalized across all 32 franchises.
9. **Napper Interactive Multi-League Experience (`NapperPage`, `src/components/napper/`)**:
   - Sleeper-inspired dark theme interface (`src/napper.css`: `#121926` background, `#1a2332` panels, `#00ceb8` cyan accents) featuring a 3-panel layout:
     - **Left Rail**: Single "Back to Home" button above direct navigation, league switcher with user/opponent live scores, league records (a `COMPLETE` league reads "Season complete"), a **restart card** above the list for each finished league of an earlier NFL season ("Start the new season" → `POST /restart`, then the new league's draft room), and user profile card (`@jrereyi2000`, trophies counted from championships won, pending trades badge).
   - **Center Stage**: 5 interactive tabs:
       - `MATCHUP`: After a player's game is final, his card shows the result line and box score under his name instead of kickoff/opponent (`PostGameLine`, starters and bench; also on the `TEAM` tab), and his projection turns teal when he beat it, red when he fell short (`projClass`). Split head-to-head comparison from the selected league's saved rosters, with slots derived from `roster_format`, actual weekly points, active-season projections, NFL opponent/kickoff/status, season records, team points share (projections before games begin, actual points once scoring starts), and configured bench slots. Standard leagues omit `SUPERFLEX`. Selecting a player opens the same hero and sticky anchor tabs as the Mu Fantasy Analytics player modal with continuous Game Logs, Season Stats, and Outlook sections (no Latest News tab/section), recolored for Napper and populated by `GET /api/player/{player_id}`.
       - `TEAM`: The active user's actual league roster with player-specific headshots, game details, and weekly points, without projected-point labels or a lineup optimizer. Starters, bench, then an Injured Reserve section (empty IR slots included; a healthy player left in IR is labeled "Healthy"). An amber banner lists starters who won't score that week (injured or on bye) and suggests a swap or IR move; the lineup is never changed automatically. Click-to-swap starter/bench/IR assignments use atomic server validation (IR moves only for IR-eligible players); a settings icon next to the team name opens a persisted rename dialog.
       - `PLAYERS`: Available current-week free agents with player-specific headshots, actual opponent/kickoff details, stored weekly projections, season averages, search, and Add/Drop claims. Selecting a player opens the same Mu Fantasy Analytics modal structure and real player detail data, styled with Napper's dark navy and teal palette.
       - `LEAGUE`: Compact weekly scoreboard cards styled to match the Matchup banner's navy gradient, muted metadata, bold team typography, and teal points-share gauge, with team records, projections, and actual starter scores. Clicking a card opens its full starter/bench comparison in a modal using the Matchup view. Standings calculate PF/PA from season starter points, W-L-T from completed matchups, and seed by record percentage then PF. Includes the playoff bracket from `GET /playoffs`: quarterfinals (week 15) with the seeds 1–2 byes, semifinals (16) and championship (17) with seeds, scores (projections before kickoff), winners highlighted, the champion, and a status pill ("Projected · if the season ended today" until week 14 is final). Scoreboard cards in playoff weeks carry a round tag with both seeds; an empty playoff week shows the server's note. The Matchup tab keeps a week picker under its empty state, so a bye or eliminated week can be left. The separate Scores tab is removed. Manager strategy controls appear only before the draft. Below the bracket, **League History** (`NapperLeagueHistory`, `GET /league/{id}/history`): one card per season (champion, the user's record, final place and finish), expanding to that season's final standings; the latest finished season offers "Start the new season" once a newer NFL season has begun.
       - `TRADES`: Active trade market, incoming AI proposals with rationale breakdown, and proposal creation modal. The header shows the trade deadline ("end of Week 11", amber; red once passed), and the propose button is disabled after it.
       - `CHAT`: Full-screen league stream tab on narrower viewports.
     - **Right Rail**: Autonomous League Chat and awards stream featuring automated bot cards ("RB/WR/TE Benchwarmer of the Week", "High Scorer of the Week", "Trade Alert", "Waiver Claim") alongside contextual banter from AI managers across 4 distinct archetypes (`TRASH_TALKER`, `ANALYTICS_NERD`, `WAIVER_HAWK`, `DIE_HARD`), plus interactive user chat input.

10. **Team Hub Front Office tab (`FrontOfficeTab`, `src/components/team/`)**:
   - The fifth tab on `TeamPage` (`main | roster | stats | history | front office`; History is §3.3l), fed by `GET /api/team/{abbr}/front-office` (§4.2) for the current season. Below 560px the tab bar scrolls sideways instead of centring, so all five items stay reachable. Choosing a tab from the bar clears any contract focus. The Roster tab's Experience column reads "Rookie" for 0, "1 yr" / "N yrs", and "—" when it isn't recorded.
   - **From the Roster tab:** each row has a Contract column ("View →"). It opens this tab with that player in focus (`ContractFocus {playerId, name, nonce}`): the contracts table resets to All, scrolls his row to the middle of the screen once and highlights it for 2.6s; a player with no ACTIVE contract (a release, an in-season pickup without a deal) gets "No active contract on file for … this season." above the table instead.
   - **Front Office & Staff** (first on the tab): a Direction badge (Contend / Retool / Rebuild with a one-line gloss) beside the top three needs, numbered, each with its reasons, and an "Urgent: …" tag for an injury trigger. Below, staff cards: the head coach (titled "Head Coach & General Manager" when he holds both; slant, tenure and whom he replaced, championship and Coach of the Year tags, this season / with team / career records (with team reads "With team (since 2026)" when the tenure began before the first fully recorded season; "—" with "early seasons not on record" only when a season since isn't on record; "Career (this league)" for a coach whose earlier career isn't recorded), offense and defensive front, and the three tendencies as Low / Medium / High pills with their meaning, labelled "measured this season" or "reputation"); OC and DC cards (an unnamed stand-in reads "Interim OC"); and a GM card with his bio, or for a coach-GM a "Roster Control" card.
   - **Staff Contracts** (`StaffContractCard`, right after the people block): the `staff_contracts` block as four cards — each person's name, the role, the annual salary, "N of M years left · signed YYYY" and a gold **Full Control** badge on the head-coach card when he holds it; "No staff contracts are on file" when the block is null.
   - **Cap sheet:** four tiles (cap space with its league rank, total spend against the adjusted cap, dead money, next rookie reserve), a stacked bar of salaries / dead money / space across the adjusted cap ("Over the cap by …" when space is negative), and the cap row's basis line. An estimated cap row labels the tiles `est.`.
   - **Contracts:** position-group chips (All, Offense, Defense, Special Teams) and a horizontally scrolling table with a sticky player column: years left ("thru YYYY"), the five year columns (this season highlighted; a projected year in italics with `est.`; a $0 or missing year as "—"), total, bonus, cut savings and dead money if cut. Sort by player, years left, this season's hit or total. Tags: Contract year, No-trade, Incentives, New deal from YYYY (hover: its terms), Signing (an in-season CPU signing, whose bonus and cut terms aren't known). Under All, a Committed footer sums each year (scanned, plus projected `est.`, and players under contract). A term that isn't recorded shows "—", never $0.
   - **Transactions:** type chips with counts (All, Signed, Released, Re-signed, Extended, Restructured, Trade; empty types hidden) over a timeline grouped by league week (newest first, Offseason last). A move row: type badge, player (linked) and position with Notable / Starter / Practice squad tags, and its terms: a signing's origin ("from ATL" or free agent), years and value, and depth slot ("WILL2 on the depth chart"); a release's dead money and where he signed next; a re-signing's or extension's terms and the season its new deal starts. A trade card shows the partner's logo and a Received / Sent pair (players with cap hit, picks as "2037 R4" with the original team).
   - **Draft capital:** a round × draft grid for the next three drafts, each draft's header counting picks held, acquired and traded. Its own pick is an "Own" chip (with the overall number once set); an acquired pick reads "via ATL" with that team's logo; a traded pick is struck through as "to DET · Wk 6". Every pick chip, each draft-year header and a **Draft Central →** link under the title open `#draft?tab=needs&team=ABBR` (Draft Central's Team Needs & Capital, filtered to this team).
   - **Personality (docs/done/PERSONALITY_DISPLAY_PLAN.md, §5.2 item 14):** the head coach and named coordinator cards carry a collapsible "Personality" row (`PersonalityRow` in `StaffCards.tsx`; the panel mounts and fetches only when opened) when the staff block gives their `id`; under the staff, `FrontOfficePeople` shows the GM (by `staff.gm.id`), the owner and the scouting director (by team abbr), each card only when `/api/personality` has a profile, with the name and a compact panel. `server/front_office_api.py` does not yet put `id` on `head_coach`, `coordinators` or `gm`, so today the coach, coordinator and GM panels don't show; owners and scouting directors need the owners plan's U6 tables.
   - Loading, error and empty states for every block.

11. **Draft Central & Scouting Hub (`DraftPage`, `src/components/draft/`)**:
   - Accessed via `#debug` → **Enter Draft Central →** (`#draft`, not in the top-level site navbar). Features a dark broadcast masthead with live scouting step selector (Steps 4–24), a scrolling Scouting Wire ticker of weekly risers/fallers, a global `ProspectModal` dossier, and 5 primary sub-navigation views:
     - **Consensus Big Board (`ConsensusBigBoard.tsx`, `board` tab, default home view):** Top 150+ prospects ranked by consensus grade with stock movement badges ($\Delta\text{rank}$), position/conference/round filters, name/school search, step time-machine selector, and 1-line cumulative college season stat summaries.

Displays bio, physical measurables, consensus grade & rank, award ribbons, and 4 sub-tabs: **College Game Log & Stats** (cumulative season totals + chronological week-by-week college box scores with opponent, score, stage, scout verdict `SHINES`/`STEADY`/`STRUGGLES`, and game headline), **Combine & RAS Profile** (Step 24 40-yard dash, vertical, broad jump, 3-cone, shuttle, bench press, positional percentile bars 1–99, composite RAS 0–10, and Pro Day notes), **Scouting Timeline & Rank History**, and **Scouting Report** (V2.10: edition tabs, the role and grade line, trait bars 1–9 with the word, strengths/concerns/flag chips, body prose, signed "Mu Scouting Department · <edition> edition"; hidden entirely when the report endpoint 404s). The modal takes an optional `team`: the War Room passes its franchise abbreviation, so `GET .../report?edition=&team=` serves that team's own director-voiced row (the endpoint refuses a team outside the user teams); from Draft Central's board, with no team, the department row is the one shown.

     - **32-Team Needs & Draft Capital Matrix (`TeamNeedsMatrix.tsx`, `needs` tab):** All 32 franchises filterable by division/direction (`CONTEND`/`RETOOL`/`REBUILD`) or sortable by Draft Capital Index (#1–32), or narrowed to one team via `team=ABBR` in the hash, displaying top positional needs with urgency tiers (`CRITICAL`, `HIGH`, `MODERATE`), incumbent starter age/depth, and a 7-round pick inventory (`OWN` vs `ACQUIRED` via trade).
     - **Media Mock Draft (`MockDraftView.tsx`, `mock` tab):** Round 1 (Picks 1–32) media projection with team logos, traded pick provenance, prospect college stat lines, consensus grades, and analyst fit rationales.
     - **Live Broadcast Draft Day War Room (`DraftWarRoom.tsx`, `war-room` tab):** Broadcast-styled Round 1 live room sharing `localStorage["mu_debug_token"]` with `#debug`. Includes pre-draft order lock with owner overrides, Web Audio NFL draft chime on new picks, On-The-Clock command center (GM recommendation, rationale, 3 alternatives, Madden console steps, 1-click **Record Pick in Madden**, off-script search, and **Undo Last Pick**), draft-day trade alerts (round and trade-down marked), after pick 32 the Rounds 2–7 panel (the round's Madden steps and **Start Round N**), instant pick letter grades (`A+ FRANCHISE CORNERSTONE`, `A+ GRAND THEFT STEAL`, etc.), 32-team private GM board switcher, and projected rest of Round 1. An additive **Official Compensatory Picks** panel reads `GET /api/draft/compensatory?draft_season=` and lists every CBA/JC-2A award with a distinct `COMP` (amber) / `JC2A` (purple) badge, team, round, slot, overall pick and stored reason; a database without the migration or a class with no awards shows no panel.

Masthead with the count of NFL records set or tied in this league and, while the current regular season is unfinished, "marks in progress through Week N". Controls: Regular season / Postseason segment, scope chips (Single season, Single game, Rookie; postseason: Single game, Single postseason, Super Bowl, Career), a subject select (shown when a season type has more than one subject), All-time / Mu Era toggle and a franchise picker. Every filter lives in the hash, so a view can be linked.

An empty category says the first league season to post one sets it.

On phones each row stacks label and pace, then numbers, then the bar.

The header also counts the team's Super Bowl titles. `compact` is the Team hub's **Records & Titles** panel at the end of the Stats tab: a card per Super Bowl title (linked to the game), the records set in this league (value, holders, "League record" tag) and a "Full record book · N more franchise records →" link to `#records?team=`.

Each is visibly separate, and the league totals stay league-only.

The client checks are conveniences; the server decides. `personality.css` uses the site tokens and stacks at ≤ 640px (checked at 375px: no horizontal overflow).

A prospect's page never reaches this (his player page needs a `players` row), and an undrafted one reads "revealed after the draft".
- **Franchise modules (`src/components/franchise/`, V2 core U12, U15, U17; routed at `#franchise`):** standalone `({teamAbbr})` modules built against `/api/franchise/*` (shapes in `src/types/franchiseRoster.ts`, `franchiseMarket.ts`, `franchiseInbox.ts` and `press.ts`, plan §2.7a–b, FRONT_OFFICE_INBOX_PLAN §2.12 and PRESS_CONFERENCE_PLAN §2.11). **Depth Chart**: the save's 35 slots grouped Offense / Defense / Special Teams / Situational, up to 6 each; click-to-swap or drag within a slot; injured players tagged INJ; **Let Staff Set** shows the changed slots and Apply replaces the local chart; **Save** queues it (applied at the next league office write). **Roster & Cap**: Active / Practice Squad / IR against the 65 / 12 limits, a 5-year cap sheet, and per-player Cut, PS promote/demote and IR moves through `MoveDialog` (preview with cap savings, dead money this and next year, cap room after and legality reasons; a red warning when savings are negative; a post-June 1 toggle for cuts; then queue). **Training Room**: medical ledger with IR place/activate through the same dialog. **Free Agency**: the market (position, min OVR, max age, `team` for scheme fit; sort by fit, OVR, worth or age) and an offer form ($M) answered with ACCEPT / REJECT / COUNTER, a utility bar (parts × W_DEFAULT weights, the acceptance bar as a marker; the personality adjustment signed: a positive segment or a hatched cut for a negative one, never a negative width; a total above 1 labelled, clipped only in the drawing) with a `PolicyLine` (base → final U, signed adjustment, shadow note and plain-language reasons, or the neutral reason) when the response carries `policy_explanation`, and the agent's note; a counter loads back into the form; offers aren't instant signings. **Contract Room**: expiring contracts with CBA window reasons and tag / 5th-year option values; **Extend** (same answer shape); **Restructure** preview (cap saved now, added future dead money, cap hits by year; preview only). **Trade Machine**: partner team, players and next-3-draft picks on each side, evaluate → AI GM verdict and dialogue, surplus bars, cap legality and room after for both, a loadable counter; evaluating never makes the trade. **Talk to their GM** posts the built package to `POST /{abbr}/inbox` as a `GM_TALK` thread (`as: "GM"`, `gm_team`, the send side as V2.9's `trade_assets` payload `{players, picks}`, an optional note) and opens `#franchise-inbox`; a 409 (a talk with that GM is already open) shows an inline note with an inbox link instead of navigating. A **League Talks** section below the builder reads `GET /api/franchise/trade-talks?season=` for the roster's season and renders the published CPU transcripts newest first, each expandable to its turns (team abbreviation, posture chip, action, message, turn assets) and the final deal's assets; it shows only the plan's public shape — no surplus, options, `choice_source` or legality — with empty, loading, error and unavailable states. Negotiation pieces (`TermsForm`, `NegotiationResult`, `UtilityBar`) are exported from `FreeAgencyModule.tsx`. **Game Center** (`GameCenterModule.tsx`): overview tiles (record, cap room, roster counts, pending moves), the next opponent's dossier (ratings and per-game ranks), unit matchups with edges, and **Play Game** (`POST /game/launch`, dry run by default, a confirm step for a real launch, refusals shown). While JR's presser for the last game is SCHEDULED, LIVE or REVIEW, a **Go to the podium** button opens the Press Conference panel. **Press Conference** (`PressConferencePanel.tsx`, PRESS_CONFERENCE_PLAN §2.11): the room's attendees as name cards (a tier badge on each national), the transcript as it grows, the raised hands as pickable cards (a follow-up marked, with how often each reporter has been picked), the picked reporter's question with **Answer** / **No comment** / **That's all, thanks**, a "hands going up…" wait while the next round runs, a review screen with editable answers, on-record toggles and checker warnings, then **Approve and publish**, and read-only links to the opponent's presser and the week's other pressers from `GET /press/history`. **Inbox** (`InboxModule.tsx`, FRONT_OFFICE_INBOX_PLAN §2.13): a take-control panel for the GM and head coach when JR controls no one on the team, a Personas menu to take and release, and the conversation inbox — an acting-as filter, open/all, kind chips and unread dots; messages with template tags and a +/−/~ appraisal marker (reason on hover, never a trust number); reply options, the contract_terms / trade_assets / promise / vision forms, a text box with a confirm-before-acting draft card, a Go to Depth Chart link in role talks and a generic notice link keyed by the thread's `link_table` (a press notice's `press_conferences` row resolves to "Go to Game Center"; `OPEN_PRESSER` navigates there after recording the act); a new-conversation picker from `/inbox/kinds` whose start forms include the wave-4 pickers: `player_pick` lists the eligible players for `CONTRACT` (the ones `franchise_api._eligibility` accepts) and the active roster for `ROLE_TALK`, as NAME · POS · OVR and `team_pick` (`GM_TALK`) lists teams as NAME · TEAM, both from `GET /inbox/targets?kind=`; Start posts `player_id` (as text) or `gm_team` (the team abbreviation) beside `kind`, `as` and `note`. A failed targets fetch shows "Targets unavailable" and keeps Start disabled; an empty list says there is nobody to start with. The API is `server/inbox_api.py` (U5); the page is live against it. **Draft War Room** (`DraftWarRoomModule.tsx`): the team's war-room status, Round 1 slots and picks with grades, the draft capital ledger for the next 3 drafts and its board with `ProspectModal`, linking to `#draft?tab=war-room`. An **Interviews** card: budget meters (combine and visits left), the window line ("Combine interviews open until the re-signing stage"), eligible prospects with **Combine interview** / **Visit** buttons (which POST `/api/franchise/{abbr}/inbox` as a `PROSPECT` thread), and past interviews with their summary grade and an Inbox-tab link. **Report Card** (`ReportCardPanel.tsx`): the eight grade tiles with band coloring, the overall score/grade and league rank/percentile, CapEx renovation buttons per physical category (each tier's cost), and the OpEx policy toggles, all from `GET /api/team/{abbr}/report-card` / `POST .../facilities/upgrade` / `POST .../facilities/policy`. **Staff Contracts** (`StaffContractCard.tsx`): the team's staff contracts from `GET /api/team/{abbr}/front-office`'s `staff_contracts` block — each role's salary, years left and a Full Control badge; fetches the block itself on this page. Loading, error, empty and 'franchise API not available yet' (404) states. Shared helpers (`franchiseFetch`, `useFranchiseData`, `MoveDialog`) are exported from `RosterCapModule.tsx`; styles reuse `team/frontOffice.css` plus local `fr-` rules.

## 6. The Automated Pipeline Workflow (End-to-End)

### 6.0 Weekly run (capture pipeline, `docs/done/PIPELINE_MIGRATION.md` phase 5)
The capture pipeline runs alongside the old stream ingestion below until phase 6 retires that.
1. **Start** (JR, Oct 14: on demand; the broadcast trigger that watched for Advance Week was too brittle and was removed): after Advance Week, JR taps a button on the `#debug` page (phone or Mac). JR knows the run is going because his controller disconnects when Remote Play takes the console. Buttons: **Scan week** (the full run below), **Backfill previous week** (the same, `--no-articles`), **Game scan** (`--mode games`: every game of last week, box scores + player stats loaded with `--replace` over the backfill's lines, ~7 min a game, never articles), **Season scan** (`--mode season --no-articles`: start-of-season cadence run capturing the 18-week schedule, all 32 team rosters, all 32 Team Salary screens (contracts, right after rosters), the 32 team overalls and rankings cards, the 32-team injury report, and the draft board line-by-line in that exact order with prospects after schedule, rosters, contracts, team overalls, and injuries; capture timeout 2 × 75 min + 150 min for contracts; automatically rolls over `league_state` to `(current_season + 1, 1)` if `current_week != 1`; extracts, loads schedule, players, contracts (after the roster load; stops unless TEAM SALARY's year is the new season), team overalls/ratings into `team_seasons`, prospects, and Week 1 injuries; runs preseason calibration engines: 100-league simulated ADP drafts, scheduled game excitement projections, and Week 1 fantasy projections, then Napper week 1 AI lineups (`run_napper_week(season, 1, trades=False)`; a failure only logs a warning), then the player season ledger (`step_season_ledger` → `engines.season_ledger.run_ready`, §3.3m: last season's captured rosters to this one's; optional, skipped without the migration), then the GM season rollover (`step_gm_rollover` → `engines.gm_rollover.rollover`, §3.3f; optional, skipped when the GM migration isn't applied), then the scouting season step (`step_scouting_season`, team management step 4, §2.18: `fo_quality.recompute` for the new season with this year's rookies at year 0, then `dev_quality.recompute` (player development, skipped without its columns; a failure only warns and never blocks the init), then `scouting_engine init` for the incoming class at the current step; each part optional); publishes Week 1 preseason magazine unless `--no-articles`, shrinks media), **Team overalls scan** (`--mode team-overalls --no-articles`: captures all 32 team overalls and rankings cards from Options > User Teams > Triangle into `team_overalls.csv`, loading `team_ovr`, `off_ovr`, `def_ovr`, and ranks into `team_seasons`, no articles), **Roster scan** (`--mode roster --no-articles`: captures all 32 team rosters, extracting cards, loading players, shrinking media, no articles), **Contract scan** (`--mode contracts --no-articles`: every team's Team Salary screen, extracted and loaded into `player_contracts` / `team_cap_seasons` (§3.3d), ~40 min, no articles; a by-hand `--teams CAR,NO` re-scans only those teams), **Draft prospect scan** (`--mode prospects --no-articles`: captures the scouting draft board line-by-line, extracts prospects via Apple Vision OCR, loads them into `draft_prospects`, shrinks media, no articles; normally part of the start-of-season cadence after schedule and rosters); each can resume a stopped run folder.
2. **Weekly run** (`pipeline/weekly_capture.py`, a job of `server/debug_api.py` or run by hand; one at a time via `captures/.weekly_run.lock`, log in `captures/<run>/weekly_run.log`): notice → `madden_capture.py --connect` → `madden_capture.py --out <run>` (Season Stats, Team Stats, last week's schedule, and the Injury Report; from Week 19 a playoff run instead: `--only playoff`, last round's schedule, the injury report, and every game's box score and lines, ~7 min a game, plus the coming round's matchups; Week 22 is an articles-only run for the Week 23 slate; at Week 23, after playing the Super Bowl, Scan week captures the game directly from the in-game postgame stats screen via `madden_capture.py --only postgame` without advancing Madden to the offseason or navigating backward through the schedule) → League Transactions (the weekly/playoff capture reads the list from `--since` = the newest heading loaded this season, `<season> SEASON - WEEK 1` if none; optional: a failure only logs) → notice to turn the controller back on and restart the broadcast (weekly/playoff runs append the IR returns projected for the next week, §3.3b) → `extract.py` (Gemini vision for tables + on-device Apple Vision OCR for injuries and League Transactions (`transactions.csv`, flagged rows re-read by Gemini one cropped row at a time); during postseason weeks, injury extraction filters screenshots to only the teams playing games that week) → `pipeline.load_capture` (loads games, then `transactions.csv` (League Transactions, §3.3e) before Season Stats so a moved player's line finds his new team, then injuries; in postseason weeks, `load_injuries` validates against `games` to only commit injuries for teams playing that week; maps postgame stat labels and formats into standard box score fields; `extract.py` `postgame_columns` renames the postgame screen's labels (PLAYER→NAME, YDS→YARDS, passing AVG→YPA, defense ASSIST/TOTAL/PDEF/FF/FR/FYDS/BLOCKS/TDS, kicking LONG/BLOCKS/XP BLK, punting BLOCKS/IN 20) to the box score's via `POSTGAME_RENAME`, and writes box-score columns it lacks (passing SACKS) blank via `POSTGAME_MISSING`) → IR returns (Step 6c, weekly/playoff runs right after a fresh load, `step_ir_returns`: a terminal banner and a high-priority "take players off IR" notice listing the healed players still on IR before the new `league_state` week, §3.3b; optional, a failure only logs) → `generate_team_and_player_stats(season, strict=True)` (an engine error raises) → GM trade proposals (weekly and playoff runs only, `step_gm`, team management step 3: Gemini bios for GMs still on the template, then `engines.gm_trade_engine.run_week` for `league_state`'s week (after the Super Bowl load: offseason stage 1, once) with the Gemini rationale writer; CPU-to-CPU deals are played by `engines/gm_talks` with a `gm_talks` model voice (templates without a key), and `step_gm` flushes that writer; skipped when the GM migration isn't applied; optional: a failure only logs a warning; `N new trade proposals for JR` notice when N > 0) → front-office inbox (weekly and playoff runs only, `step_inbox` → `engines.inbox.scan.step_inbox`, §2.21b: inbound conversations for the personas JR controls in registry user teams, kinds' promise reviews, stale-thread expiry and the relationship-event outbox flush, for `league_state`'s week with the `inbox` model voice; a no-op with no registry user team, no controlled persona or without the inbox migration; optional: a failure only logs a warning) → scouting (Step 7c, `step_scouting`, team management step 4, §2.18: the draft class's consensus step for `league_state`'s step, catching up missing steps in order, then rewriting any newly stored report edition's prose (`scouting_reports.rewrite`, top 64, label `scout_report`); also after the GM step of a Next offseason stage run; skipped without the migration or before the class is initialized; optional: a failure only logs a warning) → season archive (Step 7d, `step_season_archive`, §3.3h: once a season's Super Bowl is complete, freeze it, once; same modes and seasons as the carousel) → coaching carousel (Step 7d, `step_coach_hot_seat`, in weekly, playoff and postgame runs, §2.19: whatever is ready for league_state's season and the one before: Black Monday in the Week 18 run so the Week 19 articles see the firings, each playoff team once it is out, coordinator reviews, and the hiring cycle once the Super Bowl is complete; skipped without the migrations; optional: a failure only logs a warning; `Mu: coaches fired` / `Mu: coaches hired` notices with what to mirror in Madden) → `newsroom.weekly_run.run_weekly_swarm` → shrink (PNG → WebP q90 full resolution, `stop_debug` / `scope_debug` / `week_debug` / `team_debug` / `probe` / `explore` deleted, CSVs kept; ~1.7 GB → ~46 MB) → notice. Any failed step stops the week (nothing after it runs, so a failed load means no backfill, engines or articles) and sends an urgent notice with the `--resume` command. Resume starts at the first step not done: capture resumes and preserves completed categories (`stats/done.txt`), completed teams (`roster/done.txt`, `injuries/`), finished games (`games/<NN>/DONE`), completed Team Salary teams (`contracts/done.txt`, `contracts/targets.txt`), and completed season scan phases (`season_schedule`, `roster`, `contracts`, `team_overalls`, `injuries`, `prospects`) while discarding only partial frames of incomplete categories/teams; capture is done when the run wrote `.capture_done` (older weekly runs: `week.json`), extract when the mode's CSVs exist (weekly: `schedule.csv` + `stats_*.csv` + `injuries.csv` if `injuries/` present; playoff/postgame: `game_scores.csv` + `schedule.csv` if `schedule/` present + `injuries.csv` if `injuries/` present; games: `game_scores.csv`; contracts: `contracts.csv` + `team_cap.csv`, also required in a season run that captured `contracts/`), load when the `captures` row is `loaded`; the backfill and articles are safe to rerun.

### 6.0b PC Save Watcher Daemon (`pipeline/watch_save.py`, `db/franchises.py`, `docs/done/PC_MIGRATION_PLAN.md` §5.2)
On PC/WSL2, Madden saves directly to disk (`CAREER-*` files in Windows `Documents/Madden NFL 27/saves/` accessible via `/mnt/c/`). `pipeline/watch_save.py` automates ingestion without Remote Play, OCR, or controller macros:
1. **Detection & Debounce:** Polls the watched saves directory (CLI argument, `--saves-dir`, or `.env` `MADDEN_SAVES_DIR`; a single file path also works). Debounces write bursts: only triggers when `st_mtime` and `st_size` have remained stable for `--debounce` seconds (default 10s) and `size > 0`. Tracks processed modification times per file so each save state is handled exactly once; a backlog is processed oldest first so weeks load in order. Tuning clones (`CAREER-TUNE*`, hyphen optional because Madden's Save As cannot type one — `CAREER-TUNECOACHBEFORE` is caught too; P1-24) are skipped: they keep the real franchise's `LeagueID`, so a scan would route a disposable tuning season into the live database. A `--dsn` naming a `madden_tune_*` database (P2-04's deliberate tuning ingest) or `--allow-tune-save` opts in, and routing additionally refuses a tuning clone whose destination is any other database. A tuning `--dsn` may also carry `--auto-init` (create + seed the tuning database from the clone) or `--reseed --confirm-reseed <db>` (the reset path); the database gets no registry entry, only a `league_state.madden_league_id` stamp, and its ingest child runs with `MU_NO_LLM=1` so it makes no model calls (P2-07). See `docs/reference/TUNING_LEAGUE.md`.
2. **Snapshot:** Invokes `node pipeline/save_reader/pc_save_reader.mjs <save> --out captures/<run>/save.json` (season, week, teams with their team ratings and decoded cap blocks, rosters, top-level salary_cap block, and `franchise.league_id`; reader_version 8, whose teams carry `roster` and `practice_squad` pgid lists and whose snapshot carries a top-level `free_agents` list, a `coaches` list (every live Coach record, free agents included) and a `staff` list (each real team's HC/OC/DC coach pgids, empty seats null)).
3. **Franchise routing (one database per franchise):** The save's `Franchise.LeagueID` (random per franchise, the same across every save slot and week; checked on CAREER-WEEK1–3 of one franchise, -1851690351, against CAREER-GIANTS-AUTOSAVE, 2027975635) is looked up in the registry `data/franchises.json` (`db/franchises.py`; gitignored and machine-local like the databases; `MU_FRANCHISE_REGISTRY` overrides the path). Each entry holds the database (`madden_<--franchise-name slug>`, else `madden_l<league id as 8 hex digits>`), name, user teams, the save files seen, and creation time; the registry also names the **active** franchise (the first one registered, or `python3 -m db.franchises active <db|name|id>`). A snapshot without a league id (reader before v3) falls back to an id from the file name.
   - **New franchise:** without `--auto-init` the save is an error (notified). With it, the franchise is registered, its database created (`CREATE DATABASE`), and `db/seed_clean_db.py:run_clean_seed` applies `init_db.sql` and seeds the 32 teams, records, coaches, coordinators, GM personas, draft capital, writer personas and Napper profile with the save's calendar season and week and the franchise's `--user-team`; then `league_state.madden_league_id` is stamped.
   - **Existing franchise:** a missing or empty database is created/seeded only with `--auto-init`; a database that has data is never seeded. A `madden_league_id` stamp that differs from the save's id stops the load (the registry points at the wrong database).
   - **`--reseed`** (with `--once` only) drops and recreates the franchise's database, then seeds it; it needs `--confirm-reseed <database name>`. `madden`, `madden_2036`, `madden_test`, `postgres` and anything not named `madden_*` are never created or dropped.
   - **`--dsn DSN`** skips routing and loads into that database (tests, one-off loads).
   - **`--dry-run`** never registers, creates or seeds; a franchise without a ready database is a no-op.
4. **State check** against the franchise database's `league_state` (`classify_week`): `same_week` no-op; `older_week` or `season_gap` (more than one season ahead) notify and no-op; `no_current_week` (preseason/offseason) no-op; `new_week` or right after seeding advances. `--force` bypasses the check. With the league office on, an offseason stop is `new_stage` (ingested: load + league office, no engines, articles or mod pack) until `league_office_runs` has a WRITTEN or PLANNED run for its season/stage/week/wave, then `same_stage`.
5. **Execution Chain** (`run_ingest`: a child `python -m pipeline.watch_save --ingest <snapshot>` with `DATABASE_URL` set to the franchise database, because the loader, engines and newsroom read `DATABASE_URL` at import time; the child writes `captures/<run>/ingest_result.json`):
   - Runs `pipeline.load_save.load(snapshot_path, season=season, commit=(not dry_run))`, loading players, completed games, line stats, season totals, contracts, injuries, highlights, and updating `league_state.current_week` in a single transaction with a `captures` row (mode `save`).
   - Runs start-of-season calibration engines (`weekly_capture.step_preseason_engines`: fantasy ADP drafts, excitement projections, fantasy projections) if `save_week is None` (preseason), or in-season analytics engines via `weekly_capture.run_weekly_engines` (backfill & analytics engines, GM proposals, scouting, season archive, and coaching carousel). `--no-engines` stops after the load.
   - GPU queue hook (`queue_nightly_jobs`, §7.5): logs how many `pipeline.gpu_queue` jobs are pending and leaves them for the nightly runner. It never runs the queue inline: the ingest usually happens while Madden is still open, when the runner waits indefinitely, and no job handlers are registered in the watcher.
   - Runs newsroom articles synchronously via `weekly_capture.step_articles` → `newsroom.weekly_run.run_weekly_swarm` when articles are enabled and the save has a current week. Deferred/Colab batch routing (`docs/in_progress/V3_STUDIO_PLAN.md` §3; former V2 §5.1) is planned; the watcher does not yet enqueue article slates or expose a media-mode switch. The queue hook only reports pending jobs; execution belongs to the separate nightly runner.
   - **League office (V2 core U16, §2.21a):** on a new week or stage (not the seeding load or a forced re-load; never with `--dry-run`/`--no-league-office`; `--league-office-dry-run` passes dry_run=True) runs `pipeline.league_office.run(cur, snapshot, save_path, stage="auto")` in-process, before the articles so they can report its moves. Failures are logged and notified ("Mu: league office failed" / "needs recovery", the latter naming `python3 -m pipeline.league_office --recover <run_id>`) and never stop the articles. While Madden27.exe runs it refuses to replace the save unless `LEAGUE_OFFICE_FRANCHISE_CLOSED=1` (JR sets it when he works at Madden's main menu with the franchise closed); the refusal is a warning, and the daemon retries once Madden27.exe has closed, only if the save's sha256 is unchanged. Its write keeps season/week (`classify_week`: same_week) and the daemon skips a save whose sha256 equals the league office's output, so its own write is never re-ingested; `mark_processed` uses the mtime seen before processing. A written run's `summary.retirement_window` comes back as `result["retirement_window"]`; `retirement_window_notice` adds one line to the "offseason stage done" notification (and to "week done" for the PRESEASON / CUTDOWN saves): the decision count at the decision stage, else restored / not restored (with the planner reasons) / conflicts / vanished rostered players by name and last team / your-team restores / a skipped stop. Its priority is high when a rostered player vanished, a classify conflict exists or a restore was blocked for any reason other than `authority_missing` / `stage_mismatch`; in-season runs (role image) add nothing.    - **Tuning progression bootstrap (`bootstrap_tuning_progression`, P2-03):** a tuning database is created from `init_db.sql` and loaded, which never touches progression state, so with a `madden_tune_*` destination the ingest applies `progression_checkpoint.bootstrap_pass(..., form_neutral=True)` for the save's season right after the seeding load (after it, because the pass maps players by pgid from the database). It is gated on the save being neutral — every `ConfidenceRating` 50, which `CAREER-MU2026` is by construction — and never fails an ingest. Without it the league office refuses at the first progression stage ("explicit neutral bootstrap is required before offseason progression" at OFFSEASON_START; "player N: explicit neutral bootstrap required" at the next season's first regular week).
   - **Tuning draft order (`lock_tuning_draft_order`, P2-03):** with a `madden_tune_*` destination only, the parent locks the coming draft's order (`engines.draft_room.lock_order(cur, season + 1)`) before the DRAFT stage's `run_ingest`, because the live franchise's order is locked by hand in the Draft Room and a tuning league has nobody to press it — without it the league office has no picks to write. Idempotent, and a failure is a warning that names the reason rather than a failed ingest.
   - Writes the mod pack for each user team's next game (the save's current week, Madden's next unplayed week) via `mod_packs.build_pack` + `write_pack`, selecting the first; skipped with a log line while MMCModManager.exe is open or when the config or `Mu Base` pack is missing.
   - **Press conferences (PRESS_CONFERENCE_PLAN §2.2):** after the articles and the mod pack, on a real weekly ingest (not `--dry-run`, `--no-articles`, `--no-engines`, or a preseason/no-week save), `run_ingest` reads the season's latest week with completed games from the database (`press_week`; the save is made after Advance Week, so its own week is Madden's next unplayed one) and, when the press tables exist, starts `python3 -m newsroom.press_room run-week --season S --week N` with `DATABASE_URL` set, as a detached process it never waits for. Without the press tables nothing is spawned.
   - **Weekly Database + Save Freeze (`pipeline/weekly_freeze.py`):** After a committed ingest (and initial franchise seed), takes an atomic paired snapshot into `captures/freezes/<db>/<label>/` holding `db.dump` (PostgreSQL `pg_dump -Fc`), a raw copy of the Madden `CAREER-*` save file, and `manifest.json` with sha256 checksums and metadata (`season`, `week`, `stage`, `wave`, `league_id`, `source_save`). Labels: `<season>_w<NN>`, `<season>_off_<STAGE>[_w<WAVE>]`, or `<season>_pre`. If the league office writes changes to the save after Madden closes (`retry_league_office`), the week's freeze folder is automatically re-frozen so the frozen save file reflects the modified state. Skipped with `--no-freeze` or `--dry-run`.
   - **Time-Machine Rollback & Scratch Restore:**
     - `python3 -m pipeline.weekly_freeze restore --db <db> --label <label> --saves-dir <dir> --confirm <db>`: restores both PostgreSQL database and Madden save file to any historical week in complete sync, first creating a safety snapshot (`pre_restore_<timestamp>`) so rollbacks can be undone, and verifying `Madden27.exe` is closed.
     - `python3 -m pipeline.weekly_freeze restore-scratch --db <db> --label <label> [--scratch-db madden_snap]`: restores database dump only into a throwaway scratch DB (`madden_snap`, refusing franchise databases), used by V3 media backfills to inspect point-in-time football evidence while preserving canonical franchise memories and articles.
     - Subcommands: `freeze`, `restore`, `restore-scratch`, `verify`, `list`.
   - **Relationship event producers (§3.3r, off by default):** right after the load, before the offseason-stop branch, so weekly ingests and offseason stops both run it, `step_relationship_producers` opens its own connection and transaction and runs one SAVE `run_tick` for the snapshot's (league season, tick) with the snapshot's roster. It does nothing unless the switchboard's `producers` feature is shadow or active (`MU_RELATIONSHIP_PRODUCERS=off` is the kill switch, `=on` forces it on), is skipped with a logged reason when the producer or relationships tables aren't migrated, and never fails the ingest (logged, notified, recorded as a FAILED run). The inbox flush is still not connected; the coach's promise reviews run in the next step.
   - **CPU coach promises (§7.11, off by default):** right after the producers step and before the personality evolution and trade-request steps, `step_coach_promises` opens its own connection and transaction and runs `engines.agent_loops.watcher.promise_tick` for the snapshot's (league season, tick). It reviews every due promise first (`coach.review_promises` against the MADDEN chart for that tick; injured or unread defers once, then resolves `unknown`), then offers a promise to each player with two trailing unsatisfied role weeks (from the relationships ledger's `role_window` events) on every team not in the registry's `user_teams` who lost a depth-1 base starting slot since the previous tick (`coach.promise_options` + `decide_promise`, subjects `player:<id>:promise`). It runs when the switchboard's `coach_loop` feature is shadow or active (`MU_COACH_PROMISES=off` is the kill switch, `=on` forces it on), commits the decisions in both modes (active also appends `promise_made` / `promise_resolved` through the relationships store; shadow appends no envelopes), is skipped with a logged reason when the decisions/lifecycle/relationships tables aren't migrated or the league has no lifecycle universe, and never fails the ingest. The ingest result carries `coach_promises`.
   - **Personality evolution (§7.11, off by default):** right after the producers step, on the OFFSEASON_START ingest (tick 24) only and before the league office, `step_personality_evolution` opens its own connection and transaction and runs `evolution_run.run_season` for the season just ended in the league's lifecycle universe (with `external` = `development_evolution_candidates(...)`: the development plan's candidates, source `DEVELOPMENT`, only when the switchboard's `development_learning` feature is on too, gated by `evolution_development.development_mode`; the result carries `development_candidates`), writes the report to `verify_output/personality_evolution/evolution_<universe>_<season>.md` and notifies "Mu: N personality changes in <season>". It does nothing unless the switchboard's `evolution` feature is shadow or active (`MU_PERSONALITY_EVOLUTION=off` is the kill switch, `=on` forces it on), is skipped with a logged reason when the evolution tables aren't migrated or no universe is registered, and never fails the ingest (logged, notified, recorded as a FAILED run). The ingest result carries `personality_evolution`.
   - **Trade-request reviews (PERSONALITY_ACTIVATION_PLAN §2.4, off by default):** after the producers and evolution steps, on every ingest where the switchboard's `trade_requests` feature isn't off (`MU_TRADE_REQUESTS=off` kill switch, `=on` forces it), `step_trade_requests` opens its own connection and transaction, builds each player's request context (relationships incidents, core view) and clock (`trade_request_clock`: tick plus the GM window), and records decisions through the trade-requests store. Shadow writes the decisions to `verify_output/personality_trade_requests/` and persists nothing; active persists. Skipped with a logged reason when the tables aren't migrated or no universe is registered; never fails the ingest. In the weekly engines, `trade_request_signals` hands `gm_trade_engine.run_week(request_signals=...)` each ACTIVE episode's `gm_request_signal` only when `trade_requests` is active: the requesting team's GM shops the player (search trigger SELL, flag `trade_request:<id>`) with its normal valuation, legality and acceptance — no price change, no deadline, no forced trade — and teams in the registry's `user_teams` get no automatic shopping.
   - Dispatches completion phone notifications via `pipeline.notify.notify`.
6. **Concurrency & Failure:** Acquires `captures/.weekly_run.lock` to prevent concurrent execution with `weekly_capture.py` or other watcher instances; registry writes are serialized by `data/franchises.json.lock`. Failed runs send high-priority ntfy error alerts and mark the mtime to prevent crash loops.
7. **Flags:** `--once` (newest save, then exit), `--dry-run` (skips the league office and freeze), `--no-league-office`, `--league-office-dry-run`, `--no-articles`, `--no-engines`, `--no-freeze`, `--season N` (override season), `--force` (bypass week comparison), `--auto-init` (set up a new franchise's database), `--franchise-name NAME` (names a new franchise's database), `--user-team` (comma-separated user team abbreviations for a new franchise, e.g. `IND`), `--reseed` + `--confirm-reseed DB`, `--dsn` (with `--auto-init`/`--reseed`, create/seed/reset a `madden_tune_*` tuning database from a `CAREER-TUNE-*` clone), `--allow-tune-save` (process `CAREER-TUNE*` clones; implied by a `madden_tune_*` `--dsn`), `--lock-file`, `--debounce`, `--poll-interval`.
8. **Active franchise elsewhere:** `server/api.py` calls `db.franchises.export_active_dsn()` before its imports, so with no `DATABASE_URL` the site serves the active franchise (an explicit `DATABASE_URL` wins; restart after switching). `db/backup_db.sh`, `restore_db.sh`, `clear_news_feed.sh` and `tools/verify_session.sh` use `MU_DB` or the active franchise. Engines, newsroom and other CLIs read only `DATABASE_URL`: `export DATABASE_URL="$(python3 -m db.franchises dsn)"`.

### 6.1 Stream ingestion (retired in phase 6)
The entire intelligence apparatus is triggered autonomously via an optimized, concurrent pipeline designed to ingest streaming video and output localized AI content in real time.

1. **Ingestion (Live Stream & Worker Pool Concurrency):**
   - `pipeline/ocr_extractor.py` and `TemplateClassifier` monitor the Madden video stream at 1 FPS.
   - Dynamic batch jobs and single-frame stats are queued to an asynchronous **`ApiWorkerPool`** (default 3 concurrent workers, scalable via `--workers`).
   - Multiple extraction jobs run simultaneously against Gemini (`gemini-3.8-flash`), with thread-safe synchronization of game IDs, session state, and real-time database UPSERTs.
   - When the user scrolls Post-Game stats, box scores are instantly UPSERTED into `player_stats`.
   - When the user scrolls the Weekly Schedule, it logs final CPU-simmed scores and win/loss records.
   - When the user scrolls Season Stats, it overwrites the `season_stats` ledger.
2. **Mathematical Backfill:**
   - `engines/game_stat_generator.py` (regular-season games only: playoff games get lines only from a games capture, and captured playoff lines are never subtracted from the regular-season totals) is invoked for `league_state.current_season` (no season is hardcoded in the backfill or the pipeline's calls). It subtracts the player's lines already stored this season (matched by `player_id`, on any team, so a traded player's old-team games count; a `season_stats` row without one falls back to name + team + position) from the `season_stats` and distributes the remaining stats into the missing CPU-simmed games, so season totals match `season_stats`. Each player's remainder is split across those games in proportion to each game's combined score (weight $\max(1, \text{total points}/40)$), so per-game box scores for CPU-simmed games are synthetic: only season totals and final scores are real (see the caveat in 2.6). The exception is a team with exactly one missing game, the normal weekly case: its lines are that week's exact change in the season totals and are tagged `line_source = 'WEEKLY'`; lines spread over several games are tagged `DISTRIBUTED` (§2.13 uses only real lines). It inserts with the line's `player_id` and skips a row that hits either unique key. Team rows are the sums of those player lines, with third/fourth-down fields left NULL; right after the insert it runs `engines/team_box_estimator.run(season)` (§2.6), which fills every still-NULL per-game conversion, red-zone and penalty cell from the `team_seasons` remainder (an estimator failure stops a strict run).
   - In addition to offensive skill positions, `generate_defense_and_special_teams_stats(season_year, games_df)` backfills per-game lines for kicking (`game_stat_kicking`), defense (`game_stat_defense`), punting (`game_stat_punting`), blocking (`game_stat_blocking`), punt returns (`game_stat_puntreturn`), and kick returns (`game_stat_kickreturn`) from their respective `season_stat_*` tables for completed games missing game lines. In a weekly run where a team has 1 missing game, the game line equals that week's exact change in season totals. Multi-game distributions use domain-specific weights (kicking: points scored, defense: defensive stop score $\max(1, (50 - \text{pts\_allowed})/10)$, punting: lower points $\max(1, (40 - \text{pts})/10)$, blocking: even, returns: opponent score/punts), with sacks allocated in 0.5 half-sack steps and rate metrics (`fg_pct`, `xp_pct`, `average`, `net_average`, `tackles = solo + assists`) computed automatically. CLI flag `--no-dst` allows skipping defense and special teams backfill if desired.
3. **Culture Engines (Dependency-Ordered Execution & Batch Updates):**
   - Appended to the end of the backfill generator, `engines/game_stat_generator.py` first runs `gotw_engine.batch_evaluate(season, only_missing=True, game_ids=...)` to score the Game Excitement Index ($E$) for newly completed games (those with no `excitement_index`) and any games it just backfilled. Previously scored games are left unchanged. This must precede TWI, which only counts games with a non-null `excitement_index`.
   - Right after $E$ it runs `game_script_engine.run(season)` (§2.14): every completed game without a script, or whose recorded facts changed, gets its canonical story in `game_scripts` (the story's drama follows $E$).
   - It then runs `TWIEngine().backfill_twi()` followed by `PopularityEngine().calculate_popularity()`, sequentially in dependency order, because franchise popularity reads the `watchability_index` that TWI writes. These two used to run in parallel, so popularity could read stale or partially updated TWI.
   - Between TWI and franchise popularity it runs `GameCreditEngine().calculate(season)` (Section 2.4) `TeamEfficiencyEngine().calculate(season)` (Section 2.6), `TendencyEngine().calculate(season)` (Section 2.12), `CotyEngine().calculate(season)` (Section 2.11) and `PlayoffCloutEngine().calculate(season)` (Section 2.7). They read only `games` / `team_stats` / `player_stats` / `awards` (and, for COTY, `team_seasons.team_ovr` and the coach tables), so their position is not a dependency.
   - Once franchise metrics are computed, `PlayerPopularityEngine().calculate_popularity()` executes vectorized batch updates using PostgreSQL `executemany` (reducing DB execution time from ~1s to ~0.16s).
   - `RecordsEngine().calculate(season)` (`engines/records_engine.py`) evaluates the season against the record book and stores newly broken or tied franchise records and NFL all-time top 10 entries into `franchise_records` and `league_record_entries` (source `LEAGUE`, §2.9).
   - Then `project_scheduled_games(season)` refreshes `games.projected_excitement` for every still-scheduled game, so the next assignment brief and primer picks see current projections.
   - Then `project_upcoming_week(season)` (`engines/fantasy_projection_engine.py`) writes fantasy projections for the first week that still has scheduled games. It reads only `games`, `player_seasons`, `player_stats`, `game_stat_kicking`, `game_stat_defense` and `injuries`, so it has no dependency on the culture engines.
   - Finally, `simulate_season(season)` (`engines/fantasy_league_sim.py`) re-simulates the 100 fantasy leagues through that week (rostered %, start %, standings). It needs the season's stored draft (from `fantasy_adp_engine`) and skips with a message if there is none.
   - Then `run_napper_week(season)` (`engines/napper_weekly.py`) updates every IN_SEASON Napper league of the season for that same week: the playoff bracket (`sync_playoffs`: the round for that week, the champion after week 17), AI lineups (IR moves, starters), the waiver run from week 2 (`engines/napper_waiver_engine.run_waivers`: the user's queued claims and AI pickups, once per league and week), AI trade proposals (skipped if the league already has AI proposals that week, so re-runs add no duplicate offers or banter), decisions on pending offers to AI teams (both only through the week 11 trade deadline; from week 12 pending offers expire instead), AI lineups again (waiver adds and traded players arrive on the bench), and `napper_leagues.current_week` = the week. Each league commits on its own; a Napper failure only logs `[WARN]` and never fails the stats sync. Offers to the human team stay pending.
4. **The Swarm Trigger & Editorial Commissioning:**
   - The swarm is a separate step from the stats sync. `game_stat_generator.py` only syncs stats and runs the engines; the video pipeline (`pipeline/main.py`, both live and file modes) calls `newsroom.weekly_run.run_weekly_swarm(season)` right after it on the same thread. The admin dashboard's `season_stats` edits and a direct `python3 -m engines.game_stat_generator` run no longer publish anything.
   - **Publication week:** a Week N slate is published before Week N kicks off (recaps Week N−1, previews Week N). `run_weekly_swarm` picks N = the latest *fully completed* week + 1, where fully completed means every non-`BYE` game that week is `COMPLETED`; Week 1 if none. A partly played week doesn't count, so a mid-week Season Stats capture maps to an already-published slate. After Week 21 it publishes Week 22; Week 23 (Super Bowl) and the Week 1 preseason slate must be run by hand with `--week`. Once the Super Bowl week is finished it publishes nothing.
   - **Once per week:** it skips the week if `news_feed` already has a national-slot article for it (`slot` = `Hero Slot`, `Standalone`, or `Slot N`; local wakeups use `Local Beat N` and don't count), unless `--force`. It holds a PostgreSQL advisory lock on (season, week) for the run, so two triggers can't generate the same week at once.
   - **Memory refresh:** in a live run, before the brief, `agent_memory.refresh_season_summaries` rewrites the "season so far" summary of every agent with at least 3 new takes since its last summary (§7.7).
   - `run_weekly_swarm` compiles a dual-horizon Weekly Slate Digest:
     - **`season` / `calendar_week` / `recap_week`**: labels for the publication week and the week being recapped.
     - **`recap_slate`**: Completed scoreboard from `week - 1` (score, margin, excitement, team IDs), most exciting first, for retrospective recaps. Each game carries `game_story` (§2.14: storyline, halftime, the winning score and two key moments from its game script).
     - **`standout_performances`**: The top 5 individual stat lines from `week - 1`, ranked by passing, rushing and receiving yards and touchdowns.
     - **`preview_slate`**: Upcoming scheduled matchups for `week`, ordered by projected excitement. `projected_excitement` comes from `games.projected_excitement` on the 70–100 display scale, for prospective previews.
     - **`excitement_scale_note`**: Tells writers that Excitement Index values are on the 70–100 scale (≈70 dull, ≈80 typical, 90+ classic) and that projections are rough pre-game estimates. `recap_slate` values and the writer DB tools (`get_weekly_slate`, `get_team_season_schedule`, box score and advanced analytics) use the same display scale.
     - **`season_landscape`**: The league as it stood entering the week. `division_standings` gives every division's teams, best record first, as one line each (`City Team (ID: n) W-L[-T], PF, PA, diff | 5-Yr: W-W-W-W-W (SB, PO)`), counted from completed **regular-season** games before the publication week by `newsroom/season_landscape.division_standings` (playoff games excluded; `standings_through_week` is `week - 1`, capped at 18; `tests/test_season_landscape.py`), enriched with 5-year trailing regular-season records and playoff results from `team_season_results`. `most_watchable_teams` and `most_popular_teams` are the top 5 by `team_seasons` watchability and popularity, labelled with the same standings records.
     - **`league_transactions`** (omitted in a week with no new moves; `roster_moves.brief_block`): the moves visible to this week's articles that last week's couldn't see (`new_this_week`), as `notable_moves` (at most 12 move lines, notable first, never an OVR), `counts` by type, `cap_watch` (teams under $2M in cap space, most squeezed first, each with its basis) and a `note` (use a move only when it bears on the subject, most articles carry none; terms only from these lines or the contract tools; invent colour, never a term). Built from `db_tools.fetch_moves` / `fetch_cap_rows` with the brief's (season, week); `TRADED` legs are left out.
     - **`league_trades`** (Phase 8; omitted when empty; `swarm_dispatcher.new_week_trades` + `roster_moves.trades_block`): `executed_trades` (trade lines of last week's executed trades, `roster_moves.new_trades`: the weekly run writes Week N's articles right after the GM step proposes Week N's trades and JR makes them after that, so the Week N+1 edition is the first to report them) with a `trade_note` (fact; invent the colour, never a player, pick, figure or team), and `rumors` (rumor and leak lines from last week's `rumor_ok` proposals and `gm_trade_leaks` rows, through the deadline) with a `rumor_note` (only ever talks, never a trade that happened). Built last.
     - **`curatorial_guidance`**: Tells writers they may choose their own games, teams and players, except that an `EDITORIAL DESK SUBJECT ASSIGNMENT` in the prompt fixes the subject; then the freedom applies only to angles within it.
     - The brief is identical for every article in a run (Agent Wire posts get their own facts packets, §7.8). (The former `slate_manifest`, a duplicate of `recap_slate`, and `league_leaders`, now inside `season_landscape`, were removed.)
   - It then fires `SwarmDispatcher().dispatch_weekly_national(live=True, save_to_db=True, max_workers=5)`, which commissions the full 10-slot Editorial Matrix slate (`docs/EDITORIAL_MATRIX.md`) via the autonomous Editorial Assignment Desk. The optional `article_count` argument truncates the slate and is for tests/debugging only.
   - Local on-demand team wakeups (`POST /api/news/team/{team_id}/wakeup`; only `live=true` calls Gemini and saves, `live=false` is a dry run) also utilize `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5)` to generate the team's local beat portfolio, then (live, saved wakeups only) the team's Agent Wire posts through `newsroom/social_publish.run_team_social`, which also shares each new local article from its reporter (§7.8). The portfolio is planned by `newsroom/local_portfolio.plan_local_portfolio` (see §7.2).
   - The Editorial Desk commissions a structured 10-article matrix (Hero, Slot 1, Slot 2, Slots 3–5 Feature Trio, Slots 6–8 Local Matchup Primers, and Standalone Power Rankings), matches each format to an eligible national writer or beat reporter, and dispatches them with custom curatorial directives and explicit temporal framing (`RETROSPECTIVE`, `PROSPECTIVE`, or `CUMULATIVE`). Other local beat formats (`LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD`, `LOCAL_PLAYER_SPOTLIGHT`, `LOCAL_SEASON_PROGRESS_REPORT`) are not part of the weekly national run; they are produced only by on-demand team wakeups.
   - **Only real output is saved:** `_execute_agent` writes to `news_feed` only when `live=True` and the model returned text. A missing API key, a Gemini exception, an empty response, or offline mock text (`live=False`) is logged as `[NOT SAVED]` and returned with an `error` field instead. A weekly run where every article failed therefore leaves the week unpublished, and the next trigger retries it (`tests/test_article_saving.py`).
   - **Agent Wire posts:** the old reaction tweets (random pundits and fans prompted with the full brief) are gone. After the national and fantasy slates, `run_weekly_swarm` calls `newsroom.social_publish.run_social_week`, which plans and publishes the week's ~100 Agent Wire posts; team wakeups post through `run_team_social` (§7.8). `--social-only` / `--skip-social` run or skip that step; `--fantasy-only` skips it; `--skip-fantasy` keeps it. The result dict gains a `social` status.
   - **Parallel Multithreaded Execution:** Dispatcher leverages Python `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` (default 5 workers), collapsing total weekly generation time from ~90s sequential down to ~12–15s parallel.
   - **API Connection Pooling:** FastAPI backend (`server/api.py`) utilizes `psycopg_pool.ConnectionPool` (min 4, max 20 connections) with sub-3ms query latency across all REST endpoints.
   - **Persistence & Entity Tagging:** Articles are parsed for creative headlines (`# Headline`) and teaser excerpts (`> **EXCERPT:** ...`), then saved to `news_feed` with explicit `article_type` and `slot` identifiers alongside relational tags in `article_teams` and `article_players`.

## 7. Media Swarm Prompting, Curatorial Autonomy & Historical Anchoring
To eliminate editorial homogenization and ground long-form journalism in authentic football culture, prompts for the National Writers chain strict analytical constraints:
- **Core Model Standard:** All autonomous writer and reaction agents utilize Google's **`gemini-3.8-flash`** with autonomous ReAct database function calling (`automatic_function_calling` with a 50-call cap).
- **Mandatory Headline & Excerpt Directives:** Prompts enforce strict extraction markers:
  ```markdown
  # [Your Creative, Engaging Headline]
  > **EXCERPT:** [A sharp, 1-to-2 sentence summary / teaser for the front page]
  ```
  Both fields are parsed upon generation and stored directly in `news_feed(headline, excerpt)`.
- **Temporal Publishing Alignment (`TEMPORAL_ARTICLE_MODES`):**
  - **`RETROSPECTIVE`** (`MACRO_SLATE_RECAP`, `SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY`, `LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD`, `PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY`): Publishes during calendar `week` evaluating the concluded action from `week - 1`.
  - **`PROSPECTIVE`** (`SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS`, `LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER`, Super Bowl Previews): Previews upcoming scheduled matchups for `week`.
  - **`CUMULATIVE`** (`POWER_RANKINGS`, `AWARDS_TRACKER`, `PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE`, `FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION`, etc.): Evaluates hierarchy entering `week` based on cumulative results through `week - 1`.
- **Curatorial Autonomy & Slate Digest (`newsroom/config/curatorial_autonomy_directives.json`):** Writers are fed both full scoreboards (last week's results and this week's schedule) and the division standings in the brief's `season_landscape`, rather than a narrow pre-filtered Top 5 list. Subject selection is layered: the article type's own curatorial autonomy block (`article_types.json`, or a playoff override's) comes first, and the writer's directive from `curatorial_autonomy_directives.json` is appended as "YOUR SPECIFIC WRITER SELECTION FILTER". If only one exists, it is used alone. An Editorial Desk subject assignment (§7.3) overrides both. Thirteen writers have a directive; each is written as what the writer leans toward plus alternatives, never as a single required angle (personality plan phase 1), so the same lens doesn't drive every column:
  - *Barnwell:* games where the result and the numbers disagree: lucky one-score winners, unlucky teams better than their record, favorites exposed by upsets; other weeks a league-wide trend or a decision that swung a game.
  - *Sando:* front-office pressure: aging, mediocre rosters (GM job security) or young blue-chip rosters (coaching development).
  - *Joyner:* schematic complexity and play-level efficiency: extreme tempo, boom-or-bust performances, tactical mismatches, or a defense that did the breaking (sacks, tackles for loss, takeaways from the box score's defensive lines and `get_defense_special_teams_leaders`; his data table charts a defense's recorded numbers, never pressure rates, snaps or targets).
  - *Rosenthal:* entertainment and vibes: high-tempo, high-excitement chaos and electric young quarterbacks.
  - *Chadiha:* the human element and historical stakes: aging stars, adversity, historic franchises under pressure.
  - *Yates:* statistical anomalies, milestones and fantasy volume that support factual lists.
  - *Simmons:* the "wonkiest" game: upsets, bad beats, historic franchises over- or under-achieving the eye test.
  - *Acho:* exposed flaws and public overreactions: popular favorites that lost, high-tempo offenses shut down (shown in the box score's defensive lines and the defenders' season numbers; his column format names those plus `get_team_efficiency_profile` as the defensive and situational evidence).
  - *The Athletic:* process, scheme and roster trajectory; young-core surges and schedule-adjusted winners; avoids garbage-time inflation.
  - *Skip Bayless:* superstar drama and the "clutch gene": prime-time chokes or game-winning drives by marquee players.
  - *Kimes:* games where efficiency tells a different story than the score, and smart defensive schemes, evidenced by the box score's defensive lines and `get_defense_special_teams_leaders` (coverage rotations and pressures are her read of them; her column format credits unheralded defenders with their recorded numbers).
  - *Orlovsky:* the most extreme quarterback performances only, good or bad.
  - *Clark:* locker-room dynamics, player sacrifice and leadership under pressure.
- **Historical Comparisons (optional, 1990–2023):** National writers may compare a team or player to a real NFL team or season from 1990–2023 when the parallel genuinely sharpens the argument. It isn't required; the prompt says most articles need none, allows at most one, forbids inventing a historical team, and gives no canned examples (the old ones, e.g. the 2000 Ravens, got reused everywhere). Beat reporters don't receive this instruction.
- **Marquee Teams & Superstar Reporting Rule (Angle Rotation & Narrative Momentum):** National sports coverage naturally centers around the league's marquee franchises, undefeated powerhouses, and superstar quarterbacks (Crawford, Maye, Whitfield, etc.). Writers are instructed not to avoid them, but generic praise and repetitive overviews are strictly forbidden. When evaluating a top-tier contender or MVP candidate, writers must adopt one of five specific investigative angles: (1) The Vulnerability / The Nitpick (subtle flaws on film or in situational stats), (2) The Scheme / The Antidote (how opponents are scheming against them), (3) The Complacency & Focus Trap (the psychological toll of being the hunted), (4) The Future Bill & Roster Toll (cap commitments, expiring contracts, coordinator poaching), or (5) The Foil / The Contender's Challenge (framing rivals around whether they can threaten the giant). Writers must also maintain *Narrative Momentum*: assume an informed reader who already knows the standings and dive straight into the latest strategic wrinkle or key question without re-introducing baseline records.
- **Beat Writer Opening Variety Rule:** Beat reporters must not open articles with facility or sensory clichés ("The mood inside the locker room...", "The atmosphere inside the building...", "Walk through the facility..."). Prompts mandate rotating across four distinct hooks: (1) Film Breakdown Hook (specific play from last week corrected in practice), (2) Press Conference / Quote Hook (candid coordinator or captain quote), (3) Personnel Angle (unheralded starter or backup stepping in), or (4) Historical / Matchup Stakes Hook.
- **Headline & Excerpt Variety Directive:** To break formulaic headline monoculture, the *Anti-Colon Rule* limits colon-separated headlines (`[Topic]: [Subtitle]`) to no more than 1 in 4 pieces, requiring writers to alternate between bold declarative statements, provocative questions, narrative hooks, player/coach quotes, and analytical theses. Excerpts must be sharp, thesis-driven lead statements and must not open with stock clauses ("Film charting reveals...", "As the regular season concludes...").
- **Banned Journalistic Clichés & Buzzwords:** The shared `natural_language_rule` explicitly bans overused sports-writing idioms: "paper tiger", "blueprint to victory", "existential", "litmus test", "bellwether", "championship pedigree", "look no further than", "house of cards", "smoke and mirrors", "fool's gold", "silver lining", "flashing red", "ticking time bomb", "in the crucible of", "the mood inside...", and "That's the list." as a closing line.
- **Modular Game Capsules (`SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS` & `LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER`):** Game lookahead capsules avoid repetitive 6-part bulleted headers by organizing into dynamic, cohesive 2-to-3 paragraph capsules that organically integrate strategic context, key situational splits (`get_team_efficiency_profile`), flashpoint matchups, and projected scores. Local primers organize their final checklist under dynamic tactical game-plan mandates rather than a rigid "Blueprint to Victory" header.
- **Invented detail vs. data (JR, Oct 15: invent freely what the data can't contradict):** Scores, records, stat lines, injury statuses and rankings must come from the brief or the tools. How each game unfolded comes from its game script (§2.14), which the shared `natural_language_rule` block calls canon (`GAME SCRIPTS ARE CANON`): quarter scores, scoring plays and their order, scorers, clock, lead changes, the winning score, key moments, adjustments and defensive standouts are shared by every writer and never contradicted. Beyond the script writers invent the texture no data records (snaps between the scores, play calls, pressure and coverage described in words, blocks, drops, sideline scenes, crowd, quotes), plus anonymous sources such as Sando's "NFC executive" quotes; a defender with no recorded line for a game is praised in words, not numbers. Betting lines and non-existent injury speculation are never used: prompts forbid citing unverified medical timetables or inventing injuries. **Contracts and moves** (JR's R1/R13, `docs/EDITORIAL_MATRIX.md` *Roster Moves & Contracts*): that a move happened (who signed, released, re-signed or restructured whom, which team, which week), its terms (years, total, this season's cap hit, bonus, cut savings, dead money, no-trade clause), team cap space, spend and dead money, rosters and free-agent status, and the year a contract runs through come only from the contract tools or the brief and are never contradicted; they appear only when they matter to the article's subject (most articles carry no cap numbers). A projected yearly figure (`est.`) is hedged in prose. Never invented even though untracked: guaranteed money, incentive details, option years. Free to invent: negotiation colour, anonymous front-office or agent quotes, motives, locker-room reaction, depth-chart meaning, a reason for a cut that doesn't contradict data (no invented injury, no "cut for cap space" when the team has room unless framed as opinion), and unnamed, unpriced interest from other teams. A trade is done only when executed; anything else is a rumor (Phase 8): rumors come only from `get_trade_rumors` / the briefs (`rumor_ok` proposals, through the Week 8 deadline), are worded as talks, and carry no player names or figures beyond what the rumor line gives; only these rumors may be described as actual talks. The national research block also names `check_trade_package` for the R6/R7 hypothetical packages. `article_structure_directives.json`'s "do not invent … contract details" stays as the policy (R11). Official weekly injuries from the league's capture are integrated across newsroom tiers: national writers cover marquee injuries ($\ge 88$ OVR, $\ge 50$ Pop, starting QBs), local beat reporters cover all injured starters, fantasy analysts cover skill starters and handcuffs, and Agent Wire covers beat reports and fan shock. Madden ratings are never cited: writers may use OVR and team ratings from their tools to judge talent, but the shared `natural_language_rule` block (appended to every article and tweet prompt) forbids rating numbers, "OVR"/"overall" wording and any mention of Madden or the video game in published text.
- **Regular season vs. playoffs rule:** both research blocks say season numbers (player season stats, the defense and special-teams leaders, team situational rates, standings) are the regular season only, playoff numbers come only from playoff box scores and `postseason_stats`, and the two are never added together. `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks both blocks.
- **Team situational rule:** the national `DEFENSIVE DATA` block and the beat research block also say season third-down, red-zone and penalty rates come from `get_team_efficiency_profile` and a game's only from its `team_situational` box-score line (none = don't invent the game's totals), that third-down defense has no season total, and that down-and-distance splits aren't recorded. The directives that ask for situational football point at those tools: the regular-season and postseason lookahead Stat to Know, the matchup primer (its Defensive Mandate may be a red-zone target against the opponent's red-zone TD rate), the schematic autopsy and its Weeks 20–22 override, the postgame report card, the season progress report, the contender blueprint, the playoff autopsy, the QB duel (its blitz-conversion line is replaced by team rates plus the QBs' interceptions and sacks taken), the Super Bowl comprehensive preview, masterclass and Tale of the Tape. `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks them.
- **Player splits rule:** both research blocks list `get_player_scheme_splits` and say to cite a split with its game count, as a tendency, and to leave splits out when its `verdict` says there aren't enough real games. Seven article types end their `curatorial_autonomy` with a `SPLITS DATA:` line: `LOCAL_PLAYER_SPOTLIGHT`, `PLAYER_PROGRESS_REPORT`, `QUARTERBACK_DUEL_TAPE_BREAKDOWN`, `LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER`, `FANTASY_START_SIT`, `FANTASY_MATCHUP_EXPLOITS` and `FANTASY_PLAYOFF_STREAMERS` (their `data_queried` list the tool; fantasy types by tool name). `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks the registration and hookups.
- **League coaching staffs:** every prompt `compile_agent_prompt` builds (national, local, fantasy, custom and offseason articles) ends its `WEEK CONTEXT` with a `LEAGUE COACHING STAFFS (Season N)` block from `engines.coach_profile.league_staff_directory`: one line per team with its head coach, OC and DC that season, and the rule that this league's staffs differ from the real NFL, so writers name a coach only from the list and never from real life, and call an "unnamed" coordinator by title without supplying a name. It exists because writers covering many teams (power rankings, slate lookaheads) don't call `get_coach_profile` for each one and fell back on real-life coaches (Mike Tomlin, Shane Steichen, Matt LaFleur in 2036). If the coaching tables can't be read, the prompt has no block (`STAFF DIRECTORY UNAVAILABLE` is logged). Agent Wire posts (§7.8) write from facts packets and don't carry it.
- **Coaching tendencies rule:** both research blocks (`COACHING TENDENCIES:`; the beat block also tells reporters to query their coach and, before a game, the opponent's) say the schemes and Low / Medium / High tendencies from `get_coach_profile` and `get_matchup_edges` frame scheme talk. Pass lean and fourth down are measured in this league (§2.12) and can be stated as what the team does; man coverage is the staff's real-world philosophy and is presented as reputation, never as what the defense has done; there is no blitz data, so writers never put a number on how often a defense blitzes or call it a season-long habit. Never a percentage, never a count or rate of how often a team blitzed or played man in a game; describing in words what a defense did in one game is fine when it fits the game script.
