Thirteen article types end their `curatorial_autonomy` with a `COACHING DATA:` line naming the tool and what to use it for: `PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY` (seat temperature), `COACHING_HOT_SEAT_AUDIT` (every eliminated coach it sorts), `FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION`, `LOCAL_SEASON_PROGRESS_REPORT`, `SEASON_PROGRESS_AUDIT`, `SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY`, `QUARTERBACK_DUEL_TAPE_BREAKDOWN`, `SUPER_BOWL_COMPREHENSIVE_PREVIEW`, `SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS`, `LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER`, `LOCAL_PLAYER_SPOTLIGHT`, `LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD` and `SUPER_BOWL_MEDIA_INTERVIEW_AUDIT` (their `data_queried` list the profile or the coaching matchup), as do the playoff overrides of the schematic autopsy and the slate lookahead. `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks the registration, both rule blocks and the hookups.
- **Defensive data rule:** the national writers' research block (`DEFENSIVE DATA`, between the tool list and the optional historical comparisons) and the beat reporters' research block tell writers that defense and special teams have real season numbers (and game lines where captured) and to back defensive claims with named players, with three limits: a player Madden doesn't list has unknown numbers, not zeros; listed defenders never sum to team sacks or takeaways; pressures, blitzes, coverage, snap counts and targets aren't recorded, so they are never given as numbers or rates, but may be described in words when it fits the box score and the game script (a pass rush that lived in the backfield, a corner who blanketed his man). `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks the tool is registered and the Week 19 directives point at it; `tests/test_defense_tools.py` covers the line formatting.
- **Cap and move data lines:** nine article types end their `curatorial_autonomy` with a `CAP DATA:` line naming the contract tool and what it's for, each with the relevance rule ("Only when it bears on the story: most … need one or two cap figures or none"), the basis and `est.` hedging: `FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION` (from Week 15 next season's space as the rebuild runway), `SEASON_PROGRESS_AUDIT`, `PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY` (followed by its `TRADE PACKAGES:` rule), `SUPER_BOWL_RUNNER_UP_POSTMORTEM` (grounds its Championship-Window Outlook's contract/cap pressures), `FRANCHISE_ARCHITECTURE_BLUEPRINT` (followed by its `TRADE PACKAGES:` rule), `DRAFT_BLUEPRINT_ROSTER_AUDIT` (the rookie reserve; no speculative trades), `PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE` and `LOCAL_PLAYER_SPOTLIGHT` (`get_player_contract`), `LOCAL_SEASON_PROGRESS_REPORT`. Four end with a `ROSTER MOVES:` line (`get_league_transactions` / the brief's blocks; a move only when it bears on the subject, never an invented one): `POWER_RANKINGS` (never rank a team on an invented move), `SEASON_PROGRESS_AUDIT`, `LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER` (a new signing who may play), `LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD` (the next man up after a release). Their `data_queried` list the tools; `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks the lines and the brief hookups.
- **Contract facts rule:** both research blocks list the three contract tools (below) with a `CONTRACT FACTS RULE:` (moves, terms and cap figures only from the tools or the brief and only when they matter to the subject, most articles carrying no cap numbers; `est.` figures hedged; "not known" never filled in; colour invented, never a term, a figure or a move). `tests/test_writer_config.py`: the tools are registered and named in both blocks; `test_contract_asks_name_the_cap_tools` (JR's R14) lets a type ask for cap or contract content only if its `data_queried` or `curatorial_autonomy` names `get_team_cap_sheet` or `get_player_contract`, and no persona may ask; `test_rumor_and_trade_wording` fails on any sentence in the article types, personas, research blocks, `SOCIAL_RULES` or the two matrices that lets a trade be reported as done without saying it was executed.
- **Database Context & Research Tools:** Agents have autonomous access to query live simulation context via ReAct AFC tools:
  - `get_weekly_slate`: Returns the complete scoreboard for all games in a given week with final scores, victory margins, excitement indices, and team IDs.
  - `get_season_standings`: Returns full NFL division standings with wins, losses, win %, points scored (PF), points allowed (PA), and point differential, from regular-season games only.
  - `get_top_popular_players`: Returns the top 20 most popular players across the league with Madden OVR, age, experience, and popularity indices.
  - `get_top_rated_players`: The highest-rated players by Madden OVR at every position (default 200, capped at 300; long snappers excluded), one compact line each with team, OVR, age, experience and season totals: passing/rushing/receiving, tackles/sacks/INT/forced fumbles for listed defenders, FG for kickers, net average for punters. This is the pool for league-wide player rankings such as the Top 100. Ratings run high (this season the 100th-best player is OVR 92 and 733 players are 80+), and the popularity list holds only 41 of the 108 highest-rated players, so it can't serve as the pool.
  - `get_all_team_popularities`: Returns all 32 teams ranked by popularity index, watchability rating, and overall roster quality.
  - `get_player_context` / `get_player_season_stats`: Resolves player by name or ID (season stats are the regular season; when the player has captured playoff lines, a separate `postseason_stats` line, summed from the season's completed non-regular-season games in `game_stat_lines` before the article's week, with a note to keep the two apart); returns a 5-year historical statline summary (`five_year_statline_summary`), trailing per-season averages (`five_year_per_season_averages`), career arc assessment (`career_arc_assessment`: Breakout Campaign, Prime / Consistent, Decline, etc.), age, years of experience, physical measurements (height/weight), career awards list, Madden OVR, cumulative season stats, stored popularity components (SpikeIndex, $R_{\text{rating}}$, $F_{\text{platform}}$, $T_{\text{success}}$, $A_{\text{awards}}$, $E_{\text{exposure}}$), player Playoff Clout, and season touch/yard share for RB/FB/WR/TE (augmented with rolling 3-game touch share `recent_3_game_touch_share_pct` and `usage_delta_pct` for seasons with captured weekly game logs). Season stats add sacks taken for passers and, from `season_stat_lines`, `games_played` plus defense (tackles with solo/assisted, sacks, TFL, INT and return yards, pass deflections, forced fumbles, recoveries, defensive TDs, safeties), kicking (FG with long and 50+, XP), punting (average, net, inside the 20), kick/punt returns and sacks allowed, only the categories the player is listed in. Defenders, kickers and punters drop the all-zero offensive lines; a defender (or K/P) with no listed line gets a note that the numbers are unknown, not zero.
  - `get_team_context`: Resolves team by name, abbreviation, or ID; returns win-loss record, 5-year historical record (`five_year_record`), 5-year chronological trajectory with division finishes and playoff exits (`five_year_arc`), franchise state (`franchise_state`: Championship Window, Perennial Contender, Ascending Core, Rebuilding, Roster Purgatory), watchability, popularity, Madden team ratings, top 3 players, and a one-line `head_coach` (name, season with the team, schemes) pointing to `get_coach_profile`.
  - `get_team_season_schedule`: Returns a team's complete season schedule and game log: week-by-week opponents, scores, win/loss outcomes, victory margins, one-score game breakdown, excitement ratings, and game IDs.
  - `get_game_box_score`: Returns team box score and top individual game contributions, plus `team_situational` per team with only real values (captured, or listed in `exact_fields`; estimated backlog values are never shown): third/fourth-down and two-point conversions (with attempts when known), red-zone TDs and FGs (with trips when known), penalties or penalty yards, quarter-by-quarter scoring, first downs and time of possession (captured box scores); plus, from `game_stat_lines`, `defensive_performances` (defenders with a sack, INT, forced fumble, recovery, defensive TD, safety, 7+ tackles or 2+ TFL; biggest playmakers first) and `kicking` lines. Games the capture didn't cover get a `defense_note` telling the writer not to cite individual defensive stats. It ends with `game_script`, the game's rendered script (§2.14), which the tool description tells writers not to contradict.
  - `get_defense_special_teams_leaders(category, team_identifier, limit, season, rookies_only)`: season leaders from `season_stat_lines`, league-wide or for one team (limit capped at 50); each line shows `rookie` or `exp N` from `player_seasons.years_of_experience`, and `rookies_only=True` keeps first-season players only (for DROY). Categories (`LEADER_CATEGORIES`): sacks, interceptions, tackles, tackles_for_loss, pass_deflections, forced_fumbles, takeaways (INT + fumble recoveries), defensive_tds, field_goals, punting (net average), kick_returns, punt_returns, sacks_allowed (fewest, linemen). Each line carries the player's full defensive or special-teams line, and the note warns that listed players don't sum to team totals and that pressures, snaps, targets and coverage aren't recorded.
  - `get_team_injury_report(team_identifier, week, season)`: Official weekly injury report for a team. Resolves depth-chart starter status and flags `is_key_injury: true` if OVR $\ge 88$, Pop $\ge 50$, or starting QB. National preview slates inject key injuries (`preview_slate['all_games'][i]['key_injuries']`), and beat briefs inject the team's injured starters (`team_injury_report`).
  - `get_advanced_team_analytics`: Reads the stored TWI components (σ_top, P_draft, Y_prod, Purgatory Penalty), TWI, franchise POP, team Playoff Clout, starter age (top 22 by OVR), and $B$ / $L$ / $D$ / $N$ / Legacy Floor from `market_constants`.
  - `get_advanced_game_analytics`: Completed games return pace/production ($P$ from `gotw_engine.production_score`), Upset Leverage ($U$), excitement, and both teams' Opponent-Adjusted Game Credit. Scheduled games return projected $U$ (`excitement_projection.expected_upset`) and the underdog's win probability.
  - `get_opponent_adjusted_credit`: Opponent-Adjusted Game Credit (Section 2.4). No team → all 32 ranked with credit, recent-form credit, Trajectory Multiplier and label, strength of schedule, raw point differential per game, expected wins and win luck; with a team → that summary plus a game-by-game credit log.
  - `get_coach_of_the_year_race(limit, season)`: Section 2.11. Head coaches ranked by COTY score (default top 10), each with record and win%, wins above expectation and expected wins, `team_ovr` and its rank, win% rank, roster outperformance, last season's win% and the change (null unless the team's full previous regular season is recorded), and the first-season flag; the note says when improvement is left out. Registered for every writer and named in the national research block.
  - `get_clutch_profile(team_identifier, quarterback, season)`: Section 2.15. Late-game records from the game scripts for a team or a quarterback (his starts): fourth-quarter comebacks, game-winning drives, blown double-digit and fourth-quarter leads, records by halftime and three-quarter state, overtime record, points per game by quarter, the biggest comeback win and lead lost, and the games behind each count; regular season and postseason separate. Neither = the league leaders. Named in the national research block and in the beat block (the reporter's team and quarterback); the note tells writers to cite the counts as fact and never compare them with real-NFL career totals.
  - `get_matchup_edges`: Section 2.8. Pass, rush and ball-security edges plus Trench Edge for both offenses in a matchup; with no opponent, uses the team's next scheduled game. A `coaching_matchup` block gives, for each offense against the other defense, the offense's coach, scheme, pass lean and fourth-down tendency and the defense's front and coverage tendency, each tier marked `measured` or `reputation` (§3.3a, §2.12).
  - `get_player_scheme_splits(player_identifier, seasons=2)`: Section 2.13. A QB, back, receiver or tight end's per-game production against Strong / Average / Weak scoring defenses, pass rushes and coverages over this season and last: overall per-game line, each group's games, blended per-game averages and change from his average, real and skipped synthetic game counts, a `verdict` when no group has 3 real games, and a note on citing splits.
  - `get_offseason_movement(team_identifier, season)`: the player ledger into a season (§3.3m): retired, free agents (unsigned, never "retired" when no retirement list was captured; signed-in-season team named), changed teams, drafted, other arrivals; overalls only rank. `get_player_career` also returns `moves_between_seasons` and `status_now` from the ledger.
  - `get_player_career(player_identifier)` / `get_team_history(team_identifier)`: a player's whole league career since 2026 and a franchise's season-by-season history (§3.3l); 2026–2034 seasons flagged `history`; `get_player_career` also gives age, OVR, its change and dev trait by season from 2035 on (`ratings_by_season`). With real NFL history loaded (§3.3x), `get_player_career` adds `real_nfl_career` (seasons, totals, playoff totals, awards, draft), `career_including_real_nfl` (real + league regular-season totals) and `real_nfl_note`, and `get_team_history` adds `real_nfl_seasons` (1999–2025, with non-All-Pro award winners) and a note; the rule: real NFL seasons through 2025 are fact, league seasons from 2026 are this league, a combined total is quoted only as a "career" total. `swarm_dispatcher`'s tool line says the same.
  - `get_coach_profile(team_identifier, season)`: the team's head coach that season: season with the team and start year, who he replaced, offensive scheme and defensive front, three tendencies (pass lean, fourth down, man coverage; no blitz rate) in words with their source (measured this season, measured last season, real-world tier, or real-world staff philosophy), this season's regular-season and playoff record, `record_with_team` (regular season over every season of this tenure) and `playoff_record_with_team` (postseason W-L with this team over the same tenure, Super Bowls included; `0-0` when he has none), counted from `record_with_team_since`: the tenure's first season, or 2026 (`coach_profile.RECORDS_FROM`) when the tenure began earlier; each finished season from its `coach_season_lines` row (2026–2034 generated, with exact per-coach totals; 2035 on archived, §3.3h), the current season from `games` (`with_team_record`); both null only when a finished season has neither a line nor all 17 games; `career_scope` (`since joining this league` for a `mu_era_only` snapshot, §3.3h), career line (regular season and win%, winning seasons, playoffs, Super Bowls), Super Bowls with the team, Coach of the Year seasons, and a note on citing tendencies. Records count only games the article may see (§3.3a); the article's own season's awards are hidden while an article is being written. `coaching_tree` `{label, line, mentors, proteges}` (`coaching_tree_block`, read through the season before while it's played, through the season once awards are visible; omitted when there's nothing to say) gives his coaching lineage (§3.3a).
  - `get_press_conference(team_identifier, season, week)`: the team's recent postgame head-coach press conference transcripts — the six most recent CLOSED or DECLINED pressers, newest first, **strictly before** the article's publication week (`run_context.cutoff_week`, always applied: an explicit `week` is an extra `week =` filter, and a future season's cutoff of 0 returns nothing) — with every on-record question and answer, or the note when the coach declined. Off-the-record answers, and the questions they answer, are never printed. Beat writers only; national writers are never offered it and never quote pressers.
  - `get_team_efficiency_profile`: Section 2.6. Pythagorean wins and pyth luck, pace & production, pass/rush yards, giveaways per game, takeaways per game, and turnover margin; all 32 sorted by pyth luck, or one team. Each team also carries `situational` (`db_tools.situational_profiles`) from the `team_seasons` Team Stats totals through the latest loaded weekly capture (not cut off by the article's week): third- and fourth-down conversions and rate, two-point tries, red-zone trips (and per game), TD and scoring rate, red-zone trips and TD rate allowed, penalties and penalty yards per game, and league ranks (`third_down_rank`, `fourth_down_rank`, `red_zone_rank`, `red_zone_defense_rank`, `discipline_rank`; 1 = best). Third downs allowed appear only from games where the opponent's `team_stats` row is real (captured, or listed in `exact_fields`), with the game count; there is no season third-down defense total.
  - `get_league_leaderboards`: Returns top 5 teams by watchability and popularity.
  - `get_draft_order`: Round 1 order (Picks 1–32) with playoff-exit brackets (§2.10), each pick with `locked`, `selection_status` and `strength_of_schedule`, plus `locked_picks`, `playoff_field_known` and `rounds_complete`; respects the run's week cutoff.
  - `get_team_draft_needs`: A team's roster needs ranked by urgency, from starter rating deficits, positional depth, age cliffs and statistical phase rankings.
  - `get_team_roster_depth_chart`: A team's full depth chart by position group (QB, RB, WR, TE, OT, IOL, EDGE, DT, LB, CB, S) with ratings, age tiers and roster demographics.
  - `get_draft_trade_value`: Jimmy Johnson trade-chart points and typical trade packages for any pick (1–260).
  - `get_franchise_rebuild_status`: A franchise's lifecycle stage (Championship Window, Youth Ascent, Roster Purgatory, Ground-Up Rebuild) and recommended draft posture. With a NULL `team_ovr` the OVR tests (≥ 85 window, ≤ 83 rebuild) are skipped.
  - `get_mock_draft(season, limit)`: this week's saved Round 1 media mock draft (`mock_draft_picks`; run and saved on first call, from the scouting consensus), pick by pick with team, prospect profile (blank fields null; `overall_rating` removed, `consensus_grade`/`consensus_rank`/`round_label` added at the cutoff), fit, rationale and `locked`; `limit` keeps the first N picks (24 at Week 20); `source` is `saved` or `generated` (§2.10).
  - `get_scouted_draft_board(season, limit, position)`: the board for class season + 1: the public scouting consensus at the article's cutoff (`consensus_rank`, `grade`, `round_label`, `rank_change`; null before the scouting board exists, `board` says which order) with `draft_prospects`' `projected_pick`, `projected_round`, `round_pick`, `name`, `pos`, `college`, `ht`, `wt`, `age`, `archetype`, `notes` (null where the scan was blank; **no Madden OVR**, Q6), in consensus order once it exists, default 32, filtered by position or position group (QB, OT, EDGE, CB, LB…).
  - `get_draft_risers_fallers(season, limit)` (team management step 4 → step 5 Phase 9 seam): the latest scouting step visible at the article's cutoff (`scouting_read.risers_fallers`): risers and fallers with name, position, college, class year, consensus rank, grade, round label, rank and grade change, and up to 3 stored college storylines behind each move (`draft_mover_line`, pure); no Madden ratings, no hidden values.
  - `get_front_office_standing(team_identifier, season)`: `fo_standing.standing_facts` for the team (GM, years in the job, rank of 32, reputation, drafting and player-development words, hot seat, early read) plus `draft_record_facts` and `development_record_facts` (risers and fallers: player, position, age, "70 -> 75", verdict, rookie year); never a score. `get_front_office_rankings(season)`: the 32 front offices' standing facts, best first (the general consensus).
  - `get_gm_record(team_identifier, season)`: `gm_record.gm_record` (§3.3f): the team's GM's record in every job he has held here and the team's earlier GMs (records, finishes, how each tenure ended, `gms_on_record_since`); never a score. Listed in the Franchise State of the Union's data, whose prompt has the writer call it.
  - `get_team_draft_record(team_identifier, season)`: the team's Round 1–2 picks of the last three drafts with their HIT / OK / MISS / BUST verdicts and streak sentences ("three straight first-round misses"; `fo_quality.team_draft_record` → `draft_record_facts`, pure); never q or a hit score.
  - `get_team_articles`: Returns recent editorial articles and analysis referencing a specific team (resolves by name, city, abbreviation, or ID).
  - `get_player_articles`: Returns recent editorial articles and profiles referencing a specific player (resolves by name or ID).
  - **Roster moves, contracts and the cap** (step 5 of `docs/done/TEAM_MANAGEMENT_PLAN.md`, `docs/done/team_management/05_NEWSROOM_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md`; each a `fetch_*` in `db_tools.py` plus the pure formatters in `newsroom/roster_moves.py`). Every money figure is printed with its basis: `scanned Week N` (the Team Salary scan's capture week), `from the signing` (a CPU signing's contract: bonus, cut savings and dead money print as "not known", never $0), `estimated: last cap scan … plus N roster moves since; dead money from in-season signings is unknown` (a `team_cap_seasons` row whose `derived_at` is later than `scanned_at`), and projected years of a re-signing or restructure, which are shown and always labelled `est.` (JR, 2026-10-20; e.g. `2037: $14.2M est.`). Money is prose (`$16.8M`, `$3.93M`, `$200K`, `-$29.5M`). The docstrings tell writers to call them only when a move or contract bears on the story.
    - `get_team_cap_sheet(team_identifier, season, limit)`: with a team, `cap_basis`, cap, adjusted cap, cap space with its league rank, salaries, dead money (`cap_penalty`), total spend, next rookie reserve, `top_contracts` (largest cap hits this season with through year, total, bonus, cut savings, dead money if cut, no-trade clause, incentive flag, basis and future hits), `expiring` (contract-year players, `years_remaining = 1`), `committed_by_year` (scanned hits for the next four seasons, plus projected new-deal hits as `est.` with their count) and a count of the team's visible moves; no team = all 32 by cap space.
    - `get_player_contract(player_identifier, season)`: team (or "free agent (released by the X, Week N)"), the ACTIVE contract as above with this season's and future hits, the `new_deal` line for a re-signing/extension (`new deal: N years, $X total, starts YYYY`), the season's replaced/released/traded contract rows and the player's visible moves; "No contract on file. Don't invent one." when there is none.
    - `get_league_transactions(team_identifier, week, types, position, notable_only, limit, season)`: visible moves newest week first, one line each (`Week 4 · SIGNED · Dolphins signed CB Matt Beason (free agent): 1 year, $4.49M · now CB3 on the depth chart · notable: yes`; releases add dead money and "free agent since Week N" or "since signed by the X (Week N)"; re-signings the headline terms and the new deal's start when known; restructures the space freed), `counts` by type and `rows_with_no_player`; a week the article can't see yet is refused. `trades` lists the visible **executed** GM trades (`fetch_trades` = `engines/front_office.executed_trades` cut off by `roster_moves.trade_visible`: a Week N trade has no capture, so the Week N edition on sees it; offseason trades follow the offseason signings rule), one `roster_moves.trade_line` each: `Week 4 · TRADE (executed) · Jets acquired WR Rich Hanson ($12.5M cap hit this season) from the Patriots; Patriots acquired CB … and the Jets' 2037 2nd-round pick from the Jets · cap this season: Jets +$3.5M, Patriots -$3.5M` (cap hits from `gm_trade_assets.cap_hit_now`; never an OVR). Its `TRADED` leg rows are left out of `moves`; `types=TRADED`, `team`, `week` and `position` filter trades too.
    - `get_trade_rumors(team_identifier, season)` (Phase 8): rumor material from `fetch_rumors` = `front_office.trade_rumors` (non-executed, `rumor_ok`, `origin = 'ENGINE'` proposals) cut off by `roster_moves.rumor_visible`: only proposals made **before** the article's week (the status timestamps are wall-clock, so the proposal's `week` is the cutoff) and only through the trade deadline (`RUMOR_LAST_EDITION_WEEK` = `TRADE_DEADLINE_WEEK` = 8; JR §6 Q7: the Week 8 edition is the last with rumors, so Week 8's own proposals never become rumors); another season's article gets none. Each is one `rumor_line`, always labelled `RUMOR, not a done deal`, with the two teams, who made the call and why (`trigger`), the kinds of assets (a position or "a draft pick", never a name or a figure) and the outcome: `talks stalled, no deal` for a `REJECTED`/`EXPIRED` proposal whose `expires_week` is before the article's week, else `outcome not known: report it only as talks` (`rumor_outcome`; an `EXECUTED` proposal is never a rumor). A leaked talk's `gm_trade_leaks` row is one `leak_line` with the stage wording (have opened talks / talks are close / talks stalled, no deal) and may name a player the leaker named, never as traded. Past the deadline the tool says so and returns none.
    - `check_trade_package(team_a, team_b, team_a_sends, team_b_sends, season)` (Phase 8, the R6/R7 helper): checks a writer's **hypothetical** package with step 3's `front_office.legality_check` (cap, no-trade clauses, roster limits, QB/K/P slots, the deadline, pick ownership, double booking, tradeable, fairness). Items are comma lists of players on the sending team now (name match) and picks (`2037 R2`, `2037 2nd-round pick (Bills)`, `2037 R2 Bills` for a pick held from another team; `parse_package_item`). It is checked at the article's week through the deadline and at the coming offseason (week 24, OFFSEASON window) from Week 9 to Week 23 (`package_check_week`). The output lists each player's real cap hit, deal length, total and end year (and a no-trade clause), and pass/FAIL lines without the numbers behind them or the name of an asset another proposal has booked (`package_check_lines`, so a check can't leak pending talks), plus the framing rule: a legal package may appear only as the writer's own idea, never as reported talks.
    - **Notability** (`roster_moves.notability`; JR, 2026-10-20): a move is notable only when the player is rated `NOTABLE_OVR` = 85+ (in line with the 90+ marquee signings; the rating is never printed), so an in-season free-agent pickup never leads the briefs or the Agent Wire. Context flags (a starter at his position by `is_starter_rank`, popularity 50+, a re-signing of $20M+, a signing of $5M+, a restructure freeing $5M+, a release leaving $5M+ dead money) describe and rank moves but never make one notable. The exception is `TRADED` (Phase 8): every executed trade is notable; trades reach the briefs and the Agent Wire as whole trades, never as legs. On 2036 Weeks 1–4, 17 of 181 moves are notable (9 re-signings, 8 restructures; no in-season signing is rated above 80).
  - `get_record_book(category, team_identifier, season)`: Section 2.9. Queries the canonical all-time NFL record book and franchise records (matching category names/labels flexibly like `season_pass_tds`, `Passing TDs in a season`, `season_pass_yards`, `season_rec_tds`, `game_pass_tds`, `season_team_points`, `season_team_wins`). Returns all-time NFL record holders, previous record holders, all-time top 10 leaderboards, franchise records for a specified team, and any all-time records broken or tied this season.
  - `search_league_memory(query, team, player_id, seasons, top_k)`: Item 9 (V2.8). Narrative search index over historical universe events (`news_feed`, `agent_memory_entries`, `franchise_records`, `league_record_entries`) powered by `newsroom/league_memory.py`. Computes numpy cosine similarity over embeddings (`gemini-embedding-001`, metered under source `'memory_index'` in `llm_usage`), returning cited snippets (headline, date, season/week, team IDs, player IDs, text excerpt, similarity score). Strictly enforces article cutoff (`is_visible_week`) so writers cannot view future weeks.
- **Fantasy research tools** (`newsroom/fantasy_tools.py`, `FANTASY_TOOLS`): given **only to `FANTASY_*` article types** (`SwarmDispatcher.tools_for(article_type)`), so other prompts don't carry their descriptions. Full PPR, RB = HB + FB. Same week rule as the other tools: a Week N article sees box scores from weeks before N only; projections (`fantasy_projections`) and simulated-league rosters (`fantasy_sim_player_weeks`) up to and including week N are visible (a later week is refused). Depth slots are OVR order within the team's position group; a player released by the article's week keeps his old team (his past lines are with it) but has depth `released` and is out of the depth order (`_roster`, `roster_moves.on_roster`).
  - `get_fantasy_rankings(position, week, sort, limit)`: a week's (default: the article's) projections with opponent, matchup stars, PPR/g, ROS rank and points, ADP rank, rostered/started %, and teams on bye; `sort='ros'` for rest of season. Weeks 2–18 only.
  - `get_fantasy_week_results(week, position, limit)`: a completed week's (default: latest visible) top scorers, biggest beats and biggest misses (projected 8+) vs. the pre-game projection, with stat line, positional finish and rostered %.
  - `get_fantasy_usage(team_identifier, recent_weeks, limit)`: carries, receptions and touches per game with team shares, last N games vs. the rest of the season; no team = league-wide touch risers and fallers (3+ games). Receptions stand in for targets (not tracked).
  - `get_fantasy_waiver_wire(week, position, max_rostered_pct, limit)`: players rostered in ≤ X% of simulated leagues ordered by ROS projection, with rostered % change, recent PPR and touches, plus most added / most dropped, and `nfl_moves` (`nfl_move_lines`: skill players the NFL teams signed in the article's week or the one before, with new team, depth slot and rostered %; then released players still rostered somewhere, as drop candidates projecting 0 until they sign; `FANTASY_WAIVER_WIRE`'s `NFL MOVES:` curatorial line points the writer at it). `tests/test_fantasy_tools.py` covers `nfl_move_lines` on hand-built rows.
  - `get_fantasy_defense_vs_position(position, view)`: PPR allowed per game to each position, season and last 4 games, rank 1 = most generous; `view='playoff_schedule'` = each offense's Weeks 15–17 opponents and average opponent rank.
  - `get_fantasy_player_profile(player_identifier)`: weekly log (opponent, PPR, projection, stat line, rostered/started %), scoring range (mean, best, worst, SD, 20+ boom and sub-8 bust weeks), touches/g, ADP with range, current ROS rank, `team_moves` (his visible moves this season, as move lines) and, for a released player, a `status` saying he has no team and projects 0 until he signs.
  - `get_fantasy_draft_board(position, limit, rookies_only, strategy)`: simulated ADP board with range and draft %, OVR, age, experience, depth slot and team offense ranks; optional ADP among one strategy's managers; once games are visible, season PPR and positional finish so far.
  - `get_fantasy_mock_draft(league, rounds)`: one simulated league's draft pick by pick with each team's strategy.
  - `get_fantasy_season_leaders(position, first_week, last_week, limit)`: PPR leaders over a week range (1–17 season, 15–17 playoffs) with games, per-game, positional finish, ADP and draft %.
  - `get_fantasy_projection_accuracy()`: projection MAE, correlation and guess-the-average MAE for projected starters (weekly top 12 QB/TE, 30 RB/WR), by position, plus the biggest over- and under-projections.
  - `get_fantasy_injuries(week, position, season)`: Weekly injury report for skill positions (QB, RB, WR, TE). Returns injured starters and role-players with depth chart rank, IR status, and the immediate `handcuff_beneficiary` inheriting vacated volume.
- **Season & week scope of the research tools (`newsroom/run_context.py`):** `_execute_agent` sets the article's season and publication week for its thread before calling Gemini (automatic function calling runs the tools on that thread) and clears it afterwards.
  - **Season:** tools take `season: int = 0`, meaning "current": the article's season inside a run, otherwise `league_state.current_season`, otherwise the latest season in `games` (`db_tools.resolve_season`). No tool hardcodes a season.
  - **Week cutoff:** a Week N article can't see results from Week N onward. `get_game_box_score` refuses those games; `get_advanced_game_analytics`, `get_team_season_schedule` and `get_weekly_slate` show them as scheduled with no score; `get_season_standings` counts the record and points from earlier games only; `get_opponent_adjusted_credit`, `get_coach_of_the_year_race`, `get_team_efficiency_profile`, `get_matchup_edges` and the credit inside game analytics use earlier games only (`fetch_team_game_rows(..., before_week=)`); `get_team_articles` / `get_player_articles` return only articles from earlier weeks, which also hides the article's own week. Earlier seasons are fully visible.
  - **Released players** (`roster_moves.on_roster`, Napper's has-game rule): a player is on his team for a Week N article iff `released_week IS NULL OR released_week > N` (N = the cutoff week; with no article context every release counts). `get_team_roster_depth_chart`, `get_team_context`'s top 3, `get_team_draft_needs`, `get_franchise_rebuild_status` and the starter age in `get_advanced_team_analytics` leave released players out; `get_player_season_stats` / `get_player_context`, `get_top_rated_players` and `get_top_popular_players` label their team "free agent (released by the X, Week N)" (`db_tools.team_label`). A CPU signing's new player has no rating or age until the next roster scan: the depth chart counts him with no age in the average, and the draft-needs analysis skips him. The brief's `key_injuries`, the beat brief's `team_injury_report` and the Agent Wire's injuries (§7.8) rank and list on-roster players only.
  - **Transactions** (`roster_moves.txn_visible`): a row headed `WEEK N` happened before Week N's games, so a Week N article sees it (like the injury report) when the capture that loaded it was taken at week ≤ N (`captures.week`); a late `WEEK N` row loaded at N+1 stays out of a regenerated Week N article, and a row with no capture (a confirmed trade) counts as loaded in time. Earlier seasons are visible, later ones hidden. Offseason rows (`week` NULL) are visible only to a Week 24 article once the `signings` offseason event is out. `new_this_week` = visible to Week N but not to Week N−1.
  - **Not cut off:** stored season totals with no per-week history (`season_stats`, `team_seasons` records and indices, player popularity components, ratings, rosters, contracts and team cap rows (except that `get_player_contract` hides a re-signing's terms and projected years while its transaction isn't visible), the draft board and team needs; `get_draft_order` does apply the cutoff, and `get_mock_draft` saves under the run's week). In normal forward runs these already stop at the previous week; when an old week is regenerated they reflect the latest data. `tests/test_run_context.py` covers the context.
- **Prohibited Internal Symbols:** Strict prompt directive banning internal mathematical symbols (`$P$`, `Y_prod`, `(88.17 W)`, `(64.84 POP)`) in favor of natural sports journalism prose.

### 7.1 Article Taxonomy & Writer Archetype Alignments (`newsroom/config/article_types.json`)
`article_types.json` defines 33 core article types: the 29 national/historic types below and the 4 local beat types in §7.2 (plus the 27 fantasy types). Each maps to its allowed writer archetypes and a writing category. A type either carries its own structure directive or, where noted, uses the writer's column format from `article_structure_directives.json`:

1. **The Macro Slate Recap** (`MACRO_SLATE_RECAP`)
   - **Allowed Writers / Archetypes:** Barnwell, Rosenthal (`BARNWELL`, `ROSENTHAL`, `Weekly Recaps`).
   - **Granularity:** Week-level.
   - **Focus:** Cross-league trends, regression candidates, aesthetic watchability power rankings.
   - **Data Queried:** $E_{\text{game}}$, $P_{\text{pace}}$, league-wide point differentials, Pythagorean win expectations.
   - **Structure Source:** Writer format (Barnwell's column or Rosenthal's Weekend Notebook; `article_structure_directives.json`).

2. **The Player Deep Profile** (`PLAYER_DEEP_PROFILE`)
   - **Allowed Writers / Archetypes:** Jeffri Chadiha (Narrative/Legacy), KC Joyner (Scientific Efficiency), Gregg Rosenthal (Aesthetic/Vibes) (`CHADIHA`, `JOYNER`, `ROSENTHAL`, `Player Season Overview`).
   - **Granularity:** In-Season Trajectory / Career Arc.
   - **Focus:** Prestige, longform player profile evaluating their season-to-date trajectory, breakout status, MVP credentials, or legacy implications.
   - **Data Queried:** Player Popularity Index ($Pop_{\text{player}}$), Awards Equity ($A_{\text{awards}}$), Playoff Clout ($S_{\text{playoff}}$), SpikeIndex, Franchise Platform ($F_{\text{platform}}$).
   - **Curatorial Autonomy:** Evaluates season-to-date leaderboards, cumulative stats, and popularity to select one player whose current campaign defines the narrative of the league—an aging legend defending legacy, an MVP frontrunner with massive cultural footprint, or a volatile breakout star, regardless of whether it is Week 3 or Week 17.
   - **Structure Directive:** 4-part profile (`# 1. The Defining Moment / The Hook`, `## 2. The Anatomy of Their Season`, `## 3. The Cultural Footprint & Legacy`, `### 4. The Horizon`).
   - **Prompt Hook:** Select a marquee player whose campaign currently defines the season. Deliver a definitive longform profile on their offensive engine, their cultural footprint, and their career horizon based on their season-to-date tape.

3. **The Franchise State of the Union** (`FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION`)
   - **Allowed Writers / Archetypes:** Sando (`SANDO`, `Front-Office Columnists`).
   - **Granularity:** 3-to-5 year franchise trajectory.
   - **Focus:** General Manager job security, roster demographic distributions, draft hit rates, rebuilding vs. purgatory.
   - **Data Queried:** $P_{\text{draft}}$, $Y_{\text{prod}}$, Purgatory Penalty, Base Market Gravity ($B$), Roster Age, Head-Coach Profile (`get_coach_profile`), Round 1 Draft Order (`get_draft_order`), Round 1 Mock Draft Simulation (`get_mock_draft`).
   - **Curatorial Autonomy:** Evaluates multi-year franchise data, demographic distributions, and standing trends. Identifies a franchise at an existential fork in the road: aging roster in purgatory, high-gravity giant collapsing, or young rebuilding core on the verge of contention. Evaluates coaching hierarchy via `get_coach_profile`. Includes the Coach-Rookie Alignment Test: for early-lottery teams (Picks 1–5), cross-references draft slot (`get_draft_order`) and primary positional need (`get_team_draft_needs`) against the head coach's tenure, scheme, pass lean, and career win percentage (`get_coach_profile`) to interrogate whether to trust the incumbent staff to groom an incoming franchise QB or foundational tackle or if drafting a blue-chip asset necessitates a clean coaching break; may name the projected prospect from `get_mock_draft`.
   - **Structure Source:** Writer format (Mike Sando's Pick Six with anonymous executive quotes).
   - **Prompt Hook:** Analyze a franchise in transition. Ignore the single-game box score. Evaluate their front office's 3-to-5 year trajectory using the Purgatory Penalty, aging roster constraints, and draft equity.

6. **The Awards Tracker** (`AWARDS_TRACKER`)
   - **Allowed Writers / Archetypes:** Field Yates (Objective/Factual), Bill Simmons (Narrative/Historical Debate) (`YATES`, `SIMMONS`, `The Hardware Race`).
   - **Granularity:** Season-level / Hardware Campaign.
   - **Focus:** Active MVP, OPOY, OROY, DPOY, DROY and Coach of the Year races, evaluating true contenders vs. empty-calorie stat accumulators, narrative momentum, rookie learning curves, the defenders driving the defensive races, and which head coaches are winning more than their rosters should.
   - **Data Queried:** Awards Equity ($A_{\text{awards}}$), Player Popularity ($Pop_{\text{player}}$), Team Success ($T_{\text{success}}$), SpikeIndex, defense season leaders (rookies flagged), player season stats, the Coach of the Year race (§2.11).
   - **Curatorial Autonomy:** Aggressively applies the "Empty Calories" Suppressor on sub-.300 teams, pinpointing the intersection of elite explosive production ($SpikeIndex$) and contender team success ($T_{\text{success}}$). A "Defensive Awards Evidence" block (also appended to both postseason overrides) builds the DPOY race from `get_defense_special_teams_leaders` (sacks, TFL, interceptions, takeaways first; forced fumbles, pass deflections, defensive TDs as tiebreakers) and the DROY race from the same tool with `rookies_only=True` (years of experience 0), confirmed with `get_player_season_stats`; a defender with no recorded line has unknown numbers and can't be a candidate; pressures, snaps and coverage numbers are never cited; team record weighs less than for MVP. For Coach of the Year it starts from `get_coach_of_the_year_race` and credits the coach getting the most beyond the roster, the schedule and last season, not simply the best record. The **COACHING DATA CITATION** constraint strictly forbids explicit mentions of internal engine mechanics or labels ("COTY score", "coach scores", "Coach of the Year metric", "historical bonus"); coaches are framed solely through real-world football accomplishments (win-loss record, undefeated seasons, all-time/franchise records broken, margin of victory, roster talent overachievement).
   - **Structure Directive:** 5-part Awards Watch, approx. 1,100–1,400 words (The MVP Frontrunner / The Heavy Crown `#` / `##`, The Contenders / The Chasers `##`, The Coach of the Year Race `##`, The Offensive Rookie Race `##`, The Defensive Races `##`: DPOY frontrunner and chasers with their lines, then a `###` DROY race). Section 3 forbids internal COTY scores or bonuses.
   - **Postseason:** Week 21 runs the `AWARDS_FINALISTS` override and Week 22 `AWARDS_WINNERS` (§7.4).
   - **Prompt Hook:** Analyze the active MVP, OPOY, OROY, DPOY and DROY races across the league. Apply the empty-calories suppressor to eliminate meaningless stats, examine the frontrunner vs. the chasers, rank the Coach of the Year race, break down the offensive rookie race, and settle the defensive races on recorded sacks, tackles for loss and takeaways.
   - **Award records:** single-winner regular-season awards in the `awards` table (`MVP`, `OPOY`, `DPOY`, `OROY`, `DROY`, `COTY`) are parsed, validated, and recorded from the Week 22 `AWARDS_TRACKER` (`AWARDS_WINNERS`) article by `newsroom/award_winners.py` (§7.6c); `SBMVP` is parsed and recorded from `SUPER_BOWL_GAME_RECAP` by `newsroom/award_winners.py` (§7.6d); year-end All-Pro First and Second Team honors are parsed and recorded from `OFFICIAL_AP_ALL_PRO_ROSTER` by `newsroom/all_pro.py` (§7.6b). Historical seasons (2026–2034) were filled from Madden's award screens (`pipeline/batch_menus.py`).
   - `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks that the type and both overrides cover Coach of the Year and point at the tool, and that the tool is registered.

16. **The National Opinion Column** (`NATIONAL_OPINION_COLUMN`)
    - **Allowed Writers / Archetypes:** Bill Simmons (Historical / Pop Culture / Narrative), Emmanuel Acho (Uncomfortable Truths / Contrarian), Field Yates (Lists / Milestones / Volume), Skip Bayless (Clutch Gene / Fourth Quarter Drama), Mina Kimes (Metric-Driven Schematic Perspective) (`SIMMONS`, `ACHO`, `YATES`, `SKIP_BAYLESS`, `KIMES`, `National Perspective`).
    - **Granularity:** Week-level / Macro Narrative.
    - **Focus:** Singular viewpoint editorial focusing on league narratives, historical debates, contrarian reality checks, milestone valuations, or fourth-quarter clutch execution.
    - **Data Queried:** Player Popularity Index ($Pop_{\text{player}}$), Awards Equity ($A_{\text{awards}}$), Base Market Gravity ($B$), SpikeIndex, Offensive Pace ($P$).
    - **Curatorial Autonomy:** Isolates a single high-profile topic carrying an outsized national cultural footprint ($Pop_{\text{player}}$) or massive market gravity ($B$). Filters topic through writer archetype: historical parallels/wonky trends (Simmons), contrarian counter-arguments (Acho), milestone anomalies/share surges (Yates), or clutch execution/choke narratives (Bayless).
    - **Structure Directive:** None on the article type; each columnist's format comes from `newsroom/config/article_structure_directives.json`:
      - *Simmons:* cold open built on one comparison → `## The Case` → `## The Levels` (4–6 `###` tiers) → `### The Bad Beat` (one game from the recap week) → walk-off prediction with a stated confidence level.
      - *Acho:* "Uncomfortable Truths": direct address naming the consensus → `## What Everyone Believes` (stated fairly) → three numbered `##` truths → `## What the Public Is Missing` → `### The Verdict` (one bolded call).
      - *Yates:* one-paragraph setup → `## The Leaderboard` (markdown table from tool results) → `## Pace & Milestones` (5–8 factual bullets with paces computed from games played) → `## Three Things to Know` → one-line close ("That's the list.").
      - *Skip Bayless:* one-sentence take → `## The Indictment`/`The Coronation` (one-score games, late-season games vs. winning teams, playoff history, awards) → `### Exhibit A–C` (one game each, from the subject's schedule) → `## Don't Tell Me About the Numbers` → `### The Final Word`.
      - *Kimes:* pop-culture thesis → `## The Metric Disconnect` → `## The Schematic Chess Match` → `### The Walk-Off`.
      - The four new formats (Simmons, Acho, Yates, Bayless) end with a grounding rule: every number must come from the brief or tool results; plays, in-game moments and quotes may be invented if they fit the game's script and box score (the script's scoring plays, order and key moments are fixed); betting lines, contract details and broadcast details are forbidden (official key injuries may be cited from the brief or `get_team_injury_report`). `tests/test_writer_config.py` fails if any writer allowed on a type without its own structure lacks a column format.
    - **Prompt Hook:** Isolate the defining cultural narrative or superstar controversy of the week. Challenge mainstream consensus, run a historical parallel, or interrogate fourth-quarter execution.

17. **The Playoff Autopsy** (`PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY`)
    - **Allowed Writers / Archetypes:** Mike Sando (Front-Office Windows & Executive Accountability), Bill Barnwell (Tactical Autopsy & Regression/Sustainability) (`SANDO`, `BARNWELL`, `Postseason Exit Diagnostics`).
    - **Granularity:** Postseason Exit / Offseason Horizon.
    - **Focus:** Forensic breakdown of a postseason elimination, identifying the schematic failure points that got exposed, evaluating championship window sustainability, and defining the immediate draft and roster mandate.
    - **Data Queried:** Opponent-Adjusted Game Credit, Under-25 Production ($Y_{\text{prod}}$), Blue-Chip Pedigree ($P_{\text{draft}}$), Purgatory Penalty, Base Market Gravity ($B$), Legacy Floor ($S_{\text{all-time}}$), Offensive Pace ($P$), Head-Coach Profile (`get_coach_profile`), Team Cap Sheet (`get_team_cap_sheet`). The directive (R6) lets real cap space, expiring deals and dead money set the offseason terms when they bear on the mandate (most autopsies need few or none) and still forbids reporting a trade that wasn't executed. Trade packages (R6/R7, Phase 8): a hypothetical package may appear only as the writer's own idea, never as reported talks, built from real players and picks with the terms the tools show, and only if it passes `check_trade_package`; only `get_trade_rumors` rumors may be described as actual talks (`data_queried` adds both tools).
    - **Curatorial Autonomy:** Evaluates recent playoff elimination results and multi-year franchise analytics. Selects an eliminated team representing a significant crossroads: aging heavyweight with slamming window, high-market-gravity giant facing intense scrutiny, or ascending young core learning from defeat. Its `COACHING DATA:` line has the writer cross-examine the head coach through `get_coach_profile`: tenure (season with the team, arrival, predecessor), playoff record with the team (`playoff_record_with_team` over his tenure, this season's playoff result and Super Bowls with the team, against the regular-season `record_with_team` and his career playoff and Super Bowl record; no postseason record with the team when `playoff_record_with_team` is null) and game management in the elimination game (fourth-down decisions, red-zone and third-down play-calling against his schemes and measured tendencies).
    - **Structure Directive:** 5-part Postseason Autopsy (`# 1. The Scene of the Crash (The Exit)`, `## 2. The Schematic Fracture (What Broke on Film)`, `## 3. The Window Audit (The Championship Window Litmus Test)`, `## 4. Coaching Staff Accountability & Seat Temperature` (e.g. `## The Hot Seat & Coordinator Cross-Examination`), `### 5. The Spring Mandate`). Section 4 weighs whether the head coach enters next season on an ultimatum, sets the elimination game's red-zone stalls, fourth-down decision points and third-down failures (its box score) against the regular-season baseline from `get_team_efficiency_profile`, and ends on a concrete verdict: dismissal, coordinator overhaul, or patience with an ascending foundation. `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks the section and the coaching line.
    - **Prompt Hook:** Conduct a definitive playoff autopsy on an eliminated contender. Pinpoint where the game plan fractured, evaluate whether their championship window is closing or just opening, and establish the front office's primary offseason directive.

    - **Granularity:** Season-Level / Year-End Roster.
    - **Focus:** The definitive First and Second-Team AP All-Pro selections, statistical justifications, positional dominance, and voting anomalies.
    - **Data Queried:** Awards Equity ($A_{\text{awards}}$), Baseline Rating ($R_{\text{rating}}$), SpikeIndex, Player Popularity Index ($Pop_{\text{player}}$), Empty Calories Suppressor, defense & special-teams season leaders, player season stats.
    - **Curatorial Autonomy:** Constructs both the complete First Team and Second Team. Weighs full-season efficiency, raw volume, and high-leverage execution. Aggressively applies the "Empty Calories" suppressor to eliminate players racking up stats on sub-.300 teams; focuses on milestone volume including sacks, interceptions and field goals (Yates) or down-to-down efficiency and which defensive totals overstate or understate impact (Barnwell). A "Defense & Special Teams Evidence" block maps each defensive and special-teams slot to its `get_defense_special_teams_leaders` categories, says an unlisted defender may be picked on talent but gets no stat line, and has the linemen, fullback, special teamer and long snapper justified without numbers.
    - **Structure Directive:** 5-part Roster Reveal, approx. 1,400–1,800 words (`# 1. The Voting Overview (The Hook)`, `## 2. The First-Team Offense (13 slots: QB, RB, FB, 3 WRs, TE, AP, 5 OL)`, `## 3. The First-Team Defense & Special Teams (12 defense + 6 special teams slots)`, `## 4. The Second-Team Offense (13 slots)`, `## 5. The Second-Team Defense & Special Teams (18 slots)`). Every selection is formatted as a Markdown bullet `- **[Slot]**: [Player], [Team] — [Rationale]`. Validated, parsed, and stored into `awards` (62 rows) by `newsroom/all_pro.py` (§7.6b).
    - **Prompt Hook:** Reveal the official AP All-Pro First and Second Teams. Construct both complete 31-player units across Offense, Defense, and Special Teams (62 total), provide statistical justifications for the skill players, defenders and specialists, and evaluate positional dominance without speculative snub commentary.

### 7.2 Local Beat Reporting Taxonomy (`LOCAL_BEAT_REPORTER`)
Local Beat Reporters cover their assigned franchise exclusively. Their research directive keeps them on their own team's games, and they don't receive the national writers' historical-comparison instruction. The beat research directive points them at `get_defense_special_teams_leaders` for defensive/special-teams leaders and `get_team_injury_report` for active roster injuries. Roster moves: when the team has moves new this week, the beat brief adds `team_transactions` (`roster_moves.team_block`: `moves_this_week` as move lines, notable first, a `cap_snapshot` line with its basis, and `reporting_guidance`: a notable move gets a paragraph on the role it leaves or fills; terms only from the lines or `get_player_contract`; invent the negotiation colour, never a figure; the cap only if it bears on the story; trade legs left out). When the team was in an executed trade last week or in a rumor from last week's proposals, it also gets `team_trades` (`roster_moves.trades_block` for that team, Phase 8); the beat research block names `get_trade_rumors` (a rumor is only ever reported as a rumor). Moves feed the existing beat articles: there is no new wakeup trigger or beat article type (JR, 2026-10-20). Starting injuries are injected directly into the beat assignment brief (`team_injury_report`; starters are ranked among on-roster players with `roster_moves.is_starter_rank`, and released players are left out). The `BEAT INJURY REPORTING RULE` requires beat reporters to cover all injured starters across offense, defense, and specialists, framing them through tactical fallout ("next man up", protection shifts, scheme adjustments) while barring speculation on non-starters or unverified medical returns.

**Weekly portfolio (`newsroom/local_portfolio.py`):** every team wakeup plans the whole portfolio, however many beat reporters the team has: the Postgame Report Card if the team played last week, the Matchup Primer if it plays this week (aimed at that game via an Editorial Desk subject assignment), the Player Spotlight always, and the Season Progress Report from Week 6. Types the team already has that week (e.g. a national Slot 6–8 primer) are skipped. Articles are dealt round-robin across the team's reporters, starting at a different reporter each week, so one reporter writes all of them and no reporter is stuck on the postgame report. Each is saved under the team with slot `Local Beat N` (`tests/test_local_portfolio.py`).


1. **The Postgame Report Card** (`LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD`)
   - **Beat Archetype:** Local Beat Writer / Postgame Columnist (2–4 hours post-whistle).
   - **Focus:** Immediate unit execution versus expectations, unit letter grades (A+ through F), offensive line protection breakdowns, third-down stalls, and coaching decisions.
   - **Data Queried:** Unit Offensive Pace ($P$), Opponent-Adjusted Game Credit, Giveaways per Game (ball security), Pass Rush Rating (Madden rank).

2. **The Local Matchup Primer & Game-Plan Blueprint** (`LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER`)
   - **Beat Archetype:** Senior Beat Reporter (Friday / Saturday morning preview).
   - **Focus:** Home-team perspective matchup reality, 3 hyper-specific micro battles, game-plan victory blueprint, and final score prediction.
   - **Data Queried:** Matchup Edge (pass, rush, ball security), Upset Leverage ($U_{\text{projected}}$), Trench Edge (O-line vs. pass rush ratings), both teams' defense & special-teams leaders.
   - **Defense:** each of the three micro-battles is anchored in both players' season numbers where they exist (sacks and TFL vs. sacks allowed, catches and yards vs. INT and pass deflections), with no invented pressure rates, snaps or targets; the Defensive Mandate is a sack or takeaway target tied to named defenders (it was a third-down stop percentage, which isn't recorded).

3. **The Local Player Spotlight** (`LOCAL_PLAYER_SPOTLIGHT`)
   - **Beat Archetype:** Franchise Beat Reporter / Film Analyst.
   - **Focus:** Single local player's role evolution, developmental leap, tape & assignment execution, coaching trust, and roster implications.
   - **Data Queried:** SpikeIndex, Touch Share & Scrimmage Yard Share (season), Positional Multiplier ($M_{\text{pos}}$), Blue-Chip Pedigree ($P_{\text{draft}}$), Under-25 Production Share ($Y_{\text{prod}}$), defense & special-teams lines.
   - **Defense:** Defenders and specialists are eligible: the curatorial block points at `get_defense_special_teams_leaders` and `get_player_season_stats`, with the unknown-not-zero, no-team-sums and no pressure/snap/target rules (JR, Oct 14). The whole roster is in play (a pass rusher piling up sacks, a ball-hawking corner, a kicker or returner), and usage is described from recorded numbers rather than target volume or snap rate.

4. **The Local Season-to-Date Progress Report** (`LOCAL_SEASON_PROGRESS_REPORT`)
   - **Beat Archetype:** Senior Beat Columnist (Midseason / Season Audit).
   - **Focus:** Comprehensive evaluation of the home team's campaign, offensive/defensive identity check, structural strengths, lingering flaws, coaching staff seat temperature, and second-half win benchmark.
   - **Data Queried:** Trajectory Multiplier ($T$), Opponent-Adjusted Game Credit, Youth Production Share ($Y_{\text{prod}}$), Purgatory Penalty, Base Market Gravity ($B$), Round 1 Draft Order (`get_draft_order`).
   - **Curatorial Autonomy:** Evaluates franchise trajectory through local expectations. When diagnosing teams in the Purgatory Penalty, weighs their remaining schedule against their projected draft capital (e.g. escaping the middle tier vs securing a top-5 pick).

Press conferences: the team's most recent settled presser **before** the publication week adds `press_conference` to the beat brief (`press_room.brief_block`: subject, game, end reason, on-record exchanges, no-comments, corrections, reporting guidance), or `press_conference_note` when that same presser was DECLINED (`declined_note`). Both read one row (`_settled_conference`): looked up separately they could both fire, a week-4 decline riding along beside a week-5 transcript, and `week <= publication` let a week-N pregame article read week-N's postgame presser. The beat research directive names `get_press_conference` for the transcripts, and the opening-hook list no longer invites invented head-coach quotes. `dispatch_team_local` calls `press_room.ensure_team_presser(conn_info, team_id, season, week - 1)` first, so an AI team's missing or FAILED presser runs inline before its coverage.

### 7.3 The Editorial Assignment Desk & Article-First Commissioning Architecture
Rather than waking up a fixed list of writer agents who generate generic articles, the Swarm operates under an **Article-First Editorial Commissioning Architecture** (`commission_weekly_editorial_slate`):

1. **Weekly Default Distribution (Full 10-Slot Editorial Matrix):**
   - `docs/EDITORIAL_MATRIX.md` is the source of truth for the weekly slate. Every weekly run (`dispatch_weekly_national`) commissions all 10 matrix slots for the week: Hero, Slots 1–8, and Standalone.
   - `article_count` / `target_articles` truncate the slate and are reserved for tests and debugging (`tools/rehearse_wakeups.py --article-count`, `tools/rehearse_editorial_flow.py --count`); production never passes them.
   - The weekly national run does not wake up any extra beat reporters. Slots 6–8 come only from the matrix. Local beat portfolios (`LOCAL_POSTGAME_REPORT_CARD`, `LOCAL_PLAYER_SPOTLIGHT`, `LOCAL_SEASON_PROGRESS_REPORT`, plus team-specific `LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER`) come from on-demand team wakeups (`dispatch_team_local`).
   - **Slot Targeting (`newsroom/slot_targets.py`):** Before writers are assigned, `commission_weekly_editorial_slate` resolves the subject of every targeted slot per the matrix's *Slot Targeting Rules*. Matchup primers go to the week's most interesting scheduled games, ranked by `rank_games_by_interest`: projected $E$ (§2.1) plus division-game and playoff-race stakes (byes excluded, 2-week team rotation in the regular season, covering the side with fewer primers this season), and in Super Bowl week to the AFC and NFC champions. In regular-season Weeks 2–18, Slot 6 is converted into a Crisis Beat / Hot Seat Accountability primer targeting teams with the worst win-differential vs. expectation ($\Delta W = \text{Wins} - \text{Expected Wins} \le -2.0$) or active losing streaks with sub-.350 win percentages, while Slots 7 and 8 remain marquee matchup primers. Phase 4 `FRANCHISE_STATE_OF_THE_UNION` goes to a mathematically eliminated team. Week 19 `COACHING_HOT_SEAT_AUDIT` (Slot 6) goes to the team that missed the playoffs with the steepest shortfall below −1.5 wins above expectation (`team_seasons.wins − expected_wins`, `hot_seat_team_ids`; the note lists the other eliminated teams below −1.5; untargeted if none qualifies or expected wins aren't computed), resolved before the Slot 7 Exit State of the Union, which goes to a team that missed the playoffs, and W20–22 `PLAYOFF_AUTOPSY` slots go to the prior round's losers. All of these are distinct teams, most popular first.
   - Each primer is written by a beat reporter for its subject team. Every targeted article gets an `EDITORIAL DESK SUBJECT ASSIGNMENT` block in its prompt, which overrides subject-selection instructions, and is saved under the subject's `team_id`. If league data can't be loaded, slots fall back to writer-chosen subjects.
   - **Dynamic Weekly Slate Expansion for Record-Breaking Events:** In any week where an all-time NFL single-game or single-season record is broken or tied in the recap week (`week - 1`), `commission_weekly_editorial_slate` detects the milestones via `find_records_broken_in_week(cur, season, recap_week)` and dynamically expands the weekly editorial slate by appending dedicated `Record Breaker Slot` (or `Record Breaker Slot 2`, etc.) assignments beyond the default 10-slot matrix. Each record slot is commissioned with `HISTORIC_RECORD_BREAK`, assigned to an eligible writer (`CHADIHA`, `YATES`, `SIMMONS`, `BARNWELL`, `ORLOVSKY`), and injected with a mandatory `EDITORIAL DESK ASSIGNMENT (MANDATORY)` brief containing the broken record details, old record holder and value, game matchup, and historical context. Weekly national run filter `NATIONAL_SLOT_FILTER` includes `OR slot LIKE 'Record%%'`. On the frontend (`Mu_Network/src/App.tsx`, `index.css`) and API (`server/api.py`), record breaker articles are served in `historic_events` and featured with a commemorative gold/amber badge ("ALL-TIME NFL RECORD BROKEN") and `.record-breaker-card` styling.
   - **Postseason week numbering:** 19 = Wild Card, 20 = Divisional, 21 = Conference Championships, 22 = Super Bowl bye, 23 = Super Bowl. Historical imports (`pipeline/batch_menus.py`) store the Super Bowl at week 23. `db/migrations/migrate_super_bowl_week.py` moves older week-22 Super Bowl rows to week 23.
2. **Matrix-Driven Editorial Slate Planning (`docs/EDITORIAL_MATRIX.md`):**
   - Implements the definitive **18-Week Regular Season & 5-Week Postseason Editorial Matrix** to commission a structured portfolio of article types per week:
     - **Regular Season (Weeks 1–18):** Fixed Hero Slot (`PRE_SEASON_ROSTER_TIERS` in W1, `MACRO_SLATE_RECAP` in W2–18), Slot 1 (`SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS`), Slot 2 (`NFL_TOP_100_HIERARCHY` in W1, `SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY` in W2–18), Slots 3–5 (Feature Trio selected dynamically from 4 distinct seasonal phase pools; in a W2–18 edition right after a week with an executed GM trade, Slot 5 becomes `TRADE_GRADES` with the trades as its target: `SwarmDispatcher._trade_grades_target` → `roster_moves.trade_grades_due` / `new_trades` / `trade_grades_target`, Phase 8, the only Matrix change for trades), Slots 6–8 (Slot 6 Crisis Beat primer in W2–18 / 3x `LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER` in W1, Slots 7–8 `LOCAL_MATCHUP_PRIMER`), and Standalone (`POWER_RANKINGS`).
     - **Postseason (Weeks 19–23):** Custom boards tailored for Wild Card Eve (W19), Divisional Eve (W20), Championship Eve (W21), Super Bowl Bye (W22; Slot 8 features the joint HC-QB legacy column `SUPER_BOWL_HISTORICAL_STAKES`), and Super Bowl Week (W23). W19 keeps the Standalone `POWER_RANKINGS` (the season's final ranking, see 7.6); W20–W23 have no Standalone slot (9 articles).
   - Dynamically rotates national columnists (`SIMMONS`, `KIMES`, `ACHO`, `SKIP_BAYLESS`, `YATES`) into `NATIONAL_OPINION_COLUMN` slots during regular-season feature trios.
3. **Qualified Writer Matching & Load Balancing:**
   - For each commissioned article type, the Editorial Desk queries `allowed_writers` from the taxonomy (`newsroom/config/article_types.json`).
   - Picks each writer at random from the least-used allowed writers so far this week (`writer_assignment_counts`). This spreads work but doesn't prevent repeats: a writer can get more than one article in a week when the allowed lists overlap. Rotating-columnist slots name their writer directly and skip the balancing.
   - **Writer records:** every writer name in `allowed_writers` and the columnist pools is an archetype key in `agent_personas.json`. `compile_agent_prompt` renders the archetype's persona with `newsroom/personas.build_persona_block` (§7.11): `ARTICLE` habits for articles, `POST` habits otherwise; `FANTASY_*` articles use `fantasy_writers.json` instead. `get_agent_record` loads the `agent_memories` row whose `archetype` matches exactly (oldest first); old shorthand names are mapped first by `WRITER_ARCHETYPE_ALIASES` (`BAYLESS` → `SKIP_BAYLESS`). Tweet-only accounts such as `SKIP_TWEET` are separate agents and are never used for articles. `tests/test_writer_config.py` checks that every article writer has a persona with `ARTICLE` habits (beat reporters excepted), every opinion columnist has a curatorial directive, and no columnist pool or article type uses an alias.
   - Binds each writer to their specific commissioned `article_type`, ensuring prompt injection of custom curatorial lenses, structure directives, and analytical parameters.

**Head-coach quoting rule (every writer, national and beat).** A head coach is quoted only from his press conference transcript, word for word (`press_conference` in your brief, or `get_press_conference`). If there is none, do not put words in his mouth. Coordinators, players and team captains may be quoted as before. National writers never quote pressers and do not call the tool.

### 7.3.1 The Mu Fantasy Desk (`newsroom/fantasy_desk.py`, `docs/done/FANTASY_EDITORIAL_MATRIX.md`)
- **When:** `weekly_run` calls `dispatch_weekly_fantasy(season, week)` after the national slate, Weeks 1–18 (W19–23: no slate; the page keeps W18). A week is skipped when it already has `Fantasy …` slots (unless `--force`).
- **Slots** (`fantasy_slate(week)`): `Fantasy Hero`, `Fantasy 1`–`3` (front page) and `Fantasy Shelf N` ("View all analysis").
  - W1: `FANTASY_DRAFT_TIERS` ×4 (WR, RB, QB, TE, position given as a desk note) + Sleepers & Busts, Mock Draft, Rookie Rankings.
  - W2–14: Start/Sit, Waiver Wire, Weekly Reactions, Card 03 from `CARD3_SCHEDULE` (W2 Overreaction, W3 DvP, W4 Overreaction, W5 Overreaction, W6 Buy/Sell, W7 ADP Checkpoint, W8 ROS Tiers, W9 DvP, W10 Buy/Sell, W11 ROS Tiers, W12 Trade Deadline Special, W13 Playoff Schedule Planner, W14 Must-Win Week); shelf: Rankings & Tiers, Box Score & Usage, 10 Things, Matchup Exploits (W3+).
  - W15–17: Start/Sit (playoff/championship editions), Streamers, Reactions, Playoff Schedule Planner (W15) / Ceiling Plays; W18: Season in Review, Awards (with All-Fantasy Team), Draft Retro, Projection Report Card, Dynasty Early Look.
  - K/D/ST (`FANTASY_STREAMING_DST_K`) is enabled (`KDST_ENABLED = True`), running weekly on the fantasy shelf from Week 3 to Week 17.
- **Writers:** 27 `FANTASY_*` types in `article_types.json` (including `FANTASY_STREAMING_DST_K`), written by BERRY, YATES, BARNWELL and JOYNER (spread by least-used, like the national desk). Yates writes all four W1 Draft Tiers; Joyner writes 10 Things and Streaming D/ST & Kickers. Length targets are minimums ("at least N words; longer is fine"). For `FANTASY_*` articles `compile_agent_prompt` swaps in the writer's fantasy voice and selection filter from `newsroom/config/fantasy_writers.json` (tweet personas and national directives are untouched), uses `FANTASY_DESK_GUIDELINES` instead of the national research-tools block (full PPR, all numbers from tools, "rostered in X% of leagues" with no mention of simulations, official skill injuries via `get_fantasy_injuries` to explain vacated volume and handcuffs, NFL roster moves (a released player has no game and projects 0 until he signs; a signing is a pickup only if his depth slot gives him a role; moves only from `nfl_moves` / `team_moves`, never invented), clear verdicts, never invent past calls), a fantasy-calendar temporal block (`temporal_mode = "FANTASY"`), the fantasy tools (supporting QB, RB, WR, TE, K, and DEF), and the desk note as an `EDITORIAL DESK ASSIGNMENT (MANDATORY)` block. Fantasy articles are saved with `team_id` NULL.
- **Brief:** a small fantasy brief (season, publication week, fantasy phase, week label, results-through week, scoring), not the national assignment brief.

### 7.4 Playoff-Specific Dynamic Overrides Architecture (`newsroom/config/playoff_overrides.json`)
During the single-elimination tournament and Super Bowl run (Weeks 19–23), standard regular-season directives are dynamically superseded by targeted postseason overrides. The orchestrator inspects `target_weeks` at compile time and overrides the baseline article directive, curatorial autonomy filter, and structure specification without mutating baseline schemas:

- **Lookup & validation (`newsroom/playoff_overrides.py`):** `find_active_override(overrides, article_type, week)` picks the override; `normalize_temporal_mode` reads `temporal_mode` case-insensitively and accepts only `RETROSPECTIVE`, `PROSPECTIVE` or `CUMULATIVE` (anything else falls back to the article type's mode in `TEMPORAL_ARTICLE_MODES`). `SwarmDispatcher` runs `validate_playoff_overrides` on load and prints a warning per problem: unknown article type or temporal mode, target weeks outside 19–23, a week claimed by two overrides of the same type, or a misused `preview_week`. `tests/test_playoff_overrides.py` also validates the shipped config.
- **`preview_week` (optional, `PROSPECTIVE` only):** the week whose games the override previews, when it isn't the publication week. The prompt then names that week and tells the writer to fetch it with `get_weekly_slate`, since the brief's `preview_slate` only holds the publication week.

1. **`SINGLE_GAME_SCHEMATIC_AUTOPSY` Playoff Overrides:**
   - **Week 19:** no override. It looks back at regular-season Week 18, so the base article type applies.
   - **Weeks 20–22 (`PLAYOFF_ELIMINATION_ROUND_AUTOPSY` | `RETROSPECTIVE`):**
     - **Focus:** High-leverage situational football, tightened personnel packages, blitz counters, and scheme-exposure points from the elimination round just completed.
     - **Curatorial Filter:** Isolates the single clash with highest tactical leverage, third-down aggression, or where fourth-down game management swung win probability; a defense exposing an offense counts when the box score shows it (sacks, takeaways, a defensive score).
     - **Defense grounding:** the schematic collision is built from the box score (sacks, TFL, takeaways, pass deflections and the offense's lines), and the high-leverage moments are ones the box score supports (strip-sack, interception, stalled red-zone trip, long or missed field goal), with no invented down-and-distance, pressure rates, coverage percentages, snaps or targets.
     - **Structure:** 4-part Tape Autopsy (`# 1. The Decisive Blueprint`, `## 2. The Core Schematic Collision`, `## 3. The High-Leverage Breakdown`, `### 4. The Elimination Takeaway`).
   - **Week 23 (`SUPER_BOWL_SCHEMATIC_MASTERCLASS` | `PROSPECTIVE`):**
     - **Focus:** Exhaustive pre-game tactical blueprint previewing the Super Bowl clash through an X's and O's coaching lens (disregarding celebrity/media week storylines).
     - **Curatorial Filter:** Trench warfare leverage (pass rush vs. slide protection), safety disguise rotations against primary passing concepts.
     - **Structure:** 5-part Masterclass (`# 1. The Grand Chess Match`, `## 2. Trench Warfare & Point-of-Attack Leverage`, `## 3. Coverage Shells vs. Passing Architecture`, `## 4. The Critical Situational Battle`, `### 5. The Coordinator Verdict`).

2. **`SLATE_LOOKAHEAD_PREDICTIONS` Playoff Overrides:**
   - **Weeks 19–21 (`POSTSEASON_ROUND_LOOKAHEAD` | `PROSPECTIVE`):**
     - **Focus:** High-stakes single-elimination preview capsules for every game in the upcoming playoff round (Wild Card, Divisional, Conference Championship). Strict ban on betting lines/spreads.
     - **Curatorial Filter:** Mandatory full enumeration covering every scheduled tournament matchup. Mismatches use both sides of the ball: each team's defensive leaders from `get_defense_special_teams_leaders` against the quarterback's interceptions and sacks taken, never summed into team totals.
     - **Capsules:** Stat to Know may be offensive, defensive or special teams; Tactical Flashpoint names the players on both sides with their season numbers (no pressure rates, coverage percentages, snaps or targets); the X-Factor can be a defender or specialist.
     - **Structure:** Modular Postseason Capsules (`# 1. The Round Overview`, `## 2. Matchup Enumeration with kickoff time from the slate (no invented broadcast network)`, `3. Structured Sub-Sections: What We're Hearing, Stat to Know, Tactical Flashpoint, The X-Factor Player, Official Prediction`).
   - **Week 22 (`SUPER_BOWL_EARLY_TALE_OF_THE_TAPE` | `PROSPECTIVE`, `preview_week: 23`):**
     - **Focus:** Comprehensive bye-week Tale of the Tape comparing both Super Bowl finalists from top to bottom.
     - **Curatorial Filter:** Contrasts cumulative efficiency profiles across every unit and neutral-site dome variables.
     - **Structure:** 6-part Tale of the Tape (`# 1. The Championship Tale of the Tape`, `## 2. The Macro Profile & Efficiency Baselines`, `## 3. Unit Clash 1: Team A Offense vs. Team B Defense`, `## 4. Unit Clash 2: Team B Offense vs. Team A Defense`, `## 5. The Volatility & Spike Audit`, `### 6. The Bye-Week Installation Mandate`).

3. **`AWARDS_TRACKER` Playoff Overrides** (both `CUMULATIVE`; award voting covers the regular season only, so writers judge Weeks 1–18 and don't credit playoff games; both overrides strictly enforce the **COACHING DATA CITATION** constraint prohibiting explicit mentions of "COTY score", "coach scores", "Coach of the Year metric", or "historical bonus", framing cases in real-world records and achievements):
   - **Week 21 (`AWARDS_FINALISTS`):** three finalists each for MVP, OPOY, OROY, DPOY, DROY and Coach of the Year (coaches from `get_coach_of_the_year_race`), with the projected winner (approx. 1,400–1,700 words; defenders' cases on sacks, TFL, interceptions, takeaways); the snub may be a player or a coach. Structure: `# The Ballots Are In`, one `##` per award with three bolded finalists, `## The Projected Winners`, `### The Snub`.
   - **Week 22 (`AWARDS_WINNERS`):** the publication's winner and runner-up for each of the six awards (approx. 1,400–1,700 words). Structure: `#` headline naming the MVP, a paragraph announcing the six winners, one `##` per award in the order MVP, OPOY, OROY, DPOY, DROY, Coach of the Year (`## MVP: [Player], [Position], [Team]`; `## Coach of the Year: [Coach], [Team]`) with the case and the runner-up, `### The Season in One Line`. Grounded purely in on-field records, margins, and overachievement without engine scores or bonus numbers.

4. **`SUPER_BOWL_CONTENDER_BLUEPRINT` Playoff Overrides** (both `CUMULATIVE`; only teams playing that week's playoff games are in scope, judged on the regular season plus their playoff games so far):
   - **Week 20 (`DIVISIONAL_ROUND_CONTENDER_AUDIT`):** the eight divisional-round teams, three wins from a title. Structure: `# The Championship Standard`, `##` heavyweights (2–3 teams), `## The Vulnerable Favorite`, `### The Dangerous Underdog`.
   - **Week 21 (`FINAL_FOUR_CONTENDER_AUDIT`):** the four conference finalists ranked 1–4 by title chances. Structure: `#` hook, four numbered `## [Rank]. [City] [Team] ([W-L])` sections (path, case, fatal flaw), `### The Verdict` naming the champion.

*(Note: Week 22 Slot 8 commissions `SUPER_BOWL_HISTORICAL_STAKES` directly from `POSTSEASON_EDITORIAL_SLATES` (§7.1, #28) as the dedicated HC-QB legacy column rather than via a dynamic override.)*

### 7.5 Database Schema & Newsroom REST API Specifications
To support seamless frontend newsroom consumption, longform editorial content is persisted with full metadata and relational tagging:

1. **`news_feed` Database Schema:**
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS news_feed (
       id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
       season INT,
       week INT,
       team_id INT,                -- teams.id (no FK constraint in live schema)
       content_type VARCHAR(50),   -- 'ARTICLE' | 'TWEET'
       persona VARCHAR(50),        -- e.g. 'BARNWELL', 'SANDO', 'LOCAL_BEAT_REPORTER'
       headline VARCHAR(255),
       content TEXT,
       created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
       excerpt TEXT,
       article_type VARCHAR(64),   -- e.g. 'MACRO_SLATE_RECAP', 'POWER_RANKINGS'
       slot VARCHAR(32)            -- 'Hero Slot', 'Slot 1'..'Slot 8', 'Standalone', or 'Local Beat N'
   );
   ```

2. **Relational Entity Tagging:**
   - **`article_teams`**: Maps mentioned franchises (`PRIMARY`, `FEATURED`, `MENTIONED`) with mention frequencies. Team mentions come from `newsroom/entity_patterns.team_mention_pattern`: full name, nickname, city (except shared New York / Los Angeles) and uppercase abbreviation, all **case-sensitive**, so ordinary words ("was", "no", "ten", "bills") are not team mentions. Abbreviations that are English words (`NO`, `WAS`, `TEN`, `MIN`, `CAR`, `SEA`, `DEN`) are never matched, even in all caps; those teams are found by nickname or city (`tests/test_entity_patterns.py`). A team is `PRIMARY` if it's the article's assigned team, appears in the headline or a header, or is mentioned 5+ times; `FEATURED` at 3+; otherwise `MENTIONED`.
   - **`article_players`**: Maps mentioned players with their active franchise, position, mention tier, and mention frequencies.

3. **Newsroom REST API Endpoints (`server/api.py`):**
   - **`GET /api/news/week/{week}?season={season}`**:
     - Returns the complete weekly news slate partitioned into canonical display slots:
       - **`hero`**: Hero Slot article (top banner).
       - **`secondary`**: Slots 1 and 2 (e.g. Schematic Autopsy, Slate Lookahead).
       - **`features`**: Slots 3, 4, and 5 (seasonal feature trio).
       - **`local_primers`**: Slots 6, 7, and 8 only (the national desk's local matchup primers, with Slot 6 dedicated to the Crisis Beat in Weeks 2–18).
       - **`standalone`**: Standalone Power Rankings 32-team hierarchy.
       - **`other`**: Any other article that week (e.g. unslotted); the frontend shows these with the main stories.
     - Team-page beat coverage (slot `Local Beat N`, from on-demand team wakeups) is excluded; it appears only via `GET /api/team/{abbr}/news`.
     - Mu Fantasy articles (`article_type` `FANTASY_*`, slots `Fantasy …`) are excluded; they belong to the fantasy page.
     - Includes resolved author objects (`display_name`, `handle`, `archetype`) and attached entity tags (`tagged_teams`, `tagged_players`).
   - **`GET /api/news/article/{article_id}`**:
