     - Returns full article text, headline, teaser excerpt, assigned slot, author metadata (`handle`, `display_name`, `archetype`, `bio`, `team_abbr`), `related_articles` (up to 6 articles written that same week powering the "Keep Reading" rail, newest first), and all tagged entities for reading view rendering.
   - **`GET /api/author/{author_key}`**:
     - Returns author profile (`handle`, `display_name`, `archetype`, `bio`, `team`) and full article archive across all weeks and seasons (`articles`, `total_articles`) matching the author's handle, archetype, or agent ID, with tagged teams for each article. Powers the dedicated `#author-{handle}` full-page view.

### 7.6 Stored Weekly Power Rankings (`newsroom/power_rankings.py`)
The Standalone `POWER_RANKINGS` article is the source of the stored weekly ranking:
1. **Continuity in the prompt:** `compile_agent_prompt` adds a "POWER RANKINGS CONTINUITY" block, which lists the latest earlier stored week's order (or says none has been published, so every team is "Previous: — | New") and restates the header format `## [Rank]. [City] [Team] ([W-L]) (Previous: N | Change: ±N)`. This means movement indicators come from real prior rankings. In Week 19 (`FINAL_RANKINGS_WEEK`) the block also tells the writer this is the season's final ranking, judged on the full Weeks 1–18 body of work.
2. **Parsing:** each numbered header that names a team (resolved by its unique nickname, or abbreviation) or carries a W-L record is a team entry. Other numbered headers (e.g. "## 2. The Drop-Off") are treated as section breaks. The bold lead-in is the `kicker`; the first paragraph after it is the `blurb` (a horizontal rule or blank line ends it, so the walk-off isn't included).
3. **Validation:** the article must rank all 32 teams exactly once with ranks 1–32. In a live run, a failing article gets one rewrite in the same chat, with the specific errors (missing/duplicate teams or ranks, unmatched headers).
4. **Storage:** on save to `news_feed`, a valid article replaces that week's `power_rankings` rows. Only the order, kicker and blurb come from the text. `record` is snapshotted from `team_seasons`, and `previous_rank` / `movement` come from the stored previous week, not the writer's indicators. An article that still fails validation is saved as an article but no ranking is stored (logged as `POWER RANKINGS NOT STORED`).
5. **No rankings after the regular season:** Week 19 (entering the Wild Card round, cumulative through Week 18) is the last ranked week (`FINAL_RANKINGS_WEEK = 19`). The postseason slates for Weeks 20–23 don't commission `POWER_RANKINGS`, and if one is generated anyway for a week after 19 (e.g. a targeted manual run) it is saved as an article but not stored (logged as `POWER RANKINGS NOT STORED`), so the Week 19 order stays the final ranking shown by `GET /api/power_rankings`.

### 7.6b Stored Year-End All-Pro Rosters (`newsroom/all_pro.py`)
The stored teams also appear on `#awards` (`GET /api/awards/all-pro`, §4.7), which orders them by this module's slot quotas, and in the player page's Honors row.
The Postseason Week 19 `OFFICIAL_AP_ALL_PRO_ROSTER` article is the source of the stored All-Pro awards in the `awards` table:
1. **Formatting & Structure:** The article structure directive mandates Markdown bullets formatted `- **[Slot]**: [Player Full Name], [Team] — [1-sentence rationale]` across 4 sections: First-Team Offense (13 slots: QB, RB, FB, 3 WRs, TE, AP, 5 OL), First-Team Defense & Special Teams (12 defense + 6 special teams = 18 slots), Second-Team Offense (13 slots), and Second-Team Defense & Special Teams (18 slots). Total: 62 selections (31 First-Team, 31 Second-Team).
2. **Parsing & Resolution:** `parse_all_pro(text, roster_index)` resolves each bullet's player by matching Player Name + Team + Position compatibility against `load_roster_index(cur, season)` (from `player_seasons`, `players`, and `teams`). This disambiguates common surnames and players sharing a name on the same team (e.g. WR vs DT).
3. **Validation & In-Flight Retry:** Checks that all 31 First-Team and 31 Second-Team slots are filled, all players resolve to active roster players, no player is selected multiple times for the same slot, and no player holds multiple primary offensive or defensive positions (AP and Special Teams exceptions are permitted). If validation fails, `swarm_dispatcher` sends `all_pro_fix_prompt` for a one-shot rewrite within the active chat session before publishing.
4. **Storage & Downstream Exposure:** On save to `news_feed`, `store_all_pro_teams` deletes previous All-Pro rows for that season and inserts 62 rows into `awards` (`award_type` = `'First Team All-Pro'` or `'Second Team All-Pro'`, `position` = slot). These honors are immediately returned in `get_player_season_stats` / `get_player_context` (`career_awards`) with their position (e.g. `"2035 First Team All-Pro (QB)"`) and contribute 30 points (First Team) and 15 points (Second Team) to Awards Equity ($A_{\text{awards}}$) in `engines/player_popularity_engine.py`.
5. **Honorifics & Earned Hardware Directive:** `swarm_dispatcher.py` instructs all writers to check `career_awards` in player profiles and use earned honorifics in prose ("the reigning MVP", "two-time First-Team All-Pro cornerback", "former Rookie of the Year") while strictly prohibiting fabricated awards.
6. **Ballot-decided teams (media voters, D5; built 2026-11-06, switchboard-gated, off):** `newsroom/award_ballots.py` can decide the teams instead of the article: each of the 20 panel voters fills every First-Team slot to its quota (`all_pro_ballot`, a player named once per ballot) from `engines/award_candidates.py` slot candidates (slot-specific production, efficiency, team wins and roster-rating z-scores; minimum 10 games), leaned and seeded as for the awards (§7.6c); `all_pro_tally` puts the most-voted players per slot on the First Team and the next on the Second Team, each player once at his best-voted slot, ties to the higher base score, short slots filled by base score; `store_all_pro` writes the 62 `awards` rows (position = slot) and one `award_ballots` row per voter and slot (`award` `ALL_PRO:<slot>`). The article would then report the stored teams (`all_pro_facts`) and is checked by `check_against_stored(text, load_stored_teams(cur, season), roster_index)`. `swarm_dispatcher` reads the switchboard's `media_voters` mode (`award_ballots.feature_mode`, a savepointed read; no league, no tables or an error read off): off (default) and shadow keep the parse-and-store path above. **Active (P1-12, 2026-11-09):** before the Week 19 article is written, `_ballot_brief` runs `decide_all_pro` (= `run_all_pro`, stores the panel's teams), appends `all_pro_facts` to the writer's task instruction as the final stored teams, and after generation checks the article with `check_against_stored` against the stored teams, asking for one rewrite (`all_pro_fix_prompt`) on a miss; the Week 19 storage step no longer runs the ballots again, it only re-checks and logs. Any ballot error falls back to today's path. The feature can't reach shadow until the U6 migration `2027_02_02` exists (`features.REQUIREMENTS`).

### 7.6c Stored Year-End Award Winners (`newsroom/award_winners.py`)
The stored winners also appear in the `#awards` award history (`GET /api/awards`, §4.7) and the player page's Honors row.
The Postseason Week 22 `AWARDS_TRACKER` (`AWARDS_WINNERS` override) article is the source of the six major regular-season award winners stored in the `awards` table:
1. **Formatting & Structure:** The article structure directive mandates six level-2 (`##`) headers announcing the winners in order: `## MVP: [Player], [Position], [Team]`, `## OPOY: [Player], [Position], [Team]`, `## OROY: [Player], [Position], [Team]`, `## DPOY: [Player], [Position], [Team]`, `## DROY: [Player], [Position], [Team]`, and `## Coach of the Year: [Coach], [Team]` (or `## COTY: ...`).
2. **Parsing & Resolution:** `parse_award_winners(text, roster_index, coach_index)` matches player recipients against `load_roster_index(cur, season)` by name, team, and position, and matches the coach recipient against `load_coach_index(cur, season)` by name and team.
3. **Validation & In-Flight Retry:** Checks that all 6 awards (`MVP`, `OPOY`, `OROY`, `DPOY`, `DROY`, `COTY`) are present and resolve to real active roster players and head coaches. If validation fails, `swarm_dispatcher` sends `award_winners_fix_prompt` for an in-flight rewrite within the active chat session before publishing, which also reminds writers never to cite internal engine mechanics (COTY scores, bonus numbers) in the Coach of the Year section.
4. **Storage:** On save to `news_feed`, `store_award_winners` deletes previous regular-season award rows for that season and inserts 6 rows into `awards` (`award_type` = `'MVP'`, `'OPOY'`, `'OROY'`, `'DPOY'`, `'DROY'`, `'COTY'`). `COTY` rows record `coach_id`, `coach_name`, and `team_id`; player award rows record `player_id`, `player_name`, `team_id`, and `position`. `SBMVP` is parsed and recorded from the post-Super Bowl `SUPER_BOWL_GAME_RECAP` article (§7.6d).
5. **Downstream Exposure:** Player awards immediately contribute to Awards Equity ($A_{\text{awards}}$: MVP 60 pts, OPOY/DPOY 40 pts, OROY/DROY 25 pts) in `engines/player_popularity_engine.py`, appear in player profile `career_awards`, and are cited by writer tools. Coach of the Year is visible in `engines/coach_profile.py` (`awards_visible`).
6. **Ballot-decided winners (media voters, D4; docs/done/OWNERS_SCOUTS_VOTERS_PLAN.md U7, built 2026-11-06, switchboard-gated, off):** `engines/award_candidates.py` scores candidates (`candidates(cur, season, award)`, top 15): MVP/OPOY from offensive players with production z within position group (QB passing/rushing line; skill players scrimmage yards, TDs, catches), efficiency z (passer rating, yards a carry, yards a catch), team-wins z and `record_pace` = max(0, production − 2); base blends MVP 0.5/0.3/0.2 (production/wins/efficiency, + 0.6 for a QB, − 0.2 for a TE), OPOY and OROY 0.65/0.1/0.25; DPOY/DROY from a defensive line (sacks 1, INT 1.5, TFL 0.5, passes defended 0.4, forced fumbles 1, tackles 0.05) 0.85 plus wins 0.15; rookies only (`years_of_experience` 0) for OROY/DROY; COTY from `coty_scores` (base (score − 50)/10); a player needs 10 games (`season_stat_general`; no row counts as eligible). `newsroom/award_ballots.py`: a panel of 20 national-writer archetypes from `agent_personas.json` (`VOTER_ARCHETYPES`, no fan, meme, fantasy or aggregator accounts) each ranks five (`ballot`), leaning the blend (`ANALYTICS_BELIEVER` efficiency +0.15 and production −0.05, `OLD_SCHOOL` wins +0.15, production +0.05, efficiency −0.10, `HISTORIAN` record pace +0.15, a view tagged `AWARDS` wins +0.05) and adding seeded noise (sd 0.35, `sha256(['ballot-v1', season, voter, award])`); `tally` scores 10-5-3-2-1, ties to more first-place votes; `store_results` replaces the six winners in `awards` and upserts `award_ballots` (season, award, voter, ranking JSONB, `ballot_version` `ballot-v1`); `run_awards(cur, season)` does all of it and `results_facts` gives the article its winners and top-five tallies. `check_against_stored(text, load_stored_winners(cur, season), roster_index, coach_index)` checks the article names every stored winner (`stored_winners_fix_prompt` for the rewrite). The Week 22 article reads the switchboard's `media_voters` mode (`award_ballots.feature_mode`): off (default) and shadow keep the parse-and-store path above. **Active (P1-12, 2026-11-09):** before the Week 22 article is written, `_ballot_brief` runs `decide_awards` (= `run_awards`), appends `results_facts` to the writer's task instruction as the final stored winners, and after generation checks the article with `check_against_stored` against the stored winners, asking for one rewrite via `stored_winners_fix_prompt` on a miss; the Week 22 storage step no longer runs the ballots again, it only re-checks and logs. Any ballot error falls back to today's path. Shadow is unreachable until the U6 migration `2027_02_02` (the `award_ballots` table) exists. All weights are review-only estimates.

### 7.6d Stored Super Bowl MVP (`newsroom/award_winners.py`)
The stored SB MVP also appears on the `#awards` champion cards and award history (`GET /api/awards`, §4.7) and the player page's Honors row.
The post-Super Bowl `SUPER_BOWL_GAME_RECAP` article is the authoritative source of the Super Bowl MVP honor stored in the `awards` table:
1. **Formatting & Structure:** The article structure directive mandates an exact level-2 (`##`) header awarding the Pete Rozelle Trophy / Super Bowl MVP: `## Super Bowl MVP: [Player Full Name], [Position], [Team Name]`.
2. **Parsing & Resolution:** `parse_sb_mvp(text, roster_index)` extracts the recipient from the header (supporting flexible variations like `## Super Bowl MVP`, `### Super Bowl MVP`, `Pete Rozelle Trophy / Super Bowl MVP`, and `SBMVP`) and resolves the player against active rosters using `resolve_player_award`.
3. **Validation & In-Flight Retry:** Checks that the Super Bowl MVP header is present and resolves to a real active roster player. If validation fails, `swarm_dispatcher` sends `sb_mvp_fix_prompt` for an in-flight rewrite within the active chat session before publishing.
4. **Storage:** On save to `news_feed`, `store_sb_mvp` deletes any previous `SBMVP` row for that season and inserts a single row into `awards` (`award_type` = `'SBMVP'`, `player_id`, `player_name`, `team_id`, and `position`).
5. **Downstream Exposure:** Stored `SBMVP` honors immediately contribute 25 points to Awards Equity ($A_{\text{awards}}$) in `engines/player_popularity_engine.py`, 40 points to Playoff Clout ($S_{\text{playoff}}$) in `engines/playoff_clout_engine.py`, appear in player profile `career_awards` (`get_player_context`), and feed draft ADP bumps.

### 7.7 Evolving Agent Memory (`newsroom/agent_memory.py`)
Memory is read per person (`agent_memories.person_key`, §3.5): every account sharing a person key sees one take log, prediction record and summary, so Skip Bayless's column and his tweets remember together; writes stay per account and a summary is stored once, under the person's first account (`newsroom/relationships.person_agent_ids`). Every agent (national writers, beat reporters, pundits and fans) keeps its hand-written identity line in `agent_memories.persistent_memory`, which never changes (the exceptions: `2026_10_22_agent_wire_social.sql` swapped the name inside the line for agents it renamed; `2027_01_07_writer_identity_lines.sql` rewrote the lines written as rules — Barnwell, Joyner, Sando, Simmons, Yates, Ochocinco and the bandwagon fans — as character, §7.11). Four evolving layers sit on top of it, written by `db/migrations/2026_10_20_agent_memory.sql`'s tables and `2027_01_18_writer_voice.sql`:
1. **Takes log (`agent_memory_entries`).** After a live post is saved (`SwarmDispatcher._record_agent_memory`): a tweet is stored as a take as-is (no extra call); an article gets one extra model call (`takes_extraction_prompt`, through `gemini_text` / `llm_text` capped at thinking level `low` via `engines/llm_config.py` or routed to a local Ollama model via `engines/llm_provider.py`, saving ~1,000 thinking tokens per call; configurable via `AGENT_MEMORY_THINKING`, `LLM_PROVIDER_AGENT_MEMORY`, or `model:level`) that returns up to 3 first-person stances the writer committed to, each tagged with a team (resolved by nickname) and/or player.
2. **Prediction track record (`agent_predictions`).** For `PROSPECTIVE` articles, `parse_score_predictions` reads `Projected Final: Team N, Team N` lines (and, for the Super Bowl Roundtable, `Panellist: Team N, Team N` lines, labelled by panellist) and stores each pick against the matching game in the article's preview week (`preview_week` for overrides). Posts also make picks: a `PICKS` post's structured output is stored with `pick_type` `'WINNER'` (or `'SCORE'` when it gives a score) against the post's `news_feed.id`. Picks are graded when a prompt is built: correct, wrong, push (a predicted or actual tie) or pending; a WINNER pick grades on `winner_team_id` alone.
3. **Season summaries (`agent_season_summaries`).** At the start of each live weekly run, agents with at least 3 new takes since their last summary get it rewritten through last week (one call each through `gemini_text` / `llm_text` capped at `low` or local Ollama, ≤120 words, first person). Each rewrite is a new row per `through_week`, so older weeks keep the summary they saw.
4. **Season calls (`agent_season_calls`).** `SEASON_CALL` posts (and any structured call) store long-range calls — MVP, OPOY, DPOY, ROY, Super Bowl winner, playoff team, misses the playoffs, division winner, coach fired — with their subject and week. `grade_season_calls` resolves PENDING calls from the `awards` table, the Super Bowl result, final standings and `coach_hot_seat` firings; a call made in a later week than the result stays pending. The memory block lists the person's call record and their open calls next to the pick record.

**Relationship upkeep in the weekly run.** After `refresh_season_summaries`, a non-dry `newsroom/weekly_run.py` run calls `agent_memory.grade_season_calls(cur, season)` — which grades every PENDING call the stored data can now decide (playoff field after Week 18, awards and the Super Bowl once stored) — and then `relationships.apply_graded(cur, season, week - 1)` once, so every pick and call of the season up to and including that week — `<=`, not `=`, so a skipped publication week is not lost — moves trust toward the backed subject. A Week 1 run grades the previous season's calls, applies the **whole** finished season (`apply_graded(cur, season - 1, None)`) and then calls `relationships.decay(cur, season)` as the season rollover: the season-end calls (MVP, the awards, SUPER_BOWL, COACH_FIRED) can only be graded after the Super Bowl, and without that apply they moved no trust at all. Applied refs are recorded per event in `persona_relationship_event_refs` (one row per writer, subject and ref; `2027_02_22`). `apply_graded` treats a graded event as applied when it is in that table, in the row's evidence, or in the sticky `APPLIED_REFS` entry — the **union**, so the table is an optimisation and a freshly built or restored database still guards on the evidence and the sticky list. Nothing is inferred from the order of the evidence: that inference lost real events when a call was graded in the same week as a pick, when a season pass came back out of order, or when a pick's game completed after a later call. `decay` keeps the sticky entry. Rows written before the table are backfilled once by `db/migrations/2027_02_22_backfill_applied_refs.py`, recording only what is proven (the evidence refs and the sticky list); a ref trimmed out before the sticky existed stays unrecorded, so a later weekly run or a forced rerun may re-apply that one rather than risk skipping one that never ran. Both run inside `update_writer_relationships`, whose failures are printed and never block the slate. The clean seed calls `relationships.seed_writer_relationships` right after `seed_agent_accounts` (§1.2, §3.3p).

**In the prompt:** under "PERSISTENT WORLDVIEW & MEMORIES", after the identity line, `build_memory_block` adds the latest summary, the 6 most recent takes ("stay consistent, or say plainly that you've changed your mind"), up to 3 earlier takes about the article's subject team, and the track record: the season's winner-picking record plus the 5 most recent graded picks with the final score, telling the writer to own misses in their own voice. Only memories from before the article's publication week are used, and graded results only count games from earlier weeks, so regenerating an old week can't see the future. If the memory tables don't exist yet, prompts simply have no memory block.

**Failure handling:** memory recording runs after the article is committed and never affects it; failures are logged as `MEMORY NOT RECORDED`. Deleting `news_feed` rows cascades to their takes and predictions; `db/clear_news_feed.sh` also clears the summaries. Tests: `tests/test_agent_memory.py`, `tests/test_llm_config.py`, `tests/test_llm_provider.py`; `tools/verify_newsroom.py` builds memory blocks for each kind of agent against the live database, and exercises the whole write path (parse and store a prediction, store takes and a tweet take, check the week cutoff, gather summary inputs, store a summary, read the graded block back) inside a transaction it rolls back.

**Press conferences (`kind = 'PRESS'`).** `press_room.close_effects` gives every reporter in the room one `agent_memory_entries` row with `kind = 'PRESS'` (week = the game's week, team_id = the conference team, player_id = the subject of its first player question) carrying its exchanges and its own appraisal's memory and reasons (≤ 600 characters). The TAKE queries are unchanged, so press memories never leak into takes. Reporters' appraisals are stored in `press_attendees.judgment` (appraisal + relationship-event envelopes + appended flag); `flush_relationship_events` appends them through `personality/relationship_store.append_events`, and nothing writes `persona_relationships`. `build_memory_block` adds `YOUR RECENT PRESS CONFERENCES (you were in the room):` with the person's newest `PRESS_SHOWN = 3` `kind = 'PRESS'` rows from before the publication week; it reads them only when `press_conferences` exists, and the TAKE queries are unchanged, so press memories never mix with takes.

### 7.8 Agent Wire Social Desk (`newsroom/social_desk.py`, `docs/done/SOCIAL_MATRIX.md`)

**Status:** build steps 3–6 are built: planning, the post writer (JR chose Gemini 3.8 Flash for every post kind after the side-by-side test), publishing from the weekly run and team wakeups, and the `/api/social/*` endpoints (§4). Step 7, the Agent Wire frontend on live data, is built (§5). First live week: 2035 Week 18 (Oct 14), 100 posts and 20 trends. After it, JR asked for a player-first mix and 20 ex-player accounts (Oct 14; `db/migrations/2026_10_25_former_players.sql`), described below.

- **What it does:** `load_week_context(cur, season, week)` reads one publication week (including each recap game's script, `ctx["game_scripts"]`, §2.14; a game's facts carry it as `how_it_happened`: storyline, halftime, winning score, key moments), plus league topics (`ctx["league_topics"]`), team needs, pick history, team strength and the writer relationships strong enough to be a post angle (`ctx["strong_relationships"]`). `plan_social_week(ctx)` returns a week of 80–130 assignments sized by `week_mix`, each an account, a post kind, a subject, a **facts packet**, a `focus` (1–3 facts), `pick_games`, `subjects` (for relationship lookup) and `topic_id` (no model call, nothing written). Week N looks back at Week N-1's completed games and ahead to Week N's games; standings and season totals count only games before Week N, and a game in Week N or later never shows a score, so replanning an old week can't leak results.
- **What each kind is filled with (player-first mix, JR Oct 14; `week_mix` now sets how many of each, below):** shares (one per article stored for the week, from the writer's account; Skip's column shares from `SKIP_TWEET`, the roundtable panel never shares; local beat articles from one of that team's reporters); **reactions only from die-hards, one per team that played, no extras** (only die-hards post about a team as a team); **performances** (top full-PPR offensive lines, with big defensive and kicking games mixed in: the 2nd, 5th and 8th ordinary (non-buzz) performance post goes to the next of up to `DEF_PERFORMANCE_MAX` = 3 lines from the recap week's captured box scores (`ctx["defense_lines"]` from `game_stat_lines`, games with no captured defensive or kicking lines contribute none) that score `DEF_PERFORMANCE_MIN` = 12+ on `defense_play_score` (6/sack, 8/INT, 4/forced fumble, 3/recovery, 12/defensive TD, 6/safety; kicking 3/FG made, +3 per 50+ make, +12 for a 55+ yarder; the bigger of defense and kicking), biggest first; e.g. 2 sacks, an INT plus a forced fumble, a defensive TD, 4 field goals or a 55-yarder. Their facts carry the game line (`defense_stat_line`), game, result and opponent but no season totals or fantasy points; pundit preferences `DEF` and `K` in `PUNDIT_AFFINITY`. Buzz posts come first and a busy week trims the bucket to buzz only (2035 Week 18), so defensive days get posts only in weeks with ordinary slots), written by fantasy accounts, pundits, ex-players and bandwagon fans in rotation, never die-hards; **injuries (`BEAT_INJURY`, `INJURY_SHOCK`; `load_week_context` ranks starters among on-roster players and drops players released by the publication week):** beat accounts post factual reports on injured starters with recovery timetables; die-hard fan and meme accounts react in shock, panic or gloom when marquee superstars ($\ge 88$ OVR, $\ge 50$ Pop, starting QBs) suffer significant injuries; **bad games** (`BAD_GAME`: players who averaged 12+ full-PPR points over 3+ earlier games and scored at most 65% of that, biggest drop first, then QBs with 3+ interceptions; players with no line are skipped, since they may have been inactive), mostly bandwagon fans clowning the flop, plus pundits, an ex-player and @GridironMemes; **comparisons** (`COMPARISON`): 5 die-hards argue their team's best player beats last week's opponent's best at the same position, 3 ex-players rank the league's top five at their old position with their old team's best player alongside, pundits fill the rest with top-five debates; beat notes; standings (from Week 3: a pundit and a bandwagon fan); previews (fans of the top projected games, plus 2 fantasy start/sit posts in Weeks 2–17); memes; replies (placeholders; parents are picked after writing). Player names stored in capitals ("JERRY RAYFORD") are posted in normal case, and season ranks say RB, not HB.
- **What the league is talking about (JR, Oct 14; `Week.player_buzz`, `Week.team_stories`; frequencies checked against the 2035 season):**
  - **Player games**, tier 1 ("the league is talking"): 400+ passing yards, 5+ passing TDs, 150+ rushing or receiving yards (TE 90+), 3+ total TDs or 40+ full-PPR points. Tier 2 ("historic"): 6+ passing TDs, 200+ rushing or receiving yards (TE 150+), 4+ total TDs, 50+ PPR, or a tier-1 game that is the season's best by full-PPR points at its position (from Week 4). Season context in the regular season: round numbers crossed that week (5,000 passing yards, 50 passing TDs, 1,500/2,000 rushing yards, 1,500 receiving yards and 20 total TDs make news alone; 4,000 passing yards, 40 TDs, 1,000 yards and 15 TDs are only mentioned when the game is already news), NFL single-season records (breaking one is tier 2; being on pace for or already past one is tier 1 from Week 12, context before that). **Record book (§2.9):** when the record tables exist, `load_week_context` loads the book as it stood before the season (`load_record_book`: franchise records and all-time entries; league-wide records and top 10s only for categories with full real-NFL coverage, so the record book's partial categories never claim an NFL rank), and the desk uses it instead of the hardcoded `SEASON_RECORDS` / `TEAM_POINTS_RECORD` (kept as the fallback). A season total that breaks the player's franchise record that week is tier 1 ("the most passing TDs in a season in Panthers history: 49 (old record 47, George Crawford, 2034)"), one already past it is context, a tie of the NFL record is tier 2, and a season that climbs into the NFL top 10 is context (tier 1 from Week 12 for a top-3 season). Single games are checked against the NFL record and top 10 (tie or break tier 2, top 10 tier 1) and the franchise's single-game record where the book has one (tier 1). This season's other players and earlier games count too, so a teammate who already passed a record keeps it. Team storylines add franchise records for wins and points ("Most points in a season in Steelers history: 468 (old record 436, the 2014 Pittsburgh Steelers)") and take the NFL points record from the book. Ties among many holders read "shared with 9 players, most recently Sam Darnold, 2029". Tier 1 gets three performance posts (pundit, ex-player preferring the player's team and position, bandwagon fan), tier 2 four (plus a fantasy account) and a comparison on where the game ranks among the season's best at the position. Facts carry `why_people_are_talking` (up to 3 reasons, with "the 2nd-most in a game this season" ranks) and `how_big`; each post gets its own angle. These posts sit at the front of their buckets; ordinary performances fill the rest. QBs with 2+ interceptions in a loss count as bad games (no QB threw 3 in a 2035 game).
  - **Team storylines (`TEAM_STORY`, regular season, teams that played last week; up to 8 posts):** unbeaten or winless from 5 games (tier 2 from 10, with real NFL history in `nfl_history_through_2025`: the 1972 Dolphins and 2007 Patriots, the 2008 Lions and 2017 Browns), winning or losing streaks of 6+ (tier 2 from 10), a 6+ game winning streak ending (tier 2 for the first loss after an 8-0 or better start), a first win after 0-5 or worse, wins by 35+, 50+ points, upsets (a 0.35+ gap in winning percentage before the game, both teams with 5+ games) and the points record (606, 2013 Broncos: on pace from 6 games, past it, or broken that week as tier 2). One story per team with up to 3 reasons. Good news: tier 1 a pundit and a bandwagon fan, tier 2 two pundits (the second takes the skeptic's case), the team's ex-player if it has one, and a bandwagon fan. Bad news: the meme page and pundits, plus bandwagon fans hopping off and an ex-player at tier 2. Filed under the team, so they show in its Team Hub. A team wakeup for a team with a storyline always gets at least one national voice, and that post is the storyline. Agent Wire labels them "Storyline".
  - **Weekly mix (`week_mix`, JR's D4; AGENT_WIRE_VOICE_PLAN §2.4):** the week's total = clamp(base 80 + 4·tier-1 buzz + 6·tier-2 buzz + 3·trades + 2·one-score games + 5·playoff week, 80, 130) from `mix_total` in `social_desk.json`. Event-driven kinds count inside it: one die-hard reaction per team that played, one share per shareable article, beat notes for teams with news (bounded by `event_limits`, default 3–8), and the trade, move, injury and draft-board posts their own rules allow. The rest is split over `mix_weights` multiplied by the week's signals — no buzz lowers PERFORMANCE (×0.7), a big trade week raises TRADE_IDEA (×1.5), Weeks 12–18 raise AWARD_RACE, POWER_TAKE, STANDINGS and DRAFT_POSITION, the postseason raises PICKS and the preseason raises PREVIEW — with seeded ±25% jitter (`mix_jitter`) and each kind kept within its `mix_limits` [floor, ceiling]. Leftover posts go to performances, eliminated fans' PLAYER posts or previews. `BUCKET_SIZES`, `TRIM_ORDER`, `TARGET_POSTS`, `REPLY_RANGE` and the fixed angle lists (`FAN_ANGLES`, `BANDWAGON_ANGLES`, `BEAT_ANGLES`, `PREVIEW_ANGLES`, `REPLY_STANCES`) are gone; a post's angle is now an optional hint from its topic or the writer's relationships (`BUZZ_ANGLES` stays).
  - **League topics (`load_league_topics`; AGENT_WIRE_VOICE_PLAN §2.4):** stored data before Week N only, each `{topic_id, kind_hint, subjects: [{type,id}], focus: [facts], heat}`: MVP/OPOY and record chases from season leaders and the record book, `coty_scores`, `coach_hot_seat`, stored `power_rankings` and their movement, the playoff picture and division races (`season_landscape`), contract-year starters (`player_contracts`), rookie leaders and the week's injuries. Each source runs in its own savepoint, so a missing table simply yields no topics of that type. HOT_TAKE, AWARD_RACE, POWER_TAKE and QUESTION draw on them (kind hint first, hottest first).
  - **Picks and season calls (D3):** `plan_picks` gives 10–16 writers a week (least-used this season first, about half national voices, a third die-hards picking their own game) a `PICKS` post with `pick_games` = up to 4 of this week's games, the slate's most exciting first, spread across the slate. `plan_season_calls` gives 6–10 national voices two call types each in the preseason (Week 1), midseason (Week 9) and the trade-deadline week; calls are stored and graded later (§7.7). Each call assignment carries `candidates` — every team, the award-race leaders from the topics, and every head coach in his seat this season (`ctx["coaches"]`, read from `coaches` + `coach_tenures` with a savepoint) — so the model's named subject resolves through `parse_post_json` and the call stores.
  - **Live and fan kinds (§2.7):** `LIVE_MOMENT` (a fan or pundit on one play from a recap game's script, with the score at that moment and no knowledge of the finish), `QUARTER_UPDATE` (a beat writer on a team in the game, with that quarter's scores and moments), `TRADE_IDEA` (fans and pundits proposing a trade from a team's needs, never news, no dollar figures) and `DRAFT_POSITION` (die-hards of losing teams on where they would pick). Die-hard reactions now carry one `focus` (a scripted moment, a player's line or a coaching call) with the score and record only as background. `REPLY` gains a quote-post form (a beat writer on an insider, anyone on the aggregator or stats account, else about one reply in three).
  - **Relationship-driven angle:** `load_week_context` loads every writer relationship at |trust| ≥ 0.5; an assignment about that player, coach or team carries the bias as its `angle` in one plain line.
  - **New national accounts (D7):** the label-first `AGGREGATOR` (Gridline_Now, @GridlineNow, "Gridline Now") and `STATS_DESK` (Stat_Margin, @StatMargin, "Stat Margin"), both national with team null, are drawn into the mix when seeded: the aggregator echoes the biggest trade or move and joins the weekend's biggest game; the stats account takes a performance, a comparison and topic posts.
  - **Engagement:** `buzz_heat` in `social_desk.json` multiplies a buzz post's subject heat (tier 1 ×1.5, tier 2 ×2.2), and `TEAM_STORY` has kind factor 1.3, so these posts draw the replies and lead the trends.
- **Roster moves (team management step 5; `load_moves`, docs/done/team_management/05_NEWSROOM_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md §2.8):** `load_week_context` adds `ctx["moves"]`, the moves new for the publication week (`roster_moves.new_this_week` over `db_tools.fetch_moves`, annotated with notability; each with its move line, the money strings in it, the acting team, the new depth slot and the player's seasons with that team) and `ctx["team_caps"]` (each team's cap line with its basis); missing tables mean no moves (a savepoint keeps the connection usable). Four kinds, window Mon – Wed, facts packets only (every term and figure is in the move or cap line):
  - `MOVE_NEWS`: the insiders (`SCHEFTER_TWEET`, `RAPOPORT`, `Accounts.insider`, under the pundit cap) break the week's most notable moves, at most `MOVE_NEWS_MAX` = 3, most notable first; planned right after shares so the insiders aren't used up first. With `CAP_TAKE` it fills the `MOVES` bucket.
  - `BEAT_MOVE`: a beat team with a notable move gets it instead of its plain `BEAT` note; a starter injury (`BEAT_INJURY`) still comes first. Facts: the team's move lines and its cap line. `plan_team_wakeup` gives the first beat reporter not filing the injury report a `BEAT_MOVE` the same way.
  - `MOVE_REACTION`: a die-hard of the acting team on each of the `MOVE_REACTION_MAX` = 2 most notable moves, appended to reactions like `INJURY_SHOCK` (`seasons_with_your_team` when he's had 2+ seasons there and is leaving, staying or restructuring).
  - `CAP_TAKE`: one pundit, only when a team is over the cap (the deepest one) or, failing that, a release this week left $10M+ dead money (`CAP_TAKE_DEAD_MONEY`). Facts: the team's cap line (and the release line).
  - Kind factors (`social_desk.json`): `MOVE_NEWS` 1.4, `BEAT_MOVE` 1.0, `MOVE_REACTION` 1.3, `CAP_TAKE` 1.1. `docs/done/SOCIAL_MATRIX.md` §2 doesn't list these kinds yet: the sub-plan's table text for it wasn't among JR's §2.6 approvals.
  - `TRADED` leg rows never become move posts: trades post as whole trades (below).
- **Trades and rumors (Phase 8; `load_trades`):** `load_week_context` adds `ctx["trades"]` and `ctx["rumors"]` from `db_tools.new_week_trades` (last week's executed GM trades; rumors from last week's `rumor_ok` proposals and `gm_trade_leaks` rows, only through the Week 8 deadline), each with its team ids and its `trade_line` / `rumor_line` (a leak uses `roster_moves.leak_line`, which may name a player its leaker named but still never as traded; `db_tools.fetch_rumors` looks only the integer proposal ids up in `gm_trade_proposals` and passes leak rows through, a leak's outcome coming from its stage — `STALLED` → stalled, `OPENED`/`CLOSE` → open); a trade also carries its money strings, player names and each GM's stored rationale (`gm_said`). Missing step 3 tables mean none (savepoint). Window Mon – Wed, facts packets only. Trades and rumors are planned before `MOVE_NEWS` (bucket `MOVES`), so with the insiders' pundit cap they come first:
  - `TRADE_NEWS`: an insider breaks each executed trade, at most `TRADE_NEWS_MAX` = 3. Facts: both teams with records, the trade line (every player, pick and dollar figure), grounding that it was executed.
  - `TRADE_RUMOR`: an insider posts at most `TRADE_RUMOR_MAX` = 2 rumors. Facts: both teams and the rumor line (a leak's line is `leak_line`; a leak the `insider_key` got is assigned first to that account, and the other insiders may post it from the following edition, still through Week 8); grounding says no trade happened, no player names (except a player a leak's leaker named, still never as traded), no dollar figures (the money guard then rejects any `$`). The **rumor guard** (`clean_post(..., rumor=True)`, `RUMOR_PROBLEM`) flags done-deal wording (traded, acquired, agreed to, finalized, completed, shipped, "done deal" unless "not a done deal"); `write_post`'s one rewrite covers it and `publishable` drops a post that still has it.
  - `TRADE_REACTION`: a die-hard of each team on each trade insiders broke (appended to reactions), with `your_team` and, when stored, `your_gm_said` (the GM's rationale, to quote, mock or back).
  - `BEAT_MOVE` also covers a team in one of last week's trades (`trades_this_week` in its facts), and trade teams go first in the beat-note order, so both teams get one; `plan_team_wakeup` does the same.
  - Kind factors: `TRADE_NEWS` 1.5, `TRADE_REACTION` 1.3, `TRADE_RUMOR` 1.2. `docs/done/SOCIAL_MATRIX.md` §2 doesn't list them yet (same reason as the move kinds).
- **Player statements (COACH_PLAYER_AGENT_LOOPS_PLAN §2.5, U3b; built 2026-11-09; `load_player_statements`):** `load_week_context` adds `ctx["player_statements"]`, the public `LEAK` decisions (a shadow season records its leaks as private and spends no model call on them) from `engines/agent_loops/player.py` for the publication week's news window (recap Week N-1 and Week N, plus the finished season's whole offseason window — (S-1, ticks 24–32) — for the Week 1 edition, since CPU contract talks run at ticks 25/26/30 there), ordered by (tick, subject_key), at most `LEAK_MAX_PER_WEEK` = 3, `[]` when `agent_loop_decisions` is missing (a `to_regclass` guard). Each item carries only the row's facts: player name, position, team, statement text (the loop's figure-free template when the model text is null), player_id, season and tick, plus `offered`/`asked` when present. `PLAYER_STATEMENT` is event-driven (counted inside the week's total, window Mon – Wed) and planned in its own bucket after the trades/rumors: an insider reports each one (a pundit when no insider is left under the cap), subject `{player, team}`, filed under his team. Facts: the recorded statement, player/team/position, offered/asked only, and the grounding "A STATEMENT, not a signing: he said he wants a deal. Never say a deal was made, agreed or signed, and use only the figures the statement itself contains." Writer: `KIND_INSTRUCTIONS["PLAYER_STATEMENT"]` (a statement, not a signing; no new figures; no trade or deal claim) and `KIND_SHAPES["PLAYER_STATEMENT"]`; `_post_time` places it Monday–Wednesday. Tests: `tests/test_agent_loops_statements.py` (loader table guard, window ticks, cap, recorded facts, one grounded assignment per statement, mix count, and a no-leak week changing nothing).
- **Draft board (step 5 Phase 9, JR-approved text 2026-10-20; `load_draft_movers`, `draft_board_subjects`):** `load_week_context` adds `ctx["draft_movers"]` from `scouting_read.risers_fallers` (the latest consensus-board step visible to the week; public fields only, as `db_tools.draft_mover_line`; `{}` with no step 4 tables or no visible board). @MockDraftMarty (`DRAFT_SICKO`) posts `DRAFT_BOARD`: `DRAFT_BOARD_POSTS` = 1 a week in the regular season (the bigger of the top riser and top faller) and 2 from Week 19 on (both), in the `MEME` bucket on top of its count, window Tue – Thu, kind factor 1.0. Facts: the class, riser/faller, name, position, school, consensus rank and grade, rank and grade change, and up to 3 stored storylines. The prompt quotes ranks, grades and storylines exactly and never mentions Madden ratings. `docs/done/SOCIAL_MATRIX.md` row 8b. No posts until the board has a second step (the first has no movement).
- **Ex-players (`FORMER_PLAYER`, 20 accounts):** real retired stars plus 2026 NFL Top 50 players who aren't on a 2035 roster (treated as retired before 2035), written "in the style of" like the pundits: Mahomes, Josh Allen, Justin Jefferson, Ja'Marr Chase, McCaffrey, Saquon, Micah Parsons, T.J. Watt, Derrick Henry, Dak, Maxx Crosby, Herbert, Brady, Marshawn Lynch, Cam Newton, Vick, Brees, Strahan, Calvin Johnson, Larry Fitzgerald. `assigned_team_id` is the old team and the identity line says "I played <POS> for the <team>"; the planner reads the position from it. Their posts are league-wide and never filed under the old team (outside its team wakeup). Every assignment by an ex-player, and by the ex-player pundits (`FORMER_TEAM_SLANT`: Ochocinco CIN, Shannon DEN, J.J. Watt HOU, RG3 WAS, Clark PIT, McAfee IND), carries `slant_team`, which the writer turns into a "soft spot for your old team" line. Followers 0.8–6M, like rate 0.004. Agent Wire labels them "Former <team>" with an orange badge.
- **Postseason (Week 19+):** a few extra reactions, then the room goes to `PLAYER` posts by fans of eliminated teams (their own team's top players, alternating with players still alive). Alive teams are this week's scheduled teams, or last week's playoff winners in the Super Bowl bye week. **Preseason** (no completed games): every team's fans preview their opener, then pundits. **Fantasy season over (Weeks 19–23 / playoffs / offseason):** the fantasy football season ends after Week 18 (`fantasy_phase(week) is None`). During playoffs and offseason, tweets about fantasy are never generated: fantasy accounts (`FANTASY_GURU`, `BERRY`, `YATES`) and the `fantasy` role are completely disabled in account selection, buzz assignments (tier 2 buzz uses a pundit rather than fantasy), performance rotations, and replies; fantasy article shares and previews are suppressed; facts packets omit `fantasy_points_ppr`, prior PPR averages, and PPR-based rankings (ranking by real yardage/TDs instead); prompts enforce a mandatory rule forbidding fantasy mentions; and `publishable` / `save_post` enforce hard blocking against fantasy terminology.
- **Accounts:** least-used first under weekly caps (pundit 3, fantasy 4, beat 2, fan 2, bandwagon 3, ex-player 3), with position affinities for pundits (e.g. QB → RG3, Cowherd, Stephen A). The pundit pool mirrors `TWEET_EXCLUDED_ARCHETYPES` (which includes `MEL_KIPER`, a long-form draft writer) and leaves out all fantasy accounts (`FANTASY_ARCHETYPES`: `FANTASY_GURU`, `BERRY`, `YATES`), memes, and draft accounts, so fantasy analysts are never drawn as general pundits. Deterministic for a season and week.
- **Dry run:** `python3 -m newsroom.social_desk --season 2035 --week 18 [--json plan.json] [--dsn DSN]` prints the plan; `--dsn` (or `DATABASE_URL`) selects the database. When the week's slates aren't stored yet it plans placeholder shares, one per national and fantasy slot.
- **Writer (`newsroom/social_writer.py`, build step 4):** `build_post_prompt` puts the account's persona (`agent_personas.json`, rendered by `newsroom/personas.build_persona_block` with `POST` habits, the post kind's tags, QB when the subject is a quarterback, the team's result signals and the account's last 15 posts for signature use, §7.11; a raw persona dict passed in is rendered without database context), its identity line and memory block, and `SOCIAL_RULES` (one post of at most 280 characters, numbers only from the facts packet, no invented injuries or betting lines; contract figures, signings, releases and trades only from the facts, a trade done only if the facts say it was executed, a rumor kept a rumor, never an invented contract figure (JR's R12), a game's `how_it_happened` never contradicted, facts treated as background boundaries rather than a stat-checklist, cadence/syntax variety guidelines forbidding repetitive LLM clichés like "expeditiously", "pure cardio", or formulaic jersey buying/trashing, and everything else free to invent the way real people post: what they saw, a play they can't stop thinking about, hot takes, jokes, rumors framed as rumors, grudges; no tools and no metric names even if the persona mentions them, no ratings or Madden, at most 2 hashtags; and in postseason/offseason, a strict prohibition on fantasy football or PPR mentions) in the system instruction, and a per-kind task plus the facts packet in the prompt (replies also get the parent post). For non-fantasy personas, `build_post_prompt` sanitizes raw fantasy metrics (`fantasy_points_ppr`, prior PPR averages, decimal points in buzz facts) so real-football accounts never quote decimal fantasy stats. `write_post` (model may carry a thinking level, `gemini-3.8-flash:low`, in `social_desk.json` `model` / `model_by_kind`, or route to local Ollama via `engines/llm_provider.py` with automatic fallback to Gemini on connection error/timeout) makes one LLM call with no tools and asks once for a shorter version if the post runs over 280 characters; `clean_post` strips labels, quotes, markdown and links, keeps 2 hashtags and flags problems (length, ratings, fantasy mentions after season over, "expeditiously"). Facts packets describe a game's excitement in words ("an entertaining game") and never carry the index. Usage and cost come from `usage_metadata` (`PRICES`: 3.8 Flash $0.75/$3.75 per 1M until Dec 31, 2026; 3.5 Flash-Lite $0.30/$2.50; local Ollama models $0.00).
- **Writer voice and structured output (AGENT_WIRE_VOICE_PLAN §2.3, §2.7):** The prompt also carries the writer's `relationship_block(cur, person_key, assignment["subjects"])` (person key cached per account) and a `pick_shape` sampled from the account's recent shapes; `write_post` receives the assignment (with the planner's pick cards normalized by `social_publish.normalized_assignment`) so `parse_post_json` can resolve names, winners and calls. `build_persona_block(..., relationships=False)` lets the post path suppress its own copy; articles keep the default. Recent shapes come from `news_feed.post_shape`, written with each post (`2027_02_10`); rows from before the column (or a database without it) fall back to `infer_post_shape` on their text. Every `KIND_INSTRUCTIONS` entry (old and new kinds — `PICKS`, `HOT_TAKE`, `AWARD_RACE`, `POWER_TAKE`, `QUESTION`, `SEASON_CALL`, `LIVE_MOMENT`, `QUARTER_UPDATE`, `TRADE_IDEA`, `DRAFT_POSITION`, the quote form `REPLY_QUOTE`, and `FANTASY_PREVIEW`/`DRAFT` variants) is a **situation + intent** brief: what happened and whose point of view, and what the post is for. No instruction lists alternative moods or moves; `SOCIAL_RULES` states the measured shape instead (most posts under 25 words, no closing punctuation needed, at most one number unless you are a stats account) and loses its own example-move list. `POST_SHAPES` (`one_liner`, `question`, `fragmented_live`, `contrast`, `list_of_three`, `callback`, `prediction`, `observation`, `sarcasm`, `plain_statement`) are sampled per post by `pick_shape(account, kind, recent_shapes, seed)` — weighted by the archetype's optional `post_shapes` and narrowed by `KIND_SHAPES`, never one of the account's last 3 — and shown as one `SHAPE:` line. `agent_personas.json` gains a `post_style` per archetype from the real-tweet audit (`length`, `numbers`, `case`, `punctuation`, `hashtags`, `profanity` for fan archetypes only per D6, `off_topic_share`) rendered by `render_post_style`, plus the two national archetypes `AGGREGATOR` (label-first: "Savage:", "BREAKING") and `STATS_DESK` (one striking stat, no opinion). `build_post_prompt(..., relationship_block="", shape=None)` adds `YOUR BIASES` from the writer's relationships and treats `assignment["focus"]` (1–3 facts) as the subject with the rest of the packet as "background, use at most one". The model returns JSON `{"text", "about": [{type, name, lean}], "picks": [{game, winner, score, confidence}], "calls": [{call_type, subject, detail}]}` with `text` first; `parse_post_json(raw, assignment)` resolves names to ids against the assignment's facts and games, drops unknown names, and falls back to the plain text when JSON fails; `clean_post` then runs on `text` unchanged. `too_similar(text, corpus, threshold=0.55, same_kind=)` rejects a post whose word-trigram Jaccard against the week's posts or the account's last 15 is too high, or whose first three words match a post of the same kind this week; `write_post` adds it to the conditions for its one rewrite.
- **Money guard (`social_writer.allowed_money` / `clean_post(..., allowed=)`):** every post is checked against the dollar amounts in its facts packet (and, for a reply, its parent's text), compared to the nearest $10K ("$118M" = "$118 million"); a dollar figure that isn't there is a problem (`MONEY_PROBLEM`). `write_post` asks for its one rewrite when a post runs long or names such a figure (one call covers both), and `social_publish.publishable` drops a post that still does (`[NOT SAVED]`). The rumor guard (Phase 8, above) works the same way for `TRADE_RUMOR` posts.
- **Model comparison:** `python3 tools/social_model_compare.py [--week 9] [--models gemini-3.8-flash gemini-3.8-flash:low gemini-3.5-flash-lite] [--prompts old|new|both] [--db DSN] [--dry-run]` (`model:level` sets the thinking level; `--prompts` compares the pre-U2 post writer loaded from git at `0b73ab5` with the current one on the same sampled assignments, `both` also writing a blind A/B Markdown file for JR, and `--dry-run` saves the prompt pairs with no model calls) writes the same 20 planned posts (6 reactions, 3 performances, 2 beat notes, 1 standings, 2 previews incl. a fantasy start/sit, 2 memes, 2 shares when the week has stored articles, and 2 replies from rival fans) with each model, prints cost per post, and saves posts, prompts and usage to `captures/social_compare/`. It reads the database and writes nothing to it. The generalized quality test harness `python3 -m tools.llm_compare (--task {agent_wire,memory_takes,memory_summary,scouting_notes,gm_persona,gm_rationale,gm_negotiation,inbox_reply,inbox_appraisal} | --suite [--tasks T ...]) --season S --week W --models M1 M2 ... [--limit N] [--db NAME|DSN] [--json-mode] [--ollama-timeout S] [--num-ctx N] [--out DIR]` (docs/done/PRE_PC_WORK.md §7, docs/done/PC_MIGRATION_PLAN.md §7.4) extends side-by-side evaluation across all 9 short tasks and generates structured JSON and interactive HTML reports in `verify_output/` (`--suite` adds one combined `compare_suite_<ts>` report). Inputs come from the `madden_2036` archive unless `--db` or `LLM_COMPARE_DB` names another database; the process sets `DATABASE_URL` to it and `PGOPTIONS=-c default_transaction_read_only=on`, so every connection, including the newsroom helpers' own, is read-only, and calls pass `log_tokens=False`. Ollama specs are `ollama:<tag>` with optional `@think` / `@nothink`; they run with `allow_fallback=False`, so a timeout scores as a failure rather than Gemini's answer. `--json-mode` requests JSON output on the three GM tasks.
- **Quality report (AGENT_WIRE_VOICE_PLAN §2.6, §2.7 rule 6):** `python3 -m tools.social_quality_report --db <dsn> --season S [--weeks a-b] [--json out]` reads Agent Wire posts (`slot LIKE 'Agent Wire%'`, `content_type='TWEET'`) on a read-only connection and reports, per kind and overall: distinct two-word openers / posts (lowercased, punctuation and apostrophes dropped, digit runs collapsed to `#`), mean pairwise word-trigram Jaccard within a week, forward-looking share (`PICKS`, `SEASON_CALL`, `PREVIEW`, `HOT_TAKE` or a will/next week/pick/calling it/prediction word match), share citing 3+ numbers, kind mix, posts per account, median words per archetype (`persona`), share without closing punctuation and mean numbers per post. Missing tables/columns print a readable message instead of a traceback. It also prints an archive-wide S5 baseline check (the whole `madden_2036` archive, both seasons: REACTION 553 posts/317 openers, PLAYER 160/72, BEAT_INJURY 88/40); the per-kind table is the requested season.
- **Publishing (`newsroom/social_publish.py`, build step 5):**
  - `run_social_week(conn_info, season, week)` (called by `weekly_run` after the slates): skips a week that already has posts with slot `Agent Wire` (unless `force`), plans, writes the non-reply posts in parallel (5 workers), then plans and writes the reply pass, then refreshes trends. `dry_run` prints the plan only. Posts with an API error, no text, over 280 characters after the one rewrite, a ratings/Madden mention, or a fantasy mention after the fantasy season are logged `[NOT SAVED]` and skipped.
  - `run_team_social(conn_info, season, week, team_id, local_articles)` (called by `dispatch_team_local` on live, saved wakeups): `plan_team_wakeup` gives each of the team's beat reporters a distinct note cycling through `BEAT_ANGLES` (film notes, locker room vibes, coordinator adjustments, practice observations, injury context) to avoid duplicate reporter angles, each die-hard a reaction to last week's game or a preview of this week's (alternating), 3 pundits if the team's popularity is above 70 or 1 above 55 (each posts about one of the team's top lines last week, or a top-five debate at its best player's position), the team's ex-player, if it has one, on a top-five debate at his old position, and a share of each local article written in that wakeup by its reporter; agents who already posted in an earlier wakeup for the team and week are skipped. Saved with slot `Agent Wire Local`.
  - **Deduplication guards:** `_publish` inspects existing tweets via `find_existing_tweet_for_assignment` prior to generation, reusing already published posts for downstream reply planning and skipping redundant Gemini calls; `save_post` enforces content-level deduplication (`find_duplicate_content_tweet`, comparing normalized text for the author, season, and week) and assignment deduplication, returning `None` and logging `[DUPLICATE SKIPPED]` without writing duplicate rows to `news_feed`. In postseason/offseason, `save_post` also refuses any post with a fantasy archetype or fantasy terms.
  - **Saving:** each post is a `news_feed` row (`content_type` 'TWEET', `persona` = archetype, `agent_id`, `post_kind`, `posted_at`, `reply_to_id`, `linked_article_id` for shares, `subject_game_id`, `subject_player_id`, `likes`, `reposts`, `reply_count`, `views`, `hashtags`, `post_shape`). Teams are tagged by `EntityTaggingService` from the text plus both teams of the post's game; a player subject is tagged `PRIMARY`. Every post except a share is stored as the author's take (`agent_memory.store_tweet_take`). After the save, `social_publish._record_post_relationships` applies the structured `about` to the writer's relationships (`relationships.apply_take`), stores each pick in `agent_predictions` (`pick_type` WINNER/SCORE, `article_id` = the post, `label` = confidence, `winner_team_id`, scores only for SCORE) and each season call in `agent_season_calls`; failures log `RELATIONSHIPS/PICKS NOT RECORDED` and never block the post.
  - **Replies (`social_desk.plan_replies`):** the 20 replies go to the 8 most-liked posts (3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2). A fan's post gets the other team's fans first, then its own team's fans and bandwagon fans; a pundit's or writer's gets a set foil (`CONTRARIAN`, e.g. Shannon ↔ Skip, Stephen A ↔ McAfee, Barnwell → Skip, Sando → Cowherd), then fans of the teams involved; a meme gets the roasted team's fans; a beat note gets that team's fans. Replies count against the weekly caps and carry the parent's facts and text.
  - **Variety:** posts receive dynamic creative perspectives framed as guidance rather than rigid templates. Dedicated angle pools include expanded `FAN_ANGLES` (legacy claims/debates, "best player in the league" / "best at position" / "best all-time", pre-game dread of opponent stars, attacking players / receipts, trauma/PTSD, apology forms, coaching hot seats), `BANDWAGON_ANGLES` (jumping on/off, front-runner flexing without repetitive jersey buying tropes), `BEAT_ANGLES` (film notes, locker room vibes, adjustments), `PREVIEW_ANGLES` (key matchups, matchup fear, legacy stakes), and `BUZZ_ANGLES`. Rules discourage stock fan phrases ("casuals", "real fans", "plastic franchise", "bleed … forever") and clichés. Replies to the same post take different stances in turn: push back, agree and add, joke. The first live week (Oct 14) showed nearly every fan post leaning on the same phrases and four near-identical bandwagon replies to one Barnwell share, which these rules fix.
  - **Simulated time (`posted_at`):** Week 1's Thursday is the first Thursday after Labor Day of the season year, each week 7 days later; kickoffs come from `games.game_time` (default Sunday 1:00 PM) and games last 3h10m. Reactions land 5–90 minutes after their game ends, game memes 30 minutes–10 hours after, performances and bad games between the game's end and Monday night, storylines and move posts Monday 9:00–Wednesday 20:00, comparisons Tuesday 9:00–Thursday 20:00, beat notes, shares and draft posts Tuesday morning–Wednesday evening, standings Tuesday, postseason player posts Tuesday–Saturday, previews from Thursday (at most two days before kickoff) until an hour before kickoff, fantasy start/sit Friday–Sunday morning, replies 3–240 minutes after their parent. Planned posts (everything except reactions, game memes and replies) that land between 1:00 and 6:59 move to 7:00–9:59 that morning. Seeded per post, so a rerun gives the same times.
  - **Engagement:** `followers` is set once per account (`agent_memories.followers`, seeded by `agent_id`): insiders (Schefter, Rapoport) 1–5M, other national voices 0.5–3M, The Flex Spot 250–600K, @GridironMemes 600K–1M, @MockDraftMarty 50–150K, beat reporters 20–150K and fans 200–25K scaled by their team's popularity, bandwagon fans 500–8K. Likes = followers × the role's like rate × subject heat (game excitement and team popularity, player popularity, or the shared article's slot) × a kind factor (memes 1.6, replies 0.25) × log-normal noise; reposts, reply counts and views are ratios of likes. Stored on the row, so they never change between loads.
  - **Trends (`refresh_trends`):** after every weekly run and team wakeup, the week's teams, players, games and hashtags are scored by summed engagement (likes + 2 × reposts + 3 × replies) with a recency weight, weighted by kind (players 1.3, games 1.2, teams 0.8, hashtags 0.5), and need a minimum number of posts (games 3, others 2). Generic hashtags (#NFL, #Week17 and the like) never trend. The top 20 replace the week's `social_trends` rows; titles are templates ("Bills–Chiefs", the player's name, "#BillsMafia") and the description is the top post's text.
  - **Settings:** `newsroom/config/social_desk.json` holds the model (and per-kind overrides), workers, follower ranges, like rates, kind factors (including every TRADE_* and the new kinds), share-slot heat, the trend weights and stoplist, and the weekly mix: `mix_total`, `mix_jitter`, `mix_weights`, `mix_limits` and `event_limits`. `db/clear_news_feed.sh` also backs up and clears `social_trends` when it deletes posts.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_social_api.py` (post shape, labels, For You order), `tests/test_social_publish.py` (calendar, post windows, followers, engagement, publishable posts, fantasy suppression after season over, trends, replies, team wakeups, tweet deduplication guards for normalized content and assignments, pundit pool vs the dispatcher, relationship block and sampled shape passed into the prompt once, picks/calls/about stored from structured output, normalized pick cards), `tests/test_seed_clean_db.py` (seed writes relationships; person_key present, Skip shared, the two D7 accounts), `tests/test_social_quality_report.py` (two-word openers, trigram overlap, forward-looking and 3+ number shares, kind mix, per-account counts, median words per archetype, and the missing-table guard, all on synthetic posts), `tests/test_social_writer.py` (cleanup, prompts, old-team slant, cost) and `tests/test_social_desk.py` (synthetic league: the week_mix total and its reaction to buzz, trades and one-score games, floors/ceilings and determinism, one die-hard reaction per team and no one else reacting, per-kind focus/pick_games/subjects/topic_id, no score leaks, caps, fantasy weeks, complete fantasy suppression in playoffs and offseason (`test_no_fantasy_tweets_in_playoffs_or_offseason`), preseason/postseason/Super Bowl bye, bad games, comparisons, ex-players, name tidying, buzz tiers, record book, team storylines, defensive/kicking performances, shares, league topics from data before Week N with missing-table degradation, picks spread and least-used rotation, season calls only in call weeks, live moments/quarter updates, trade ideas and draft position, quote replies, the aggregator and stats accounts, relationship-driven angles, and leak routing — fresh leak to its `insider_key` insider, older leaks open the next edition, de-duplicated, under the two-rumor cap — and leak/quote lines in `tests/test_newsroom_trades.py` and `tests/test_roster_moves.py`).

### 7.9 On-Demand Custom Article Commissioning (`newsroom/custom_commission.py`)
Provides autonomous and interactive on-demand article generation from user prompts, accessible via CLI and the `#debug` Control tab ("Commission Custom Story"):
- **Two-Step Editorial Flow:**
  1. *Prompt Classification (`classify_prompt`):* A fast `gemini-3.8-flash` structured pass analyzes the user's prompt, publication season, and week. It resolves:
     - `target_desk`: `NATIONAL` (macro recaps, schematic autopsies, player deep profiles, columns, coach hot seats, beat coverage) or `FANTASY` (waiver wire, start/sit, rankings, sleepers/busts, draft tiers).
     - `article_type_id`: One of 33 national or 25 fantasy types from `newsroom/config/article_types.json`.
     - `writer_archetype`: Eligible writer matching the format and tone (e.g. Joyner for film, Barnwell for regression, Kimes for scheme, Sando for front office, Berry/Yates for fantasy, or Local Beat Reporter for team beats).
     - `team_id`: Target franchise ID if team-specific, else `None`.
     - `desk_note`: Mandatory directive specifying the exact angle, players, and matchups to investigate.
     - `rationale`: 1-sentence analytical reasoning for the proposed pairing.
  2. *Swarm Execution (`commission_custom_article`):* Dispatches the writer agent via `SwarmDispatcher` with the full ReAct database toolset (28+ tools for national, `FANTASY_TOOLS` for fantasy). National articles are saved to `news_feed` with `slot="Special Commission"`, routing to `slotted_response["other"]` on `GET /api/news/week/{week}` and appearing in the expanded "This Week's Stories" grid (`showAllStories` in `App.tsx`). Fantasy articles are saved with `slot="Fantasy Spotlight"` and appear in `/api/fantasy/articles` and on the Mu Fantasy hub.
- **CLI Usage:** `python3 -m newsroom.custom_commission --prompt "..." [--season N] [--week N] [--desk NATIONAL|FANTASY] [--type T] [--writer W] [--team ID] [--desk-note "..."] [--classify-only] [--dry-run]`
- **REST Endpoints (`server/debug_api.py`):**
  - `POST /api/debug/classify_article`: returns proposal and catalog dropdown lists.
  - `POST /api/debug/commission_article`: starts background job in `captures/jobs/` with live log streaming and attaches `url_hash` (`#article-{id}` or `#article-fantasy-{id}`) upon completion.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_custom_commission.py`.

### 7.10 The Offseason Editorial Package (Week 24: "Offseason") (`newsroom/offseason_service.py`, `newsroom/offseason_run.py`, `docs/done/OFFSEASON_EDITORIAL_SLATE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`)
Follows the franchise from the Super Bowl through the first round of the next NFL Draft. Published as a unified 6-article package under the concluded season and synthetic publication week 24 (labeled "Offseason" in `App.tsx` and the edition bar), while decoupling publication time from each story's narrative anchor date (`event_date + 1 week`) and enforcing an anti-leakage information cutoff:
- **National Desk Grid Slots (1 Hero, 2 Secondary, 3 Features):**
  - Stored under canonical newsroom slot keys (`Hero Slot`, `Slot 1`, `Slot 2`, `Slot 3`, `Slot 4`, `Slot 5`) in `news_feed`, with `server/api.py` categorizing `Hero Slot` into `hero`, `Slot 1` & `Slot 2` (and `Secondary *`) into `secondary`, and `Slot 3`, `Slot 4`, `Slot 5` (and `Feature *`) into `features`.
  - In `Mu_Network/src/App.tsx`, Week 24 ("Offseason") renders a full-width editorial layout (`gridTemplateColumns: "1fr"`) hiding the in-season sidebar (`Trending Local Coverage` and `Power Rankings`), featuring:
    - `Hero Slot`: `SUPER_BOWL_GAME_RECAP` (`BARNWELL`, `ROSENTHAL`, `CHADIHA`) — defining turn, box scores, turning points, official Super Bowl MVP; zero post-game event leakage.
    - `Slot 1` (Secondary): `SUPER_BOWL_CHAMPION_RETROSPECTIVE` (`CHADIHA`, `SANDO`, `ROSENTHAL`) — full-season title arc, regular-season identity translation to January. Displayed under `Secondary Slots (1 & 2) · Retrospective & Loss Analysis`.
    - `Slot 2` (Secondary): `SUPER_BOWL_RUNNER_UP_POSTMORTEM` (`SANDO`, `BARNWELL`) — tactical diagnosis of championship defeat, top offseason mandate.
    - `Slot 3` (Feature): `COACHING_CAROUSEL_AUDIT` (`SANDO`, `BARNWELL`) — grades the offseason hiring cycle (Mu's carousel moves, §2.19, including coordinator firings, poaching and promotions, plus JR's teams' manifest moves); evaluates head coach slants (`OFFENSIVE`, `DEFENSIVE`, `CEO`), coordinator origins (e.g. ex-Panthers OC), and scheme inheritance rules (imported offensive scheme preserves existing defense under DC, and vice versa; `docs/done/COACH_SLANTS_AND_COORDINATORS_PLAN.md`); zero offseason free-agency, offseason trades or draft (in-season moves are season history, R3) leakage. Displayed under `Feature Slots (3, 4 & 5) · Offseason In-Depth Audits`.
    - `Slot 4` (Feature): `FREE_AGENCY_SIGNING_GRADES` (`YATES`, `BARNWELL`, `SANDO`) — grades curated marquee veteran additions (90+ OVR only); strict ban on numeric OVR (converted to qualitative tiers: 95+ "Tier 1 superstar / cornerstone", 90-94 "High-impact marquee starter / Pro Bowl caliber"); "All-Pro" descriptor is strictly forbidden unless verified in the database `awards` table; zero draft leakage.
    - `Slot 5` (Feature): `NFL_DRAFT_CLASS_RECAP` (`MEL_KIPER`, `YATES`, `BARNWELL`) — Round 1 deep-dive focus (picks 1–32) using actual results from `draft_prospects` (`actual_pick`, `drafted_team_id`, `actual_round`, `actual_round_pick`) comparing against `projected_pick` to highlight steals and reaches, backed by full multi-round draft class context across all 7 rounds (224+ picks) stored in `draft_prospects`.
- **Service & Manifest (`newsroom/offseason_service.py`):**
  - All-in-one manifest parser (`captures/offseason/<season>/manifest.json`) recording season, event dates, coaching moves, marquee signings, and draft results.
  - Transactionally applies coaching moves and coordinator tenures, enforcing exactly one active HC, OC, and DC per team.
  - **Mu's coaching carousel** (§2.19): for a season the carousel decided (`mu_runs_carousel`), Mu owns every CPU team's coaching moves: `preview_manifest` adds `hot_seat_firings` and `mu_coaching_moves` (the Carousel packet, once the hiring cycle ran; each head-coach hire carries `coaching_tree` `{label, line}` or null, read through the season on a tuple cursor of the same connection) and warns about fired coaches still waiting on the cycle and about manifest `coaching_moves` at CPU teams (`hot_seat_warnings`, pure); `apply_coaching_moves` applies JR's teams' moves only (`skipped_moves` lists the rest); the coaching facts packet is `mu_coaching_packet` (each head-coach hire with the predecessor's record and how he was fired, the hire type and origin, the opening's rank with its selling points and drawbacks (parts at or above 0.75 / at or below 0.25, plus coaching churn), the schemes; `coordinators_fired`; `coordinator_moves`) plus JR's teams' manifest moves. Earlier seasons (2035) use the manifest as before.
  - **Signing candidates from League Transactions** (team management step 5, phase 7): `preview_manifest` adds `signing_candidates`, the season's offseason `SIGNED` rows (`transactions.week` NULL; `fetch_offseason_signings`) of players rated 90+ (`SIGNING_CANDIDATE_MIN_OVR`), most expensive first, each with player, position, new team, former team (the signing row's, else the team that last released him, else "unknown (fill in)"), OVR and qualitative tier for JR, and `terms` ("4 years, $96.4M total (from the signing)"). JR still picks the 2–3 marquee signings into the manifest. The signings facts packet gives each manifest signing `signing_terms` from its matching offseason `SIGNED` row (by player name) or "not recorded: state no contract terms" (R5). No transactions table or no offseason rows = no candidates, no failure. `tests/test_offseason_service.py` `TestSigningCandidates` covers the pure helpers.
  - Pre-packages facts bundles with strict temporal cutoffs (`newsroom/run_context.py` `set_offseason_cutoff`). The anti-leakage boundaries bar *offseason* moves only (JR's R2/R3): the Super Bowl stories and the Coaching Carousel may cite in-season signings and releases as season history, and the signing grades cite contract terms only from the signing terms or `get_player_contract`, never inferring a missing one (R5). The three Super Bowl types and the Carousel carry the same narrowing in `article_types.json`; `SUPER_BOWL_RUNNER_UP_POSTMORTEM` and `FREE_AGENCY_SIGNING_GRADES` list the contract tools in `data_queried`.
- **Madden Draft Recap Capture & Ingestion (`madden_capture.py`, `pipeline/extract_draft_results.py`, `pipeline/draft_results.py`):**
  - Live console Remote Play capture via `python3 madden_capture.py --only draft-results [--draft-picks N] [--row-by-row]`: navigates Weekly Hub → DRAFT RECAP tile → permitted Cross → held-L2 dropdown switch to NFL. Defaults to paged mode (10 rows per page across all rounds via `capture_list`), extracted into `draft_results.csv` and `draft_results.json` via `pipeline.extract_draft_results`; optional `--row-by-row` captures picks one by one via player card crops (`pick_NNN.png`). The recap rows give no team, so the extract assigns each pick's team by overall pick from `draft_picks` owners for the class (league season + 1): the Draft Room's locked `overall_pick` order when all 224 are locked, else `draft_order.draft_order_with_owners` for rounds 1–7 (a traded pick goes to its owner); prospects are matched against that class only.
  - Ingestion via `python3 -m pipeline.draft_results --season <season> --file <path> [--dry-run]` directly enriches `draft_prospects` across all rounds (`actual_round`, `actual_round_pick`, `actual_pick`, `drafted_team_id`, `selection_notes`). Also accessible via `python3 -m pipeline.weekly_capture --mode draft-results`.
- **CLI Runner (`newsroom/offseason_run.py`):**
  - `python3 -m newsroom.offseason_run --season <season> --input <manifest> [--dry-run] [--only super_bowl|coaching|signings|draft] [--force]`
- **REST Endpoints (`server/debug_api.py`):**
  - `POST /api/debug/offseason/preview`: validates manifest and returns structured preview with resolved teams, coaches, slants, qualitative tiers, `signing_candidates` and warnings.
  - `POST /api/debug/offseason/run`: runs the offseason package background job with live log streaming.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_offseason_service.py` (28 tests), `tests/test_offseason_catalog.py` (7 tests), `tests/test_coordinators.py` (14 tests), `tests/test_draft_results.py` (20 tests), `tests/test_extract_draft_results.py` (7 tests), `tests/test_weekly_capture.py` (21 tests).

**Personality core (built 2026-10-31; feature-independent, not activated in production):** `personality/core.py` supplies universe/role/birth-key UUID identity, deterministic generated initialization using the existing six sliders/catalogue, sparse reviewed real profiles, explicit neutral unknown/missing profiles, `feature_view` and validated one-change-per-season candidates. **Core extensions (2026-11-04, docs/done/PERSONALITY_CORE_EXTENSIONS_PLAN.md):** `feature_view` is `views-v2` (`FEATURE_VIEW_VERSION`): generated and reviewed `real` profiles are read in full by every feature (D1), evidence is provenance only, and the real-person simulation-evidence gate on evolution is gone (evidence passed with a change is still recorded). `apply_override` is JR's audited override after first use (actor `JR`, a reason, season and tick 1–32, the same validation as any profile, revision +1, `last_changed_season` untouched so it sits outside the annual slot). `Identity.adopted` / `adopt` bring a legacy writer or GM under the core with its legacy ID and current values. `carry_over` (D3) copies sliders to a new role's profile, keeps the traits the catalogue allows that role, redraws nothing, and records a `from` link (a carried generated profile may hold 0–5 traits). `profile_as_of` rebuilds the profile at a `(season, tick)` from receipts. Store: `override`, `adopt_legacy`, `link_role_change`, `history` (reads across role links) and `read_as_of`; `change` now writes `kind='evolution'` and the event's `tick`, so it needs `2027_01_29` applied. No domain formula or hired player-agent role is added. `personality/store.py` persists canonical sliders/traits in the existing tables with catalogue/profile/alias/event sidecars from `db/migrations/2027_01_16_personality_core.sql`; insert-once initialization, verified aliases, revision/source-event deduplication, before/after receipts and legacy-edit detection use caller-owned transactions, savepoints and per-identity advisory locks. Read failures propagate instead of silently generating personalities. The migration has only been exercised in isolated rolled-back `madden_test` schemas, not applied to a franchise DB. `python -m personality [preview] --universe U --role player --birth-key K --season S [--origin generated|real|unknown] [--out PATH]` previews locally without a DB (no subcommand = preview, byte for byte); the subcommands `override`, `adopt (--writers | --gms | --role R --legacy-id ID)`, `link --from ROLE:KEY --to ROLE:KEY`, `history` and `as-of` use `DATABASE_URL` or `--dsn` (refusing `madden_2036` and `postgres`), print JSON, commit unless `--dry-run`, and exit 0 / 2 invalid / 3 not found / 4 conflict. Core API, feature boundaries, deferred ingestion/classification and parallel ownership are documented in `personality/README.md`. Existing legacy personas remain unchanged until JR runs `adopt` (not yet run on any franchise DB). Slider steps and trait changes are both supported: the validator and `chk_persona_sliders_budget` accept totals 24–36 (§3.3p), and a database without `2027_01_17_persona_slider_band.sql` rejects a step that leaves 30. Feature effects and numeric event rules remain in separately owned policies. Tests: `tests/test_personality_core.py`, `tests/test_personality_cli.py` (offline, fake connection) and opt-in `tests/test_personality_core_store.py` (explicit scratch DSN, isolated schemas rolled back; the extension cases have not yet been run against a database).

**Person lifecycle (docs/done/PERSONALITY_DRAFT_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-04, migration applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), nothing applied to a franchise):** `personality/lifecycle.py` is pure. A universe is `mu:<uuid>`, registered once against the save's `franchise.league_id` and the starting snapshot's SHA-256 (`snapshot_sha256` drops the reader's `read_at`/`source`/`source_modified`), with a start cutoff and a pgid lifetime (alias namespace `save-pgid:<lifetime>`, default `1`). A cutoff is `{season, phase, sequence}` with the fixed phase order `league_start, preseason, regular_season, playoffs, resign, free_agency, draft, post_draft`. Identity: a person's `source_person_id` UUID is allocated once and the core birth key is `source:<uuid>`; draft prospects adopt scouting's `prospect_uid` (class = save season + 1); starting-roster players (Signed/PracticeSquad/FreeAgent at the universe's start cutoff) derive `uuid5(LIFECYCLE_NS, universe|save-roster|season|pgid)`; later roster rows only resolve by alias (handoff), never allocate; imported classes use a durable `personality-class-sidecar-v1` (supplier ID → UUID, kept through reorders and renames; rows without a supplier ID stay pending). Classification receipts (`origin, source_ref, source_sha256, reviewer, reason, reviewed_at, effective_at, scope`) cover a scope `roster:<season>`, `class:<draft season>`, `staff:<role>` or `person:<role>:<uuid>`; disagreeing receipts quarantine, none means pending, `unknown` means pending (never an unknown profile, plan Q1), a `real` player receipt quarantines (every player is generated, D12). Staff need a supplied `source_person_id` (else pending), real coaches a reviewed `profile` (else pending), generated staff a `creation_receipt`. `validate_inventory` rejects a league mismatch, a cutoff before the start and, at the start cutoff, any snapshot but the registered one; it reports unsupported statuses, missing/duplicate pgids, alias collisions and cross-role people. `plan_lifecycle(inventory, existing, core_version, catalogue_version)` refuses a non-current core or catalogue and gives each person an action: `initialize` (with a restricted `proposed_profile` preview, no catalogue, and its hash), `bind` (new aliases), `retain`, `pending` or `quarantine` (alias conflict, legacy or unmanaged core collision, classification conflict). The inventory and the manifest carry the reviewed `classifications` themselves, not only their hash: the applied batch is the durable record of what classified whom, and consumers read the receipts there (the scouting directors' `staff:scout`, §2.18); `finalize_manifest` hashes them with everything else.
