JR edits a proposed profile in the manifest, then `finalize_manifest` (CLI `validate --rehash`) recomputes hashes and marks it `edited`; it must pass core validation. `validate_manifest`, `compare_manifests`, `proposed_profile` and `validate_handoff` (same pgid lifetime or a reviewed post-write import receipt verifies; a name match is a candidate only) complete the pure API. **Persistence (`personality/lifecycle_store.py`, §3.3p ledgers):** caller's cursor and transaction only, a savepoint per call, never commits or connects. `apply_lifecycle(cur, manifest, expected_hash=, review_receipt=)` re-validates the manifest, needs a review receipt (`reviewer, reviewed_manifest_sha256, decision='approve', reason, reviewed_at`) naming that hash, locks the universe, checks the schema fingerprint and the DB's `league_state.madden_league_id` stamp, and requires the current `export_state` to be what the preview saw (else stale: preview and review again); then registers the universe (immutable), initializes each `initialize` person through `store.ensure` (or, for a JR edit before first use, the same insert path with the edited, validated profile at revision 0), checks the stored profile hash against the reviewed one, writes lifecycle rows and bindings (core aliases for all but `draft:` board IDs), checks `bind`/`retain` people against their expected revision and profile hash, and records the batch. The same batch replays its receipt; a reused ID with another payload, or a reverted batch, is refused. `revert_batch(cur, batch_id, expected_after_hash=, review_receipt=)` works only while nothing used the batch (no core receipts, no role links, no extra aliases or bindings, unchanged profile hash and state), deletes batch-created bindings, core aliases, lifecycle people and profile rows (history, traits, core profile, sliders) and marks the batch `reverted`; catalogues and the universe stay. `resolve_person(cur, universe, role, namespace, external_id, cutoff=, feature=, current=False)` returns `{status, identity, view, profile_revision, profile_hash, reason, cutoff}` with status ready / missing (neutral view) / unknown (neutral) / ambiguous (core alias disagrees) / future / quarantined; a ready person without a core profile raises (corrupt); a cutoff before a recorded change reads through `store.read_as_of`, and a change inside the cutoff's own season raises `HistoricalResolutionError` unless `current=True`. `require_ready(cur, references, cutoff=, feature=, mode='observe'|'enforce')` reports, or raises `NotReadyError` (exit 3) for unresolved required references; it never activates an effect. Creator hooks: `initialize_person` (one verified generated/real person with a durable creator receipt; replays bind new aliases, a different classification conflicts; needs a registered universe), `bind_person`, `close_binding`, `archive_person` (archive, never delete); `available(cur)` says whether the migration is applied. Tests run on SQLite (`tests/test_personality_lifecycle_store.py`); the PostgreSQL scratch case has not been run (no PostgreSQL in the build environment). **Ingestion and staff hooks:** `pipeline/load_save.load_personality` runs last in `load_snapshot` (same transaction). Without a context it observes (`report["personality"]["pending"]`: loaded roster and class pgids with no binding; nothing written). With `--personality-manifest/--personality-review` it requires the manifest's snapshot hash to equal this snapshot's, applies it, then binds `db-player` for every loaded player whose `save-pgid` is bound (the players row was matched on `madden_pgid`, so a drafted rookie or an undrafted signing keeps his prospect identity with no pick or team needed), the board rows this load wrote (`draft:<class>:<capture>`), unique `scout:<class>` keys, and each manifest `handoffs` entry `validate_handoff` verifies (a reviewed post-write import receipt; a name match stays pending); any lifecycle conflict is a `LoadError` that aborts the load. A kept board is not mapped. `pipeline/load_capture.class_personality` does the same for an imported class from a reviewed `personality-class-entry-v1` bundle (`universe_id`, `cutoff`, sidecar, `class:<draft season>` generated receipt; JR's review names its canonical hash): mapped rows are initialized once through `initialize_person` and bound to their board row (rename/reorder keeps the person), unmapped rows stay pending. Scouting only observes (§2.18). Staff: §2.19. Lifecycle availability is not an effect: no personality changes any loader, scouting, hiring or draw outcome.

**Real-coach profiles (docs/done/REAL_COACH_PROFILES_PLAN.md; all waves built 2026-11-05, re-seated to the 2026 staffs 2026-11-06):** one reviewed file per 2026 HC/OC/DC in `newsroom/config/coach_personas/<TEAM>_<ROLE>.json` (`coach-profile-v1`: `key` `coach:<TEAM>:<ROLE>`, `name`, `role`, `team`, `seed_ref` {table, team, role, name}, six `sliders` with `slider_evidence`, 3–5 `traits` with `trait_evidence`, 6–10 `views` `{text, when}`, 2–5 `signatures` (strings or `{text, detect}`), `want`, `fear`, `voice`, `ties`, `evidence` [{id, url, publisher, published, accessed, summary, confidence}], `review` {status draft|approved|edited|rejected, reviewer, reviewed_at, notes}). Each is a fictional character inspired by the real coach (D13). `personality/coach_profiles.py` (pure apart from reading files; `seed_index` parses `db/seed_clean_db.py` with `ast`, so psycopg is never imported) validates: file name/key/team/role agree and `seed_ref` matches one seed row with the same name; sliders 0–10 totalling 24–36, each non-5 slider citing evidence; traits coach-eligible, no conflicts, at most two per category, each cited (then `core.initialize` as the final check); view tags from `newsroom.personas.ALL_TAGS`; evidence `published` ≤ `SOURCE_CUTOFF` 2026-09-08 (the eve of the 2026 season) with an http(s) URL and publisher, confidence low/medium/high, a low source never behind a slider or trait; no free-text field shares more than `MAX_QUOTE_WORDS` 15 consecutive words with a source summary; ties to `coach` (by `seed_ref`), `player` or `gm` (`{name, team_2026}`) only, never reporters, each cited; a reviewed file names reviewer and date. Only `approved`/`edited` files leave the module: `core_initial_values` (core evidence `slider:<s>`/`trait:<t>`: first cited URL and date, lowest cited confidence, reviewer, joined summaries, `features: ['all']`), `lifecycle_entries` (role `coach`, origin `real`, `birth_key` `curated-coach:<TEAM>:<ROLE>:2026`, alias `db-coach` or `db-coordinator` with the `seed_ref`, initial values, review receipt with the content SHA-256 of the file's canonical JSON; the lifecycle plan applies them), `persona_for(doc, view)` (the `render_persona` shape; a stored core view's sliders/traits replace the file's) and `tie_events(doc, resolve)` (one validated `relationships-v1` `meaningful_interaction` per resolved tie: `basis reviewed_evidence`, season 2026 tick 1, private, payload `prehistory: true`, `significance meaningful`, `opportunity_ref` `coach-profile:<key>:tie:<n>`, `source_event_id` `mu:coach-tie:<key>:<n>`; unresolved ties, including a subject not in the league, come back with a reason and are dropped, Q3). Review: `tools/coach_profile_review.py` (§1.2). Profiles change voice and context only; no effect until each owning plan activates one. Status: the schema, module, template and tool are built; `CAR_HC.json` (Dave Canales) is the spike, approved by JR on 2026-11-04 with one edit (status `edited`); the others follow its method (5–8 sources, sliders at 5 without evidence, 3–4 traits) and are drafts (2026-11-05) until JR reviews them per batch. On 2026-11-06 the seed moved from the 2024 to the 2026 staffs: 31 profiles kept their seat, 32 moved with their coach (re-keyed, back to draft, "moved seat 2026; re-research for 2026 sources"), 33 whose coach no longer holds an HC/OC/DC seat were deleted, and the 33 new seats were then researched and the 32 moved files refreshed with 2026 sources (all 96 validate, 95 drafts); coach ties were re-pointed by person and ties to departed coaches dropped; only reviewed files reach the lifecycle manifest. The review page cites sources by ID on each claim and summarises each source once, in its Sources table. JR approved all 96 on 2026-11-07; the same day every file was converted to `coach-profile-v2` (§7.11 Inferred sliders and refreshing focus: motivation, current focus with subjects, inferred sliders; 431 inferred sliders across the 128 coach and owner files, 78 focus slots naming 44 subjects) and JR re-approved them in that form (all 96 files `approved` as of 2026-11-07).

**Owner profiles (docs/done/OWNERS_SCOUTS_VOTERS_PLAN.md U1, built 2026-11-06; research U2–U3):** `personality/owner_profiles.py` holds `OWNERS_DATA` (32 rows: team, owner as of the eve of the 2026 season, first season as controlling owner; Green Bay's row is the team president, the Packers being publicly owned) and validates `owner-profile-v1` files in `newsroom/config/owner_personas/<TEAM>.json`: the coach schema and rules (evidence cutoff 2026-09-08, confidence, quote check, sliders, views, signatures, review) with role `OWNER`, key `owner:<TEAM>`, `seed_ref` {table `OWNERS_DATA`, team, name}, owner-eligible traits, and ties to a coach seat, a GM or a player. `lifecycle_entries` give role `owner`, `birth_key` `curated-owner:<TEAM>:2026`, alias `db-owner` / `team_owners`; `tie_events` resolve the owner as `{kind: owner, seed_ref}` (`source_kind` `owner_profile`, `mu:owner-tie:<key>:<n>`); `core_initial_values` and `persona_for` are the coach functions. Catalogue: owner traits `MEDDLER`✕`HANDS_OFF`, `DEEP_POCKETS`✕`BUDGET_CONSCIOUS` (category `work`) and `HEADLINE_HUNTER`✕`PATIENT_BUILDER` (`ambition`), scout traits `TRAITS_CHASER`, `TAPE_GRINDER`, `CHARACTER_HAWK`, `FLOOR_SEEKER`✕`CEILING_GAMBLER` (`football_mind`), each with `group` `ownership`/`scouting`, role weight only for its role and empty effects; the ownership pairs sit in two existing categories so an owner can hold one trait from each pair within the core's two-per-category rule (the plan's separate Ownership category would have needed core and catalogue-validator changes). Fourteen existing traits gained small owner weights (`LOYAL`, `GRUDGE_HOLDER`, `PEACEMAKER`, `LEGACY_BUILDER`, `RING_CHASER`, `HOMETOWN_GUY`, `SPOTLIGHT_SEEKER`, `QUOTABLE`, `GUARDED`, `MEASURED`, `ANALYTICS_BELIEVER`, `OLD_SCHOOL`, `FAMILY_MAN`, `HISTORIAN`) so owners have 3–5 traits; no other role's seeded draw changes. Review: `tools.coach_profile_review --kind owner`. Status: all 32 files written 2026-11-06 (U2 AFC, U3 NFC) as drafts from 2–3 dated web sources each, sliders mostly at 5, three traits each (one per ownership pair where the evidence allowed); open review notes ask JR to confirm the Tampa Bay (Joel Glazer) and Seattle (Neeru Khosla; Vinod is the public voice) persona choice, and Green Bay's row is the team president. Only reviewed files reach the lifecycle manifest. JR approved all 32 on 2026-11-07, converted the same day to `owner-profile-v2` (motivation without confidence tags, current focus, inferred sliders) and re-approved in that form (all 32 files `approved`). The owner wiring (U5, §2.19) reads them through `engines/owner_context.owner_views`. Scouting directors are generated (not reviewed): one per team through the lifecycle creator hook, kept across seasons (`engines/scout_directors.py`, §2.18, §3.3p).

**Development and coaching (docs/done/PERSONALITY_DEVELOPMENT_COACHING_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-06, off by default, no migration, no active preset):** pure `engines/personality_development.py` (players/mentors read `feature_view(..., 'development')`, generated profiles in full) and `engines/personality_coaching.py` (coaches read `'coaching'`; reviewed real-coach profiles in full under views-v2), the read-only adapter `engines/personality_development_inputs.py` (missing = neutral, storage errors propagate, reads never seed; verified pipeline alias binding and per-week staff exposure records remain prerequisites), default-off progression receipt hooks (§2.21), the depth-chart `score_adjustments` seam (§2.17c) and `tools/personality_development_demo.py`. Activation gates G3–G5 stay with JR: reviewed candidate configs from paired multi-season reports, binding/schema readiness and a shadow period, then separate go-aheads for learning and for opportunities. Development evolution candidates (source `DEVELOPMENT` for `personality.evolution_run.run_season(external=...)`) are a later dependency; nothing sends any yet. Hiring and owner patience stay with the carousel/hot-seat owners (owners plan).

**Trade requests (docs/done/PERSONALITY_TRADE_REQUESTS_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-06, no live caller, migration `2027_01_25` applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), no production policy):** a request records that a player wants a move after verified sustained dissatisfaction. It is not trade execution, a price discount or a player veto, and it writes no profile, mood, trust or relationship fact (reference: `docs/reference/PLAYER_TRADE_REQUESTS.md`).
- **Inputs:** incidents (`LOST_ROLE`/`BROKEN_PROMISE`/`TREATMENT`, states OPEN/REPAIRED/DISPUTED/UNKNOWN) come from the relationships plan's shared outputs through `incidents_from_shared`: a sustained-role `frustrated` reaction (observations = its unsatisfied role-window run), an unresolved material breach (observations = contiguous known role windows since), and prior causes that stopped being open → REPAIRED (accepted repairs or trailing satisfied windows). A reaction result in `off` mode gives none. The view is `feature_view(profile, 'trade_requests')`; missing → neutral baseline; nothing initializes a profile. Clock ordinal = `season * 1000 + tick`. Authority from the franchise registry's `user_teams` (`control_context`), never Madden's ALLUSER flag; unknown blocks automated responses; suggestions off suppresses GM advice, not the factual request.
- **Decision:** four eligible lost-role observations, or two after a broken promise/material treatment, on the current team (no severe-incident shortcut); incomplete assessments and closed windows defer without using the season. One draw per (universe, persona, season): sha256 of `['trade-request-v1', universe, persona, season]`, first 8 bytes / 2^64; NO_REQUEST uses it; no reroll by retry, new incident, team, checkpoint name or policy change; an active request carries over seasons. Trait rule `trait-v1` (offline proposal): DIVA/GRUDGE_HOLDER higher, PEACEMAKER lower, both baseline, never stacked. No production odds; `offline-illustration-v1` (.05/.10/.15) is refused in ENABLED mode. Modes DISABLED (no effect, no slot) / SHADOW (hypothetical, persists nowhere) / ENABLED.
- **Lifecycle:** ACTIVE → WITHDRAWN (reconciled after two repaired observations with repair IDs and no other open cause, or a verified player withdrawal / JR correction), RESOLVED_TRADE (executed trade only), CLOSED_EMPLOYMENT (verified departure; unknown defers) or VOIDED_CORRECTION; team response separate (refusal is not withdrawal); terminal never reopens; revision and checkpoint order checked. Private until a verified `DISCLOSE`; public facts stay dated (`current` false) until disclosed again. Handoffs (functions only): `contract_request_context` (§2.17b) and `gm_request_signal` (§2.17). Store §3.3v; preview `tools/player_trade_request_preview.py`. Scheduling, live context building and the GM search signal are the activation plan's U3; contract willingness stays with the contract policy.

**Retirement decisions (docs/done/PERSONALITY_RETIREMENT_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-06, no live caller, migration `2027_01_26` applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), no approved policy):** a neutral annual baseline first, then separately reviewed personality modifiers (§2.17f). The policy reads only `feature_view(profile, 'retirement')` (missing → neutral; a corrupt profile blocks effects-enabled finalization only) and never mutates profiles; COASTING has no numeric effect and LEGACY_BUILDER cannot make a player immortal (bounded aggregate, sigmoid). Recording a retirement is not proof Mu controls the decision or its save write: authority is inventoried in `docs/reference/RETIREMENT_AUTHORITY.md`, and activation (G4–G6) is separate from profile availability.

**Inferred sliders and refreshing focus (docs/done/INFERRED_SLIDERS_AND_FOCUS_PLAN.md; approved by JR 2026-11-07, built 2026-11-07 (waves 1–3); off by default, migration `2027_02_03` applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09), all 128 profiles converted to v2 and awaiting JR's re-review):**
- **Inferred sliders (`personality/slider_inference.py`, pure; `newsroom/config/slider_leans.json`):** a coach or owner slider at 5 with no `slider_evidence` is a no-evidence slider. Its inferred value is `clamp(5 + lean + jitter, 2, 8)`: `lean` = the person's traits' leans summed and capped at ±`LEAN_CAP = 2` (each trait leans at most two sliders by −2..+2; e.g. ANALYTICS_BELIEVER openness +2, LOYAL warmth +2, PATIENT_BUILDER temperament −2, CAR_GUY none), `jitter` = −1 below 0.25, +1 at or above 0.75, else 0 of the draw sha256(json `['slider-inference-v1', key, slider]`) first 8 bytes / 2^64. Band balancing: while the effective total is above 36 (below 24), the unlocked inferred value above (below) 5 farthest from 5 moves one step toward 5 (ties in SLIDERS order); evidenced and JR-locked values never move. Functions: `load_leans`, `neutral_sliders`, `inference_draw`, `infer_sliders(doc, leans=None, *, locked=None)` → `{version, values, basis {traits, lean, jitter, balanced}}`, `check_inference` (values cover exactly the no-evidence sliders, unlocked values equal a fresh inference, locked ones are no-evidence sliders, effective total 24–36), `effective_sliders`, `inferred_evidence(doc, s)` (unlocked: `{source 'inferred:slider-inference-v1', date reviewed_at, confidence 'low', reviewer, reason 'inferred from <traits>; no direct evidence', features ['voice']}`, which passes core validation and changes no feature read; locked: `{source 'jr-set:<reviewed_at>', confidence 'high', reviewer 'JR', features ['all']}`), `is_inferred`. Spike over the 128 profiles (2026-11-07): 431 sliders inferred (values 2:4, 3:20, 4:89, 5:179, 6:92, 7:36, 8:11), 71 reach 3 or 7 and so show in the voice, 21 profiles balanced, none outside 24–36, distinct slider vectors 93 → 119; owner `patience` line scale moves at most 0.03.
- **Focus model (`personality/focus.py`, pure; `newsroom/config/focus_templates.json`):** `FOCUS_RULES_VERSION = 'focus-v1'`. `validate_file_focus(doc)`: `motivation.want`/`fear` nonempty, at most `MAX_MOTIVE_WORDS = 14` words, naming no focus subject or tie target (full name or surname); `focus.want`/`fear` null or `{text (1–14 words), subjects (0–2: `{kind player|gm, name, team_2026}` or `{kind coach, seed_ref}`, not the holder), until_season (null or ≥ 2026)}`. `stale_causes(row, facts, season)`: subject status `retired` → SUBJECT_RETIRED, `elsewhere` → SUBJECT_LEFT_TEAM, `not_in_seat` → SUBJECT_LEFT_ROLE, `gone` → SUBJECT_LEFT_LEAGUE, no binding → SUBJECT_UNRESOLVED; holder's team or seat differs from the row's anchor → HOLDER_MOVED; `until_season < season` → EXPIRED; `unknown` or a None fact is never stale. `load_templates` (48 templates: per seat HC/OC/DC/OWNER and slot, one per direction CONTEND/RETOOL/REBUILD, hot-seat or playoff ones, people-led ones and a `GENERIC_<SEAT>_<SLOT>` with no `when` or `needs`; placeholders `{qb1}`, `{young_star}`, `{top_defender}`, `{top_weapon}`, `{head_coach}`, `{gm}`, `{team_name}`; filled text ≤ 14 words). `draft_focus(...)`: eligible = seat and slot match, every `when` key equals the fact (a None fact fails), every `needs` person present; a template whose `traits_any` meets the traits counts twice; pick by `focus_draw` (sha256 of `['focus-v1', universe, persona, season, slot]`) over the eligible list sorted by id → `{text, subjects (with bindings), template_id, anchor {team, seat}}`. `change_note(old_row, new, causes, season)`, e.g. `2031: with Lamar Jackson retired, he now wants a title with Tyler Shough in his prime.` (≤ 30 words).
- **Focus store:** `persona_focus` / `persona_focus_runs` (§3.3p), `personality/focus_store.py`.
- **Profile schema v2 (`coach-profile-v2` / `owner-profile-v2`; v1 still validates and converts):** top-level `want`/`fear` are replaced by `motivation` {want, fear} and `focus` {want, fear} (each null or `{text, subjects, until_season}`), plus `slider_inference` {version, values, locked} covering exactly the no-evidence sliders. `validate_profile_file` checks the focus rules (`focus.validate_file_focus`), `check_inference` (unlocked values equal a fresh inference; JR's `locked` values any 0–10) and, for v2, the effective total in 24–36 instead of the file total; the quote check covers motivation and focus text. `core_initial_values` returns `effective_sliders` with an `inferred:` (or `jr-set:`) evidence entry per inferred slider, so the values reach the core only through the reviewed lifecycle apply. `persona_for(doc, view=None, change_notes=None, focus=None)`: v2 gives motivation as `want`/`fear` and the file focus (or the stored rows from `focus_store.read_focus`) as `focus_want`/`focus_fear`. Helpers `is_v2`, `with_inference(doc)` (fill the block, keeping JR's locks) and `convert_v2(doc, version, today=)` (mechanical: motivation from want/fear, null focus, inferred sliders; a reviewed file goes back to `draft` with the note `converted to v2 on <date>: check motivation, focus and inferred sliders`). The review tool (§1.2) gains `infer` and `convert-v2`; `report` shows a slider **Source** column (`evidence (E1, E2)`, `inferred (LOYAL +2, seed −1)`, `, balanced`, `set by JR`) and, for v2, **Motivation** and **Current focus** sections (subjects and when the focus refreshes); `apply-review` can edit `slider_inference`, `motivation` and `focus`. The `_TEMPLATE.json` files are v2.
- **Refresh run (`personality/focus_facts.py`, `personality/focus_run.py`; switchboard feature `focus_refresh` after `evolution`; watcher step §6.0b):** `focus_facts.facts(cur, universe_id, season, *, bindings=None)` (read-only): each core coach's seat and team from his db-coach / db-coordinator alias and the tenures (the tenure covering season + 1 first, else an open one covering the season; none → seat and team None), each owner's team from his birth key `curated-owner:<TEAM>:2026`; team direction (`gm_team_seasons`), playoffs and Super Bowl (`games`), hot seat (`coach_hot_seat` / `coordinator_hot_seat`: not fired and score at or above HOT_SEAT_PRESSURE × firing line); people from the active roster and latest `player_attributes.overall_rating` (qb1, young_star age ≤ 25, top_defender, top_weapon WR/TE/RB) plus head_coach (not for the HC himself) and gm, each with a binding (`db-player`, `db-coach`, `db-gm`); and each active row's subject status (player on the holder's team `with_team`, another team `elsewhere`, a `player_retirements` row `retired`, no roster row `gone`; a coach or GM still in the seat the subject names `with_team`, else `not_in_seat`). A missing table leaves its facts None and is listed in `missing`. `focus_run.seed` writes seq-0 rows for each reviewed v2 file's non-null focus slots (person found by the HC's `coaches.coach_name` / the coordinator's 2026 tenure → core alias, or the owner's birth key; subjects resolved on the 2026 rosters, unresolved ones kept with `binding: null`), once per person and slot. `run_season(cur, universe_id, season, *, dry_run=False, docs=None, templates=None)`: seed, read the facts, then per active row: no cause → keep; a stale `profile`/`template` row → `draft_focus` and `supersede` (`source 'template'`, `stale_causes`, `reason` = the change note); a stale `jr` row → `jr_stale`, never replaced; an empty slot gets a draft only when the holder's team or seat differs from his profile's. `noop` when an APPLIED run has the same input hash (sha256 of the facts and active rows); `dry_run` writes nothing. Report `{status, counts {people, rows, kept, replaced | would_replace, jr_stale, by_cause, missing_sources}, changes, jr_stale, unresolved}`; `render_report` (markdown, `verify_output/personality_focus/focus_<universe>_<season>.md`), `stored_report`, `record_failure`. `set_focus` (a `jr` row, actor `JR`, superseding the active one; text ≤ 14 words, ≤ 2 bound subjects) and `revert(cur, focus_id, reason)` (the active row → `reverted`, a new `jr` row copying the row it superseded, reason `revert:<focus_id>: <reason>`; a seq-0 row cannot be reverted). CLI in §1.2. Owner holders resolve once the lifecycle apply has written owner profiles (`curated-owner:` birth keys).

**Personality evolution (docs/done/PERSONALITY_EVOLUTION_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-06, off by default, migration `2027_01_30` applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09)):** big simulated events slowly change players and coaches (writers and GMs keep their authored personalities, D2), at most one change per person per season, by fixed rules and a seeded draw.
- **Rules (`personality/evolution_rules.py`, `EVOLUTION_RULES_VERSION = 'evolution-v1'`, pure):** `Rule {rule_id, roles, when(facts), change(facts), chance, priority, note, facts}`; a fact that is None (source missing) never fires a rule, and no rule reads money or contracts. `TITLE_LEGACY` (player/coach; won the Super Bowl, has RING_CHASER, `seasons_in_league` >= 4; RING_CHASER -> LEGACY_BUILDER; 0.35, priority 1), `FIRED_TEMPER` (coach fired; temperament +1; 0.50, 1), `MENTOR_RETIRES` (player; his mentor retired, age >= 27, no MENTOR/LONER; add MENTOR; 0.25, 2), `VETERAN_LEADER` (player; age >= 31, >= 5 seasons on his team, no MENTOR/LONER; add MENTOR; 0.10, 4), `BENCHED_TEMPER` (player; >= 6 eligible unsatisfied role weeks; temperament +1; 0.30, 2), `CUT_GRUDGE` (player; released then signed elsewhere, no PEACEMAKER; add GRUDGE_HOLDER; 0.15, 3), `MVP_CONFIDENCE` (player; MVP, OPOY, DPOY or First Team All-Pro; confidence +1; 0.40, 2), `LONG_INJURY_DRIVE` (player; >= 8 weeks out; drive +1; 0.20, 3), `PROMOTED_CONFIDENCE` (coach; coordinator promoted to HC; confidence +1; 0.40, 2), `LOSING_OPENNESS` (coach; two losing seasons in a row and not fired; openness +1; 0.25, 3), `COY_CONFIDENCE` (coach; COTY; confidence +1; 0.40, 2). Chances are review-only starting points (plan §8 Q1); tuning means a new rules version. Each rule's `note` template is filled from the facts (`fill_note`).
- **Draw and arbiter (`personality/evolution.py`, pure):** `draw(universe, persona, season, rule_id)` = first 8 bytes of sha256(json `['evolution-v1', universe, persona, season, rule]`) / 2^64. `rule_candidates(facts)` gives every firing rule as a candidate (`eligible` below its chance, else `drawn_out`), citing the source IDs of the facts the rule reads. External candidates (other features' review results, `{source RELATIONSHIPS|DEVELOPMENT|OTHER, persona_type, persona_id, status, candidate, priority?}`) join only when `ready`, at `EXTERNAL_PRIORITY = 0` unless they carry a priority. `arbitrate(candidates, external, *, season, profiles=None)` per person: with profiles, a change core validation would refuse is `blocked` with the reason (sixth trait, conflict, slider at 0/10, total outside 24-36, `annual_slot_used`, `no_profile`), never forced; the lowest priority wins, ties to the lowest draw (externals 0), then rule_id; the rest are `superseded`. `change_event(chosen, profile, season)` = `{event_id 'evo:<universe>:<persona>:<season>', source_event_id (first cited ID), season, tick 24, expected_revision, rule_version, reason (the filled note), kind, slider/step | remove/add}`, which `core.apply_change` accepts. `change_notes(history, *, as_of, limit=MAX_CHANGE_NOTES=2)`: newest first from `store.history` evolution receipts' `reason` (and JR overrides whose reason starts `note:`), prefixed `<season>: ` when the note doesn't name its season.
- **Season facts (`personality/evolution_facts.py`, read-only):** `season_facts(cur, universe_id, season) -> {persona_id: facts}` for the universe's core players and coaches with a `db-player`, `db-coach` or `db-coordinator` alias: `{universe_id, season, persona_id, role, birth_key, profile_view, age, seasons_in_league, tenure_seasons_on_team, team_id, position_group, won_super_bowl, made_playoffs, losing_seasons_in_row, awards, unsatisfied_role_weeks, released_by_team, signed_elsewhere_after_release, injury_weeks_out, mentor_retired, coach_fired, coach_promoted_to_hc, coach_kept_on_hot_seat, source_event_ids {fact: [ids]}, missing {table: reason}}`. Sources: `player_seasons`, `team_seasons`, playoff `games`, `awards`, coach/coordinator tenures and hot seats, `staff_moves`, `player_retirements`, `player_attributes` (Awareness) and the relationship ledger's active events; a missing table leaves its facts None. Rows are cited as `<table>:<key>` (awards `mu:award:<id>`, staff moves `mu:staff:<id>`), events by source_event_id. Relationship events count inside the window (season-1 tick 24, season tick 24]; `mentor_retired` is `find_mentor` over last season's roster and Awareness plus that mentor's `player_retirements` row for last season; `coach_promoted_to_hc` is a `staff_moves` HC HIRED row from the previous hiring cycle with from_role OC/DC; coaches' `seasons_in_league` counts franchise tenure seasons only.
- **Run, report, revert (`personality/evolution_run.py`):** `run_season(cur, universe_id, season, *, dry_run=False, external=())` reads the facts, returns `noop` when an APPLIED run has the same input hash, otherwise arbitrates rule and `ready` external candidates over the stored profiles, submits each chosen change through `store.change` (a refusal marks it `blocked`), records every candidate and the run, and returns the report (`status`, `counts` {people, candidates, drawn_out, blocked, superseded, applied | would_apply, by_rule, missing_sources}, `candidates`); `dry_run` writes nothing. `render_report` is deterministic markdown; `report_path` = `verify_output/personality_evolution/evolution_<universe>_<season>.md`; `record_failure` writes a FAILED run unless the season already has an APPLIED one. `revert(cur, candidate_id, reason)` is a JR `store.override` back to the before-state (`override_id 'revert:<candidate>'`, `expected_revision` = the receipt's after revision, so it refuses once the profile changed again; `reverts` names the receipt) and marks the candidate `reverted`; the evolution receipt stays. `change_notes_for(cur, identity, as_of)` is `change_notes` over `store.history` without reverted changes. CLI in §1.2. Other features send candidates through `external` (the relationships plan's `validate_evolution_candidate` result plus `source`, `persona_type`, `persona_id`). Nothing sends `RELATIONSHIPS` candidates yet. **Development candidates (`personality/evolution_development.py`, rule set `development-evolution-v1`, review-only):** `season_receipts(cur, season)` reads the earned season's APPLIED `progression_events` carrying the `personality_development_v1` block; `candidates(receipts, people, *, universe_id, season, receipt_mode)` (pure) gives `SUSTAINED_PREPARATION`: a player persona carrying COASTING with at least `MIN_CHECKPOINTS = 3` receipts (of the given mode, `enabled` or `shadow`) on which his own preparation channels (drive, film, technical preparation, coasting) were net positive and an effect resulted (`attributed_effect` / `shadow_effect`) → `{kind trait, remove COASTING}`, source `DEVELOPMENT`, status `ready` (the rule set is the review, like the evolution rules; `review_status approved`, reviewer `rule:development-evolution-v1`, `feature_scope ['development_learning']`), `priority 3` (among the rules, not `EXTERNAL_PRIORITY`), citing the receipts' event_ids (event_id `dev:<universe>:<persona>:<season>:SUSTAINED_PREPARATION`). `development_mode(evolution_mode, development_mode)` gates it: either off → none; development active → `enabled` receipts; development shadow → `shadow` receipts only while evolution is shadow (a dry run), never against an applying evolution. `external_candidates(cur, universe, season, *, receipt_mode)` reads nothing when the gate is None. JR accepted this COASTING rule as-is for now (2026-11-07: 3 positive-preparation receipts, priority 3); he will tune it after experimenting with a few seasons.
- **Prompts and watcher:** `render_persona` shows a persona's optional `change_notes` list (first `MAX_CHANGE_NOTES = 2`, newest first) under the voice as HOW YOU HAVE CHANGED LATELY; `coach_profiles.persona_for(doc, view=None, change_notes=None, focus=None, lineage=None)` passes notes through, and a non-empty `lineage` (a `coaching_trees.lineage_line`) as `lineage`, which `render_persona` prints right after the voice as `YOUR COACHING LINEAGE (a fact about you): ...`. Nothing fetches notes for a prompt yet (players and coaches don't write); callers use `change_notes_for`. The OFFSEASON_START watcher step is §6.0b. JR's gate: a `season --dry-run` report, then the switchboard's `evolution` feature to shadow/active.

**Feature switchboard (`personality/features.py`, docs/done/PERSONALITY_ACTIVATION_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-06, every feature off by default, migration `2027_01_31` applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09)):** one switchboard per franchise, keyed by league id (a lifecycle universe id `mu:<uuid>` resolves through `persona_lifecycle_universes`). `FEATURES` is the D2 go-live order: producers, relationships, profiles, evolution, contracts_ambition, contracts_relationships, development_learning, trade_requests, retirement, development_opportunity, coach_loop, player_loop, owner_patience, owner_hiring, coaching_tree_hiring (`engines.coaching_tree_hiring`, no migration), owner_spending, owner_meddling, scout_directors, media_voters. `mode`/`config`/`snapshot` read `off` for a missing row, a missing table or an unknown league; `snapshot` is the frozen per-ingest view (`snapshot_mode(snap, feature)`). `set_mode(..., version, config, review_ref, now={season, tick}, force_reason=None)`: going `off` is always allowed; `shadow` (and `active`) need the feature's code installed (`REQUIREMENTS`: its module found and its migration file present, so the owner/scout/voter features wait for the owners plan's `2027_02_02` migration); `active` needs every earlier feature active (D2; `profiles` also counts once a lifecycle batch is `applied` for the league's universe) and either a shadow of the same version since tick 24 of the previous season or earlier (D3, one full simulated season) or an imported clearance for that feature and version (D4); `force_reason` skips D2/D3 and is recorded; staying in shadow keeps the shadow start, a new version restarts it; every change writes `personality_feature_mode_changes`. Clearances: `export_clearance` (tuning franchise; needs the full shadow season and a readable report, whose sha256 it records with the tuned config and `current_database()`), `import_clearance` (real franchise; rechecks the season and the report hash, refuses a tampered report or a different clearance for the same version, replays an identical one), `activate_cleared` (sets each cleared feature active in order with its clearance's version and config, stops at the first feature neither active nor cleared). `producers` and `relationships` in shadow mean observe only. The contract store's `read_contract_activation` now reads `contracts_ambition`/`contracts_relationships` from here (still `off`). `relationship_policy(feature_config)` turns the `relationships` feature into the relationships plan's policy (off None, shadow `observe`, active `enabled` with the config's reviewed sections) for `server/personality_api.py`; `newsroom/award_ballots.feature_mode` reads `media_voters`; the watcher's evolution step reads `development_learning` for development candidates. CLI in §1.2; tables in §3.3p.

**Coach and player agent loops (docs/done/COACH_PLAYER_AGENT_LOOPS_PLAN.md; U1–U2 built 2026-11-06, U3a wiring and U3b social statements built 2026-11-09, no live caller, migration `2027_02_01` applied to madden_test (2026-11-07) and madden_mu2026 (2026-11-09); the coach-promise watcher is built 2026-11-09, off by default):** CPU coaches and players choose among options their owning engines already allow; acceptance, valuation, legality and the chart algorithm never change.
- **Loop pattern (`engines/agent_loops/base.py`):** `Option {key, action, detail, label}` (the label is all the model sees). `decide(cur, *, league_id, season, tick, kind, subject, options, persona, weights, facts, seen, llm, marquee=False, ...)` returns the stored row when `(league_id, season, tick, kind, subject_key)` is already decided (record, don't replay; no model call); otherwise it always runs `policy_choice` (a weighted draw seeded `random.Random("loop:{season}:{tick}:{kind}:{subject}")`), then asks the model only when `seen` (JR's threads, a presser answer, a leak) or `marquee` while the league week has fewer than `MARQUEE_PER_WEEK = 4` model-backed `CHART`/`PROMISE`/`CONTRACT` decisions. `model_choice` makes one `gm_llm.call` (JSON `{choice, message}`): a key outside the options falls back to the policy key as `MODEL_REJECTED` (text dropped), no answer leaves `POLICY`, and a `MODEL` choice's text is kept only if `grounded(text, facts)` (every figure, all-caps slot and mid-sentence capitalized name appears in the facts). `make_loop_llm()` = `gm_llm.make_llm('agent_loop')`. `MemoryStore` (tests, previews) and `SqlStore(cur)` (§3.3p) share `get/put/find/count_model`.
- **Coach loop (`engines/agent_loops/coach.py`, estimates):** `chart_options(neutral_chart, scored_candidates, close_window)` = `NEUTRAL` plus up to `CHART_VARIANTS = 3` one-swap variants (a base-slot starter and the first man behind him, both healthy and eligible, neutral scores within `close_window`, the promoted man starting at no other base slot), closest first; `chart_weights` = NEUTRAL 1.0, variants 0.15 + 0.5 x the gap in the development plan's `opportunity_adjustments` (YOUTH_DEVELOPER, or team vision VETERANS for a veteran lean), plus `0.6 x clamp(1 + 0.1 (drive - 5) + 0.1 (warmth - 5), 0, 2)` for options that keep an open promise the neutral chart doesn't. A starting-QB call or a benched `incumbent` is marquee. `choose_chart` (subject `team:<id>:chart`) returns the chart and the decision. Promises: `promise_options` gives `NONE`/`PROMISE {slot, depth 1, review_tick = tick + 3}` only after `PROMISE_MIN_UNHAPPY_WEEKS = 2` trailing unsatisfied role weeks, no open promise and a review by week 23; `p_promise = clamp(0.25 + 0.05 (warmth - 5) + 0.1 PLAYERS_COACH - 0.1 DISCIPLINARIAN, 0.05, 0.6)`; `decide_promise` returns a `promise_made` envelope (subject the player, target/actor the coach, criterion `{type: depth_chart_slot, slot, max_depth}`, due at the review tick, `source_kind 'agent_loop'`) when the caller passes resolved PersonRefs (`resolve_person` via `personality.store.resolve_alias`). `review_promises(cur, season, tick, *, league_id, chart_depth, injured)` judges due promises from the MADDEN chart: kept/broken, or, if he is injured or no chart was read, a `DEFER` review and one re-review a week later that resolves `unknown` if still so, so each promise gets exactly one `promise_resolved`. `append_events` appends through `personality.relationship_store`.
- **Player loop (`engines/agent_loops/player.py`, estimates):** `contract_options(offer, player, team, market, bar, *, accepts, leak_ok=False)`: when the engine accepts, `ACCEPT` plus the clearing counters; otherwise the counters and `REJECT`, plus `LEAK_AND_COUNTER` (the ASK counter and a statement) when `leak_ok` and ASK exists. That statement is public in an active season and private in shadow, which also spends no model call on it. Counters are `COUNTER_MIN` / `COUNTER_ASK` / `COUNTER_HARD` from `free_agency_engine.counter_options(k=3)`, only those that exist. `contract_weights`: push = clamp(0.5 MONEY_FIRST + 0.08 (confidence − 5) − 0.6 attachment, −1, 1); ACCEPT 1.0 + 0.5 attachment − 0.6 max(push, 0), MIN 0.8 + 0.4 max(−push, 0), ASK 0.5 + 0.5 push, HARD 0.15 + 0.6 push, REJECT 0.1, leak 0.1 (1 + SPOTLIGHT_SEEKER + 0.8 QUOTABLE) × 0.3 if GUARDED, floor 0.01. `respond_contract(cur, player_view, offer, ctx, *, llm, seen)` (subject `player:<id>:offer:<offer_id>`; marquee when the ask's AAV ≥ `ctx['marquee_floor']`, the season's 50th-highest from `marquee_floor`) returns `{decision, status ACCEPT|COUNTER|REJECT, counter, leak}`; a leak is a public `LEAK` decision (subject `player:<id>:leak`, always seen) whose facts are only name, position, team, "a new deal", offered and asked years/money, its text the grounded model statement or a figure-free template (`statement_text`). `leak_allowed`: `LEAK_MAX_PER_PLAYER_SEASON = 1`, `LEAK_MAX_PER_WEEK = 3`. `respond_inbox(cur, thread, player_view, facts, *, llm, ...)` (always seen; subject `thread:<id>:msg:<seq>`) gives the reply and stance in JR's `CONTRACT` threads (its own `inbox_options`: `ACCEPT` when the engine accepted, only the engine's clearing counters when it countered — a `REJECT` beside a live counter let the player's words turn the offer down while the thread kept his counter — and `REJECT` when it rejected) and `ROLE_TALK` threads (`BUY_IN` / `PATIENT` / `FRUSTRATED`). **U3a wiring (built 2026-11-09).** The league office runs the coach loop for CPU charts and the player loop for CPU contract counters through the `counter_chooser` seam (§2.21a, §2.17b). The inbox `CONTRACT`/`ROLE_TALK` kinds call `player.respond_inbox` through the optional `loop_reply(cur, thread, intent, facts, llm, history=(), note=None)` hook that `voice.compose` asks first when a model is present; the reply is stored with source `LLM` (`inbox_messages.body_source` does not admit a `MODEL` source), carries no appraisal, and uses `message_seq=len(history)` with the resolved league id so each turn has its own `INBOX_REPLY` subject. `CONTRACT` passes the engine decision as `engine_status` and its counter as `counters.COUNTER_MIN` (the kind keeps no full clearing set); `ROLE_TALK` passes the thread state's `unhappy_weeks`. The switchboard features `coach_loop` and `player_loop` are installed (REQUIREMENTS point at `engines.agent_loops.base` and `2027_02_01_agent_loops.sql`) and off by default. **Promises and the marquee floor (AGENT_LOOPS_FOLLOWUPS_PLAN, built 2026-11-09).** The coach-promise watcher now runs `coach.promise_options` / `decide_promise` / `review_promises` each save ingest (`engines/agent_loops/watcher.py`, §6.0b): reviews first, then creation for CPU teams only; shadow records the decisions, active also appends the envelopes; JR's registry `user_teams` never run. CPU contract cases pass the season's marquee floor (the 50th-highest AAV from ACTIVE `player_contracts`), so a top-50 ask may spend the week's model budget; missing contract data keeps them policy-only. **U3b (built 2026-11-09):** the social desk's `PLAYER_STATEMENT` posts read the week's public `LEAK` rows for the publication window (at most `LEAK_MAX_PER_WEEK`; §7.8).


**Relationships and reactions (docs/done/PERSONALITY_RELATIONSHIPS_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-04, observe-only, nothing connected or applied):** five pure-or-explicit modules beside the core; profiles are never written, seeded or reseeded by them.
- **Canonical events (`relationship_events.py`, `RELATIONSHIP_SCHEMA_VERSION = 'relationships-v1'`):** one envelope `{schema_version, universe_id, event_id, source_event_id, source_kind, source_refs, kind, occurred_at {season, tick}, subject PersonRef, target PersonRef | TeamRef (null only for a correction), actor, basis (verified_simulation | reviewed_evidence + reviewer), confidence, reviewer, evidence_scope, visibility (private | public), attribution {responsible, reason_code, evidence_refs}, payload, supersedes_source_event_id}` per occurrence × subject × target × kind. PersonRef roles are the core's (`writer, gm, player, coach, owner, scout`); TeamRefs use the caller's trusted `team_registry` key (`team:<teams.id>`, kept through relocation). Kinds and required payloads: `tenure_window`, `role_window`, `meaningful_interaction`, `promise_made` (issuer, beneficiary, measurable criterion, due_at not before it was made, authority_ref), `promise_resolved` (kept | broken | waived | renegotiated | unknown; waiver/renegotiation need the beneficiary's acknowledgment; unknown is never broken), `treatment`, `repair`, `situation` (`valid_until` may be null), `home_familiarity`, `correction` (a replacement or a null retraction). Extra payload keys (producer rule names, appraisal reasons) are kept. A `mentorship` `meaningful_interaction` may carry an optional `direction` (`DIRECTIONS = ('mentor', 'mentee')`, the subject's role toward the target; rejected on other relationship kinds; absent envelopes hash as before). `validate_event_batch` dedupes identical facets, refuses facet, transport-ID and source-ref conflicts and checks ticks against the calendar `{season: ticks}`; `select_active` applies correction chains (cycles, competing corrections and missing targets excluded with reasons), knowledge (`head`) and effective-time cutoffs, drops a resolution without its promise and a repair without a breach, and orders by season, tick, kind order, source and facet. Missing calendar seasons block decay (`CalendarGapError`), never history reads.
- **Trust and attachment (`relationships.py`):** `validate_policy` (`mode` off | observe | enabled, the activation switchboard's off / shadow / active; `trust` and `attachment` are null for evidence-only observation or complete numeric sections, and `enabled` needs both; NO coefficients ship). `project_relationships(events, *, subject, as_of, known_through, policy, calendar)` gives one-way edges `{status known | unknown | conflicted, trust (−1..1; null when unknown or not numeric; known neutral is 0), confidence, coverage, meaningful_ties (each `{person, kind, direction, source_ids, relevant_to_team}`; kind and direction come from the first directed mentorship toward that person, else the first event; relevant_to_team only while the tie's own tenure covers as_of), unresolved_breaches, attachment {tier none | weak | established | strong | unknown, eligible, dimensions, blocking_reasons}, hometown, explanation [{code, source_ids, before, after, excluded_reason}], rule_version, policy_hash, input_hash, as_of, known_through}`. One source counts once per edge; positive contributions fade with the policy half-life; a breach (meaningful dismissal/disrespect, a broken promise) is attributed only to its responsible party or the promise issuer, keeps its full weight and caps trust at its floor until an accepted corrective repair (restitution, commitment met, reconciliation) closes it; an apology only acknowledges; repair never restores past neutral. Attachment is a conjunction of covered tenure, affirmative role/treatment evidence and relevant connections (no friend-count bonus; an open material breach blocks established/strong; partial history is unknown, not none; hometown never counts). `relationship_context(state, *, target=None)` is identical and neutral for off and observe.
- **Reactions and mood (`reactions.py`):** computed at read time from active facts and the relationship state; priorities breach > sustained role frustration (at least two contiguous unsatisfied role windows, never one scan) > job/injury uncertainty > transition > achievement; same-domain conflicts become `mixed`; `select_mood` gives one primary and up to two non-contradictory secondary tags (`neutral, frustrated, uncertain, encouraged, eager, mixed`), ranked by priority, policy severity, recency and source. A loss gives no reaction; an injury is uncertainty, never resentment. Unknown-origin identities stay neutral; a missing profile reacts to recorded events only; real-inspired and generated personas react alike. `reaction_context` is neutral unless enabled; `public_context` keeps only public-source reactions, framed as the fictional character's interior. `validate_evolution_candidate(candidate, *, profile, source_events, slider_band=None)` returns review_required | ready | blocked for the evolution plan's arbiter (support must be active, the subject's, non-duplicate and not after the season; the core's own `apply_change` runs on a copy; `blocked_slider_band` only when the caller's database band, e.g. `(30, 30)` without `2027_01_17`, rejects it). Nothing calls `store.change`, writes mood, or touches ratings, form, Madden morale or contracts.
- **Store and preview:** the ledger is §3.3t; the offline preview is §1.2.
- **Event producers (§3.3r, docs/done/RELATIONSHIP_EVENT_PRODUCERS_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-04, off by default):** relationship events now come from the simulation as well as the inbox and pressers: tenure and role windows, releases (dismissal), re-signs (recognition), arrivals and departures, injuries, awards, team results, contract years and coach facts, all by fixed versioned rules with no model calls (D1). A lost role is a demotion only, while healthy, below a role held 4 eligible weeks (D2). A one-time catch-up rebuilds events from stored weekly data, never HISTORY rows (D3). Events for people without an identity, coaches included, wait in a held queue and append once the lifecycle plan registers them (D4). There is no `home_familiarity` source.
- **On the site (D3 as built, docs/done/PERSONALITY_DISPLAY_PLAN.md; built 2026-11-06):** `server/personality_api.py` (§4.8) and the Personality panel (§5.2 item 14) show everyone in the league in words: slider sentences with a 0–10 bar (a description, not an engine effect; `SHOW_SLIDER_BARS` hides the bars), traits with their tendency, this week's mood tag, evolution change notes, ties as labels (trusts / on good terms with / wary of / at odds with / holds a grudge against / mentor to), attachment tier words, open promises and only the PUBLIC trade-request projection. No trust values, coefficients, chances or draws are served. Prospects stay hidden until drafted (404 `hidden_until_drafted`). JR edits any core-managed profile on the page with the `#debug` token through `store.override` (actor JR, reason required; a `note:` reason enters the change notes). Mood, ties and attachment follow the switchboard's `relationships` feature for the league (`Sources.relationship_policy` → `features.relationship_policy`): off → unavailable; shadow → an observe policy, so still neutral and unavailable; active → the enabled policy built from the feature's version and reviewed `trust`/`attachment`/`reactions` config (an incomplete config is unavailable with its reason). `personality_api.RELATIONSHIP_POLICY`, when set, overrides the switchboard (tests).


Personality plan phases 1, 2, and 3 (`docs/in_progress/PERSONALITY_PLAN.md`): personas are character, not orders. Phase 4 has a review-only historical Panthers evidence sample (`docs/reference/PERSONALITY_PANTHERS_SAMPLE.md`, 2026-10-30): two scratch-roster players and two coach seed candidates, sparse catalogue mappings, neutral sliders, provenance and proposed wording-only permissions. JR rollout decision (2026-10-30, personality plan §5.1): control the simulation through 2034, prioritize persistent generated-draft-class personalities and bounded contract/development/trade/career effects in owning engines; initialize generated people already at the starting checkpoint and participating decision-makers. Stop expanding current-player research; retain the Panthers sample as an evidence-method reference. The review-only generated-player design (`docs/reference/PERSONALITY_GENERATED_EFFECTS_DESIGN.md`) audits existing hooks, proposes a capped contract-utility adjustment with matched fictional examples, specifies prospect identity/persistence and event evolution, and sequences later progression/request/retirement work; trial coefficients are not activated. Offline checks covered 100 deterministic profiles and 17 existing free-agency tests passed. No production seeding or new effects are activated by this decision; sparse real-person validation and enforceable evidence permissions remain unresolved for real-person activation. Unified across writers, GMs, players, coaches, owners, agents and scouts.
- **Phase 1: Writer Structure (`agent_personas.json`):** Each of the 38 archetypes (`archetypes`; old `article_personas` folded in as `formats.ARTICLE`) defines:
  - **`voice`**: who they are and whose style they write in.
  - **`sliders`**: temperament, sociability, confidence, openness, warmth, drive, 0–10 each, totalling exact 30 budget. Rendered as one sentence ("By nature you are …"); 0–3 and 7–10 get a word, 4–6 are left out.
  - **`traits`**: 3–5 keys from `persona_traits.json` (the shared catalogue: category, role draw weights, label, a "tends to …" prompt, optional `when` tags, conflicts). At most two per category, no conflicting pair.
  - **`views`**: opinions, each with `when` tags. A piece shows at most 3 matching views (most matched tags first, ties seeded), topped up to 2 from the general views (empty `when`); unmatched situational views stay out of the prompt.
  - **`signatures`**: 2–5 optional moves with an optional `detect` regex. Moves found in the writer's last 3 articles (or 15 posts) are listed as used and left out of the offer.
  - **`want`** and **`fear`**: background motivation, shown under IN THE BACKGROUND with "do not state it".
  - **`formats`**: habits for `ARTICLE` and/or `POST`.
  - **`post_style`** (optional, `social_writer.render_post_style`): the measured posting shape for this archetype from the 2026-11-02 real-tweet audit — `length` (word range), `numbers` (per post), `case`, `punctuation`, `hashtags`, `profanity` (mild and rare, fan archetypes only per D6), `off_topic_share`. **`post_shapes`** (optional): weights for `social_writer.POST_SHAPES`, used by `pick_shape`.
- **Phase 2: Expanded Catalogue & DB Migration (`persona_traits.json`, `2027_01_09_personas.sql`):**
  - **50-Trait Catalogue**: 7 categories (Cognitive, Social, Risk/Strategy, Emotional, Values, Football Philosophy, Quirks). Each trait includes symmetric conflicts, role probability odds (`writer`, `gm`, `player`, `coach`, `owner`, `scout`, `media`), "tends to" prompt text, application `when` triggers, and engine effects. Validated by `validate_trait_catalogue()`.
  - **Database Persistence**: Five tables keyed by `(persona_type, persona_id)`: `persona_sliders`, `persona_traits`, `persona_views`, `persona_relationships`, `persona_trait_history` (§3.3o).
  - **Seeding & Loader**: Deterministic pseudo-random seeding `f"{persona_type}:{persona_id}"` deals a slider total of exactly 30 (`SLIDER_BUDGET`) and non-conflicting role-weighted traits. `validate_slider_budget` (used by `save_persona`, `seed_writers_to_db` and `POST /api/debug/personas`) requires each slider to be an integer in 0–10 and the total in `SLIDER_BUDGET_MIN`–`SLIDER_BUDGET_MAX` (24–36), else `ValueError('Slider total N outside budget band 24-36')`; hand edits and event moves may leave the total anywhere in the band (JR, 2026-11-02). `load_personas(cur=None)` loads from DB tables when a cursor is provided, falling back seamlessly to `agent_personas.json` if the DB is empty or unreachable. Single-entity helpers `get_persona(cur, type, id)` and `save_persona(cur, persona)` support CRUD and transaction rollbacks. All database reads guard against missing relations via `persona_tables_exist(cur)` and nested savepoints (`with cur.connection.transaction():`), guaranteeing that unmigrated databases never abort the ambient PostgreSQL transaction.
- **Phase 3: GM Integration & Debug UI:**
  - **GM Trade & Negotiation Reflection**: `engines/gm_personas.py` seeds GM personas via `ensure_gm_persona()`. `engines/gm_trade_engine.py` (`read_books`) attaches sliders and traits to `b["gm"]`. `engines/gm_negotiation.py` injects GM disposition and active traits into negotiation prompt context (`message_prompt`) and reflects loyalty/patience in dialogue templates (`template_message`), leaving deterministic trade math unaffected.
  - **Debug Review Endpoints (`server/debug_api.py`):**
    - `GET /api/debug/personas?type={writer|gm|...}&id={id}`: lists seeded personas with sliders, traits, and views, plus a `core` block (origin, revision, persona_id, view_version, links) for core-managed personas.
    - `POST /api/debug/personas/{persona_type}/{persona_id}`: manual edit endpoint protected by `X-Debug-Token`. Unmanaged personas: `save_persona`, validating slider budgets and trait catalogue rules. Core-managed personas: sliders and traits through the personality core's audited override (`reason` required, §4.5); views stay legacy. `save_persona` raises `CoreManagedError` for a core-managed persona's sliders or traits, and `seed_writers_to_db` / `seed_gms_to_db` skip core-managed IDs (printed, and appended to an optional `skipped` list). `SUPERSTITIOUS` and `WORKOUT_FANATIC` carry `writer` odds 0.05 (2026-11-04, so all 40 writers validate as adopted core profiles).

**Tags.** Topics come from the article type id (keyword rules: DRAFT/MOCK → `DRAFT`, TRADE → `TRADE`, QUARTERBACK → `QB`+`SCHEME`, RECAP/AUTOPSY/REPORT_CARD → `GAME_REVIEW`, …; `OFFSEASON_*` → `OFFSEASON`), the post kind (`POST_KIND_TAGS`), and the week (19–23 `PLAYOFFS`, 24+ `OFFSEASON`). Signals come from the season's completed regular-season games before the week (`signals_from_games`): for the subject team `RECORD_OUTRUNS_DIFF` / `RECORD_TRAILS_DIFF` (wins − Pythagorean wins ≥ 1.0 / ≤ −1.0, 4+ games), `CLOSE_GAMES` (a lopsided one-score record: 4+ games decided by 1–7 points, at least 75% or at most 25% of them won), `CONTENDER` (≥ .650) / `STRUGGLING` (≤ .350), `WIN_STREAK` / `LOSING_STREAK` (3+), `BLOWOUT` (last game by 17+), `UPSET` (last game won by the side whose prior win% was .250+ lower; both teams 3+ games). Without a subject team, league-level signals need a standout (luck ≥ 2.0, streak ≥ 5).

**Prompt block** (`render_persona`, order): voice; HOW YOU HAVE CHANGED LATELY (up to 2 evolution change notes, when given); slider sentence; TENDENCIES (traits whose `when` matches or is empty); HOW YOU WRITE A COLUMN / A POST; VIEWS OF YOURS THAT MAY BEAR ON THIS PIECE; SIGNATURE MOVES (optional, at most one); USED IN YOUR LAST FEW PIECES; IN THE BACKGROUND (want/fear); YOUR RECENT PIECES (the last 5 article headlines, articles only: find a different angle). Deterministic for a seed of agent, season, week, format, type or kind, team and subject. `build_persona_block` adds the database parts (signals, recent work from `news_feed` before this week) inside a savepoint; a failure drops only those parts. Recent work is the agent's own rows by `agent_id`; articles saved before 2026-10-28 have no `agent_id` (the insert didn't store it until then) and are matched by `persona` = archetype, except for archetypes many agents share (`SHARED_ARCHETYPES`: beat reporters, die-hard and bandwagon fans, former players). Used by `compile_agent_prompt`, the Agent Wire writer (`social_publish._Writer.prompt`), `tools/social_model_compare.py`; `custom_commission.load_article_catalog` reads the archetypes for writer matching. A post prompt adds the archetype's `post_style`, the sampled `SHAPE` and the writer's relationship block as `YOUR BIASES` (AGENT_WIRE_VOICE_PLAN §2.3). `build_persona_block(..., subjects=None)` appends the same relationship block for articles when a cursor and `agent_id` are given (the post path passes `relationships=False` so its block appears once), so `swarm_dispatcher` needs no change.

**Tests:** `tests/test_personas.py` (Phase 1 structure: slider budget, trait mix and conflicts, known tags, views, signatures, tone constraints, signals, view selection, avoid list, database fallback); `tests/test_personas.py` also snapshots `seed_sliders` for five fixed IDs; `tests/test_personality_contract_demo.py` adds `test_preferences_never_invert_base_weights` (Money First k < 0.20 and Ring Chaser k < 0.45 never invert the base weights); `tests/test_personas_db.py` (Phases 2 & 3: catalogue integrity, the 24–36 slider band, the writer loader skipping out-of-band rows, migration and init_db text checks, conflict symmetry, deterministic seeding, DB persistence, fallback resilience when tables are missing, GM integration, and debug API endpoints).

**Offline player-contract demonstration:** `python -m tools.personality_contract_demo [--out verify_output/personality_contract_demo]` writes synthetic `report.json` and `README.md`: seven situations, 21 default comparisons and 525 coefficient/cap combinations, using current free-agency component scores and role constraints with proposed modifiers outside the production engine. Compares money/contention, career-gated strong ring preference, earned attachment tiers separately from smaller hometown preference, equal-strength $10M/$11M offers, aggregate caps, threshold crossings and star-backup rejection. Earned attachment tiers are hypothetical history inputs, not counts of relationships; financial security is explicit, not inferred from OVR. This isolates immediate score eligibility and preference; no noise, counteroffers, cap/legal validation, market execution, database or save writes. Context bonuses apply to all compared ambition variants only where explicitly established. No production integration is activated. `tests/test_personality_contract_demo.py` (6 checks) and existing free-agency tests (17) pass; the inline comparison also passed browser interaction and narrow-layout checks.

**Contract policy comparison report** (PERSONALITY_CONTRACT_POLICY_PLAN U1): `python3 -m tools.personality_contract_policy_report --input tests/fixtures/contract_policy/cohorts.json --out verify_output/contract_policy --mode neutral|shadow|compare` scores fictional cohorts with the free-agency engine's own components plus `engines/personality_contract_policy.py`, makes paired seeded decisions (the engine's ranking noise, mood and counter search) and writes byte-identical `report.json`/`report.md`: signed deltas and cap saturation, ranking/threshold/counter flips, accepted AAV and cap-share distributions, team concentration, missing profile/career/security rates, family activation and a contender-gate sweep listing every cross-certification drop. Offline trial evidence for JR's review; no DB, no activation, the demo files above are unchanged. Profile/catalogue availability is not activation; players read as generated profiles; the relationships plan owns trust/attachment/breach classification; no money-to-work-ethic inference.

**Comparison:** `python3 tools/persona_side_by_side.py [--season 2036] [--week 12] [--slate 4] [--barnwell-weeks 8 12 16] [--model M]` writes the week's first national slate articles (beat and fantasy skipped) plus a Barnwell column for each given week twice, with the old personas (`article_personas` over `archetypes`) and old writer slate filters read from git at `6b8aa81`, and with the current ones; nothing is saved to `news_feed` or memory (Gemini calls still log to `llm_usage`). Output: both persona blocks, headlines, texts and simple measures (words, regression mentions, a Regression Warning heading, subheadings) in `verify_output/persona_side_by_side_<season>_w<week>.md` and `.json`.

### 7.12 Dual ReAct Tool Execution Engine (`newsroom/tool_loop/`)
Dual ReAct tool calling architecture for newsroom writer agents (docs/done/PC_MIGRATION_PLAN.md §7.3, §7.4; docs/not_started/PRE_PC_WORK_2.md Item A6). Encapsulates Gemini AFC while providing a drop-in multi-turn tool execution loop for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, vLLM, Ollama `qwen2.5:14b`, OpenAI).
- **Schema Converter (`newsroom/tool_loop/schema.py`):** `python_func_to_openai_tool(fn) -> dict` converts Python callables, docstrings (Google/Sphinx), type hints, LangChain tools (`@tool`, `args_schema`), and Pydantic `BaseModel` classes into standard OpenAI tool definitions `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": ..., "description": ..., "parameters": {...}}}`. Excludes `*args`/`**kwargs` and accurately determines required fields.
- **OpenAI Multi-Turn Loop (`newsroom/tool_loop/openai_loop.py`):** `run_openai_tool_loop(client, model, system_instruction, prompt, tools, max_steps=50, temperature=0.7, provider="openai") -> ToolLoopResult`. With `client=None` it builds an `openai.OpenAI` client for `provider` from `PROVIDER_ENDPOINTS` (`resolve_endpoint`): openai (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`), deepseek (`DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` default `https://api.deepseek.com`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`), glm (`GLM_BASE_URL` default `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4`, `GLM_API_KEY`), vllm (`VLLM_BASE_URL` default `http://localhost:8000/v1`), ollama (`OLLAMA_OPENAI_BASE_URL`, else `engines.llm_provider.get_ollama_base_url()` + `/v1`); a hosted provider without its key returns an error result. Needs the `openai` package for the default client. Drives `client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, tools=openai_tools)`. Handles assistant message creation, robust JSON argument parsing (returns descriptive errors to model if malformed), execution of target Python callbacks with console logging, appending tool response messages, and turns continuation up to `max_steps`. Includes automatic fallback synthesis if the model completes research without final markdown text.
- **Gemini AFC Loop (`newsroom/tool_loop/gemini_loop.py`):** `run_gemini_tool_loop(client, model, system_instruction, prompt, tools, temperature=0.7, max_steps=50) -> ToolLoopResult`. Encapsulates `newsroom/swarm_dispatcher.py` (lines 1494–1540), preserving logging wrappers, signature preservation via `@functools.wraps`, AFC configuration (`maximum_remote_calls=max_steps`), token tracking via `UsageMeter` (all AFC calls) or, without a meter, the summed `usage_metadata` of the AFC turn's final response and the synthesis follow-up (intermediate AFC calls are not visible there), and fallback synthesis prompts.
- **Router (`newsroom/tool_loop/router.py`):** `execute_agent_tool_loop(provider, client, model, system_instruction, prompt, tools, **kwargs) -> ToolLoopResult`. Dispatches to `run_gemini_tool_loop` if `provider == "gemini"` or `run_openai_tool_loop` if `provider in ("openai", "ollama", "vllm", "deepseek", "glm")`. Infers provider if omitted: a `provider:` / `provider/` prefix or a provider name in the model (`gemini`, `deepseek`, `glm`), then an Ollama-style `name:tag` model (`qwen2.5:14b`, `gemma4:12b`) → ollama, then `LLM_PROVIDER`, else gemini. A prefix naming the resolved provider is stripped before the call (`ollama:qwen2.5:14b` → `qwen2.5:14b`), and the resolved provider is passed to the OpenAI loop.
- **Standardized Result Model (`newsroom/tool_loop/models.py`):** `ToolLoopResult(text: str, usage: dict, tool_calls_count: dict[str, int], iterations: int, error: Optional[str])`.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_openai_tool_loop.py` (32 tests covering default provider endpoints, prefix stripping, schema conversion, multi-turn loop, parallel calls, tool errors, malformed JSON, max_steps, fallback synthesis, usage accumulation, Gemini AFC encapsulation, and provider routing).

### 7.13 Nightly GPU Queue Scheduler (`pipeline/gpu_queue/`)
Standalone offline task scheduler enforcing strict sequential GPU residency across local models on the PC's RTX 5070 Ti (16GB VRAM) (docs/done/PC_MIGRATION_PLAN.md §7.5, §7.8; docs/not_started/PRE_PC_WORK_2.md Item A7). Solves VRAM contention between active Madden gameplay, 14–27B LLMs, and image generation.
- **Priority Tiers (§7.8):** Enforces strict execution order:
  - **Tier 1 (Text):** Newsroom text generation (Agent Wire batches, agent memory takes, scouting notes, GM text).
  - **Tier 2 (Image):** Player headshot generation (`headshots/local/`) and portrait texture conversion (`headshots/portrait_converter/`).
  - **Tier 3 (Audio):** TTS production and synthetic pregame/postgame broadcast segments.
- **Madden Active Process Guard (`pipeline/gpu_queue/process_check.py`):** Queries Windows/WSL2 `tasklist.exe` or Unix `pgrep` for `Madden27.exe`. Matches exact process names (`tasklist.exe` CSV, `pgrep -i -x`, or `ps -eo comm=`), never full command lines. Immediately unloads active models from VRAM if Madden launches, pauses queue execution, and resumes when Madden exits or Madden is idle: `is_madden_idle_fn` decides idleness, and with `idle_timeout` set Madden must be reported idle continuously that many seconds (the clock resets when it isn't). `idle_timeout` without `is_madden_idle_fn` is ignored; time since Madden started never counts as idle.
- **Sequential Model Residency & Batching (`pipeline/gpu_queue/runner.py`):** Batches pending jobs for the currently loaded model to eliminate redundant model swapping overhead, unloading each model completely before loading the next tier's weights into VRAM. Jobs run through handlers registered per kind (`register_handler`); a job whose kind has no handler is marked failed ("No handler registered…") before any model loads, unless a `default_handler` is passed (`mock_job_handler` does no work, for dry runs and tests). `run_loop(requeue_stale=True)` first returns jobs left `running` by a crashed run to `pending` (`GPUQueue.requeue_running`).
- **Pluggable Storage (`pipeline/gpu_queue/queue.py`):** Operates without PostgreSQL dependencies using thread-safe SQLite WAL mode (`data/gpu_queue.db`) or atomic JSON file replacement (`data/gpu_queue.json`). `get_next_job` claims a job with `store.claim()`, a conditional pending→running update (one `UPDATE … WHERE status='pending'` in SQLite, so runners in separate processes never take the same job), and reselects if it lost the race.
- **Standalone CLI (`pipeline/gpu_queue/cli.py`):** `python -m pipeline.gpu_queue.cli [enqueue|list|run|clear|check-madden]`. No real job handlers are wired into the CLI yet, so `run` refuses without `--dry-run` (mock handler: marks jobs completed without doing work). `run` requeues stale `running` jobs first unless `--no-requeue-stale`; also `--once`, `--poll-interval`, `--max-iterations`, `--ignore-madden`, `--no-stop-on-empty`. `list`/`clear --status` take any status, including `cancelled`.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_gpu_queue.py` (28 tests covering job claiming and stale-job requeue, missing-handler failures, idle timeout, SQLite/JSON persistence, tier prioritization, model batching, Madden process detection, and model lifecycle unloads).
### 7.14 Postgame Press Conferences (`newsroom/press_room.py`, `newsroom/press_agents.py`, `newsroom/press_facts.py`, PRESS_CONFERENCE_PLAN, V2.2)

Every head coach holds a postgame presser after every completed game, the way the real league does. Writer agents raise their hands, the coach picks who asks, reporters ask and follow up and pick up on each other, and the coach answers — an AI coach as his own agent, JR's coach as JR typing in the Game Center. The presser ends when the reporters run out of questions or the coach has had enough. Who attends is cast by pre-game interest (§2.22). The 31 AI pressers run in the background after the week is ingested; JR's waits behind a button on the Game Center and counts as declined if he presses Play Game without taking it. Transcripts become the only source of head-coach quotes in that week's beat coverage. Every reporter remembers what was said and judges how the coach treated it; that judgment is recorded as relationship events for the relationships plan, which owns trust, and never touches a sim number.

**Fact sheet and line checker (`newsroom/press_facts.py`).** `fact_sheet(cur, game_id)` builds the frozen facts both pressers of a game share: the game (final and quarter scores, type, week, home/away, broadcast window), the box-score text, the game-script summary (shape, storyline, lead changes, largest lead, the winner's deficit, key moments), both teams (record before and after, streak, division place and conference seed, the head coach with id/name/tenure/schemes/tendencies and the hot-seat line when present, the team line with nulls for unrecorded stats, every recorded player line with season per-game averages from earlier games, new injuries, this week's roster moves and broken records), the league (this week's other results, the top of the standings, the playoff picture from Week 10), `names` (every person the sheet contains) and a flat `(stat, subject, value)` `numbers` index. Unknown stays null, never 0. `check_line(text, sheet, speaker)` returns `{"kind": "NUMBER"|"NAME"|"EVENT", "span", "claim", "recorded"}` for wrong scores, `N <stat>` phrases tied to the nearest preceding name or the team, records and streaks, first-place and playoff claims, unknown two- and three-word names (with an exception list for real press-pool figures), and unsupported `<name>'s touchdown/interception/fumble/sack` attributions; ages, contract figures and historical claims are out of scope, and opinions and tone always pass. A per-game average is accepted spoken either truncated or rounded (`int(value)` or `round(value)`), and a coach is flagged on the hot seat only when `coach_hot_seat` has him fired or at the producer rules' pressure share of his firing line — the table writes a row for all 32 teams each offseason, so "a retained row exists" once put every returning coach on the hot seat and docked him 2 patience.

**The agents (`newsroom/press_agents.py`).** `reporter_turn` writes one reporter action (`ASK`|`FOLLOW_UP`|`REACT`|`PASS`, with `about`, `tone` and `reply_to`) from the persona (POST habits, `GAME_REVIEW`), the memory block, the reporter's one-way `relationship_context` when enabled (omitted while neutral), the beat/national line, the frozen fact sheet, the transcript and its hand/pick counts; text is at most 60 words, uses only sheet numbers and names, may not repeat a question, and is checked with `press_facts.check_line` — one retry with the problem spelled out, then the hand is dropped. `coach_turn` writes `OPENING`/`ANSWER`/`CLOSING` from the coach profile (name, tenure, schemes, tendencies, record, hot seat), the personality view when one exists (`personality.store` + `core.feature_view(profile, 'press')`) else the neutral line "plain, professional, guarded about injuries and the game plan", the result and mood, the sheet, the transcript and hand-written podium guidance; at most 120 words, checked and retried once, then the passing sentences or "We'll look at the tape on that one." with `source = 'FALLBACK'`. `coach_pick` shows the AI coach the raised hands (names, outlets, roles, follow-ups marked) and his own pick/skip history from `press_hands` (`skip_history`) but never the drafted questions; `coach_views` is the empty slot for the coach's own views (None today), and an invalid pick is retried once then replaced by `fallback_pick` (last asker's follow-up, then least picked, beats before nationals, seeded ties; `source = 'FALLBACK'`). `patience_budget` starts at 14, +1 for a win, −1 for a loss by 17+, −1 per loss beyond a two-game losing streak, −2 on the hot seat, and `round((temperament − 5) × 0.5)` when a personality exists, clamped to [6, 20]; an answered question costs 1 (a pointed or repeated one 2). Safety rules are code: `MAX_QUESTIONS = 25`, `MAX_FOLLOW_UPS_IN_A_ROW = 2`, a reporter who passes twice in a row is done, and a presser ends on PATIENCE, SUBJECT_ENDED (wants to end with ≤ 3 questions left), RAN_OUT or CAP. `reporter_judgment`/`validate_judgment` produce the appraisal (exchanges, treatment, memory) with own-turn filtering, NO_COMMENT never positive, treatment consistency and declined-presser rules, ≤30-word reasons and a `check_line`-safe memory; `judgment_events` turns it into relationships-plan envelopes (subject the reporter, target/actor the coach, `verified_simulation`/`medium`/`public`, stable `press:<conference>:turn:<id>`, `press:<conference>:treatment:<agent>` and `press:<conference>:declined` source ids) that `personality.relationship_events.validate_event` accepts.

**Research corpus (`tools/press_corpus.py`, `docs/reference/PRESS_CONFERENCE_CORPUS.md`).** 175 real head-coach postgame pressers from 2023–2025 (30 of 32 teams, 161 regular season and 14 postseason), parsed into 2,092 questions. `python3 -m tools.press_corpus stats` writes `newsroom/config/press_corpus_stats.json`; `eval --transcripts DIR` compares a directory of generated pressers on questions per presser, follow-up rate, question length and question-type mix. It is reference and test material only: no transcript text enters a prompt (D8) and the raw transcripts stay in the git-ignored `data/press_corpus/`.

**The engine and the runner (`newsroom/press_room.py`).** `schedule_week` casts a week and inserts both coaches' conferences (AI subjects SCHEDULED for the runner; a user-controlled subject SCHEDULED with the first round of hands pre-drafted, so JR can pick at once). `run_session` is the state machine: the coach's OPENING, then in parallel a `reporter_turn` for every attendee who isn't done (validated, one retry, then the hand is dropped), the hands recorded in `press_hands`, the coach's pick (`coach_pick` for an AI coach, JR through the API), the QUESTION turn, the ANSWER (validated; a user subject's session pauses at `awaiting_answer`), then the patience and done flags and the end conditions, repeating until CLOSING. Reporter hands drafted before an answer stay valid when the answer did not touch their `about` subject (`PRESS_REPOLL = 'changed'`; `'all'` re-polls everyone), which keeps the wait between JR's answer and the next raised hands to one parallel round. `run_week` runs the AI pressers `PRESS_WORKERS = 6` at a time, retries FAILED ones, completes effects left behind by an interrupted run, never lets one failure stop the week, and returns `{closed, failed, scheduled_user, calls, input_tokens, output_tokens, seconds}`. `close_effects` runs once per conference on CLOSED or DECLINED (judging each reporter, storing the envelopes, writing the PRESS memory); `flush_relationship_events` appends waiting envelopes through the relationships store and leaves them waiting when it is absent. `decline` turns a SCHEDULED or LIVE presser into DECLINED and approves a REVIEW one as it stands (D7); `expire_user_pressers` is the next ingest's fallback. `subject_controller` reads the franchise registry's `user_teams` (an empty list means JR controls no team). `approved_quotes(cur, season, week, team_id=None)` returns CLOSED, on-record ANSWER turns joined to their questions and is the stable V3 quote interface; `brief_block`/`declined_note` feed the beat briefs; `get_press_conference(team, season, week)` is the beat writers' tool, cut by publication week. The model routes through `generate_text(..., source='press')` (so `LLM_PROVIDER_PRESS` applies) with `PRESS_MODEL` as the override. The CLI is `run-week --season S --week W [--workers 6] [--team ABBR] [--model M] [--dry-run]`, `show --conference ID`, `wakeup --team ABBR --season S --week W` and `cast --season S --week W`; `--dry-run` prints the casts and the first round's prompts and makes no model calls; `wakeup`'s `--week` is the game week its presser covers, and the wakeup it starts runs for the league's current week. Approve and decline open their wakeup connection with `row_factory=dict_row` (`maybe_start_team_wakeup` reads dict rows, and a tuple cursor raised a swallowed `TypeError`, so the beat wakeup never started); the session reads `league_state.madden_league_id` for the personality switchboard (a hardcoded 1 always read `off`) and resolves the coach's persona through the `db-coach:<id>` alias, so `relationship_store` accepts the presser events; `_effects_pending_ids` covers DECLINED pressers and earlier weeks, not only this week's CLOSED ones.

**What the corpus found.** Pressers after losses and blowout losses are longer than after wins (13.1 and 13.5 questions versus 10.9), and follow-ups are fewer after a blowout loss (5.8% versus 14.6% after a win) — the opposite of a model in which a bad loss ends the presser early. Mean question length 21.5 words, mean answer 80.5; question types PLAYER_PERFORMANCE 18.8%, TEAM_EXECUTION 14.3%, EMOTION_STORY 6.4%, SCHEME_ADJUSTMENT 6.3%, COACHING_DECISION 5.2%. The local-model spike measured one warm five-call round at 5.3 s on `gemma4:12b` (~74 s, 64 calls per presser extrapolated); the cloud half was not measured because the build worktree had no credentials.

### 7.15 Annual Compensatory Picks Announcement (`newsroom/compensatory_picks_article.py`, COMPENSATORY_PICKS_PLAN U3)
Deterministic league-office announcement, built only from `compensatory_pick_awards` joined to teams (and the source player/coach) plus the season's `qualifying_free_agents` counts: headline, excerpt, a round-by-round award list with each stored `reason`, "By the Numbers" counts, a JC-2A section and the QFA-ledger paragraph. Every number comes from the rows. Written in the SANDO front-office voice under `article_type COMPENSATORY_PICKS_ANNOUNCEMENT`, slot `Standalone`, stored in `news_feed` on `--publish` (skipped when an article already exists for the season/week/type unless `--force`). CLI: `python3 -m newsroom.compensatory_picks_article --draft-season N [--season N] [--week W] [--dry-run] [--publish] [--force]`. Scheduling is stage/season driven: `--week` defaults to `OFFSEASON_STAGE_WEEKS["FREE_AGENCY"]` (26) because weeks 19–23 are the playoffs (the plan's "Week 21" is not an offseason slot); the weekly/league-office scheduling hook is a follow-up.

### 7.15b Annual NFLPA Team Report Cards (`newsroom/report_card_article.py`, NFLPA_REPORT_CARD_PLAN U2)
Deterministic exposé built only from `team_report_cards` joined to teams: the full 1–32 ranking with all eight category grades, the overall grade/score and top/bottom-5 summaries (each figure from the rows). SANDO voice, `article_type NFLPA_REPORT_CARD`, slot `Standalone`, stored in `news_feed` on `--publish` (skipped for an existing season/week/type unless `--force`). CLI: `python3 -m newsroom.report_card_article --season N [--week W] [--dry-run] [--publish] [--force]`. `--week` defaults to `OFFSEASON_STAGE_WEEKS["FREE_AGENCY"]` (26) because weeks 19–23 are the playoffs (the plan's "Week 21" is not an offseason slot); the weekly/league-office scheduling hook is a follow-up.
